# Effective Diophantine methods and certified rational points

Revision 4 · `BP-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~4` · 16 October 2026 · [packet](../packets/EffectiveDiophantineMethods.json) · [suggested statements](../suggested/EffectiveDiophantineMethods.lean)

This roadmap plans proofs that a finite rational-point or Diophantine solution list is exhaustive. Its route is exact algebraic and local precision certificates, lattice exclusion, explicit logarithmic bounds, descent and saturation, Chabauty–Coleman, the Mordell–Weil sieve and explicit quadratic Chabauty. Mathematical completeness is a conclusion of bounds and checked finite coverage, never an input assertion about the proposed answer list.

The packet is a **complete planning pass**. All seven stages are **planned**, none is closed, and every implementation status is **unchecked**. The accepted 175 target IDs are retained and three minimal-numerics targets are added. A statement with a proof placeholder is not a formalized theorem. The 27 recorded mathematical/interface/data gaps remain visible below; completeness of this planning pass does not claim to fill them.

The maintainer’s 16 October directive withdraws ComputationalNumberTheory from the active dependency graph. ED.0 owns only the mathematical certificates for selected exact algebraic values, isolations, valuations and local precision. ED.2 owns rational finite-sum error bounds for archimedean and p-adic logarithms sufficient for reduction. These have existence and soundness statements, with no algorithm or complexity model. Every other instance-specific computational input—unit/class tables, finite groups and point counts, cohomology/Hecke/Frobenius matrices, integral coefficients and L-value enclosures—is an explicit hypothesis at its consumer. Their production is outside this roadmap. The conditional theorem must still prove its bound, exhaustive coverage and final solution-set equality.

The independent [revision 4 review](../reviews/REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~4.md) accepts this plan after correcting the isolation interface, an empty height-search minimum, weighted-chain API, a symmetric-square regression and stale computational-producer signatures. It independently recovers all nine primary passages left unresolved by the [revision 3 review](../reviews/REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~3.md). The evidence register below preserves revision provenance; acceptance does not certify any instance-specific numerical transcript or complete a formal proof.

## Notation, ownership and prerequisites

- All rational intervals and boxes are closed. A root isolation identifies an actual algebraic value, with a nonzero polynomial and unique-root statement; overlapping boxes do not identify two values. General real algebraic geometry belongs to the current upstream RealAlgebraicGeometry roadmap. ED only certifies the selected values used here.
- At a finite place use additive ord with ord(0)=+∞, ord(π)=1 and e=ord(p). A ball B(c,N) means ord(x−c)≥N. The Qp specialization has e=1. Do not substitute Mathlib’s totalized integer valuation at0 for this convention. Exact dense centres lie in the number field, rather than Q when the local degree exceeds1.
- Archimedean logarithms use Mathlib’s principal Complex.log, with argument in(−π,π]; a box meeting the closed negative real axis does not give a continuous argument enclosure. A chosen p-adic branch log(π) is separate data; unit logarithms and their power relations do not depend on it.
- The pinned elliptic canonical height is half the full x-height limit. Divide both Cremona’s comparison and its constants by2. Silverman1990 Theorem1.1 uses the absolute half-height; for a number field of degree d compare it with pinned relative canonicalHeight/d and naiveHeight/(2d). Local archimedean weights are n_v=[K_v:R] and are divided by d.
- General lattice reduction, height/transcendence theory, finite-index group theory, curve/Jacobian/Picard geometry, Coleman integration and nonabelian-height theory keep their existing owners. A requested interface remains a request; a broad roadmap title does not supply an absent precise theorem.
- The current upstream roadmaps and library were read without modifying or building them. RealAlgebraicGeometry already owns general Sturm/Thom infrastructure. NumberFieldArithmetic’s prime-degree rank-one unit criterion is not a full-unit-table generator. Current TauCeti local-field logarithms already provide principal-unit convergence and deep-unit isometry; ED adds only finite-tail/precision adapters. The exact pinned baseline and later reuse information are distinguished below.

## Worked certificate mathematics

### Exact algebraic values and local precision

The polynomial X²−2 and interval[1,3/2] isolate +√2; X²+1 and the rational complex disc centred at i of radius1/2 isolate i. Finiteness of the distinct roots and rational density give arbitrarily narrow isolations. Existing field operations supply the exact sum/product/inverse values, which can then be isolated. Intervals[1,2] for √2 and √3 overlap, although the algebraic values differ. Equality therefore uses exact algebraic/common-root data, never overlap.

For x∈B(c,N), y∈B(d,M), and a≤ord(x),ord(c), b≤ord(y),ord(d), write xy−cd=x(y−d)+d(x−c). This proves product precision min(M+a,N+b). At p=3, B(3,4)·B(9,5)⊆B(27,6). Inversion at B(9,5) loses twice the centre valuation, giving B(1/9,1). A zero-centred ball retains a lower valuation bound: B(0,4)·B(9,5)⊆B(0,6). Cancellation of the centres of B(1,4)+B(−1,4) guarantees precision4, not exact0.

If the pivot log has minimal valuation s=2, all numerator and pivot errors at absolute precision9 give normalized coefficient precision7. The pivot error must also be strictly deeper than its valuation, to certify nonvanishing. This is the precision input to the integer congruence lattice; merely evaluating each logarithm to precision7 would lose two necessary digits.

### Rational archimedean logarithm errors

For positive rational x, put u=(x−1)/(x+1), r=|u|<1. Integrating a finite geometric identity gives L_N=2Σ(k<N)u^(2k+1)/(2k+1) and |log x−L_N|≤2r^(2N+1)/((2N+1)(1−r²)). The bound tends to0. At x=2,N=1, L_1=2/3 and the error is1/36, giving[23/36,25/36]. At x=1 all terms vanish. At x=0 the positivity hypothesis fails and the remainder denominator vanishes; totalized log0 is not a valid positive-log certificate.

Similarly integrate 1/(1+t²): A_N(t)=Σ(k<N)(−1)^k t^(2k+1)/(2k+1), with error≤|t|^(2N+1)/(2N+1) for |t|≤1, including both endpoints. Thus π=4arctan1 can itself be enclosed. Oddness and the inversion identity reduce other rational arguments. Refine exact algebraic boxes, apply these rational endpoint bounds and round outwards with a stated mesh; this proves existence of the log/argument precision needed by Matveev and the real lattice reduction, without an analytic evaluation oracle.

### P-adic logarithm tails and reduction residues

In a normalized local field with e=ord(p), choose d≤ord(z−1) with d>e/(p−1). For S_N(z)=Σ(1≤k≤N)(−1)^(k+1)(z−1)^k/k, use v_p(k)≤(k−1)/(p−1). Every omitted term has valuation at least d+N(d−e/(p−1)); ultrametric closedness gives ord(log z−S_N)≥ceil(d+N(d−e/(p−1))). The positive slope supplies every requested precision. Principal-unit logarithm convergence and power/additivity are imported existing theory; this target supplies the finite quantitative remainder.

At p=3,z=4,d=1,N=4, the partial sum is3−9/2+27/3−81/4=−51/4 and tail precision is at least3. At p=2,z=5,d=2,N=4 the bound is6. To evaluate the log of u=−5, square to25 (depth3), evaluate the deep-unit log and divide by2, losing one digit. For a ramified field with e=2,p=3,d=2,N=5 the tail precision is7 and division by3 loses two digits. Shallow z=3 at p=2 fails d>1, so first power to9; log of a root of unity uses the exact-zero branch.

For general units take a sufficiently deep power M=(q−1)p^h; the binomial lower bound ord((1+a)^p−1)≥min(p·ord(a),ord(a)+e) proves existence of such h. Evaluate the finite expression with ED.0 propagation, subtract ord(M) after power division, then allocate the additional pivot loss s. The full S-unit and Thue–Mahler bound/search theorems below use these derived residues and a checked reduction chain. A candidate list or asserted answer-set equality is never their numerical input.

### Heights, empty coverings and geometric examples

For Q=2^nP, a naive-height interval[λ⁻,λ⁺] and correct half-height errors c⁻,c⁺ give[(λ⁻/2−c⁻)/4^n,(λ⁺/2+c⁺)/4^n] for the actual pinned canonical height. The width is((λ⁺−λ⁻)/2+c⁻+c⁺)/4^n; uniform width control of the input log interval is necessary. If Q=O return[0,0] without a logarithm. With input width1/8 and errors2,3 the width is81/(16·4^n).

A complete Thue factor covering may be empty. Its covering theorem then proves that there are no solutions. Dispatch this case before taking a minimum or maximum over representatives. The totally complex case is distinct, and only the nonempty real-root covering constructs the usual representative-dependent constants. The raw constructor/checker contracts and tests retain this distinction.

Concrete geometric conclusions are conditional on their exact numerical and model inputs. For X_s(13), the supplied model/Hecke/rank and coefficient/tail data feed finite disc checks covering17 first-chart discs, two second-chart discs and the P0 disc. Checking roots and exclusions proves the seven-point list; it is not a hypothesis. For X_0⁺(N), all nine levels and all68 ordered points are specified below. The545 S-unit,72 Thue–Mahler and1492 genus-two cases remain target acceptance instances with unreplayed full numerical transcripts, not completed replays. Box’s X_0(43) and Caraiani–Newton Proposition7.4.5 are source acceptance cases for the relative sieve, not ED.6 replay claims.

## ED.0 — Certified algebraic numbers and local precision

**Planets.** Embedding pinned by an isolating box; Hensel embedding certificate; Certified nonvanishing; Algebraic numbers of bounded height.

<a id="ED-0-certified-enclosure"></a>

### Certified enclosures and the precision contract

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealEnclosure` · implementation unchecked.

Three enclosure types carry every approximate value of this roadmap. (i) For t ∈ ℝ, a RealEnclosure t is a closed nonempty rational interval I = [l, u] (Mathlib's NonemptyInterval ℚ) with l ≤ t ≤ u in ℝ. Its rational error bound is width(I) = u − l, and it has absolute precision n ∈ ℕ when u − l ≤ 2^(−n). (ii) For z ∈ ℂ, a ComplexEnclosure z is a pair (R, I) of closed nonempty rational intervals with Re z ∈ R and Im z ∈ I. Its error bound is max(width R, width I) and absolute precision n means width R ≤ 2^(−n) and width I ≤ 2^(−n). (iii) For a prime p and x ∈ ℚ_p, a PadicEnclosure x is a rational centre c and an integer N with ‖x − c‖_p ≤ p^(−N); N is its absolute precision, and its canonical record is the ED.0 normalized p-adic ball data (N, v, s) with (v, s) = (N, 0) when c = 0; otherwise v = min(v_p(c), N), s = 0 when v = N, and when v < N s the residue of c·p^(−v) in [1, p^(N−v)) prime to p; that record denotes the same ball and so contains x. Every check on an enclosure (width, precision, membership of a rational, exclusion of zero) is a finite comparison of rationals or of p-adic valuations of rationals. An enclosure never certifies an equality: two different numbers can have overlapping or identical enclosures.

**Hypotheses.** p is a prime in (iii); n ∈ ℕ and N ∈ ℤ. Endpoints and centres are exact rationals; no floating-point value enters a check.

**Proof route.**

- Represent real intervals by Mathlib's NonemptyInterval ℚ and read membership after casting the endpoints to ℝ.
- Represent complex boxes by pairs of such intervals; membership is membership of the real and imaginary parts.
- Represent p-adic balls by (c, N); the ultrametric inequality shows that the ball of (c, N) equals the ball of the canonical ED.0 PadicEnclosure record described above (the residue s ≡ c·p^(−v) modulo p^(N−v) changes the centre by an element of norm ≤ p^(−N)).
- Width, precision and membership are decidable rational comparisons, which is what de Weger's two-sided rounding (§2.5) achieves by hand.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealEnclosure` (structure): A rational interval [l, u] together with proofs l ≤ t and t ≤ u in ℝ.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealEnclosure.width` (data): The rational error bound u − l; it is nonnegative.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealEnclosure.abs_sub_le` (characterisation): For every rational q with l ≤ q ≤ u, |t − q| ≤ width.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealEnclosure.ofRat` (constructor): For q ∈ ℚ the degenerate interval [q, q] encloses (q : ℝ) with width 0, hence every precision.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealEnclosure.widen` (other): An interval containing a RealEnclosure's interval is again a RealEnclosure of the same number.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ComplexEnclosure` (structure): A pair of rational intervals (R, I) with Re z ∈ R and Im z ∈ I.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ComplexEnclosure.mem_box` (characterisation): z belongs to the box {w : Re w ∈ R, Im w ∈ I}.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ComplexEnclosure.normSq_le` (characterisation): |z|² ≤ max(l_R², u_R²) + max(l_I², u_I²), a rational upper bound for |z|².
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ComplexEnclosure.toRealEnclosure` (projection): When I = [0, 0], R is a RealEnclosure of Re z.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEnclosure` (structure): A rational centre c and an integer N with ‖x − c‖ ≤ p^(−N).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEnclosure.ofRat` (constructor): For q ∈ ℚ and every N, (q, N) encloses (q : ℚ_[p]).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEnclosure.toPadicApproximation` (compatibility): The canonical ED.0 normalized p-adic ball data record of (c, N) denotes the closed ball of radius p^(−N) about c, which contains x.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEnclosure.centre_ball_mem` (characterisation): The certified value lies in the rational-centred closed ball of radius p^(-N). This is supporting membership, not the ED.0 exact algebraic/ball certificates carrier adapter.

**Tests.**

- `realEnclosure_sqrt_two` (computation): [141/100, 142/100] is a RealEnclosure of √2 with width 1/100; since 1/100 ≤ 2^(−6) it has absolute precision 6 but not 7.
- `realEnclosure_ofRat_width` (degenerate): RealEnclosure.ofRat q has width 0 for every rational q.
- `complexEnclosure_I` (computation): ([0, 0], [1, 1]) is a ComplexEnclosure of Complex.I.
- `padicEnclosure_nine` (non-example): At p = 3, the zero-centred ball (0, 2) encloses 9 although 9 ≠ 0: a zero-centred enclosure does not certify vanishing.
- `realEnclosure_overlap` (non-example): [1, 2] is a RealEnclosure of both 1 and 2, so a common enclosure does not prove equality.
- `padicEnclosure_normalize_five` (compatibility): At p = 3 the enclosure (5, 1) has canonical ED.0 exact algebraic/ball certificates record (N, v, s) = (1, 0, 2): the balls of radius 1/3 about 5 and about 2 coincide.
- `padicEnclosure_normalize_zero` (degenerate): At p = 3, centre c = 0 and precision N = 2, the canonical ED.0 exact algebraic/ball certificates record is (N, v, s) = (2, 2, 0). The pinned totalized padicValRat 3 0 = 0 must not select v = 0: a v < N record requires a nonzero residue prime to p.

**Acceptance.** Every enclosure check is a comparison of rationals: [141/100, 142/100] ∋ √2 is verified by 141² < 2·100² < 142². An enclosure containing two distinct numbers exists (realEnclosure_overlap), so no equality is ever read from enclosures.

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:NonemptyInterval`; `mathlib:Padic.norm_eq_zpow_neg_valuation`; `mathlib:padicValRat`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §2.5, printed pp. 33–34. The precision contract makes this two-sided rounding explicit: every approximate value is an enclosure whose endpoints are exact rationals. The original source review checked the rendered page because the OCR text layer is garbled. `doyle-krumm-2015` — §4, before §4.1 (arXiv v4 p. 9). Doyle–Krumm's δ-approximations are real enclosures of width 2δ; the packet uses closed rational intervals.

**Consumers.** de Weger, §2.5, pp. 32–34: logarithms and roots are computed with two-sided rounding so that the exact number lies in a known interval. Doyle–Krumm, §4.1–§4.3: every height and every embedding value is replaced by a rational approximation with an explicit error δ. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice: the integers φ_i ≈ Cθ_i are rounded from a real enclosure of θ_i whose width is checked. <a id="ED-0-exact-algebraic-certificate"></a>

### Exact algebraic values with isolating intervals and discs

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/exact-algebraic-certificate` · definition · `` · implementation unchecked.

An exact algebraic value is an element z of the existing algebraic closure of Q, together with a chosen embedding into C; its certificate consists of a nonzero squarefree f in Q[X] vanishing at z and either a rational closed interval [a,b] when z is real, or a rational closed disc |w-c|≤r with c in Q(i), r>0, or a rational rectangular complex box R+iI, containing exactly the one distinct root z of f. A rational point can also use the degenerate interval [a,a]. The proof of unique containment is part of the mathematical certificate, not an assertion that a numerical root is exact. Every algebraic z has such certificates of arbitrarily small diameter, with no root on a nondegenerate boundary, and any finite set of distinct values has pairwise disjoint certificates. Existing field operations determine z+w, zw and z⁻¹ (z≠0); the targets certify their polynomial equations and arbitrarily small isolations, and prove independence of the chosen polynomial/presentation. Equality is exact equality in the algebraic closure: refine isolations and use a common polynomial/gcd to compare shared roots, never infer equality from overlapping approximate boxes. This is a certificate interface and existence/soundness mathematics, with no root-finding, representation algorithm or cost model.

**Hypotheses.** All polynomials used to isolate roots are nonzero; squarefree means distinct roots are being isolated. A complex disc or box is interpreted in the fixed embedding; no claim that arbitrary algebraic values are real.

**Proof route.**

- Use separability in characteristic zero and finiteness of the roots of f. The minimum positive distance to the other roots provides a separating neighbourhood; rational density gives smaller rational intervals, discs or rectangular complex boxes with boundary avoiding all roots.
- For real order/root-sign infrastructure reuse RealAlgebraicGeometry Layer 1 (Sturm–Tarski/Thom encoding), rather than planning a second real algebraic field or CAD. Complex isolation here only records a root and a separating rational neighbourhood.
- For field operations use the existing algebraic closure and minpoly of the result; algebraicity and finite root separation give its isolation. Polynomial identities/resultants may verify a proposed result; extraneous resultant roots do not identify the selected root.
- For equality, use the gcd of the two rational polynomials and the unique-root witnesses in refined common neighbourhoods. Distinct roots eventually have disjoint discs.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ExactAlgebraicCertificate` (structure): An algebraic value with nonzero squarefree rational annihilator, the fixed embedding and a unique-root rational interval, disc or rectangular complex box.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ExactAlgebraicCertificate.root_unique` (characterisation): Within the certified region every root of the displayed polynomial equals the selected value.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ExactAlgebraicCertificate.exists_small` (constructor): For every rational ε>0 there is a certificate containing the value with diameter<ε.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ExactAlgebraicCertificate.ofRat` (constructor): A rational q is represented by X-q and [q,q].
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ExactAlgebraicCertificate.arithmetic` (compatibility): The certified sum, product and nonzero inverse denote exactly the existing field operations; any chosen certificate of the result is interchangeable.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ExactAlgebraicCertificate.eq_iff_common_root` (characterisation): Equality agrees with the exact common-root/gcd criterion, after refining the isolations; intersecting boxes alone do not imply equality.

**Tests.**

- `exact_sqrt_two_root` (computation): X²-2 with [1,3/2] isolates +√2 and excludes -√2.
- `exact_i_disc` (computation): X²+1 with centre i and radius1/2 isolates i; the conjugate disc isolates -i.
- `exact_rat_degenerate` (degenerate): X-3 with [3,3] certifies3 with diameter0.
- `exact_overlap_not_equality` (non-example): The intervals [1,2] for √2 and [1,2] for √3 overlap but their algebraic values are unequal.
- `exact_inverse_nonzero` (compatibility): The inverse of the positive √2 has polynomial2X²-1 and positive isolation; zero has no inverse certificate.

**Acceptance.** X²-2 with [1,3/2] isolates +√2 and excludes -√2. X²+1 with centre i and radius1/2 isolates i; the conjugate disc isolates -i. X-3 with [3,3] certifies3 with diameter0.

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:NumberField.Embeddings.range_eval_eq_rootSet_minpoly`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §2.5, printed pp.32–34. Root approximations require mathematical error/isolation guarantees; ED uses finite root separation to state the exact certificate contract, without adopting numerical algorithms.

**Consumers.** ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate and ED.2/thue-analytic-constants: Root identities, conjugation, separation and nonvanishing are justified before any logarithm or root-difference denominator is used..

<a id="ED-0-isolating-interval-refinement"></a>

### Arbitrarily fine certificates of the same algebraic root

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/isolating-interval-refinement` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealRootIsolation` · implementation unchecked.

For a nonzero g ∈ Q[X], an isolating closed rational interval I selects exactly one real root r. For each n ∈ N there exists a rational subinterval J⊆I selecting the same root and with width(J)≤2^(−n)width(I). A singleton rational root stays a singleton. RealRootIsolation.refine denotes a chosen witness of this mathematical existence theorem; no bisection algorithm or cost model is exported. The real and imaginary parts of a complex algebraic value are algebraic, since Re(z)=(z+conj z)/2 and Im(z)=(z−conj z)/(2i). Applying the same existence theorem to their exact ED.0 certificates gives nested rational boxes of arbitrarily small width for the original value.

**Hypotheses.** g≠0, rational endpoints l≤u, and exactly one real root in [l,u]. The selected root is kept fixed; overlapping enclosures alone do not identify roots.

**Proof route.**

- The finite root set of a nonzero polynomial separates the selected root from every other root. Rational density gives subintervals of any prescribed positive width containing that root and lying inside the old interval; if the root is an endpoint, use a one-sided interval. If width(I)=0, keep I.
- Nonemptiness of the witness set gives refine by mathematical choice; prove preservation, inclusion and width from its specification. No general real-closed-field or root-finding development is planned: current TauCetiRoadmap RealAlgebraicGeometry Layer1 owns its stronger general interface.
- Conjugation and field arithmetic are operations of existing algebraic carriers. Certify Re and Im using ED.0/exact-algebraic-certificate and use coordinate refinements to bound a complex value.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealRootIsolation` (structure): A nonzero rational polynomial g and a rational interval containing exactly one real root of g; the record stores polynomial_ne_zero : g ≠ 0.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealRootIsolation.root` (projection): The isolated real root.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealRootIsolation.root_spec` (characterisation): g(I.root) = 0 and I.root lies in I.interval.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealRootIsolation.root_unique` (extensionality): Any real root u of g lying in I.interval equals I.root.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealRootIsolation.refine` (data): For n∈N, a chosen rational subinterval J⊆I containing the same unique root, with width(J)≤2^(−n)width(I). No computational algorithm is specified.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealRootIsolation.refine_root` (simp): (refine I n).root = I.root.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealRootIsolation.refine_width` (other): The width of refine I n is at most 2^(−n) times the width of I.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealRootIsolation.toEnclosure` (coercion): An isolation is a RealEnclosure of its root.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealRootIsolation.ofRealCertificate` (constructor): The rational real interval in an ED.0 exact algebraic box certificate whose value is real isolates that same real root.

**Tests.**

- `refine_sqrt_two` (computation): For X²−2 and [1,2], [11/8,3/2] satisfies the precision3 refinement specification; [1,3/2] fails its width bound.
- `refine_exact_rational` (degenerate): For X − q and [q, q], refine n is [q, q] for every n.
- `refine_midpoint_root` (computation): For X−1/2 and [0,1], the singleton [1/2,1/2] satisfies every refinement precision, while [0,1] fails precision1.
- `isolation_two_roots` (non-example): [−2, 2] is not an isolating interval for X² − 2: it contains ±√2.
- `refine_toEnclosure` (compatibility): (refine I n).toEnclosure is a RealEnclosure of I.root of width at most 2^(−n)·width(I).
- `isolation_zero_polynomial` (non-example): RealRootIsolation (0 : ℚ[X]) is empty, including for a singleton interval: the polynomial must be nonzero.

<a id="ED-0-archimedean-embedding-certificate"></a>

### Archimedean embeddings pinned by isolating boxes

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

Let K be a number field with a power basis pb over ℚ, generator θ and minimal polynomial f = minpoly ℚ θ of degree d. An archimedean embedding certificate for pb is a ED.0 ExactAlgebraicCertificate (f, R, I): closed rational intervals R, I such that exactly one complex root z of f satisfies Re z ∈ R and Im z ∈ I. Its embedding σ_c : K →+* ℂ is PowerBasis.lift pb z, the unique ring homomorphism with σ_c(θ) = z, and σ_c is the only embedding K →+* ℂ sending θ into the box. Every embedding of K into ℂ has a certificate. For α ∈ K with power-basis coordinates (a_0, …, a_{d−1}) ∈ ℚ^d and a certificate whose box has rational centre w = w_1 + i·w_2 and half-widths at most r, put M = |w_1| + |w_2| + 2r; then σ_c(α) = Σ_j a_j z^j and |σ_c(α) − Σ_j a_j w^j| ≤ ρ := 2r · Σ_j j·|a_j|·M^(j−1), so the box with centre Σ_j a_j w^j ∈ ℚ(i) and half-widths ρ is a ComplexEnclosure of σ_c(α). Refining the box of z (same root, smaller box; EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/isolating-interval-refinement applied to Re z and Im z) until ρ ≤ 2^(−n−1) yields enclosures of absolute precision n. A list of d certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes is complete: it contains every embedding K →+* ℂ. If I = [−b, b] is symmetric about 0 then σ_c is real (ComplexEmbedding.IsReal), and R is a RealEnclosure of σ_c(θ). The infinite place of σ_c is InfinitePlace.mk σ_c; two certificates define the same place exactly when their roots are equal or complex conjugate.

**Hypotheses.** K is a number field and pb : PowerBasis ℚ K; f = minpoly ℚ pb.gen. (f, R, I) is a ED.0/exact-algebraic-certificate for the polynomial f itself. Coordinates of α are pb.basis.repr α; all arithmetic on centres and radii is exact rational arithmetic.

**Proof route.**

- The decoded value z of the certificate is a root of f lying in the box (ED.0 exact-algebraic-certificate root specification), so PowerBasis.lift pb z is defined and sends θ to z (PowerBasis.lift_gen); two embeddings that agree on θ agree on K (PowerBasis.liftEquiv' is injective).
- If σ(θ) lies in the box then σ(θ) is a root of f in the box, hence equals z by ED.0 exact-algebraic-certificate root uniqueness, hence σ = σ_c.
- Every embedding σ sends θ to a root of f (NumberField.Embeddings.range_eval_eq_rootSet_minpoly); f has finitely many roots, so a box around σ(θ) excluding the others exists. Since f is separable of degree d, K has exactly d embeddings (PowerBasis.liftEquiv'), so d certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes exhaust them.
- σ_c(α) = Σ_j a_j z^j because σ_c is a ring homomorphism and α = Σ_j a_j θ^j; with |z − w| ≤ 2r and |z|, |w| ≤ M the identity z^j − w^j = (z − w)Σ_k z^k w^(j−1−k) gives |z^j − w^j| ≤ 2r·j·M^(j−1).
- Refinement: EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/isolating-interval-refinement gives real isolating intervals of Re z and Im z of any width; their product is a smaller box containing z, hence again a certificate with the same root, and by step 2 the same embedding.
- f has rational coefficients, so the complex conjugate of z is a root of f; if I is symmetric it lies in the box, hence equals z, so conjugate σ_c = σ_c (ComplexEmbedding.isReal_iff). The statement about places is InfinitePlace.mk_eq_iff.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate` (structure): The data (R, I) and a proof that exactly one complex root of minpoly ℚ pb.gen lies in the box.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.root` (projection): The unique root z in the box.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.embedding` (data): σ_c = PowerBasis.lift pb z as a ring homomorphism K →+* ℂ.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.embedding_gen` (simp): σ_c(pb.gen) = z.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.eq_embedding_of_mem` (extensionality): If σ : K →+* ℂ sends pb.gen into the box then σ = σ_c.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.exists_of_embedding` (constructor): Every σ : K →+* ℂ is σ_c for some certificate c.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.isReal_of_symmetric` (characterisation): If I = [−b, b] then ComplexEmbedding.IsReal σ_c.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.infinitePlace_apply` (compatibility): InfinitePlace.mk σ_c α = ‖σ_c α‖.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.norm_sub_eval_le` (characterisation): |σ_c(α) − Σ_j a_j w^j| ≤ 2r·Σ_j j|a_j|M^(j−1) for the box centre w and M = |w_1| + |w_2| + 2r.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.refine` (constructor): A certificate with box widths at most 2^(−n) and the same root, from ED.0/isolating-interval-refinement.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.complete_of_disjoint` (characterisation): A family of [K : ℚ] certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes contains every embedding K →+* ℂ.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.evalEnclosure` (data): A ComplexEnclosure of σ_c(α) of absolute precision n, computed from a refined certificate.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ArchimedeanEmbeddingCertificate.evalEnclosure_width` (other): Both widths of evalEnclosure α n are at most 2^(−n).

**Tests.**

- `archimedean_sqrt_two` (computation): For minpoly ℚ θ = X² − 2 and the box [1, 2] × [0, 0], σ_c(θ) = √2 and σ_c(1 + θ) = 1 + √2.
- `archimedean_sqrt_two_real` (characterisation): The box [1, 2] × [0, 0] is symmetric about the real axis, so σ_c is a real embedding.
- `archimedean_degree_one` (degenerate): For minpoly ℚ θ = X − 1 the box [1, 1] × [0, 0] is a certificate and σ_c(α) = α for α ∈ ℚ.
- `archimedean_ambiguous_box` (non-example): For X² − 2 the box [−2, 2] × [0, 0] contains two roots, so it is not a certificate.
- `archimedean_conjugate_place` (compatibility): For minpoly X² + 1 the boxes [0, 0] × [1, 1] and [0, 0] × [−1, −1] give conjugate embeddings with the same InfinitePlace.mk.

**Acceptance.** For ℚ(√2) the two certificates [1, 2] × [0, 0] and [−2, −1] × [0, 0] are the two real embeddings, and the enclosure of σ_c(3363 − 2378θ) at precision 14 excludes 0. For ℚ(i) the certificates [0, 0] × [1/2, 2] and [0, 0] × [−2, −1/2] give the two complex embeddings, which define one infinite place.

<a id="ED-0-hensel-root-distance"></a>

### Hensel's lemma with the exact distance to the root

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/hensel-root-distance` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.norm_sub_eq_of_hensel` · implementation unchecked.

Let p be prime, R a commutative semiring with an algebra map to ℤ_p, F ∈ R[X] and a ∈ ℤ_p with ‖F(a)‖ < ‖F′(a)‖². Let z ∈ ℤ_p be the root given by Mathlib's hensels_lemma: F(z) = 0, ‖z − a‖ < ‖F′(a)‖, ‖F′(z)‖ = ‖F′(a)‖, and z is the only root within distance ‖F′(a)‖ of a. Then for every b ∈ ℤ_p with ‖b − a‖ < ‖F′(a)‖: ‖F′(b)‖ = ‖F′(a)‖ and ‖z − b‖ = ‖F(b)‖ / ‖F′(a)‖. In particular b satisfies the Hensel hypothesis with the same root, and for integers b and N with v_p(F(b)) ≥ N + v_p(F′(a)) one has z ≡ b (mod p^N).

**Hypotheses.** p prime; F ∈ R[X] with [Algebra R ℤ_[p]], evaluated by aeval; a, b ∈ ℤ_p. ‖F(a)‖ < ‖F′(a)‖² and ‖b − a‖ < ‖F′(a)‖.

**Proof route.**

- Taylor expansion (Polynomial.binomExpansion) at z gives F(b) = F(z) + F′(z)(b − z) + (b − z)²G with ‖G‖ ≤ 1, and F′(b) = F′(z) + (b − z)H with ‖H‖ ≤ 1.
- ‖b − z‖ ≤ max(‖b − a‖, ‖a − z‖) < ‖F′(a)‖ = ‖F′(z)‖ by the ultrametric inequality (PadicInt.nonarchimedean) and hensels_lemma.
- Hence ‖(b − z)²G‖ < ‖F′(z)‖·‖b − z‖ when b ≠ z, so ‖F(b)‖ = ‖F′(z)‖·‖b − z‖ by the strict ultrametric inequality; the case b = z is trivial. Similarly ‖F′(b)‖ = ‖F′(z)‖.
- This is the public form of the private Mathlib lemma soln_dist_to_a in Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Hensel.lean, extended from a to every b in the Hensel disc.

**Acceptance.** p = 7, F = X² − 2, a = 3: F(3) = 7 and F′(3) = 6, so ‖F(3)‖ = 1/7 < 1 = ‖F′(3)‖²; for b = 10, F(10) = 98 = 2·7², so the root z = √2 ∈ ℤ_7 with z ≡ 3 (mod 7) satisfies ‖z − 10‖ = 1/49, i.e. z ≡ 10 (mod 49) and z ≢ 10 (mod 343). If F(a) = 0 the formula gives ‖z − a‖ = 0, i.e. z = a.

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:hensels_lemma`; `mathlib:Polynomial.binomExpansion`; `mathlib:PadicInt.nonarchimedean`; `mathlib:Padic.norm_eq_zpow_neg_valuation`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §2.5, printed pp. 32–33. Source of the rule that a root is certified by an error estimate (isolation or Hensel), never by a small residual. `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §15E, printed p. 263. The p-adic inputs of the reduction are roots computed by Hensel/Newton; the theorem gives the error of each Newton iterate exactly.

<a id="ED-0-padic-embedding-certificate"></a>

### p-adic embeddings pinned by Hensel certificates

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEmbeddingCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

Let K be a number field with a power basis pb over ℚ whose generator θ is integral over ℤ, so that f = minpoly ℚ θ has integer coefficients and is monic, and let p be prime. A p-adic embedding certificate is an integer a with f′(a) ≠ 0 and either f(a) = 0 or v_p(f(a)) > 2·v_p(f′(a)), an exact check on two integers. By hensels_lemma there is a unique z ∈ ℤ_p with f(z) = 0 and ‖z − a‖ < ‖f′(a)‖; the embedding σ_a : K →+* ℚ_p is PowerBasis.lift pb z, the unique embedding with σ_a(θ) = z, and σ_a is the only embedding sending θ into the open disc of radius ‖f′(a)‖ about a. Approximation contract (a mathematical existence theorem, not a Newton implementation): given N, there exists an integer b with ‖b − a‖ < ‖f′(a)‖ and either f(b) = 0 or v_p(f(b)) ≥ N + v_p(f′(a)), and then z ≡ b (mod p^N) (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/hensel-root-distance). For α ∈ K with power-basis coordinates (a_0, …, a_{d−1}) ∈ ℚ^d put e = max(0, −min_j v_p(a_j)); then (Σ_j a_j b^j, N − e) is a PadicEnclosure of σ_a(α), so N = n + e gives absolute precision n. Two certificates a, a′ define different embeddings when ‖a − a′‖ ≥ max(‖f′(a)‖, ‖f′(a′)‖). The embeddings K →+* ℚ_p correspond exactly to the roots of f in ℚ_p (PowerBasis.liftEquiv'); a simple root of f modulo p gives a certificate with v_p(f′(a)) = 0. Here v_p is Mathlib padicValRat, whose value at zero is 0; exact zero residuals are therefore handled by the explicit disjunction, rather than by treating that value as +∞.

**Hypotheses.** K a number field, pb : PowerBasis ℚ K with IsIntegral ℤ pb.gen; f = minpoly ℚ pb.gen viewed in ℤ[X]. p prime; a ∈ ℤ with f′(a) ≠ 0 and either f(a) = 0 or v_p(f(a)) > 2·v_p(f′(a)); α given by its rational coordinates pb.basis.repr α.

**Proof route.**

- The integer check f′(a) ≠ 0 and (f(a) = 0 or v_p(f(a)) > 2·v_p(f′(a))) is ‖f(a)‖ < ‖f′(a)‖² in ℤ_p (Padic.norm_eq_zpow_neg_valuation), so hensels_lemma gives the root z and its uniqueness in the disc.
- PowerBasis.lift pb z is a ring homomorphism K → ℚ_p with θ ↦ z; any σ with ‖σ(θ) − a‖ < ‖f′(a)‖ sends θ to a root in the disc, hence to z, hence equals σ_a (PowerBasis.liftEquiv').
- Choose an integer b sufficiently close to the Hensel root z by density of Z in Z_p. Continuity of f and f′, with f′(z) having the same nonzero norm as f′(a), gives the required Hensel-disc and residual inequalities. The root-distance theorem gives ‖z−b‖≤p^(−N).
- z, b ∈ ℤ_p and z ≡ b (mod p^N) give z^j ≡ b^j (mod p^N); multiplying by a_j with v_p(a_j) ≥ −e gives ‖σ_a(α) − Σ_j a_j b^j‖ ≤ p^(e−N).
- If ‖a − a′‖ ≥ max(‖f′(a)‖, ‖f′(a′)‖) then the two roots z, z′ satisfy ‖z − z′‖ = ‖a − a′‖ > 0 by the strict ultrametric inequality.
- The canonical record of the enclosure is the ED.0 PadicEnclosure record of (Σ_j a_j b^j, N − e) (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure).

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEmbeddingCertificate` (structure): An integer a with f′(a) ≠ 0 and either f(a) = 0 or v_p(f(a)) > 2·v_p(f′(a)) for f = minpoly ℚ pb.gen.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEmbeddingCertificate.root` (data): The Hensel root z ∈ ℤ_p of f with ‖z − a‖ < ‖f′(a)‖.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEmbeddingCertificate.embedding` (data): σ_a = PowerBasis.lift pb z : K →+* ℚ_p.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEmbeddingCertificate.embedding_gen` (simp): σ_a(pb.gen) = z.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEmbeddingCertificate.eq_embedding_of_near` (extensionality): If σ : K →+* ℚ_p satisfies ‖σ(pb.gen) − a‖ < ‖f′(a)‖ then σ = σ_a.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEmbeddingCertificate.root_sub_mem` (characterisation): For an integer b with ‖b − a‖ < ‖f′(a)‖ and either f(b) = 0 or v_p(f(b)) ≥ N + v_p(f′(a)), ‖z − b‖ ≤ p^(−N).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEmbeddingCertificate.evalEnclosure` (data): The PadicEnclosure (Σ_j a_j b^j, n) of σ_a(α) of absolute precision n.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEmbeddingCertificate.ne_of_far` (relation): ‖a − a′‖ ≥ max(‖f′(a)‖, ‖f′(a′)‖) implies σ_a ≠ σ_a′.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEmbeddingCertificate.embedding_algebraMap` (compatibility): σ_a restricted to ℚ is the canonical map ℚ → ℚ_p.

**Tests.**

- `padic_sqrt_two_seven` (computation): For minpoly ℚ θ = X² − 2, p = 7 and a = 3 the check v_7(7) = 1 > 0 = 2·v_7(6) holds, and σ_a(θ) ≡ 10 (mod 49).
- `padic_sqrt_two_two_roots` (characterisation): For X² − 2 at p = 7 the certificates a = 3 and a = 4 define the two different embeddings ℚ(√2) → ℚ_7.
- `padic_degree_one` (degenerate): For minpoly ℚ θ = X − 1, a = 1 is a certificate (f(1) = 0) and σ_a(α) = α for α ∈ ℚ.
- `padic_no_root_five` (non-example): For X² − 2 at p = 5 no integer a is a certificate: v_5(a² − 2) = 0 for every a since 2 is not a square modulo 5.
- `padic_embedding_rat` (compatibility): σ_a(algebraMap ℚ K q) = (q : ℚ_[p]) for every certificate a and q ∈ ℚ.

**Acceptance.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §3E–§4E: at p = 5 their polynomial has three roots in ℚ_5, each pinned by a certificate of this form. For X² − 2 at p = 7, a = 3: σ_a(θ) ≡ 10 (mod 49) and ≡ 108 (mod 343), since 108² − 2 = 11662 = 34·343.

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:hensels_lemma`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/hensel-root-distance`; `mathlib:PowerBasis.lift`; `mathlib:PowerBasis.liftEquiv'`; `mathlib:Padic.norm_eq_zpow_neg_valuation`; `mathlib:padicValRat`; `mathlib:PadicInt`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure`.

**Sources.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §3, printed p. 226. A factor g_i of degree one over ℚ_p is a root of g in ℚ_p, i.e. an embedding K → ℚ_p and a degree-one prime; the certificate pins that root. OCR fragment (g1 printed as gl). `de-weger-1989` — §3.13, printed p. 66. The p-adic linear forms are built from p-adic images of algebraic numbers; the certificate fixes which image is meant.

**Consumers.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §3–§4 and §12: the roots θ^(i) of the factors g_i(t) of degree one over ℚ_p give the embeddings K → ℚ_p in which the p-adic linear forms Λ_i live. de Weger, §3.13: the numbers α_i ∈ ℚ_p and their p-adic logarithms define the p-adic approximation lattices. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/valuation-certificate: valuations v_p(σ_a(α)) are read from enclosures of σ_a(α). EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice: the integers β_j^(m) are read from p-adic enclosures of absolute precision at least m.

<a id="ED-0-certified-nonvanishing"></a>

### Certified nonvanishing and the exact zero test

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-nonvanishing` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ne_zero_of_enclosure` · implementation unchecked.

Let K be a number field with power basis pb and α ∈ K with power-basis coordinates (a_j) ∈ ℚ^d. (a) α = 0 if and only if every a_j = 0; this exact test is the only way an identity α = 0 (or α = β, applied to α − β) is established, and for algebraic numbers given as ED.0 exact algebraic/ball certificates isolated roots the exact test is ED.0 exact algebraic/ball certificates's algebraicEqual. (b) If c is an archimedean embedding certificate and (R, I) a ComplexEnclosure of σ_c(α) whose box excludes 0 (R.fst > 0, R.snd < 0, I.fst > 0 or I.snd < 0), then α ≠ 0, and therefore τ(α) ≠ 0 for every ring homomorphism τ from K to a field. (c) If a is a p-adic embedding certificate and (c, N) a PadicEnclosure of σ_a(α) with c ≠ 0 and v_p(c) < N, then α ≠ 0. (d) The exclusion test is complete: if α ≠ 0, every ComplexEnclosure of σ_c(α) of absolute precision n with 2·4^(−n) < |σ_c(α)|² excludes 0, and every PadicEnclosure (c, N) of σ_a(α) with N > v_p(σ_a(α)) has c ≠ 0 and v_p(c) = v_p(σ_a(α)) < N; so refining until exclusion terminates. (e) No enclosure containing 0 proves α = 0: for every n the rational α = 2^(−n−1) has the precision-n enclosure [0, 2^(−n)] containing 0.

**Hypotheses.** K a number field, pb : PowerBasis ℚ K; σ_c from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate and σ_a from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate. Enclosures are those of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure.

**Proof route.**

- (a) pb.basis is a basis, so α = Σ_j a_j θ^j vanishes exactly when its coordinates do (Basis.repr is injective).
- (b) If 0 is not in the box then σ_c(α) ≠ 0, so α ≠ 0 since σ_c(0) = 0; ring homomorphisms out of a field are injective (RingHom.injective).
- (c) The strict ultrametric inequality gives ‖σ_a(α)‖ = ‖c‖ = p^(−v_p(c)) > 0 when ‖σ_a(α) − c‖ ≤ p^(−N) < p^(−v_p(c)).
- (d) If 0 and σ_c(α) lie in a box of widths ≤ 2^(−n), then |Re σ_c(α)| ≤ 2^(−n) and |Im σ_c(α)| ≤ 2^(−n), so |σ_c(α)|² ≤ 2·4^(−n); the p-adic statement is the converse direction of (c).
- (e) is a direct computation and records the stage's acceptance that numerical agreement proves no identity.

**Acceptance.** Pell unit test: in K = ℚ(√2) with the certificate [1, 2] × [0, 0], α = 3363 − 2378·θ has σ_c(α) = (1 − √2)^10 = 1.4867…·10^(−4). The exact test (a) gives α ≠ 0 from the coordinates (3363, −2378). An enclosure of precision 10 (width 2^(−10) ≈ 9.8·10^(−4)) can contain 0, while every enclosure of precision 14 excludes 0 by (d), since 2·4^(−14) ≈ 7.5·10^(−9) < 2.2·10^(−8) ≈ |σ_c(α)|². At p = 7 with the certificate a = 3 for X² − 2, the enclosure (7, 2) of σ_a(θ − 3) certifies θ − 3 ≠ 0 and v_7(σ_a(θ − 3)) = 1.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure`; `mathlib:RingHom.injective`; `mathlib:Padic.norm_eq_zpow_neg_valuation`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/exact-algebraic-certificate`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §2.5, printed pp. 32–33. Source of the rule that a root is certified by an error estimate (isolation or Hensel), never by a small residual. `doyle-krumm-2015` — §4, opening paragraph (arXiv v4 p. 9). A comparison read from approximations is valid only with an error bound; refinement until the comparison is decided is the mechanism of part (d).

<a id="ED-0-valuation-certificate"></a>

### Certified valuations from p-adic enclosures

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/valuation-certificate` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ValuationCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

Let a be a p-adic embedding certificate for (K, pb, p) with embedding σ_a : K →+* ℚ_p, and α ∈ K^×. A valuation certificate for α is a PadicEnclosure (c, N) of σ_a(α) with c ≠ 0 and v_p(c) < N (precision exceeding the valuation); it certifies Padic.valuation(σ_a(α)) = v_p(c) = padicValRat p c. Every α ≠ 0 has one: choose any integer N > v_p(σ_a(α)) and apply the enclosure-existence theorem; its centre has the same valuation by the strict ultrametric inequality. Prime ideals: 𝔭_a := {x ∈ 𝓞_K : ‖σ_a(x)‖ < 1} is a height-one prime of 𝓞_K above p with completion ℚ_p, so ramification index and residue degree are 1, and for α ∈ K^× the 𝔭_a-adic valuation is v_{𝔭_a}(α) = v_p(σ_a(α)); in Mathlib's normalisation HeightOneSpectrum.valuation K α = WithZero.exp(−v_p(σ_a(α))). Certificates multiply: valuation certificates (c, N) of α and (c′, N′) of β, with v = v_p(c) and v′ = v_p(c′), give the certificate (cc′, min(v + N′, N + v′)) of αβ with valuation v + v′.

**Hypotheses.** a is an EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate; α ≠ 0. Only primes 𝔭 arising from embeddings K → ℚ_p (degree-one primes) are covered; their valuations are read from σ_a.

**Proof route.**

- If ‖σ_a(α) − c‖ ≤ p^(−N) < p^(−v_p(c)) = ‖c‖, then ‖σ_a(α)‖ = ‖c‖ (ultrametric), so the valuations agree (Padic.norm_eq_zpow_neg_valuation).
- Existence: the enclosures of absolute precision n converge to σ_a(α) ≠ 0; once n > v_p(σ_a(α)) the centre has the same valuation (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-nonvanishing (d)).
- σ_a extends by continuity to the completion of K at 𝔭_a, whose image is closed and contains ℚ, hence is ℚ_p; thus e(𝔭_a/p) = f(𝔭_a/p) = 1 and the normalised valuation of K at 𝔭_a is v_p ∘ σ_a. In Mathlib terms the comparison is with IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation, whose value at a uniformiser is WithZero.exp(−1).
- Product rule: σ(αβ) − cc′ = σ(α)(σ(β) − c′) + c′(σ(α) − c), so ‖σ(αβ) − cc′‖ ≤ max(p^(−v−N′), p^(−v′−N)) by the ultrametric inequality, and v + v′ < min(v + N′, N + v′).

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ValuationCertificate` (structure): A PadicEnclosure (c, N) of σ_a(α) with c ≠ 0 and padicValRat p c < N.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ValuationCertificate.valuation_eq` (characterisation): Padic.valuation (σ_a α) = padicValRat p c.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ValuationCertificate.ne_zero` (other): A valuation certificate exists only for α ≠ 0.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ValuationCertificate.exists_of_ne_zero` (constructor): Every α ≠ 0 has a valuation certificate at every precision N > v_p(σ_a(α)).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ValuationCertificate.prime` (data): The height-one prime 𝔭_a = {x ∈ 𝓞_K : ‖σ_a(x)‖ < 1}.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ValuationCertificate.adicValuation_eq` (compatibility): HeightOneSpectrum.valuation K α at 𝔭_a equals WithZero.exp(−v_p(σ_a(α))).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ValuationCertificate.mul` (functoriality): Certificates for α and β give a certificate for αβ with valuation v_p(c) + v_p(c′).

**Tests.**

- `valuation_rat_eighteen` (compatibility): For K = ℚ (minpoly X − 1, a = 1), p = 3 and α = 18, the enclosure (18, 3) certifies valuation 2 = padicValRat 3 18.
- `valuation_sqrt_two_seven` (computation): For X² − 2 at p = 7 with a = 3, the enclosure (7, 2) of σ_a(θ − 3) certifies v_7(σ_a(θ − 3)) = 1.
- `valuation_unit` (degenerate): The enclosure (1, 1) of σ_a(1) certifies valuation 0.
- `valuation_zero_centre` (non-example): At p = 7 the enclosure (0, 2) of 49 is not a valuation certificate although 49 ≠ 0: its centre is 0.

**Acceptance.** For X² − 2 at p = 7, a = 3: v_7(σ_a(θ − 3)) = 1 and v_7(σ_a(θ − 10)) = 2, from the enclosures (7, 2) and (98, 3) of σ_a(θ − 3) and σ_a(θ − 10). For K = ℚ the certificate reproduces padicValRat.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-nonvanishing`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure`; `mathlib:Padic.valuation`; `mathlib:Padic.norm_eq_zpow_neg_valuation`; `mathlib:padicValRat`; `mathlib:IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §3.13, Lemma 3.17(i), printed p. 67. The p-adic orders ord_p of embedded algebraic numbers and of their logarithms are the inputs this construction certifies. The original source review checked the rendered page. `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §4, printed p. 227. For a prime 𝔭_i of degree one this order equals v_p of the image under the corresponding embedding, which is what the certificate reads. OCR fragment (𝔭_i printed as pi).

**Consumers.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §5–§8: the orders ord_p of the images of algebraic numbers decide which prime ideals divide and bound the exponents n_i. de Weger, §3.13, Lemma 3.17: ord_p(α_i) = 0 and μ_0 = ord_p(log_p α_n) normalise the p-adic linear form before the lattice is built. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2 (Thue–Mahler and S-unit equations): valuations of the coefficients of the p-adic linear forms fix the normalising factor ξ and the constants of the reduction. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3 (local images): valuations at degree-one primes are read from certified p-adic approximations.

<a id="ED-0-padic-precision-propagation"></a>

### Scalar p-adic precision under field operations

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-precision-propagation` · construction · `` · implementation unchecked.

Let L=K_v be a completed number field, with its dense embedding ι:K→L, a uniformizer π and additive valuation ord with ord(π)=1, ord(0)=+∞ and e=ord(p). A ball certificate B(c,N) for x consists of an exact c∈K and integer N with ord(x-ι(c))≥N. The Q_p specialization uses c∈Q and ord(p)=1. Given x∈B(c,N), y∈B(d,M), and certified integer lower bounds a≤ord(x),ord(c), b≤ord(y),ord(d), prove: x+y∈B(c+d,min(N,M)); xy∈B(cd,min(N+b,M+a)); if c≠0 and s=ord(c)<N, then x≠0, ord(x)=s and x⁻¹∈B(c⁻¹,N-2s). One may take a=min(ord(c),N) for c≠0 and a=N for c=0, with the analogous convention for b. For exact coefficients u_j, the error of Σu_j x_j is at least min_j(N_j+ord(u_j)); zero coefficients are omitted and the empty sum is exact zero. Polynomial evaluation follows by these finite field identities, with a stated rational/integer precision budget. If nonzero pivot ℓ_k has valuation s and every ℓ_j has valuation≥s, enclosures of all ℓ_j and ℓ_k at precision≥m+s give enclosures of -ℓ_j/ℓ_k at precision≥m, provided the pivot precision exceeds s. Thus residues needed by ED.1 are certified, including precision lost at division. Dense range gives ball certificates at every N; it is not a new completion construction or a numerical procedure.

**Hypotheses.** The completion, embedding, valuation and normalization comparisons come from the local-field/number-field owners; in a ramified completion e may exceed1. Absolute precisions are integers and may be negative. Exact zero has infinite valuation, never Mathlib's totalized integer valuation0. All inverse and quotient rules require the displayed nonzero and strict precision hypotheses.

**Proof route.**

- Apply the ultrametric inequality to addition. Write xy-cd=x(y-d)+d(x-c), so the two error terms have lower valuations a+M and b+N.
- If ord(c)<N≤ord(x-c), ultrametric strictness gives ord(x)=ord(c). The inverse identity x⁻¹-c⁻¹=(c-x)/(xc) gives N-2s.
- Induct on the finite sum/product expression using exact coefficients. A zero coefficient contributes no error term.
- For the pivot quotient, inverse precision N_k-2s multiplied by a numerator of valuation≥s and numerator error divided by the pivot both have precision≥m. DenseRange ι and the valuation topology supply all requested input balls.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.LocalBallCertificate` (structure): A centre c in K, integer absolute precision N and containment ord(x-ιc)≥N in the actual completion K_v.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.LocalBallCertificate.add` (functoriality): Addition has centre c+d and precision min(N,M).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.LocalBallCertificate.mul` (functoriality): Multiplication has centre cd and precision min(N+b,M+a) for the displayed lower valuation bounds.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.LocalBallCertificate.inv` (functoriality): For c≠0 and s=ord(c)<N, inverse precision is N-2s.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.LocalBallCertificate.linearCombination` (other): A finite exact linear combination has precision at least min(N_j+ord(u_j)), with zero coefficients omitted.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.LocalBallCertificate.normalizedLogResidues` (compatibility): Input log precision≥m+s and a certified minimal nonzero pivot valuation s imply quotient precision≥m, sufficient for the ED.1 congruence lattice.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.LocalBallCertificate.exists_at_precision` (constructor): The dense exact subfield supplies a ball certificate for every x∈K_v and every integer precision.

**Tests.**

- `precision_mul_three` (computation): At p=3, balls B(3,4),B(9,5) have valuations1,2; their product has centre27 and precision6.
- `precision_inverse_loss` (computation): At p=3, B(9,5) has inverse centre1/9 and precision1, not5.
- `precision_zero_centre` (degenerate): B(0,4) times B(9,5) has centre0 and precision6; ord(0)=0 would incorrectly lose this guaranteed precision.
- `precision_cancellation` (non-example): At p=3, B(1,4)+B(-1,4) has guaranteed precision4; cancellation of centres does not certify exact zero.
- `precision_ramified_normalization` (compatibility): If e=2 and ord(π)=1, multiplication by p gains2 digits and division by p loses2; using ord(p)=1 is incorrect.
- `precision_log_pivot` (computation): Logs of valuation≥2 known to precision9, with a pivot certified of valuation2, give normalized coefficient precision7.

**Acceptance.** At p=3, balls B(3,4),B(9,5) have valuations1,2; their product has centre27 and precision6. At p=3, B(9,5) has inverse centre1/9 and precision1, not5. B(0,4) times B(9,5) has centre0 and precision6; ord(0)=0 would incorrectly lose this guaranteed precision.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/valuation-certificate`; `mathlib:Padic.norm_eq_zpow_neg_valuation`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §2.5, printed pp.33–34; §3.13 Lemma3.17, p.67. p-adic divisions consume valuation-dependent precision; the scalar identities state exactly that loss and its effect on normalized logarithms.

**Consumers.** ED.2/padic-logarithm-enclosure and ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice: Partial sums and normalization preserve the exact residue information required to exclude exponent vectors.. ED.4 and ED.6 precision estimates: Propagate finite scalar errors; geometric series coefficient and tail information remains explicit input, not an evaluator target..

<a id="ED-0-height-enclosure"></a>

### Certified enclosures of the height of a number-field element

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.heightEnclosure` · implementation unchecked.

Let K be a number field of degree d with power basis pb and a complete list of archimedean embedding certificates (d certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes, so their embeddings σ_1, …, σ_d are all embeddings K →+* ℂ). For x ∈ K let χ_x ∈ ℚ[X] be the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by x (Matrix.charpoly of Algebra.leftMulMatrix pb.basis x) and P_x ∈ ℤ[X] its primitive integral multiple with positive leading coefficient a_x. Then Mathlib's relative height is Height.mulHeight₁ x = a_x · ∏_{i=1}^{d} max(1, |σ_i(x)|): the archimedean factors come from the certificates and the whole non-archimedean part of the height is the integer a_x. The construction heightEnclosure x n returns a RealEnclosure of mulHeight₁ x of absolute precision n: compute a_x exactly (rational linear algebra and a gcd of numerators), take ComplexEnclosures of the σ_i(x) (ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate), bound each |σ_i(x)|² in a rational interval from the box corners, apply max(1, ·), multiply the nonnegative intervals endpoint by endpoint, multiply by a_x², and take rational square-root brackets of the endpoints; the precision of the σ_i(x)-enclosures is increased until the final width is at most 2^(−n).

**Hypotheses.** K a number field, pb : PowerBasis ℚ K, and d = [K : ℚ] archimedean embedding certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes. x ∈ K arbitrary (x = 0 has height 1). No analytic function is evaluated; only |·|² of algebraic numbers is enclosed.

**Proof route.**

- For arbitrary x, first prove charpoly_leftMul_arbitrary using the tower Q⊆Q(x)⊆K and basis invariance. The pinned charpoly_leftMulMatrix theorem covers only a power-basis generator; it is one input, not this bridge.
- Over ℂ, χ_x = ∏_{i}(X − σ_i(x)): χ_x = (minpoly ℚ x)^k with k = [K : ℚ(x)], and each conjugate of x is σ_i(x) for exactly k of the d embeddings (NumberField.Embeddings.range_eval_eq_rootSet_minpoly; charpoly_leftMulMatrix for the power basis of ℚ(x) and the tower formula). By Gauss's lemma P_x = F_x^k for the primitive minimal polynomial F_x, so a_x = lead(F_x)^k.
- DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/height-comparisons gives M(F_x) = absMulHeight₁(x)^(deg x) and DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow gives absMulHeight₁(x) = mulHeight₁(x)^(1/d); with d = k·deg x this gives mulHeight₁ x = M(F_x)^k = M(P_x) (Polynomial.mahlerMeasure_mul).
- M(P_x) = a_x·∏_i max(1, |σ_i(x)|) by Polynomial.mahlerMeasure_eq_leadingCoeff_mul_prod_roots, since the complex roots of P_x with multiplicity are the σ_i(x).
- From a ComplexEnclosure with real interval [l_1, u_1] and imaginary interval [l_2, u_2], |σ_i(x)|² lies between the rational numbers dist² of the box to 0 and max(l_1², u_1²) + max(l_2², u_2²); max(1, ·) and products of nonnegative intervals are monotone, so the endpoint products enclose mulHeight₁(x)², and the widths tend to 0 as the precision of the σ_i(x)-enclosures grows.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.heightEnclosure` (data): A RealEnclosure of Height.mulHeight₁ x of absolute precision n.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.heightEnclosure_width` (other): The width of heightEnclosure x n is at most 2^(−n).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.mulHeight₁_eq_mahlerMeasure_charpoly` (compatibility): mulHeight₁ x equals the Mahler measure of the primitive part of the characteristic polynomial of x, mapped to ℂ[X].
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.mulHeight₁_eq_leadingCoeff_mul_prod_embeddings` (characterisation): mulHeight₁ x = a_x · ∏_σ max(1, ‖σ x‖) over all embeddings σ : K →+* ℂ.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.heightEnclosure_rat` (simp): For K = ℚ the enclosure contains max(|num x|, den x) (Mathlib's Rat.mulHeight₁_eq_max).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.charpoly_leftMul_arbitrary` (compatibility): For any x∈K and any Q-basis b of K, charpoly(leftMulMatrix b x)=minpoly Q x ^ ([K:Q]/natDegree(minpoly Q x)). Identify Q(x) with the simple intermediate field, use a basis of K over Q(x), restriction of scalars and basis invariance; x need not generate K.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.charpoly_leftMul_basis_independent` (compatibility): For two Q-bases b and b′ of K and any x, the left-multiplication characteristic polynomials agree by similarity.

**Tests.**

- `height_half` (computation): For x = 1/2 ∈ ℚ, P_x = 2X − 1 and mulHeight₁ x = 2.
- `height_sqrt_two` (computation): For θ = √2 in ℚ(√2), P = X² − 2 and mulHeight₁ θ = 2 (both archimedean factors equal √2).
- `height_zero` (degenerate): mulHeight₁ 0 = 1 and every enclosure of it contains 1.
- `height_golden` (computation): For the golden ratio φ in ℚ(√5), P = X² − X − 1 and mulHeight₁ φ = φ = (1 + √5)/2.
- `height_relative_not_absolute` (non-example): For √2 ∈ ℚ(√2) the relative height is 2 while absMulHeight₁ √2 = √2: the enclosure is of the relative height.

**Acceptance.** For K = ℚ every enclosure contains max(|num x|, den x) (Mathlib's Rat.mulHeight₁_eq_max). For the golden ratio φ ∈ ℚ(√5) the enclosure at precision 10 is contained in [1.617, 1.620].

**Direct prerequisites.** `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/height-comparisons`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/primitive-minimal-polynomial`; `mathlib:Height.mulHeight₁`; `mathlib:NumberField.mulHeight₁_eq`; `mathlib:Polynomial.mahlerMeasure`; `mathlib:Polynomial.mahlerMeasure_mul`; `mathlib:Polynomial.mahlerMeasure_eq_leadingCoeff_mul_prod_roots`; `mathlib:Matrix.charpoly`; `mathlib:Algebra.leftMulMatrix`; `mathlib:charpoly_leftMulMatrix`; `mathlib:Polynomial.primPart`; `mathlib:NumberField.Embeddings.range_eval_eq_rootSet_minpoly`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure`.

**Sources.** `doyle-krumm-2015` — §2 (arXiv v4 p. 2). This is Mathlib's Height.mulHeight₁ on a number field (NumberField.mulHeight₁_eq); the construction encloses it. `doyle-krumm-2015` — §4.1, Lemma 4.1 (arXiv v4 p. 9). Doyle–Krumm approximate h_K through approximations of the archimedean absolute values; the construction uses the Mahler-measure form, which needs no ideal norms.

**Consumers.** Doyle–Krumm, §4.1 and Algorithm 4 steps (4), (11), (12): every candidate's height is approximated to within a tolerance before it is kept or discarded. <a id="ED-0-bounded-height-enumeration"></a>

### Certified enumeration of points of bounded height

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/bounded-height-enumeration` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.boundedHeightPoints` · implementation unchecked.

Let L be a number field of degree d with a power basis pb whose generator θ is integral, together with a complete list of archimedean embedding certificates (d certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes, one for each root of f = minpoly ℚ θ), and let D ≥ 1 and τ ∈ (0, 1] be rationals. boundedHeightPoints L pb D τ is a pair of finite sets (S_<, S_≈) of elements of L such that: (completeness) every x ∈ L with Height.mulHeight₁ x ≤ D lies in S_< ∪ S_≈; (soundness) every x ∈ S_< has mulHeight₁ x < D and every x ∈ S_≈ has |mulHeight₁ x − D| < τ. On ℙ¹(L) (Mathlib's Projectivization L (Fin 2 → L)) the set T = {[x : 1] : x ∈ S_< ∪ S_≈} ∪ {[1 : 0]} contains every point P with Height.logHeight P.rep ≤ log D, and every point of T has logHeight < log(D + τ). Construction: (1) every x with mulHeight₁ x ≤ D has c := natDenominator x ≤ D and y := c·x integral; (2) every embedding σ satisfies |σ(x)| ≤ D, so |σ(y)| ≤ D²; (3) with Δ = disc(pb.basis) ∈ ℤ∖{0}, Δ·y ∈ ℤ[θ], so y = Σ_j b_j θ^j with Δ·b_j ∈ ℤ, and b = V^(−1)(σ_i(y))_i for the Vandermonde matrix V = (σ_i(θ)^j), giving |b_j| ≤ Ω·D² with Ω a rational upper bound for the row sums of |V^(−1)| computed from the root boxes; (4) the finite candidate set is {(Σ_j b_j θ^j)/c : 1 ≤ c ≤ ⌊D⌋, Δ·b ∈ ℤ^d, |b_j| ≤ ΩD²} ∪ {0}; (5) for each candidate an enclosure [l, u] of mulHeight₁ of width < τ (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure) puts it in S_< if u < D, in S_≈ if l ≤ D ≤ u, and discards it if D < l.

**Hypotheses.** L a number field, pb : PowerBasis ℚ L with IsIntegral ℤ pb.gen; d archimedean embedding certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate, complete_of_disjoint). D, τ ∈ ℚ with D ≥ 1 and 0 < τ ≤ 1. For a real bound B on logarithmic height take any rational D ≥ exp(B).

**Proof route.**

- Step (1) is NumberField.natDenominator_le_mulHeight₁ and Algebra.isIntegral_natDenominator_smul.
- Step (2): in NumberField.mulHeight₁_eq every factor max(w x, 1)^(mult w) and max(v x, 1) is at least 1, so w(x) ≤ mulHeight₁ x ≤ D for every infinite place w; hence |σ(y)| = c·|σ(x)| ≤ D².
- Step (3) is Algebra.discr_mul_isIntegral_mem_adjoin; the Vandermonde inverse is given by Lagrange interpolation, (V^(−1))_(j,i) = coefficient of X^j in f(X)/((X − z_i) f′(z_i)), whose enclosures come from the certificates of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate.
- Completeness follows from (1)–(4): each x of height ≤ D equals (Σ_j b_j θ^j)/c for a candidate (c, b); its enclosure has l ≤ mulHeight₁ x ≤ D, so it is not discarded.
- Soundness: u < D gives mulHeight₁ x < D; l ≤ D ≤ u and u − l < τ give |mulHeight₁ x − D| < τ.
- ℙ¹: every P ∈ ℙ¹(L) is [1 : 0] (logHeight 0) or [x : 1] (rescale the representative, Height.mulHeight_smul_eq_mulHeight), and Height.logHeight ![x, 1] = logHeight₁ x (Height.logHeight₁_eq_logHeight).

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.boundedHeightPoints` (data): The pair (S_<, S_≈) of finite subsets of L.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.mem_boundedHeightPoints_of_mulHeight₁_le` (characterisation): mulHeight₁ x ≤ D implies x ∈ S_< ∪ S_≈.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.mulHeight₁_lt_of_mem_lt` (characterisation): x ∈ S_< implies mulHeight₁ x < D.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.abs_mulHeight₁_sub_lt_of_mem_near` (characterisation): x ∈ S_≈ implies |mulHeight₁ x − D| < τ.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.boundedHeightProjectivePoints` (data): The finite set T ⊆ ℙ¹(L) of [x : 1] for x ∈ S_< ∪ S_≈ together with [1 : 0].
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.mem_boundedHeightProjectivePoints` (characterisation): Height.logHeight P.rep ≤ log D implies P ∈ T, for every P ∈ ℙ¹(L).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.boundedHeightPoints_superset` (compatibility): The toFinset of NumberField.finite_setOfPred_mulHeight₁_le L D is contained in S_< ∪ S_≈.

**Tests.**

- `bounded_height_rat_two` (computation): For L = ℚ, D = 2 and τ = 1/2: S_< = {0, 1, −1} and S_≈ = {2, −2, 1/2, −1/2}; T has 8 points of ℙ¹(ℚ).
- `bounded_height_gaussian_one` (degenerate): For L = ℚ(i), D = 1: S_< = ∅ and S_≈ = {0, 1, −1, i, −i}, the elements of height exactly 1.
- `bounded_height_integral_only` (non-example): Restricting step (4) to c = 1 misses x = 1/2 for L = ℚ and D = 2, so the denominators c ≤ D are needed.
- `bounded_height_infinity` (characterisation): [1 : 0] ∈ T for every D ≥ 1, since Height.logHeight ![1, 0] = 0.
- `bounded_height_superset` (compatibility): For L = ℚ and D = 3 the union S_< ∪ S_≈ contains {x : ℚ | mulHeight₁ x ≤ 3}, which has 15 elements (7 integers, 4 with denominator 2, 4 with denominator 3).

**Acceptance.** For L = ℚ and D = 2 the output covers exactly the seven elements 0, ±1, ±2, ±1/2 and T has eight points of ℙ¹(ℚ). For L = ℚ(i) and D = 1 the output is {0, ±1, ±i} (Kronecker: height 1 means 0 or a root of unity).

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:NumberField.natDenominator_le_mulHeight₁`; `mathlib:Algebra.isIntegral_natDenominator_smul`; `mathlib:NumberField.mulHeight₁_eq`; `mathlib:Algebra.discr_mul_isIntegral_mem_adjoin`; `mathlib:NumberField.finite_setOfPred_mulHeight₁_le`; `mathlib:Height.logHeight`; `mathlib:Height.logHeight₁_eq_logHeight`; `mathlib:Height.mulHeight_smul_eq_mulHeight`; `mathlib:Projectivization`; `mathlib:Projectivization.rep`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure`.

The candidate generator is of this denominator-and-box shape; the coordinate bound is obtained from certified root boxes in the power basis instead of an LLL-reduced integral basis. `doyle-krumm-2015` — §4.3, Algorithm 4 output (arXiv v4 p. 11). ## ED.1 — Lattice reduction and integer relations

**Planets.** Approximation lattice; Distance lemma for reduced bases; p-adic approximation lattice; p-adic reduction step; Fincke–Pohst enumeration; Lattice exclusion certificate.

<a id="ED-1-linear-form-lattice"></a>

### The approximation lattice of a real linear form

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.linearFormLattice` · implementation unchecked.

Data: n ≥ 2; real numbers θ_1, …, θ_n (and β for an inhomogeneous form); a positive rational scaling constant C; positive integer weights W_1, …, W_{n−1}; integers φ_1, …, φ_n with |φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1 and φ_n ≠ 0 (and an integer ψ with |ψ − Cβ| ≤ 1). Write Λ(x) = Σ_i x_iθ_i and Λ̃(x) = Σ_i x_iφ_i for x ∈ ℤ^n. The approximation lattice Γ ⊂ ℤ^n is the image of ℤ^n under the integer matrix A whose first n − 1 rows are diag(W_1, …, W_{n−1}) padded by a zero last column and whose last row is (φ_1, …, φ_n); thus Ax = (W_1x_1, …, W_{n−1}x_{n−1}, Λ̃(x)) and the columns of A form a ℤ-basis of Γ, with det A = W_1⋯W_{n−1}·φ_n ≠ 0. The inhomogeneous target is y = (0, …, 0, −ψ). The basic identities are ‖Ax‖² = Σ_{i<n} W_i²x_i² + Λ̃(x)², |Λ̃(x) − CΛ(x)| ≤ Σ_i |x_i|, ‖Ax − y‖² = Σ_{i<n} W_i²x_i² + (Λ̃(x) + ψ)² and |Λ̃(x) + ψ − C(β + Λ(x))| ≤ 1 + Σ_i |x_i|. Rounding contract: from a RealEnclosure [l_i, u_i] of θ_i with C(u_i − l_i) ≤ 1, φ_i := round(C(l_i + u_i)/2) satisfies |φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1/2 + C(u_i − l_i)/2 ≤ 1. The columns of A, as vectors of Euclidean ℝ^n, have integer Gram matrix AᵀA, which is the input of GN.5's exact LLL; a reduced basis AU (U unimodular) gives exact rational coordinates s = (AU)^(−1)y. de Weger takes W_i = γ for all i; Tzanakis–de Weger 1989 take W_i = 1 and C = c_0; Tzanakis–de Weger 1992 §16 take general weights.

**Hypotheses.** n ≥ 2, C ∈ ℚ with C > 0, W_i ∈ ℤ with W_i ≥ 1, φ_n ≠ 0. The rounding errors satisfy |φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1 and |ψ − Cβ| ≤ 1; these are checked from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure enclosures.

**Proof route.**

- Ax is computed coordinatewise from the definition of A (Matrix.mulVec); det A is the product of the diagonal of the lower-triangular-by-blocks matrix (Matrix.det).
- ‖Ax‖² and ‖Ax − y‖² are sums of squares of the coordinates.
- Λ̃(x) − CΛ(x) = Σ_i x_i(φ_i − Cθ_i), so the triangle inequality gives the rounding bounds; adding ψ − Cβ gives the inhomogeneous bound.
- Rounding: |round(q) − q| ≤ 1/2 for rational q (Mathlib's round), and |Cm_i − Cθ_i| ≤ C(u_i − l_i)/2 for the midpoint m_i.
- The Gram matrix AᵀA is integral, so GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/lll-exact-reduction applies and returns a GN.5/unimodular-basis-certificate.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.linearFormMatrix` (data): The n × n integer matrix A built from W and φ.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.linearFormMatrix_mulVec` (simp): A x = (W_1x_1, …, W_{n−1}x_{n−1}, Σ_i x_iφ_i).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.linearFormMatrix_det` (characterisation): det A = (∏_{i<n} W_i)·φ_n.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.linearFormLattice` (data): Γ = {A x : x ∈ ℤ^n} ⊆ ℤ^n.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.mem_linearFormLattice` (characterisation): v ∈ Γ iff W_i ∣ v_i for i < n and φ_n ∣ v_n − Σ_{i<n}(v_i/W_i)φ_i.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.linearFormMatrix_mulVec_injective` (structure): x ↦ A x is injective when φ_n ≠ 0, so the columns are a basis of Γ.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.normSq_linearFormMatrix_mulVec` (simp): ‖A x‖² = Σ_{i<n} W_i²x_i² + Λ̃(x)².
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.abs_linearForm_sub_le` (characterisation): |Λ̃(x) − CΛ(x)| ≤ Σ_i |x_i| when |φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.linearFormTarget` (data): y = (0, …, 0, −ψ) and ‖A x − y‖² = Σ_{i<n} W_i²x_i² + (Λ̃(x) + ψ)².
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.roundOfEnclosure` (constructor): From a RealEnclosure of θ_i with C·width ≤ 1, round(C·midpoint) satisfies |φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.linearFormMatrix_gram_integral` (compatibility): The Gram matrix of the columns in Euclidean ℝ^n is AᵀA ∈ ℤ^(n×n), the input format of GN.5's exactLLL.

**Tests.**

- `lfl_two_dim` (computation): n = 2, W_1 = 1, φ = (3, 7): A = [[1, 0], [3, 7]], det A = 7, (1, 3) ∈ Γ and (0, 1) ∉ Γ.
- `lfl_unimodular` (degenerate): All W_i = 1 and φ_n = 1 give Γ = ℤ^n.
- `lfl_log_rounding` (computation): θ = (log 2, log 3), C = 10^8: from enclosures of width 10^(−9) the rounding gives φ = (69314718, 109861229).
- `lfl_singular` (non-example): φ_n = 0 gives det A = 0; the columns are not a basis and the construction is rejected.
- `lfl_mem_iff` (characterisation): For W_1 = 1, φ = (3, 7): v ∈ Γ iff 7 ∣ v_2 − 3v_1.

**Acceptance.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1989, §III.2: n = 3, W_i = 1, C = c_0 = 10^140, φ_i = [c_0μ_i] for μ_i = log|ε_i^(4)/ε_i^(3)| (or log|ε_i^(2)/ε_i^(1)|), ψ = [c_0δ]. θ = (log 2, log 3), C = 10^8: A = [[1, 0], [69314718, 109861229]].

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure`; `mathlib:round`; `mathlib:Matrix.mulVec`; `mathlib:Matrix.det`; `mathlib:Submodule.span`; `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/unimodular-basis-certificate`; `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/lll-exact-reduction`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §3.7, printed p. 53. Definition of the real approximation lattice; the packet allows a separate weight W_i in each coordinate. The original source review checked the rendered page. `tzanakis-de-weger-1989` — §II.3(i), printed p. 112. The same lattice with unit weights and C = c_0. The original source review checked the rendered page. `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §16, printed p. 264. Weighted real lattice with rounding toward zero; the packet's contract |φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1 covers it. The original source review checked the rendered page.

**Consumers.** de Weger, §3.7–§3.8, Lemmas 3.7, 3.8, 3.10: short or near vectors of Γ correspond to small values of the linear form. Tzanakis–de Weger 1989, §II.3 and §III.2: the lattice with c_0 = 10^140 and then 10^12 reduces the bound for the Thue equations from 3.26·10^40 to 72 and then to 10. Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §16: the weighted real lattice is reduced in the real step of the Thue–Mahler algorithm. <a id="ED-1-reduced-basis-distance-lower-bound"></a>

### Lower bounds for lattice distances from a reduced basis

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/reduced-basis-distance-lower-bound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.sq_norm_sub_ge_of_reduced` · implementation unchecked.

Let E be a real inner product space and c_0, …, c_{n−1} ∈ E linearly independent (n ≥ 1, zero-based indices as in GN.5) with Gram–Schmidt vectors c*_i (Mathlib's gramSchmidt), and suppose ‖c*_i‖² ≥ 2^(−(n−1))‖c_0‖² for all i; this holds for every LLL-reduced family at δ = 3/4 (GN.5/lll-gram-schmidt-growth with j = 0) and is de Weger's (3.12). Let Γ be the ℤ-span of the c_i and ‖s‖ the distance from s ∈ ℝ to the nearest integer. (a) Every nonzero v ∈ Γ satisfies ‖v‖² ≥ 2^(−(n−1))‖c_0‖² (de Weger Lemma 3.4, LLL Proposition 1.11). (b) Let y = Σ_i s_i c_i with s_i ∈ ℝ not all integers and i_0 the largest index with s_{i_0} ∉ ℤ. Then every v ∈ Γ satisfies ‖v − y‖² ≥ 2^(−(n−1))·‖s_{i_0}‖²·‖c_0‖² (de Weger Lemma 3.5). (c) Let instead i_0 be any index (not necessarily the largest non-integral one) and δ_1 ≥ 0, δ_2 > 0 with ‖s_i‖ ≤ δ_1 for all i > i_0 and ‖s_{i_0}‖ ≥ δ_2; then every v ∈ Γ satisfies ‖v − y‖ ≥ 2^(−(n−1)/2)·δ_2·‖c_0‖ − (n − 1 − i_0)·δ_1·max_{i>i_0}‖c_i‖ (de Weger Lemma 3.6, zero-based).

**Hypotheses.** E a real inner product space; c : Fin n → E linearly independent; ∀ i, ‖c*_i‖² ≥ 2^(−(n−1))‖c_0‖². In (b), (c): s : Fin n → ℝ and y = Σ s_i c_i; in (b) i_0 is the largest index with s_{i_0} ∉ ℤ, in (c) i_0 is any index satisfying the bounds stated there.

**Proof route.**

- Write v = Σ r_i c_i with r_i ∈ ℤ. Gram–Schmidt is triangular: c_i ∈ c*_i + span(c*_j : j < i), so the c*_k-coordinate of Σ_i (r_i − s_i) c_i equals r_k − s_k for the largest k with r_k ≠ s_k.
- By orthogonality (InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidt_orthogonal), ‖v − y‖² ≥ (r_k − s_k)²‖c*_k‖² ≥ (r_k − s_k)²·2^(−(n−1))‖c_0‖².
- Since s_{i_0} ∉ ℤ and r_{i_0} ∈ ℤ we have k ≥ i_0; if k = i_0 then |r_k − s_k| ≥ ‖s_{i_0}‖, and if k > i_0 then s_k ∈ ℤ, r_k ≠ s_k, so |r_k − s_k| ≥ 1 ≥ ‖s_{i_0}‖. This proves (b); (a) is the same argument with s = 0 and v ≠ 0.
- (c): let t_i be the nearest integer to s_i for i > i_0 and t_i = s_i for i ≤ i_0, z = Σ t_i c_i; then ‖z − y‖ ≤ (n − 1 − i_0)δ_1 max_{i>i_0}‖c_i‖, and the argument of (b) applied to z (whose largest non-integral coordinate is i_0, with ‖t_{i_0}‖ ≥ δ_2, and |r_k − t_k| ≥ 1 > δ_2 for k > i_0) gives ‖v − z‖ ≥ 2^(−(n−1)/2)δ_2‖c_0‖; conclude by the triangle inequality.

**Acceptance.** Γ = ℤ² with c = (e_1, e_2) (LLL-reduced) and y = (1/2, 0): i_0 = 0 and (b) gives ‖v − y‖² ≥ 2^(−1)·(1/4)·1 = 1/8, while the true minimum is 1/4. Tzanakis–de Weger 1989, §III.2: for the lattices Γ_1, Γ_2 with c_0 = 10^12, |b_1| > 1.092·10^4 and ‖s_3‖ > 0.143 give l(Γ, y) > 2^(−1)·0.143·1.092·10^4 > 780 (here i_0 is the last index).

**Direct prerequisites.** `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/lll-gram-schmidt-growth`; `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/lll-reduced`; `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/lll-short-vector-factor`; `mathlib:InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidt`; `mathlib:InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidt_orthogonal`; `mathlib:Submodule.span`; `mathlib:Int.fract`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §3.4, Lemma 3.5, printed p. 43. Part (b), with de Weger's 1-based index shifted to GN.5's zero-based convention. The original source review checked the rendered page. `de-weger-1989` — §3.4, Lemma 3.6, printed p. 44. Part (c); the count n − i_0 of indices above i_0 in the 1-based source is n − 1 − i_0 here. The original source review checked the rendered page. `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §15, (35), printed p. 261. The same bound used for the p-adic lattice Γ_m.
