<a id="ED-1-homogeneous-reduction"></a>

### Reduction of a homogeneous real linear form

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/homogeneous-reduction` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.mul_abs_linearForm_ge_of_norm_ge` · implementation unchecked.

Let Γ be the approximation lattice of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice for the homogeneous form Λ(x) = Σ_i x_iθ_i (|φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1, φ_n ≠ 0). Let X_1, …, X_n ≥ 0, μ > 0 and L ≥ 0 be reals with L² ≥ Σ_{i<n} W_i²X_i² + (Σ_{i=1}^n X_i + μ)², and suppose every nonzero v ∈ Γ satisfies ‖v‖ ≥ L. Then every x ∈ ℤ^n with x ≠ 0 and |x_i| ≤ X_i for all i satisfies C·|Λ(x)| ≥ μ. Consequently, if c, δ > 0 and x is such a vector with |Λ(x)| < c·exp(−δ·max_i|x_i|), then max_i|x_i| < (1/δ)·log(cC/μ). With W_i = γ, X_i = X_1 and μ = X_1 the hypothesis is de Weger's ℓ(Γ) ≥ √((n+1)² + (n−1)γ²)·X_1 (Lemma 3.7); with W_i = 1, X_i = K_3, L = 2^(−(q−1)/2)|b_1| and the largest admissible margin μ = √(L² − (q−1)K_3²) − qK_3 (positive exactly when |b_1| > √((q² + q − 1)·2^(q−1))·K_3) it is Tzanakis–de Weger's Proposition 3.1.

**Hypotheses.** Setting of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice with β = 0. L is any certified lower bound for the nonzero vectors of Γ, e.g. 2^(−(n−1)/2)‖c_0‖ for an LLL-reduced basis (GN.5/lll-short-vector-factor) or one read from a Fincke–Pohst enumeration (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete).

**Proof route.**

- x ≠ 0 and det A ≠ 0 give A x ≠ 0, so ‖Ax‖² ≥ L².
- ‖Ax‖² = Σ_{i<n} W_i²x_i² + Λ̃(x)² ≤ Σ_{i<n} W_i²X_i² + Λ̃(x)², hence |Λ̃(x)| ≥ Σ_i X_i + μ.
- C|Λ(x)| ≥ |Λ̃(x)| − |Λ̃(x) − CΛ(x)| ≥ Σ_i X_i + μ − Σ_i |x_i| ≥ μ.
- If |Λ(x)| < c·exp(−δX) with X = max|x_i|, then μ ≤ C|Λ(x)| < cC·exp(−δX), i.e. X < (1/δ)log(cC/μ).

**Acceptance.** Computed instance: θ = (log 2, log 3), C = 10^8, W_1 = 1, φ = (69314718, 109861229). The Gauss–LLL reduced basis of Γ has c_0 = (−1054, 4513) with ‖c_0‖² = 21478085, so L² = 21478085/2 ≥ 1000² + (2000 + 1000)² = 10^7. Hence |x_1 log 2 + x_2 log 3| ≥ 10^(−5) for all (x_1, x_2) ≠ 0 with |x_i| ≤ 1000 (the true minimum there is |306 log 3 − 485 log 2| ≈ 1.02·10^(−3)). de Weger, Lemma 3.7, is the case W_i = γ, X_i = μ = X_1.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §3.7, Lemma 3.7, printed p. 54. Special case W_i = γ, X_i = X_1, μ = X_1. The original source review checked the rendered page. `tzanakis-de-weger-1989` — §II.3, Proposition 3.1, printed p. 114. Special case W_i = 1, X_i = K_3 with the LLL lower bound for ℓ(Γ). The original source review checked the rendered page.

<a id="ED-1-inhomogeneous-reduction"></a>

### Reduction of an inhomogeneous real linear form

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.mul_abs_inhomogeneousForm_ge_of_dist_ge` · implementation unchecked.

Let Γ, A and y = (0, …, 0, −ψ) be as in EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice for the form β + Λ(x) (|φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1, |ψ − Cβ| ≤ 1, φ_n ≠ 0). Let X_1, …, X_n ≥ 0, μ > 0 and L ≥ 0 be reals with L² ≥ Σ_{i<n} W_i²X_i² + (1 + Σ_{i=1}^n X_i + μ)², and suppose every v ∈ Γ satisfies ‖v − y‖ ≥ L. Then every x ∈ ℤ^n with |x_i| ≤ X_i for all i satisfies C·|β + Λ(x)| ≥ μ; consequently, if |β + Λ(x)| < c·exp(−δ·max_i|x_i|) for such x, then max_i|x_i| < (1/δ)·log(cC/μ). With W_i = γ, X_i = X_1 ≥ 1 and μ = X_1 the hypothesis follows from de Weger's ℓ(Γ, y) ≥ √((n+2)² + (n−1)γ²)·X_1 (Lemma 3.10). With W_i = 1, X_i = K_3 ≥ 2, μ = qK_3 and L = 2^(−(q−1)/2)‖s_{i*}‖|b_1| it is Tzanakis–de Weger's Proposition 3.2, whose constant √(4q² + 3q − 3/4)·K_3 dominates the required one exactly when K_3 ≥ 2.

**Hypotheses.** Setting of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice with target y. L is a certified lower bound for the distance from y to Γ, e.g. from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/reduced-basis-distance-lower-bound (b) or (c), or from a Fincke–Pohst enumeration.

**Proof route.**

- For x in the box, A x ∈ Γ, so L² ≤ ‖Ax − y‖² = Σ_{i<n} W_i²x_i² + (Λ̃(x) + ψ)², hence |Λ̃(x) + ψ| ≥ 1 + Σ_i X_i + μ.
- C|β + Λ(x)| ≥ |Λ̃(x) + ψ| − |Λ̃(x) + ψ − C(β + Λ(x))| ≥ 1 + Σ_i X_i + μ − (1 + Σ_i |x_i|) ≥ μ.
- The exponential consequence is as in EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/homogeneous-reduction.
- Comparison with Proposition 3.2: (q − 1)K_3² + (1 + 2qK_3)² ≤ (4q² + 3q − 3/4)K_3² = (q − 1)K_3² + (2q + 1/2)²K_3² iff K_3 ≥ 2.

**Acceptance.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1989, §III.2, second step: q = n = 3, W_i = 1, C = c_0 = 10^12, X_i = K_3 = 72, μ = qK_3 = 216, L > 780 from |b_1| > 1.092·10^4 and ‖s_3‖ > 0.143. Required: L² ≥ 2·72² + (1 + 216 + 216)² = 197857, i.e. L ≥ √197857 = 444.81…; it holds. With K_1 = 6.38771·10^4 and K_2 = 3.303 this gives A < (1/3.303)·log(10^12·6.38771·10^4/216) < 10.1, so A ≤ 10. Tzanakis–de Weger 1989, §III.2, first step: c_0 = 10^140, K_3 = 3.26·10^40, ‖s_3‖ > 0.029 and |b_1| > 3.247·10^46 give A < 72.4, so A ≤ 72.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice`.

<a id="ED-1-padic-linear-form-lattice"></a>

### The approximation lattice of a p-adic linear form

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.padicLatticeMatrix` · implementation unchecked.

Data: a prime p, m ∈ ℕ, n ≥ 1, p-adic integers β_0, β_1, …, β_{n−1} ∈ ℤ_p and positive integer weights W_1, …, W_n. The normalised p-adic linear form is Λ′(b) = b_n − β_0 − Σ_{j<n} b_jβ_j for b ∈ ℤ^n (homogeneous when β_0 = 0). For x ∈ ℤ_p let x^(m) ∈ [0, p^m − 1] be the integer with x ≡ x^(m) (mod p^m) (Mathlib's PadicInt.appr x m). The lattice Γ_m ⊂ ℤ^n is generated by the columns of the integer matrix A_m whose first n − 1 rows are diag(W_1, …, W_{n−1}) padded by a zero last column and whose last row is W_n·(β_1^(m), …, β_{n−1}^(m), p^m); the target is y_m = (0, …, 0, −W_nβ_0^(m)). Characterisation (Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, Lemma 14; de Weger, Lemmas 3.13 and 3.15 with the sign of y corrected): for b ∈ ℤ^n, p^m divides Λ′(b) in ℤ_p (i.e. ord_p Λ′(b) ≥ m) if and only if (W_1b_1, …, W_nb_n) + y_m ∈ Γ_m. In that case ‖(W_jb_j)_j‖ = ‖v − y_m‖ for the lattice vector v = (W_jb_j)_j + y_m. det A_m = p^m·W_1⋯W_n. The integers β_j^(m) are read from PadicEnclosures of β_j of absolute precision at least m whose centres are p-integral.

**Hypotheses.** p prime, m ∈ ℕ, n ≥ 1, β_j ∈ ℤ_p, W_j ∈ ℤ with W_j ≥ 1. The β_j are given by EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure p-adic enclosures of absolute precision ≥ m.

**Proof route.**

- For z = (b_1, …, b_{n−1}, λ) ∈ ℤ^n, A_m z = (W_1b_1, …, W_{n−1}b_{n−1}, W_n(Σ_{j<n} b_jβ_j^(m) + p^mλ)).
- Given b, set λ = (b_n − β_0^(m) − Σ_{j<n} b_jβ_j^(m))/p^m; then A_m(b_1, …, b_{n−1}, λ) = (W_jb_j)_j + y_m, and this vector is in Γ_m iff λ ∈ ℤ (the columns are a basis since det A_m ≠ 0).
- λ ∈ ℤ iff p^m divides b_n − β_0^(m) − Σ b_jβ_j^(m) in ℤ, iff p^m divides Λ′(b) in ℤ_p, because β_j − β_j^(m) ∈ p^mℤ_p (PadicInt.appr_spec).
- From a PadicEnclosure (c, N) of β_j with N ≥ m and c p-integral, β_j^(m) is the residue of c modulo p^m in [0, p^m − 1].

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.padicLatticeMatrix` (data): The integer matrix A_m built from p, m, W and the β_j^(m).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.padicLatticeTarget` (data): y_m = (0, …, 0, −W_nβ_0^(m)).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.padicLinearForm` (data): Λ′(b) = b_n − β_0 − Σ_{j<n} b_jβ_j ∈ ℤ_p.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.mem_padicLattice_iff` (characterisation): p^m ∣ Λ′(b) iff (W_jb_j)_j + y_m ∈ Γ_m.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.padicLatticeMatrix_det` (other): det A_m = p^m·∏_j W_j.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.padicLattice_antitone` (other): With fixed data, Γ_{m+1} ⊆ Γ_m.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.apprOfEnclosure` (constructor): From a PadicEnclosure (c, N) of β with N ≥ m and v_p(c) ≥ 0, the residue of c in [0, p^m − 1] equals PadicInt.appr β m.

**Tests.**

- `plfl_three` (computation): p = 3, m = 1, n = 2, W = (1, 1), β_1 = 0, β_0 = 1: Γ_1 = ℤ × 3ℤ, y_1 = (0, −1), and b = (0, 1) has Λ′(b) = 0 and (b_1, b_2) + y_1 = (0, 0) ∈ Γ_1.
- `plfl_sign` (non-example): In the same data, the translate with y = (0, +1) (the printed sign of de Weger's Lemma 3.15) characterises b_2 ≡ 2 (mod 3), not 3 ∣ Λ′(b) ⇔ b_2 ≡ 1 (mod 3).
- `plfl_m_zero` (degenerate): m = 0: A_0 = diag(W_1, …, W_n) up to the last row W_n(0, …, 0, 1), Γ_0 = ⊕_j W_jℤ, and every b satisfies p^0 ∣ Λ′(b).
- `plfl_one_dim` (compatibility): n = 1: Γ_m = W_1p^mℤ and the characterisation says b_1 ≡ β_0 (mod p^m), i.e. b_1 ≡ PadicInt.appr β_0 m.

**Acceptance.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §15E: for p_1 = 2, m = 1152 and W_j = 1 the six-dimensional lattice Γ_m has det = 2^1152. p = 3, m = 1, β_1 = 0, β_0 = 1: Γ_1 = ℤ × 3ℤ and y_1 = (0, −1).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure`; `mathlib:PadicInt.appr`; `mathlib:PadicInt.appr_spec`; `mathlib:PadicInt`; `mathlib:Matrix.mulVec`; `mathlib:Matrix.det`.

**Sources.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §15, printed p. 260. Definition of Γ_m with weights; Lemma 14 on the same page is the characterisation. The original source review checked the rendered page. `de-weger-1989` — §3.11, Lemma 3.13, printed p. 64. The homogeneous case with unit weights. The original source review checked the rendered page. `de-weger-1989` — §3.12, printed p. 65. The inhomogeneous target; the printed sign is corrected to −β′^(μ) (sourceIssues EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E2), as in Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §15.

**Consumers.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §15, Lemma 14 and Proposition 15: for each prime p_i a reduced basis of Γ_m bounds the exponent n_i by about log K_0/log p_i. de Weger, §3.10–§3.12 and Chapters 6–7: p-adic approximation lattices reduce the bounds for S-unit equations. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2 (Thue–Mahler and S-unit reduction): the p-adic linear forms in logarithms are reduced with this lattice.

<a id="ED-1-padic-reduction"></a>

### Reduction of a p-adic linear form

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-reduction` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.not_dvd_padicLinearForm_of_dist_ge` · implementation unchecked.

In the setting of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice, let X_1, …, X_n ≥ 0 and L ≥ 0 be reals with L² > Σ_j W_j²X_j². (a) Inhomogeneous: if ‖v − y_m‖ ≥ L for every v ∈ Γ_m, then every b ∈ ℤ^n with |b_j| ≤ X_j for all j satisfies ord_p Λ′(b) ≤ m − 1, i.e. p^m ∤ Λ′(b). (b) Zero target (y_m = 0, which holds when β_0 = 0 and more generally when β_0^(m) = 0): if ‖v‖ ≥ L for every nonzero v ∈ Γ_m, the same holds for every nonzero b in the box. Consequently, if Λ = ξ·Λ′ with ord_p ξ = κ known and a solution satisfies ord_p Λ(b) ≥ c_1 + c_2·b_k with c_2 > 0, then b_k ≤ (m − 1 + κ − c_1)/c_2. This is Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, Proposition 15 (weights W_j, X_j the a priori bounds, Q = Σ W_j²X_j²), and de Weger, Lemmas 3.14 and 3.16 (unit weights, X_j = X_1, condition ℓ(Γ_μ) > √n·X_1).

**Hypotheses.** Setting of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice. L is a certified lower bound, e.g. from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/reduced-basis-distance-lower-bound applied to an LLL-reduced basis of Γ_m.

**Proof route.**

- Suppose p^m ∣ Λ′(b). By the characterisation, v := (W_jb_j)_j + y_m ∈ Γ_m and ‖v − y_m‖² = Σ_j W_j²b_j² ≤ Σ_j W_j²X_j² < L², contradicting ‖v − y_m‖ ≥ L.
- In the homogeneous case b ≠ 0 gives v = (W_jb_j)_j ≠ 0, and the same contradiction arises.
- ord_p Λ(b) = κ + ord_p Λ′(b) ≤ κ + m − 1, combined with ord_p Λ(b) ≥ c_1 + c_2b_k, bounds b_k.

**Acceptance.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §15E: p_1 = 2, m = 1152, six unknowns with W_j = 1 and X_j = K_0 = 9.844·10^49, so Σ_j W_j²X_j² = 6K_0² and √6·K_0 = 2.41127…·10^50; the certified bound l(Γ_m, y) > 3.98541·10^56 (case I) exceeds it, so ord_2 Λ′ ≤ 1151 and n_1 ≤ 1153. The uncorrected1992 Appendix A3 constants do not establish this initial bound: use the1993 Baker–Wüstholz route, or start at1.511×10^50 with the corrected BGMMS factor and its H≤4919 bridge (sourceIssues E29). One-dimensional check: p = 3, m = 2, β_0 = 5 (so β_0^(2) = 5), W_1 = 1: Γ_2 = 9ℤ, y = −5, distance 4; with X_1 = 3 (9 < 16) no b with |b| ≤ 3 has 9 ∣ b − 5.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice`.

**Sources.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §15, Proposition 15, printed p. 262. Q = vW²N_0² + rK_0² is Σ_j W_j²X_j² for the source's weights and bounds. The original source review checked the rendered page. `de-weger-1989` — §3.11, Lemma 3.14, printed p. 64. Homogeneous case with unit weights. The original source review checked the rendered page. `tzanakis-de-weger-1993-correction` — pp.241–242, corrected initial bound and both repaired reduction routes. The source supplies the missing multiplicative factor and the alternate Baker–Wüstholz route that justifies the9.844×10^49 initial example bound.

<a id="ED-1-short-vector-enumeration"></a>

### Fincke–Pohst enumeration of lattice points in an ellipsoid

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.fpEnumeration` · implementation unchecked.

Input: n ≥ 1, a symmetric matrix G ∈ ℚ^(n×n) (the Gram matrix AᵀA of a lattice basis A), a centre t ∈ ℚ^n and a bound R ∈ ℚ. Quadratic completion (Fincke–Pohst (2.3)) computes rationals q_ij (1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ n) with x ᵀGx = Σ_i q_ii(x_i + Σ_{j>i} q_ij x_j)² for all x ∈ ℚ^n; the construction requires every pivot q_ii > 0, which holds exactly when G is positive definite. fpEnumeration G t R is the finite set of x ∈ ℤ^n produced by the recursion: T_n = R; for k = n, n − 1, …, 1, given x_{k+1}, …, x_n put U_k = Σ_{j>k} q_kj(x_j − t_j), let x_k run over the integers with q_kk(x_k − t_k + U_k)² ≤ T_k (a finite interval of integers found by exact rational comparison), and put T_{k−1} = T_k − q_kk(x_k − t_k + U_k)². The output is the set of completed vectors x. With the lattice basis A and y = A t, the vectors A x for x in the output are the lattice points v ∈ Γ with ‖v − y‖² ≤ R (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete). Fincke–Pohst(2.8), p.465, outputs both signs and excludes zero. De Weger's Figure2 instead prints only x before terminating at zero; E25 supplies the missing −x output. This adaptation scans the full integer intervals and also includes 0 when t = 0 and R ≥ 0; the homogeneous use removes 0. If some pivot q_ii is not positive, fpEnumeration G t R is the empty set.

**Hypotheses.** G symmetric with all pivots q_ii > 0; t ∈ ℚ^n; R ∈ ℚ. All arithmetic is exact over ℚ; square roots are never formed, the integer range at each level is decided by comparing rationals.

**Proof route.**

- Quadratic completion is Gaussian elimination on the symmetric matrix G (an LDLᵀ decomposition: q_ii are the pivots, q_ij = (L)_ji for j > i), valid when every pivot is nonzero; the identity for x ᵀGx follows by expanding (Fincke–Pohst (2.2)–(2.3)).
- At level k the condition q_kk(x_k − t_k + U_k)² ≤ T_k with q_kk > 0 defines a bounded set of integers, so every level is finite and the recursion produces a finite set; the coordinate bound is Fincke–Pohst (2.6)–(2.7).
- The order of the coordinates and a preliminary reduction of the basis (Fincke–Pohst (2.12), Steps 2–3, using GN.5's LLL) change only the running time, not the output set after the change of coordinates x = Uy.
- Replay de Weger §3.6 Figure 2 using exact rational LDL decomposition of positive definite AᵀA. At each depth enumerate all integer coordinates in the remaining squared-radius interval, including its boundary, translated by the rational target; update the nonnegative remaining radius and backtrack. Induction on depth proves exhaustive enumeration; the raw inverse-row cube is an independent finite fallback and completeness cross-check.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.quadraticCompletion` (data): The rational coefficients q_ij of Fincke–Pohst (2.3).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.quadraticCompletion_spec` (characterisation): x ᵀGx = Σ_i q_ii(x_i + Σ_{j>i} q_ij x_j)² for all x ∈ ℚ^n when all pivots are nonzero.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.quadraticCompletion_pivot_pos_iff` (characterisation): All pivots q_ii are positive iff G is positive definite.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.fpEnumeration` (data): The finite set of integer vectors produced by the recursion.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.fpEnumeration_neg` (relation): With t = 0 the set is closed under x ↦ −x.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.fpEnumeration_of_neg` (simp): If R < 0 the set is empty.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.fpEnumeration_mono` (other): R ≤ R′ implies fpEnumeration G t R ⊆ fpEnumeration G t R′.

**Tests.**

- `fp_identity_one` (computation): G = I_2, t = 0, R = 1: the output is {0, ±e_1, ±e_2} (five vectors).
- `fp_hexagonal` (computation): G = [[2, 1], [1, 2]], t = 0, R = 2: the output is {0, ±(1, 0), ±(0, 1), ±(1, −1)} (seven vectors); (1, 1) has value 6 and is excluded.
- `fp_centre_half` (computation): n = 1, G = (1), t = 1/2, R = 1/4: the output is {0, 1}.
- `fp_negative_bound` (degenerate): R = −1 gives the empty set for every G and t.
- `fp_box_non_example` (non-example): For G = [[2, 1], [1, 2]] and R = 2 the box |x_i| ≤ 1 contains (1, 1), which is not in the output: bounding each coordinate separately overcounts.

**Acceptance.** G = [[2, 1], [1, 2]], t = 0, R = 2 gives the seven vectors of the hexagonal lattice of norm at most 2. For the lattice of θ = (1, √2), C = 100, φ = (100, 141), the enumeration with R = 73 is {0} and with R = 74 contains ±(−7, 5).

<a id="ED-1-short-vector-enumeration-complete"></a>

### Soundness and completeness of the Fincke–Pohst enumeration

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.mem_fpEnumeration_iff` · implementation unchecked.

Let G ∈ ℚ^(n×n) be symmetric with all pivots of its quadratic completion positive, t ∈ ℚ^n and R ∈ ℚ. Then for every x ∈ ℤ^n: x ∈ fpEnumeration G t R ⟺ (x − t)ᵀG(x − t) ≤ R. Lattice form: if A ∈ ℤ^(n×n) is nonsingular with G = AᵀA, Γ = Aℤ^n and y ∈ ℚ^n with t = A^(−1)y, then {v ∈ Γ : ‖v − y‖² ≤ R} = {A x : x ∈ fpEnumeration G t R}. Corollaries used as distance certificates: if the output is empty then ‖v − y‖² > R for every v ∈ Γ; if t = 0 and the output is {0} then ‖v‖² > R for every nonzero v ∈ Γ; in general every v ∈ Γ satisfies ‖v − y‖² ≥ min({R} ∪ {(x − t)ᵀG(x − t) : x in the output}).

**Hypotheses.** G symmetric with positive pivots (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration); t ∈ ℚ^n; R ∈ ℚ. In the lattice form A is a nonsingular integer matrix.

**Proof route.**

- (⇐) If (x − t)ᵀG(x − t) ≤ R then, by the quadratic completion, the partial sums Σ_{i≥k} q_ii(x_i − t_i + U_i)² are at most R, so at each level k the coordinate x_k satisfies q_kk(x_k − t_k + U_k)² ≤ T_k for the tail (x_{k+1}, …, x_n); by downward induction on k the tail is produced, hence x is (Fincke–Pohst (2.6)–(2.7)).
- (⇒) Every produced x has T_0 = R − Σ_i q_ii(x_i − t_i + U_i)² ≥ 0, i.e. (x − t)ᵀG(x − t) ≤ R by quadraticCompletion_spec.
- Lattice form: ‖Ax − y‖² = (x − t)ᵀAᵀA(x − t), and x ↦ A x is a bijection ℤ^n → Γ.
- The corollaries follow because every lattice vector outside the output has squared distance > R.
- Replay de Weger §3.6 Figure 2 using exact rational LDL decomposition of positive definite AᵀA. At each depth enumerate all integer coordinates in the remaining squared-radius interval, including its boundary, translated by the rational target; update the nonnegative remaining radius and backtrack. Induction on depth proves exhaustive enumeration; the raw inverse-row cube is an independent finite fallback and completeness cross-check.

**Acceptance.** G = [[2, 1], [1, 2]], t = 0, R = 2: exactly the seven vectors {0, ±(1, 0), ±(0, 1), ±(1, −1)} satisfy xᵀGx ≤ 2, and these are the output. Γ = ℤ(1, 0) + ℤ(0, 10), y = (0, −1), R = 1/2: the output is empty, certifying ‖v − y‖² > 1/2 for all v ∈ Γ (the true distance is 1).

Independently read Fincke–Pohst (2.2)–(2.8), pp.464–465, confirms the quadratic-completion recursion and its boundary inclusion; the translated rational centre is an ED.1 adaptation.

Retain zero when the target set requires it, and both signs in the homogeneous full vector set. The affine extension must not copy the homogeneous sign shortcut.

<a id="ED-1-short-vector-reduction"></a>

### Residual enumeration for a real linear form

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-reduction` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.mem_fpEnumeration_or_lt_mul_abs` · implementation unchecked.

Let Γ, A, y (or y = 0) be as in EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice for the form β + Λ (β = 0 and ε = 0 in the homogeneous case, ε = 1 otherwise), let X_1, …, X_n ≥ 0 and K_0 ≥ ε + Σ_i X_i be rationals, R = Σ_{i<n} W_i²X_i² + K_0², and E = fpEnumeration(AᵀA, A^(−1)y, R). Then every x ∈ ℤ^n with |x_i| ≤ X_i for all i satisfies x ∈ E or C·|β + Λ(x)| > K_0 − ε − Σ_i|x_i| ≥ 0. Consequently, when K_0 > ε + Σ_i X_i, all solutions in the box of |β + Λ(x)| < c·exp(−δ max_i|x_i|) are among the finitely many x ∈ E checked individually, together with those satisfying max_i|x_i| < (1/δ)·log(cC/(K_0 − ε − Σ_i|x_i|)) (de Weger, Lemma 3.8 and the procedure after it).

**Hypotheses.** Setting of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice; X_i, K_0 rational with K_0 ≥ ε + Σ X_i.

**Proof route.**

- If x ∉ E then ‖Ax − y‖² > R by EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete, and Σ_{i<n} W_i²x_i² ≤ Σ_{i<n} W_i²X_i², so |Λ̃(x) + ψ| > K_0 (ψ = 0 when homogeneous).
- C|β + Λ(x)| ≥ |Λ̃(x) + ψ| − ε − Σ_i|x_i| > K_0 − ε − Σ_i|x_i| (the rounding bound of the lattice construction).
- With |β + Λ(x)| < c·exp(−δX) this gives the stated bound for X = max|x_i|; this is de Weger's (3.25).

**Acceptance.** For θ = (1, √2), C = 100, φ = (100, 141), W_1 = 1, X_1 = X_2 = 3 and K_0 = 6: R = 9 + 36 = 45, and every x with |x_i| ≤ 3 is either an enumerated short vector or satisfies 100|x_1 + x_2√2| > 6 − Σ|x_i| ≥ 0; the shortest nonzero vector of Γ is A(−7, 5) = (−7, 5) with squared length 74 > 45, so E = {0}.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §3.7, Lemma 3.8 and following paragraph, printed p. 55. The theorem is this case split, with K_0 = C_0. The original source review checked the rendered page.

<a id="ED-1-exclusion-certificate"></a>

### Lattice exclusion certificates for linear forms

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/exclusion-certificate` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RealExclusionCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

A lattice exclusion certificate is finite exact data, checked by rational and integer arithmetic only, of one of two kinds. Real kind: (i) the data of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice (C, W, φ and, for an inhomogeneous form, ψ), with the enclosures certifying |φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1 and |ψ − Cβ| ≤ 1; (ii) rational box bounds X_1, …, X_n ≥ 0 and a rational margin μ > 0; (iii) a distance witness for the matrix A and target y (y = 0 when homogeneous); (iv) the inequality L² ≥ Σ_{i<n} W_i²X_i² + (ε + Σ_i X_i + μ)² with ε = 1 (inhomogeneous) or 0 (homogeneous). p-adic kind: (i) the data of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice (p, m, W, β_j^(m) from enclosures of precision ≥ m); (ii) box bounds X_1, …, X_n ≥ 0; (iii) a distance witness for A_m and y_m; (iv) L² > Σ_j W_j²X_j². A distance witness for (A, y) is either an LLL witness — a GN.5 unimodular certificate (U, U^(−1)) such that the columns c_0, …, c_{n−1} of AU are LLL-reduced at δ = 3/4 (checked on exact rational Gram–Schmidt data), the exact vector s = (AU)^(−1)y, and L² = 2^(−(n−1))·‖s_{i_0}‖²·‖c_0‖² with i_0 the largest index with s_{i_0} ∉ ℤ (rejected if s ∈ ℤ^n), or L² = 2^(−(n−1))‖c_0‖² when y = 0 — or an enumeration witness: a rational R ≥ 0 and E = fpEnumeration(AᵀA, A^(−1)y, R), with L² the minimum of R and of ‖Ax − y‖² over x ∈ E (over x ∈ E∖{0} when y = 0). The certified region is the box {x ∈ ℤ^n : |x_i| ≤ X_i} (minus 0 whenever the target y, resp. y_m, is 0, which includes the homogeneous case). The raw fallback records A,y,Ainv∈Q^(n×n), B>0, 0≤L²≤B² and D∈N. Check AAinv=AinvA=I, Σ_j |Ainv_ij|(|y_j|+B)≤D for each row, and L²≤||Ax-y||² for every x∈[-D,D]^n eligible for the zero-target branch. If ||Ax-y||²<B², all coordinates lie in this checked box; otherwise L²≤B² gives the bound. Thus no real Gram–Schmidt inequality is trusted by this fallback. The raw p-adic form stores p,m∈N, positive integral W, canonical residues r₀,r_j∈{0,…,p^m−1}, rational X≥0 and RawDistanceCertificate data. Its checker verifies primality, every residue range, all weights and bounds, the weighted triangular matrix A (last row W_n(r₁,…,r_{n−1},p^m)), target y=(0,…,0,−W_n r₀), the full rational distance replay and Σ(W_j X_j)²<L². The semantic β₀,β_j∈Z_p occur only in check_sound through independently certified equalities appr(β₀,m)=r₀ and appr(β_j,m)=r_j.

**Hypotheses.** All entries are integers or rationals; θ_i, β and β_j enter only through their enclosures (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure). n ≥ 2 for the real reduction theorem and n ≥ 1 for the p-adic kind. The supporting raw rational distance/real-margin checker also makes sense for n=1; its one-dimensional tests do not instantiate the n≥2 reduction theorem.

**Proof route.**

- The LLL conditions at δ = 3/4 are GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/lll-reduced; with an integral basis the Gram–Schmidt data are rationals with denominators the integer potentials of GN.5/lll-integer-potential, so the check is exact.
- The coordinate vector s is obtained by exact rational linear algebra; ‖s_{i_0}‖ = min(fract s_{i_0}, 1 − fract s_{i_0}) is rational.
- Every field of the certificate is decidable, so the certificate is checked by evaluation; its meaning is EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/exclusion-certificate-sound.
- Raw soundness splits at normSq<B². The inverse row bounds put every possible violating vector in the finite cube. Exact endpoint inequalities and C>0 extend rounding to the actual enclosed values; then use the real exclusion inequality.
- From ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds certified enclosures choose rounded φ,ψ and checked endpoints. From GN.5 exact LLL use exact rational Gram–Schmidt data; if its lower-bound check cannot be expressed with the supplier carrier, use the exhaustive cube fallback. Choose B,D and compute the rational minimum over the cube; passing the separation check is the producer success condition, never a guarantee of success for every input.
- For the raw p-adic checker, a vector b satisfying the residue congruence yields v=Wb+y=Aa. If r₀=0, b≠0 and positive weights imply a≠0. The raw distance bound then gives L²≤||Aa−y||²=Σ(W_j b_j)²≤Σ(W_j X_j)²<L², a contradiction. PadicInt.appr_spec and the integer-cast divisibility comparison identify the congruence with p^m dividing the actual p-adic linear form; no semantic distance witness is supplied.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.DistanceWitness` (structure): An LLL witness or an enumeration witness for a nonsingular integer matrix A and target y, with its rational lower bound L².
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.DistanceWitness.bound` (projection): The rational number L² certified by the witness.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.DistanceWitness.sound` (characterisation): Every v ∈ Aℤ^n satisfies ‖v − y‖² ≥ L² (v ≠ 0 when y = 0).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RealExclusionCertificate` (structure): Lattice data, box, margin μ, distance witness and the inequality (iv) for a real linear form.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.PadicExclusionCertificate` (structure): p-adic lattice data, box, distance witness and L² > Σ W_j²X_j².
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RealExclusionCertificate.check` (other): Supporting Boolean evaluation on an already validated semantic record; the raw all-fields verifier is RawRealExclusionCertificate.check.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.DistanceWitness.ofLLL` (constructor): Build an LLL witness from the output of GN.5's exactLLL applied to the columns of A. Requires A.det ≠ 0 so the rational target coordinates in AU exist.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawDistanceCertificate` (structure): Raw A,y, rational inverse, radius B, squared lower bound and integer coordinate cap D; no proof fields.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawDistanceCertificate.box` (constructor): The product finite set [-D,D]^n over integer coordinates.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawDistanceCertificate.normSq` (data): The exact rational sum Σ_i((Ax-y)_i)^2.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawDistanceCertificate.check` (other): Decide both inverse identities, rational radius and row inequalities, and the finite box comparisons. No Classical real decision or oracle.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawDistanceCertificate.sound` (characterisation): If check=true, the squared lower bound applies to every integer vector, excluding x=0 when y=0.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawRealExclusionCertificate` (structure): Proof-free C,W,φ,ψ, homogeneous flag, rational interval endpoints for each θ_i and β, nonnegative coordinate bounds, positive margin and raw distance data.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawRealExclusionCertificate.check` (other): Finite rational endpoint-rounding, positivity, nonnegative coordinate bounds, homogeneous zero data, matrix/target matching, raw distance replay and final separation checks. No universal real predicate occurs in the raw input.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawRealExclusionCertificate.sound` (characterisation): Given check=true and independently certified membership of θ_i and β in the raw rational intervals, every eligible integer vector in the box satisfies margin≤C|β+Σx_iθ_i|.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawDistanceCertificate.ofMatrix` (constructor): Complete fallback: from an integer nonsingular matrix, target and positive rational radius compute inverse row caps, exhaust the integer cube and take min(B², all eligible squared distances). The result may have lower bound0; this is not failure of soundness.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawDistanceCertificate.ofMatrix_check` (characterisation): The producer passes check and preserves the supplied matrix and target.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawRealExclusionCertificate.ofEnclosures` (constructor): From actual ED.0/ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds certified intervals, choose rational rounding fields and the raw distance replay; return some raw certificate only when all finite checks pass, otherwise none.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawRealExclusionCertificate.ofEnclosures_check` (compatibility): Some output passes check and its endpoints still enclose the actual θ_i and β.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawPadicExclusionCertificate` (structure): Proof-free p,m, integral weights, canonical integer coefficient residues, rational box and complete raw rational distance transcript; no p-adic or proof fields.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawPadicExclusionCertificate.matrix` (data): The integer triangular matrix with diagonal W₁,…,W_{n−1},W_n p^m and last-row residue entries W_n r_j.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawPadicExclusionCertificate.target` (data): The integer target (0,…,0,−W_n r₀), using the negative constant residue.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawPadicExclusionCertificate.check` (other): Finite prime/residue/weight/box checks, exact matrix and target identity, inverse and all finite distance comparisons, and strict Σ(W_jX_j)²<L².
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawPadicExclusionCertificate.not_congruent` (characterisation): If check=true, every b in the coordinate box, with b≠0 when r₀=0, fails b_n−r₀−Σ b_j r_j≡0 modulo p^m.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawPadicExclusionCertificate.check_sound` (characterisation): Given check=true and independently certified PadicInt.appr residue identities for the actual β₀,β_j∈Z_p, every eligible b in the box has p^m not dividing β-linear form b_n−β₀−Σb_jβ_j, including exclusion of the exact-zero form.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RawPadicExclusionCertificate.matrix_target_eq` (compatibility): Under those appr identities the raw matrix and target equal padicLatticeMatrix and padicLatticeTarget, not merely lattices with equal determinants.

**Tests.**

- `exclusion_log23` (computation): θ = (log 2, log 3), C = 10^8, φ = (69314718, 109861229), U with AU = [c_0 c_1], c_0 = (−1054, 4513), y = 0, X = (1000, 1000), μ = 1000: L² = 21478085/2 ≥ 10^7, so the data form a homogeneous real certificate.
- `exclusion_trivial_box` (degenerate): X_i = 0 for all i: the homogeneous region is empty and any witness with L² ≥ μ² certifies it.
- `exclusion_integral_target` (non-example): If s = (AU)^(−1)y ∈ ℤ^n then y ∈ Γ, the LLL witness is rejected, and no positive lower bound for the distance exists.
- `exclusion_padic_one_dim` (computation): p = 3, m = 2, n = 1, W_1 = 1, β_0^(2) = 5, enumeration witness R = 15 with E = ∅ (Γ_2 = 9ℤ, y = −5, distances ≥ 4² = 16 > 15), X_1 = 3: L² = 15 > 9 = X_1², a p-adic certificate.
- `raw_distance_one` (computation): A=1,y=0,Ainv=1,B=L²=D=1 in dimension one passes: every nonzero integer has square at least one.
- `raw_distance_bad_inverse` (non-example): Replacing Ainv by zero in that data fails the inverse check.
- `raw_distance_integral_target` (non-example): A=1,y=1,Ainv=1,B=L²=1,D=2 fails: x=1 gives distance zero.
- `raw_real_ten` (computation): C=W=1, φ=θ=10, β=ψ=0, X=margin=1, A=10, inverse=1/10, B=2, lower=4,D=1 passes the complete homogeneous finite check.
- `raw_real_bad_endpoint` (non-example): Changing the upper θ endpoint from10 to12 rejects the rounding condition.
- `raw_real_bad_distance` (non-example): Replacing the distance inverse1/10 by0 rejects the full raw check.
- `raw_padic_one_dim` (computation): p=3,m=2,W=1,r₀=5,X=3,A=9,y=−5,Ainv=1/9,B=4,L²=15,D=1 passes. The complete checked cube is {−1,0,1}, with squared distances16,25,196.
- `raw_padic_wrong_sign` (non-example): Changing only the target to+5 rejects the matrix/target matching, despite the same positive distance to9Z.
- `raw_padic_bad_inverse` (non-example): Changing the inverse1/9 to0 rejects the full raw check.
- `raw_padic_composite` (non-example): p=9,m=1 with otherwise identical modulus9 data is rejected by primality.
- `raw_padic_strict_boundary` (non-example): X=4,L²=16 is rejected: separation is strict, and b=−4 actually satisfies b≡5 modulo9.
- `raw_padic_zero_box` (degenerate): p=3,m=1,r₀=0,W=1,X=0,A=3,y=0,Ainv=1/3,B=L²=D=1 passes for the empty eligible homogeneous region; it never excludes b=0 without the nonzero hypothesis.

<a id="ED-1-exclusion-certificate-sound"></a>

### Soundness of lattice exclusion certificates

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/exclusion-certificate-sound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED1.RealExclusionCertificate.sound` · implementation unchecked.

Let a lattice exclusion certificate (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/exclusion-certificate) check. Real kind: every x ∈ ℤ^n with |x_i| ≤ X_i for all i (and x ≠ 0 whenever the target y = (0, …, 0, −ψ) is 0, in particular in the homogeneous case) satisfies C·|β + Λ(x)| ≥ μ; hence for c, δ > 0 no such x satisfies |β + Λ(x)| < c·exp(−δ·max_i|x_i|) with max_i|x_i| ≥ (1/δ)·log(cC/μ). p-adic kind: every b ∈ ℤ^n with |b_j| ≤ X_j (and b ≠ 0 whenever y_m = 0, i.e. β_0^(m) = 0, in particular when β_0 = 0) satisfies ord_p Λ′(b) ≤ m − 1. This is the stage's acceptance: a lattice basis, a certified reduction, and a proved lower bound that excludes every integer vector of the specified region.

**Hypotheses.** The certificate's Boolean check is true. θ_i, β, β_j are the numbers enclosed by the certificate's enclosures.

**Proof route.**

- The distance witness is sound: an LLL witness by EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/reduced-basis-distance-lower-bound (a)/(b), using GN.5/lll-gram-schmidt-growth for the hypothesis on ‖c*_i‖ and GN.5/unimodular-basis-certificate for AUℤ^n = Aℤ^n; an enumeration witness by EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete.
- Real kind: apply EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/homogeneous-reduction or EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction with L from the witness and the checked inequality (iv).
- p-adic kind: apply EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-reduction.
- The raw p-adic form uses RawPadicExclusionCertificate.not_congruent and check_sound; the only external semantics are the certified coefficient residues. The integer nondivisibility conclusion is stronger and safer than applying an integer-valued valuation to the exact-zero branch.

**Acceptance.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1989, §III.2: the real inhomogeneous certificates with (C, X_i, μ) = (10^140, 3.26·10^40, 3·3.26·10^40) and (10^12, 72, 216), with LLL witnesses |b_1| > 3.247·10^46 (resp. 1.092·10^4) and ‖s_3‖ > 0.029 (resp. 0.143), exclude every (a_1, a_2, a_3) with 73 ≤ A < 3.26·10^40 (first step) and with 11 ≤ A ≤ 72 (second step) from |Λ| < 6.38771·10^4·exp(−3.303·A). Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §15E: the p-adic certificate at p = 2, m = 1152, W_j = 1, X_j = 9.844·10^49, L > 3.98541·10^56 excludes ord_2 Λ′ ≥ 1152 throughout the box. The uncorrected1992 Appendix A3 constants do not establish this initial bound: use the1993 Baker–Wüstholz route, or start at1.511×10^50 with the corrected BGMMS factor and its H≤4919 bridge (sourceIssues E29). Computed: the homogeneous certificate exclusion_log23 gives |x_1 log 2 + x_2 log 3| ≥ 10^(−5) for all (x_1, x_2) ≠ 0 with |x_i| ≤ 1000.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/exclusion-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/reduced-basis-distance-lower-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/homogeneous-reduction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-reduction`; `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/lll-gram-schmidt-growth`; `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/unimodular-basis-certificate`; `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/lll-original-lattice-verification`; `mathlib:PadicInt.appr`; `mathlib:PadicInt.appr_spec`; `mathlib:PadicInt.appr_lt`; `mathlib:PadicInt.pow_p_dvd_int_iff`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §3.8, summary after Lemma 3.10, printed p. 59. Statement of the exclusion principle in the inhomogeneous case. ## ED.2 — Linear forms in logarithms and S-unit equations

**Planets.** Certified Matveev constant; p-adic discrete-logarithm lattice; Tzanakis–de Weger method for Thue equations; Prime ideal removing lemma; Thue–Mahler solution certificate; S-unit equation certificate.

<a id="ED-2-logarithm-enclosure"></a>

### Certified enclosures of logarithms and arguments of embedded algebraic numbers

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/logarithm-enclosure` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.logAbsEnclosure` · implementation unchecked.

ED.2 supplies rational error certificates, not an evaluation algorithm. For x∈Q, x>0, let u=(x−1)/(x+1), r=|u|<1 and L_N(x)=2 Σ(k<N) u^(2k+1)/(2k+1). Then |log x−L_N(x)|≤E_N=2r^(2N+1)/((2N+1)(1−r²)); E_N→0, and x=1 gives exact0. For |t|≤1 put A_N(t)=Σ(k<N)(−1)^k t^(2k+1)/(2k+1); |arctan t−A_N(t)|≤|t|^(2N+1)/(2N+1), also tending to0 at |t|=1. Oddness and arctan t=sign(t)π/2−arctan(1/t) for |t|>1 reduce other rational arguments; π=4arctan1 (or Machin’s identity). Choose N satisfying the displayed rational error budget. Rational intervals [partial−error,partial+error], with outward dyadic rounding on mesh 2^(−P−1), prove arbitrarily small endpoint errors without any oracle for an analytic value. These scalar certificates supply the following box/log contract. Let K be a number field, σ : K →+* ℂ a complex embedding, α ∈ K with α ≠ 0, and let B = (R, I) be a closed rational box (ED.0 rational box containment) with σ(α) ∈ B, delivered by an ED.0 archimedean embedding certificate (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate). Let m and M be the exact rational minimum and maximum of x² + y² over (x, y) ∈ R × I (m > 0 exactly when 0 ∉ B). For a precision P ∈ ℕ, logAbsEnclosure(B, P) is the closed rational interval obtained by outward dyadic rounding with mesh 2^(−P−1) (ED.2 outward rational endpoint bounds) of [l/2, u/2], where l is the lower end of the scalar series enclosure of Real.log m and u the upper end of the scalar series enclosure of Real.log M, both at precision P (Real.log ‖z‖ = Real.log(x² + y²)/2); it returns none when 0 ∈ B. When B is contained in the complement of the closed half-line (−∞, 0] (that is, min R > 0, or min I > 0, or max I < 0), argEnclosure(B, P) is the closed rational interval obtained from the scalar arctangent enclosures at precision P of the corner values (at a corner (x, y): arctan(y/x) when x > 0, and sign(y)·π/2 − arctan(x/y) when y ≠ 0, with π/2 enclosed as 2·arctanEnclosure(1, P + 2) by Real.arctan_one) rounded outward with mesh 2^(−P−1); otherwise it returns none. Conventions pinned: log is Mathlib's principal logarithm Complex.log z = Real.log ‖z‖ + i·Complex.arg z with Complex.arg z ∈ (−π, π]; logarithms of real positive numbers are Real.log. Soundness: Real.log ‖σ(α)‖ ∈ logAbsEnclosure(B, P) and Complex.arg σ(α) ∈ argEnclosure(B, P) whenever these are defined; the outputs are RealEnclosures in the sense of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure. Precision budget: if B has diameter w and 0 < ρ⁻ ≤ ‖z‖ for all z ∈ B, then the width of logAbsEnclosure(B, P) is less than w/ρ⁻ + 3·2^{−P} (2^{−P} from the halved ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds endpoint enclosures, less than 2·2^{−P} from outward rounding) and that of argEnclosure(B, P) is less than (π/2)·w/ρ⁻ + 5·2^{−P} (3·2^{−P} from the corner and π/2 enclosures), so a requested absolute error ε is met by refining the box to diameter at most ρ⁻ε/4 and taking 2^{−P} ≤ ε/16.

**Hypotheses.** σ(α) lies in the box B (the ED.0 certificate's soundness statement); the enclosure claims nothing about points outside B Failure (0 ∈ B, or a box meeting the branch cut for the argument) is returned as data and never as an enclosure The endpoint series precision is chosen so each scalar interval has width≤2^(−P); the finer rounding mesh adds <2^(−P) total. For combined argument formulas allocate separate budgets to each arctangent/π term. The displayed 3 and5 error constants are safe upper budgets, not sharpness claims.

**Proof route.**

- Integrate the finite geometric identity for 2/(1−u²) from0 to u. Bound the remaining integral by 2|u|^(2N+1)/((2N+1)(1−|u|²)); this proves the log error formula. Integrate the finite geometric identity for 1/(1+t²) to prove the arctangent remainder bound, including endpoints ±1. Rational inequalities and geometric convergence give a suitable N for every positive error budget.
- Reuse existing complex logarithm/Taylor bounds rather than rebuilding logarithm convergence; the special rational odd-series bound supplies the rational endpoint certificate.
- For z in B, m ≤ ‖z‖² ≤ M, Real.log ‖z‖ = Real.log ‖z‖²/2 and Real.log is monotone on (0, ∞), so Real.log ‖z‖ ∈ [Real.log m/2, Real.log M/2]; the ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds log enclosures of the two rationals m, M and outward rounding give rational endpoints enclosing that interval.
- On the complement of (−∞, 0] the function Complex.arg is continuous, and on a box avoiding the closed negative half-axis its extreme values are attained at corners; at a corner (x, y) the value is arctan(y/x) for x > 0 and sign(y)·π/2 − arctan(x/y) for y ≠ 0 (this covers x ≤ 0, where y ≠ 0 on such a box); enclose each with the ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds arctangent enclosure, and π/2 as 2·arctan 1 (Mathlib's Real.arctan_one) with the ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds arctangent enclosure of 1 at precision P + 2; the six-digit bounds Real.pi_gt_d6 and Real.pi_lt_d6 do not reach precision 2^{−P} for P ≥ 20.
- Width: |Real.log ‖z‖ − Real.log ‖z′‖| ≤ ‖z − z′‖/ρ⁻ and |arg z − arg z′| ≤ (π/2)‖z − z′‖/ρ⁻ on the box (mean value theorem along the segment and the arc), the ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds enclosures add at most 2^{−P} (logarithm, after halving) and 3·2^{−P} (argument: corner arctangents and π/2), and outward rounding adds less than 2·2^{−P} (ED.2 endpoint error inequality).

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.logAbsEnclosure` (constructor): For a rational box B and a precision P, logAbsEnclosure B P : Option (NonemptyInterval ℚ), equal to none exactly when 0 ∈ B.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.argEnclosure` (constructor): For a rational box B and a precision P, argEnclosure B P : Option (NonemptyInterval ℚ), equal to none exactly when B meets the closed half-line (−∞, 0].
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.log_norm_mem_logAbsEnclosure` (characterisation): If z ∈ complexBoxSet B and logAbsEnclosure B P = some J then Real.log ‖z‖ ∈ J (as real numbers).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.arg_mem_argEnclosure` (characterisation): If z ∈ complexBoxSet B and argEnclosure B P = some J then Complex.arg z ∈ J.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.logAbsEnclosure_width_le` (other): If B has diameter w, 0 < ρ⁻ ≤ ‖z‖ on B and logAbsEnclosure B P = some J, then the width of J is at most w/ρ⁻ + 3·2^{−P}.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.logAbsEnclosure_ofRat` (compatibility): For a rational q > 0 and the degenerate box [q, q] × [0, 0], logAbsEnclosure contains Real.log q and has width at most 2^{1−P}.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.realLogPartialSum` (data): For positive rational x and N∈N, the rational L_N(x)=2Σ(k<N)((x−1)/(x+1))^(2k+1)/(2k+1).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.realLogPartialSum_error` (other): For x>0, r=|(x−1)/(x+1)|, |Real.log x−L_N(x)|≤2r^(2N+1)/((2N+1)(1−r²)).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.arctanPartialSum` (data): A_N(t)=Σ(k<N)(−1)^k t^(2k+1)/(2k+1)∈Q.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.arctanPartialSum_error` (other): For rational |t|≤1, |Real.arctan t−A_N(t)|≤|t|^(2N+1)/(2N+1), including t=±1.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.exists_scalar_log_precision` (constructor): For x∈Q, x>0, ε∈Q, ε>0, there exists N with 2E_N≤ε; its rational error interval contains log x. At x=1 use [0,0].

**Tests.**

- `logAbsEnclosure_two` (computation): For the degenerate box [2, 2] × [0, 0] and P = 30 the enclosure is some J with J ⊆ [0.6931471, 0.6931472] (Real.log 2 = 0.69314718…).
- `logAbsEnclosure_one` (degenerate): For the degenerate box [1, 1] × [0, 0] the enclosure contains 0 and has width at most 2^{1−P}.
- `argEnclosure_neg_one` (non-example): For the degenerate box [−1, −1] × [0, 0] (the point −1, on the branch cut) argEnclosure returns none, although Complex.arg (−1) = π is defined; a wrong definition returning an interval around π would be unsound for nearby points below the axis, whose arguments are near −π.
- `logAbsEnclosure_zero_box` (non-example): For the box [−1, 1] × [−1, 1], which contains 0, logAbsEnclosure returns none.
- `arg_i` (compatibility): For the degenerate box [0, 0] × [1, 1] the argument enclosure contains Complex.arg I = π/2, agreeing with Mathlib's Complex.arg_I.
- `log_series_two_first_term` (computation): At x=2,N=1, u=1/3, L_1=2/3 and E_1=1/36. Thus log2∈[23/36,25/36]; omitting the factor2 gives an interval below log2.
- `atan_endpoint_tail` (degenerate): At t=1,N=1, A_1=1 and error≤1/3; at t=−1 the partial sum is−1. A remainder formula requiring |t|<1 would fail to provide π precision here.
- `log_series_zero_rejected` (non-example): x=0 is rejected: u=−1 makes 1−r²=0, and Real.log0=0 by totalization is not a sound positive-log certificate.

**Acceptance.** For the box of the real root ∛2 of X³ − 2 refined to width 10^{−12}, logAbsEnclosure at P = 40 has width below 10^{−11} and contains Real.log 2/3. No enclosure is returned for a box containing 0, so a nonvanishing claim never rests on an interval around 0.

<a id="ED-2-certified-linear-form-constant"></a>

### Certified evaluation of Matveev's constant

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.MatveevConstantCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

Fix integers n ≥ 1 (the number of logarithms) and D ≥ 1 (a degree bound). Put e⁺ := 27182818286/10¹⁰ (so exp 1 < e⁺ by Real.exp_one_lt_d9). A MatveevConstantCertificate for (n, D) consists of rationals A_1, …, A_n with A_j ≥ 16/100, a rational s⁺ ≥ 0 with (s⁺)² ≥ n (so s⁺ ≥ √n), a rational ℓ⁺ ≥ Real.log D (the upper end of the ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds enclosure of Real.log D; ℓ⁺ = 0 is allowed for D = 1), and a rational c satisfying the exact rational inequality c ≥ Ĉ(n)·D²·(1 + ℓ⁺)·A_1⋯A_n, where Ĉ(n) := max(min(e⁺n/2·30^{n+3}·n³·s⁺, 2^{6n+20}), min((1/2)(e⁺n/2)²·30^{n+3}·n³·s⁺, 2^{6n+20})) is a rational number with Ĉ(n) ≥ C_1(n, κ) for κ = 1 and κ = 2, C_1(n, κ) = min{κ^{−1}(en/2)^κ·30^{n+3}·n^{3.5}, 2^{6n+20}} being the constant of Matveev's Corollary 2.3 (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/matveev-corollary-linear-form-bound). The certificate is admissible for a number field K ⊆ ℂ (given with σ : K →+* ℂ) with [K : ℚ] ≤ D, elements α_1, …, α_n ∈ K^× and nonzero complex numbers λ_1, …, λ_n with exp λ_j = σ(α_j), when A_j ≥ D·h_j⁺ and A_j ≥ |λ_j|⁺ for every j, where h_j⁺ ≥ NumberField.absLogHeight₁ α_j is obtained from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure, converted by h = Real.log(mulHeight₁)/[K : ℚ] (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow) and the upper end of ED.2/logarithm-enclosure and |λ_j|⁺ ≥ |λ_j| is read off from ED.2/logarithm-enclosure (for λ_j = Complex.log σ(α_j) + 2πik_j, |λ_j| ≤ |Real.log ‖σα_j‖| + |Complex.arg σα_j + 2πk_j|). The value used downstream is c: for every b ∈ ℤ^n with Λ := Σ b_jλ_j ≠ 0, Real.log |Λ| > −c·(1 + Real.log B*), B* := max_j |b_j| (ED.2/certified-linear-form-lower-bound). Every comparison in the certificate is an exact comparison of rationals; the name of Matveev's theorem supplies no number, and every number is computed here. The real/complex distinction κ of Matveev is not needed by the certificate because Ĉ(n) dominates both values; a logarithm λ_j with σ(α_j) = 1 and λ_j = 0 is never part of the family (such a term is removed from the linear form before the certificate is formed).

**Hypotheses.** n ≥ 1, D ≥ 1; A_j ≥ 0.16 is part of the certificate and is essential: Corollary 2.3 is stated under (2.4) [K : ℚ] ≤ D is enough: the bound is increasing in D and the admissibility conditions are monotone in D λ_j ≠ 0 for every j; terms with λ_j = 0 are deleted beforehand, and their coefficients do not enter B*

**Proof route.**

- Ĉ(n) ≥ C_1(n, κ): Real.exp_one_lt_d9 gives e < e⁺, (s⁺)² ≥ n gives n^{3.5} = n³√n ≤ n³s⁺, and each argument of the minimum is monotone in e and in n^{3.5}; the maximum over κ ∈ {1, 2} covers both fields K ⊆ ℝ and K ⊄ ℝ.
- Degree monotonicity: if [K : ℚ] = D′ ≤ D then A_j ≥ D·h(α_j) ≥ D′·h(α_j), so the A_j satisfy Matveev's (2.4) for D′, and C_1·D′²·log(eD′) ≤ Ĉ(n)·D²·(1 + ℓ⁺) because log(eD′) = 1 + Real.log D′ ≤ 1 + ℓ⁺.
- Admissibility uses NumberField.absLogHeight₁ α_j ≤ h_j⁺ (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure with DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow) and |λ_j| ≤ |λ_j|⁺ (ED.2/logarithm-enclosure).

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.MatveevConstantCertificate` (structure): Data n, D, A : Fin n → ℚ, s⁺, ℓ⁺, c with the rational inequalities of the statement as fields: 16/100 ≤ A j, n ≤ s⁺², Real.log D ≤ ℓ⁺, Ĉ(n)·D²·(1 + ℓ⁺)·∏ A j ≤ c.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.MatveevConstantCertificate.matveevBound` (data): The rational c, used as C_7 in Tzanakis–de Weger's Lemma 2.3 with C_8 = 1.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.MatveevConstantCertificate.Admissible` (relation): For K, σ, D-bounded degree, α : Fin n → Kˣ and λ : Fin n → ℂ with λ j ≠ 0 and Complex.exp (λ j) = σ (α j): D·absLogHeight₁ (α j) ≤ A j and ‖λ j‖ ≤ A j for all j.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.MatveevConstantCertificate.matveevC1_le` (characterisation): For κ ∈ {1, 2}: min{κ⁻¹(exp 1·n/2)^κ·30^{n+3}·n^{3.5}, 2^{6n+20}} ≤ Ĉ(n).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.MatveevConstantCertificate.admissible_of_le_degree` (other): Admissibility for a degree bound D implies admissibility for every D′ ≥ D after replacing A_j by D′A_j/D and c accordingly.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.MatveevConstantCertificate.ofHeightBounds` (constructor): From height certificates h_j⁺, logarithm enclosures |λ_j|⁺ and a precision, the certificate with A_j := max(D·h_j⁺, |λ_j|⁺, 16/100) and the least dyadic c at the requested precision satisfying the inequality.

**Tests.**

- `matveev_two_logs` (computation): For n = 2, D = 1, ℓ⁺ = 0, s⁺ = 1415/1000, A = (7/10, 11/10) (admissible for α = (2, 3) and real logarithms, since Real.log 2 < 0.7 and Real.log 3 < 1.1): c = 8·10⁸ is accepted and c = 7·10⁸ is rejected (the least admissible c is ≈ 7.83·10⁸).
- `matveev_one_log` (degenerate): For n = 1, D = 1, ℓ⁺ = 0, s⁺ = 1: Ĉ(1) = e⁺/2·30⁴ ≈ 1.1009·10⁶ (the κ = 1 value dominates).
- `matveev_small_A` (non-example): A family with A_1 = 1/10 (below Matveev's floor 0.16) is not a certificate. For the root of unity α_1 = exp(2πi/100) with λ_1 = 2πi/100 one has D·h(α_1) = 0 and |λ_1| < 1/10, so a definition omitting the floor 16/100 ≤ A_j would accept A_1 = 1/10, where Corollary 2.3 does not apply.
- `matveev_kappa` (compatibility): For n ≥ 2, (1/2)(en/2)² ≥ en/2, so Ĉ(n) equals the κ = 2 value: the certificate never undercuts Matveev's constant for non-real fields.

**Acceptance.** The certificate with n = 2, D = 1, A = (7/10, 11/10), c = 8·10⁸ is accepted; with c = 7·10⁸ it is rejected. Citing Matveev's name supplies no number: every admissible certificate carries its rational c and the checks that bound C_1(n, κ)·D²·log(eD)·∏A_j by it.

Corollary 2.3 with C_1(n) = C_1(n, κ) = min{κ^{−1}(en/2)^κ 30^{n+3} n^{3.5}, 2^{6n+20}} and the permitted B* substitution; the text layer drops the nonzero condition and the formula layout, which were read on p. 1219 of the PDF. The certificate evaluates this constant in rational arithmetic. `tzanakis-de-weger-1989` — §II.2, Lemma 2.3 and Appendix II, p. 110. TdW use Waldschmidt's bound (Acta Arith. 37 (1980), their reference [30]) with constants C_7, C_8 computed in their Appendix II; this node replaces that input by Matveev's Corollary 2.3 (imported from DT.3) with C_7 := c and C_8 := 1.

<a id="ED-2-certified-linear-form-lower-bound"></a>

### Certified lower bound for a linear form in logarithms

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-linear-form-lower-bound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.MatveevConstantCertificate.log_abs_linearForm_gt` · implementation unchecked.

Let c be the value of a MatveevConstantCertificate for (n, D) (ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant) admissible for a number field K with σ : K →+* ℂ and [K : ℚ] ≤ D, α_1, …, α_n ∈ K^× and nonzero logarithms λ_1, …, λ_n (exp λ_j = σ(α_j)). Then for every b ∈ ℤ^n with Λ := b_1λ_1 + ⋯ + b_nλ_n ≠ 0: Real.log |Λ| > −c·(1 + Real.log B*), B* := max_j |b_j| ≥ 1; equivalently |Λ| > exp(−c(1 + Real.log B*)). In Tzanakis–de Weger's notation (Lemma 2.3): |Λ| > exp(−C_7(log A + C_8)) with C_7 := c, C_8 := 1, A := B*.

**Hypotheses.** Λ ≠ 0 (nothing is claimed for Λ = 0; nonvanishing is proved separately in each application, never inferred from a numerical enclosure near 0) Admissibility of the certificate for (K, σ, α, λ)

**Proof route.**

- Let D′ := [K : ℚ] ≤ D. By admissibility and the monotonicity step of ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant, A_j ≥ max{D′h(α_j), |λ_j|, 0.16}.
- Apply DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/matveev-corollary-linear-form-bound to σ(K) ⊆ ℂ, σ(α_j), λ_j and b, with B* in place of B: Real.log |Λ| > −C_1(n, κ)·D′²·A_1⋯A_n·log(eD′)·log(eB*).
- Bound C_1(n, κ)·D′²·log(eD′)·∏A_j ≤ c by the certificate inequality and log(eB*) = 1 + Real.log B*.

**Acceptance.** For α = (2, 3) with real logarithms, n = 2, D = 1 and c = 8·10⁸: every (b_1, b_2) ≠ (0, 0) satisfies |b_1 log 2 + b_2 log 3| > exp(−8·10⁸(1 + log max(|b_1|, |b_2|))) (Λ ≠ 0 because 2^{b_1}3^{b_2} ≠ 1 by unique factorisation).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/matveev-corollary-linear-form-bound`.

**Sources.** `matveev-linear-forms-2000` — §2, Corollary 2.3, p. 1219. The form with B* = max|b_j| is the one used here; the text-layer garbles the conclusion ln|Λ| > −C_1(n)D²Ω ln(eD) ln(eB), read on the page.

<a id="ED-2-certified-padic-linear-form-constant"></a>

### Certified evaluation of Yu's p-adic constant

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-padic-linear-form-constant` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.YuConstantCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

Fix n ≥ 2, a degree bound d ≥ 1 and a prime p. A YuConstantCertificate for (n, d, p) consists of rationals h_1, …, h_n, a rational λ_p⁻ with 0 < λ_p⁻ ≤ Real.log p and λ_p⁻ ≤ h_j for all j (ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds enclosure of Real.log p), a rational L⁺ ≥ Real.log(10·n·d·h′) with h′ := max(h_1, …, h_n, 1), and a rational Φ⁺ satisfying the exact rational inequality Φ⁺ ≥ 22000·(9.5(n + 1)d)^{2(n+1)}·(λ_p⁻)^{−(n+1)}·(p^d − 1)·h_1⋯h_n·L⁺, which dominates Yu's Φ = 22000·(9.5(n+1)d/√(log p))^{2(n+1)}·(p^{f_𝔭} − 1)·h_1⋯h_n·log(10ndh′) for every prime 𝔭 above p (f_𝔭 ≤ d). It is admissible for nonzero algebraic numbers α_1, …, α_n generating a number field of degree at most d when h_j ≥ h_j⁺ ≥ NumberField.absLogHeight₁ α_j (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure, converted by h = Real.log(mulHeight₁)/[K : ℚ] (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow) and the upper end of ED.2/logarithm-enclosure), h_j ≥ |log α_j|⁺/10 (ED.2/logarithm-enclosure, principal logarithm; the factor 1/(10d) of Yu is replaced by 1/10, which is admissible for every d ≥ 1) and h_j ≥ λ_p⁻ is replaced by the requirement h_j ≥ ℓ_p⁺ for the upper end ℓ_p⁺ of the enclosure of Real.log p. The value used downstream is Φ⁺: for b ∈ ℤ^n ∖ {0} with α^b ≠ 1, the p-adic valuation v_p (normalised by v_p(p) = 1) of α^b − 1 under any embedding into a finite extension of ℚ_p satisfies v_p(α^b − 1) < Φ⁺·Real.log(d·max(|b_1|, …, |b_n|, 3)) (ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound). For α_j ∈ ℚ this specialises to d = 1, f_𝔭 = 1, h_j ≥ max(log H(α_j), |log α_j|/10, log p), the form of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/yu-p-adic-lower-bound.

**Hypotheses.** n ≥ 2 (Yu's statement; a single p-adic unit is handled by DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/one-term-p-adic-lower-bound or by adjoining a second term with zero coefficient) The α_j are nonzero and α_1^{b_1}⋯α_n^{b_n} ≠ 1 in the application; the constant itself is pure rational arithmetic

**Proof route.**

- Monotonicity in the residue degree: p^{f_𝔭} − 1 ≤ p^d − 1 since f_𝔭 ≤ [ℚ(α) : ℚ] ≤ d (Yu remarks the same on p. 242).
- (√(log p))^{2(n+1)} = (log p)^{n+1} ≥ (λ_p⁻)^{n+1}; d ↦ (9.5(n+1)d)^{2(n+1)} and d ↦ log(10ndh′) are increasing, so the certificate dominates Φ computed with the true degree.
- The hypotheses h_j ≥ max(h(α_j), |log α_j|/(10d_0), log p) of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/yu-explicit-p-adic-bound for the true degree d_0 ≤ d follow from h_j ≥ h_j⁺, h_j ≥ |log α_j|⁺/10 and h_j ≥ ℓ_p⁺.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.YuConstantCertificate` (structure): Data n, d, p, h : Fin n → ℚ, λ_p⁻, L⁺, Φ⁺ with the rational inequalities of the statement as fields.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.YuConstantCertificate.yuBound` (data): The rational Φ⁺.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.YuConstantCertificate.Admissible` (relation): For α : Fin n → K with [K : ℚ] ≤ d: absLogHeight₁ (α j) ≤ h j, ‖Complex.log (σ (α j))‖ ≤ 10·h j and Real.log p ≤ h j.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.YuConstantCertificate.yuPhi_le` (characterisation): Yu's Φ for any prime 𝔭 of ℚ(α) above p, computed with the true degree, is at most Φ⁺.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.YuConstantCertificate.ofHeightBounds` (constructor): From height certificates, logarithm enclosures and a precision, the certificate with h_j := max(h_j⁺, |log α_j|⁺/10, ℓ_p⁺) and the least dyadic Φ⁺ at that precision.

**Tests.**

- `yu_rational_two_primes` (computation): For n = 2, d = 1, p = 5, α = (2, 3) and h = (ℓ₅⁺, ℓ₅⁺) with ℓ₅⁺ ≥ Real.log 5 (both heights log 2, log 3 are below log 5): Φ⁺ ≥ 22000·(28.5)^6·(log 5)^{−3}·4·(log 5)²·log(20·log 5) ≈ 1.017·10^{14}, and the certificate is rejected for Φ⁺ = 10^{14}.
- `yu_degree_one` (degenerate): For d = 1 the residue factor is p − 1 (f_𝔭 = 1), so the certificate for rationals uses p − 1 and not p² − 1.
- `yu_unit_requirement` (non-example): The certificate is not admissible with h_j = 7/10 (≥ Real.log 2) at p = 5 for α_j = 2: the condition h_j ≥ log p fails, and a definition omitting it would undercut Yu's hypothesis.
- `yu_compat_rat` (compatibility): For rationals the certified Φ⁺ yields a constant C = 2Φ⁺ log p with |α^b − 1|_p ≥ (eB)^{−C}, the form of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/yu-p-adic-lower-bound.

**Acceptance.** For p = 5, n = 2, d = 1, α = (2, 3): the least admissible Φ⁺ at precision 2^{−20} exceeds 10^{14}, and the certificate records it as an exact rational. The p-adic source (Yu 1994) is registered separately from the archimedean one (Matveev 2000).

**Direct prerequisites.** `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/yu-explicit-p-adic-bound`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/yu-p-adic-lower-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/logarithm-enclosure`.

**Sources.** `yu-p-adic-logarithms-1994` — §0.1, p. 242 (bound read on the page image; the text layer drops the displayed formulas). The display that follows is Ξ < Φ log(dB) with B = max(|b_1|, …, |b_n|, 3) and Φ = 22000(9.5(n+1)d/√log p)^{2(n+1)}(p^{f_𝔭} − 1)h_1⋯h_n log(10ndh′), h′ = max(h_n, 1) (Yu orders h_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ h_n); Ξ = ord_𝔭(α_1^{b_1}⋯α_n^{b_n} − 1). `yu-p-adic-logarithms-1994` — §0.1, p. 242. Yu's own remark p^{f_𝔭} − 1 ≤ p^d − 1 (relation symbols lost in the text layer), used for the residue-degree bound.

**Consumers.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, the p-adic bound for the Thue–Mahler exponents: the p-adic logarithmic-form bound for ord_𝔭 of X − θY divided by its S-unit part. de Weger 1989, the S-unit chapter: ord_p(z) for x + y = z is bounded by a p-adic linear form in the logarithms of the other primes of S. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-initial-bounds: the initial bound for the p-adic exponents. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-initial-bounds: the initial bound for the prime exponents z_i.

<a id="ED-2-certified-padic-lower-bound"></a>

### Certified upper bound for the p-adic valuation of a multiplicative form

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.YuConstantCertificate.padicValuation_lt` · implementation unchecked.

Let Φ⁺ be the value of a YuConstantCertificate for (n, d, p) (ED.2/certified-padic-linear-form-constant) admissible for nonzero algebraic numbers α_1, …, α_n of a number field K, [K : ℚ] ≤ d, and let ι : K → L be a field embedding into a finite extension L of ℚ_p, with v_p the valuation of L normalised by v_p(p) = 1. Then for every b ∈ ℤ^n ∖ {0} with α_1^{b_1}⋯α_n^{b_n} ≠ 1: v_p(ι(α_1^{b_1}⋯α_n^{b_n}) − 1) < Φ⁺·Real.log(d·max(|b_1|, …, |b_n|, 3)). For α_j ∈ ℚ the valuation is padicValRat p.

**Hypotheses.** b ≠ 0 and α^b ≠ 1 (nonvanishing of α^b − 1 is part of the hypothesis; it is proved structurally in each application) Admissibility of the certificate

**Proof route.**

- The prime 𝔭 of ℚ(α_1, …, α_n) induced by ι lies above p; v_p(ι(x)) = ord_𝔭(x)/e_𝔭 ≤ ord_𝔭(x) for x ≠ 0 with ord_𝔭(x) ≥ 0, and the claim is trivial when v_p(ι(α^b) − 1) ≤ 0.
- DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/yu-explicit-p-adic-bound gives ord_𝔭(α^b − 1) < Φ·log(d_0B) with the true degree d_0 ≤ d; Φ ≤ Φ⁺ by the certificate and log(d_0B) ≤ log(dB).

**Acceptance.** For p = 7 and α = (2, 3) ∈ ℚ², with a certificate admissible for (n, d) = (2, 1): for every (b_1, b_2) ≠ 0, padicValRat 7 (2^{b_1}3^{b_2} − 1) < Φ⁺·log max(|b_1|, |b_2|, 3); e.g. (b_1, b_2) = (1, 2) gives padicValRat 7 (17) = 0 and (3, −1) gives padicValRat 7 (8/3 − 1) = 0, while 2³ − 1 = 7 gives valuation 1, all below the bound.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-padic-linear-form-constant`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/yu-explicit-p-adic-bound`; `mathlib:padicValRat`.

**Sources.** `yu-p-adic-logarithms-1994` — §0.1, p. 241. Yu's setting (the text layer prints 'p' for both p and 𝔭); the conclusion Ξ < Φ log(dB) is on p. 242.

<a id="ED-2-padic-logarithm-enclosure"></a>

### Certified p-adic logarithm values with explicit tails

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/padic-logarithm-enclosure` · construction · `` · implementation unchecked.

Use the existing principal-unit logarithm on L=K_v and a fixed branch value log(π); do not reconstruct local-field logarithm theory. Write ord(π)=1 and e=ord(p). For a deep unit z with d≤ord(z-1), where d is a positive rational satisfying d>e/(p-1), let S_N(z)=Σ_{1≤k≤N}(-1)^(k+1)(z-1)^k/k. Then ord(log(z)-S_N(z))≥ceil(d+N(d-e/(p-1))). If z=1 the sum and logarithm are exactly0. A finite certificate records a power M≥1, an exact unit u and z=u^M with certified depth d, and finite scalar enclosures for the partial sum. Since log(u)=log(z)/M, dividing the final enclosure loses ord(M)=e·v_p(M) digits. For arbitrary x=π^a u, add a·log(π) with the branch enclosure and ED.0 precision laws. For Q_p use M=p-1 at odd p and M=2 at p=2 for any unit; for a finite extension with residue cardinality q use M=(q-1)p^h with a supplied proof of deep containment. Such an h exists by continuity/powering on principal units (torsion that becomes1 uses the exact-zero branch). The tail bound grows without limit; dense exact centres and ED.0 finite-expression precision therefore give rational/algebraic ball certificates of any requested precision. For minimum nonzero pivot-log valuation s, evaluate to precision m+s and apply ED.0/padic-precision-propagation to obtain all normalized coefficients modulo π^m. The theorem proves existence and soundness of adequate evaluations; a pre-existing oracle for log values or an assumption that an S-unit solution list is exhaustive is not a hypothesis.

**Hypotheses.** p is prime; the local field, exact dense embedding and normalized valuation are fixed. For the displayed uniform tail choose d>e/(p-1); ord(z-1)>0 alone does not justify this linear bound. The normalized-log lattice is used only after the pivot log is proved nonzero and all basis/valuation comparison data for its coordinates are supplied. A chosen branch log(π) is fixed for ED.4/ED.6. ED.2 units and ratios use only the principal-unit logarithm and have no branch ambiguity.

**Proof route.**

- Import principal-unit series convergence, multiplicativity and continuity from the local-field logarithm owner. Current TauCeti.NumberTheory.LocalField.Logarithm already proves the HasSum and deep-unit isometry; these are reuse, not targets of this node.
- For k≥1, v_p(k)≤(k-1)/(p-1). Thus ord((z-1)^k/k)≥kd-e(k-1)/(p-1). For k>N, this is≥d+N(d-e/(p-1)); ultrametric closedness gives the same bound for the whole tail.
- Use ED.0/padic-precision-propagation on the N-term expression, subtract the certified error, and divide by M with the explicit loss ord(M). Handle z=1 separately.
- Power u^(q-1) is a principal unit. Repeated p-powers reach a deep unit or become1; use the binomial valuation bound min(pd,d+e), including equality/cancellation as a lower bound, and continuity. No operation count is asserted.
- For every requested m choose N so ceil(d+N(d-e/(p-1)))-ord(M)≥m, choose finite expression precision≥m+ord(M), and refine the input balls sufficiently. Apply the pivot quotient theorem before constructing ED.1 residues.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.PadicLogEvaluationCertificate` (structure): The actual local field/branch, unit, deep power, partial-sum centres, scalar error precisions and certified tail/power-division budget.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.padicLogPartialSum` (data): The finite sum Σ_{1≤k≤N}(-1)^(k+1)(z-1)^k/k.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.padicLog_tail_precision` (other): The normalized uniformizer valuation of the tail is≥ceil(d+N(d-e/(p-1))) under d>e/(p-1).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.PadicLogEvaluationCertificate.sound` (characterisation): The true logarithm lies in the displayed ball, including the ord(M) division loss.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.PadicLogEvaluationCertificate.exists_precision` (constructor): Every unit has a logarithm ball at every integer absolute precision, using a deep power and the explicit tail bound.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.PadicLogEvaluationCertificate.ofPower` (compatibility): For z=u^M divide its logarithm enclosure by M and lose e·v_p(M) uniformizer digits.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.PadicLogEvaluationCertificate.normalized_residues` (other): At a nonzero minimal pivot of valuation s, log precision m+s gives normalized lattice coefficient precision m.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.PadicLogEvaluationCertificate.rootOfUnity` (simp): A unit killed by the chosen power has logarithm0, with an exact zero certificate.

**Tests.**

- `padic_log_three_four` (computation): In Q_3, z=4, d=1,N=4: S_4=3-9/2+27/3-81/4=-51/4 and the tail has valuation≥ceil(1+4/2)=3.
- `padic_log_two_five` (computation): In Q_2, z=5,d=2,N=4: the tail valuation is≥6. For u=-5 use M=2,z=25,d=3 and subtract1 digit after division by2.
- `padic_log_torsion` (degenerate): log_3(-1)=0 via M=2, and log_2(-1)=0 via M=2; the exact power1 branch has zero tail.
- `padic_log_shallow_rejected` (non-example): At p=2,e=1,z=3 one has depth1; d=1 fails the strict deep-unit hypothesis, so the displayed linear tail budget cannot be used directly. Squaring gives9 of depth3.
- `padic_log_ramification` (compatibility): At e=2,p=3,d=2,N=5 the tail bound is7; division by a power M divisible by3 loses2 digits per factor3.
- `padic_log_enumeration_precision` (characterisation): For desired normalized precision7 and pivot valuation2, provide log enclosures at absolute precision9; precision7 before division is insufficient.

**Acceptance.** In Q_3, z=4, d=1,N=4: S_4=3-9/2+27/3-81/4=-51/4 and the tail has valuation≥ceil(1+4/2)=3. In Q_2, z=5,d=2,N=4: the tail valuation is≥6. For u=-5 use M=2,z=25,d=3 and subtract1 digit after division by2. log_3(-1)=0 via M=2, and log_2(-1)=0 via M=2; the exact power1 branch has zero tail.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-precision-propagation`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/valuation-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate`; `ColemanIntegration:L0`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — §2.3 pp.28–29; §2.5 pp.33–34; §3.13 Lemma3.17 p.67. The principal-unit series and powering identity give the evaluation route; ED makes the omitted error budget an explicit tail inequality and tracks division precision.

**Consumers.** de Weger §3.13, Lemma3.17; TdW1992 §§10–15: The finite p-adic coefficients used by the reduction lattice are approximations to actual logarithms with a proved precision budget.. ED.2/thue-mahler-certificate and s-unit-certificate: Adequate scalar log precision exists by this theorem; exhaustive enumeration is deduced from bounds and reduction, not assumed as an oracle output..
