<a id="ED-2-thue-mahler-equation"></a>

### Thue–Mahler equations and their normalised solution sets

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-equation` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.thueMahlerSolutions` · implementation unchecked.

A Thue–Mahler equation is given by g ∈ ℤ[X] with n := g.natDegree ≥ 3, irreducible over ℚ, leading coefficient f_0, an integer c ≠ 0 and distinct primes p_1, …, p_v (v ≥ 0; Tzanakis–de Weger take v ≥ 1, and v = 0 is the Thue equation F(X, Y) = c with normalised solutions) with gcd(c, p_1⋯p_v) = 1; with F := Polynomial.homogenize g n its normalised solution set is thueMahlerSolutions g c p := {(X, Y, z) ∈ ℤ × ℤ × ℕ^v : gcd(X, Y) = 1, gcd(Y, f_0) = 1, F(X, Y) = c·p_1^{z_1}⋯p_v^{z_v}}. The conditions gcd(X, Y) = 1 (essential: otherwise (kX, kY) with k a product of the p_i gives infinitely many solutions) and gcd(Y, f_0) = 1 are part of the definition; the second is automatic when f_0 = ±1. The equation with right side −c·∏p_i^{z_i} is the instance (g, −c, p). With x := f_0X, y := Y, θ := f_0ξ (ξ the class of X in K := ℚ[X]/(g)), the equation becomes N_{K/ℚ}(x − yθ) = f_0^{n−1}c·∏p_i^{z_i} with gcd(x, y) = 1, and θ is a root of the monic G := integralNormalization g (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/thue-equation-monic-reduction). The set is finite (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/thue-mahler-effective-finiteness); this stage certifies it exactly (ED.2/thue-mahler-certified-solution-set).

**Hypotheses.** n ≥ 3, irreducibility, c ≠ 0, the p_i distinct primes not dividing c Solutions are triples with coprime (X, Y) and gcd(Y, f_0) = 1; the exponents z_i are natural numbers

**Proof route.**

- F(x, y) = c∏p_i^{z_i} ⟺ f_0·N(X − Yξ) = c∏p_i^{z_i}, since f_0∏_i(X − Yξ^{(i)}) = F(X, Y).
- N(f_0X − Yθ) = f_0^n N(X − Yξ) = f_0^{n−1}·F(X, Y); gcd(f_0X, Y) divides gcd(f_0, Y)·gcd(X, Y) = 1 under the two coprimality conditions, and conversely gcd(f_0X, Y) = 1 gives both conditions.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.thueMahlerSolutions` (constructor): thueMahlerSolutions g c p : Set (ℤ × ℤ × (Fin v → ℕ)) as in the statement.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.mem_thueMahlerSolutions` (characterisation): (X, Y, z) ∈ thueMahlerSolutions g c p ↔ IsCoprime X Y ∧ IsCoprime Y f_0 ∧ thueForm g X Y = c·∏ p_i^{z_i}.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.thueMahlerSolutions_monic` (equivalence): (X, Y, z) is a solution iff (x, y) = (f_0X, Y) is coprime with N(x − yθ) = f_0^{n−1}c∏p_i^{z_i} and f_0 ∣ x.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerEquation` (structure): Bundled g, c, p with the hypotheses of the statement.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.thueMahlerSolutions_finite` (other): The set is finite (DT.4/thue-mahler-effective-finiteness).

**Tests.**

- `thueMahler_cubic` (computation): For g = X³ − 2, c = 1, p = (5): (X, Y, z) = (1, 0, 0) and (−1, −1, 0) are solutions, and (3, 1, 2) is one since 27 − 2 = 25 = 5².
- `thueMahler_noncoprime` (non-example): (5, 0, ·) is not a solution for g = X³ − 2, c = 1, p = (5) although 5³ = 5³: gcd(5, 0) = 5 ≠ 1; dropping coprimality makes the set infinite ((5^k, 0, 3k)).
- `thueMahler_v_zero_compat` (compatibility): The triples with z = 0 are exactly the coprime solutions (with gcd(Y, f_0) = 1) of the Thue equation F(X, Y) = c (ED.2/thue-equation).
- `thueMahler_sign` (degenerate): For c = −1 the instance (g, −1, p) is a different equation; for g = X³ − 2 it contains (1, 1, 0) since 1 − 2 = −1.
- `thueMahler_nonprimitive_zero_primes` (non-example): (2,0) solves X³−2Y³=8 but is excluded by coprimality in the zero-primes normalized equation.

**Acceptance.** (3, 1, 2) ∈ thueMahlerSolutions (X³ − 2) 1 (5), since 3³ − 2 = 5².

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-equation`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/thue-mahler-effective-finiteness`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/thue-equation-monic-reduction`; `mathlib:Polynomial.homogenize`; `mathlib:Polynomial.integralNormalization`.

**Sources.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §1, (1)–(2), p. 223. The equation F(X, Y) = c·p_1^{z_1}⋯p_v^{z_v}; the text layer prints '&#x3E;' for '≥'. The normalisation (X, Y) = (Y, f_0) = 1 is TdW's (2). `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §2, pp. 225–226. The passage to x = f_0X, y = Y, θ = f_0ξ and the inputs (an order containing θ, its fundamental units).

**Consumers.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, (1): the equation solved by the method. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-certified-solution-set: the set certified exactly. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6: worked Thue–Mahler examples. Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §§1Ex–18Ex: the example x³ − 23x²y + 5xy² + 24y³ = ±2^{z_1}3^{z_2}5^{z_3}7^{z_4}.

**Revision notes.** v=0 identifies normalized coprime Thue solutions only. For X³−2Y³=8, (2,0) is a Thue solution but not normalized. This is not an all-solutions reduction.

<a id="ED-2-prime-ideal-removing-lemma"></a>

### The Prime Ideal Removing Lemma

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/prime-ideal-removing-lemma` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.prime_ideal_removing` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, let θ be an algebraic integer of degree n with minimal polynomial G ∈ ℤ[t] and discriminant D_θ, K = ℚ(θ), p a prime, G = G_1⋯G_m the factorisation into monic irreducibles over ℚ_p, 𝔭_i the prime of K above p corresponding to G_i, with ramification index e_i and residue degree d_i (e_id_i = deg G_i), θ_i^{(1)}, …, θ_i^{(n_i)} the roots of G_i in ℂ_p, ord_p the valuation of ℂ_p with ord_p(p) = 1, e := max_i e_i. Let x, y ∈ ℤ with gcd(x, y) = 1. (i) For every pair i ≠ j there is at most one 𝔭 ∈ {𝔭_i, 𝔭_j} with ord_𝔭(x − yθ) > max(e_i, e_j)·ord_p(θ_i^{(k)} − θ_j^{(l)}) (any k, l). (ii) If d_i > 1 or e_i > 1, then ord_{𝔭_i}(x − yθ) ≤ e_i·ord_p(θ_i^{(k)} − θ_i^{(l)}) for any k ≠ l. Corollary: there is at most one 𝔭_i above p with ord_{𝔭_i}(x − yθ) > ½e·ord_p(D_θ), and it has d_i = e_i = 1; if p ∤ D_θ, at most one 𝔭_i above p divides x − yθ, and it has d_i = e_i = 1. Consequently the ideal (x − yθ) factors as 𝔞·𝔟·𝔭_1^{u_1}⋯𝔭_v^{u_v} with 𝔭_i a prime of degree one above p_i, 𝔞 of absolute ideal norm |f_0^{n−1}c|, 𝔟 supported on the other primes above the p_i with exponents bounded by (i) (at the other degree-one primes) and (ii) (at the primes with d_i > 1 or e_i > 1), and u_i + ord_{p_i}(N𝔟) = z_i, for finitely many explicit choices (TdW (9)).

**Hypotheses.** gcd(x, y) = 1 is essential (it gives ord_p(x − yθ_i^{(k)}) = 0 when p ∣ y) Orders of ℂ_p-elements are rational; the bounds are computed from finitely many p-adic root approximations (ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate) and are exact rationals The prime ideals above each listed rational prime, their e/f values, and factorizations of the finitely many coefficient/difference ideals are supplied with exact ideal equalities and valuation comparisons in the actual completions. No prime-ideal factorization procedure is a target.

**Proof route.**

- (i): if (x − yθ) = 𝔭_i^{v_i}𝔭_j^{v_j}𝔞 then ord_p(x − yθ_i^{(k)}) = v_i/e_i through the embedding K → K_{𝔭_i} → ℂ_p, similarly for j; hence ord_p(y(θ_i^{(k)} − θ_j^{(l)})) ≥ min(v_i, v_j)/max(e_i, e_j), and ord_p(y) = 0 (if p ∣ y then p ∤ x and both orders vanish) (TdW pp. 231–232).
- (ii): if deg G_i > 1 take two roots k ≠ l of G_i; both x − yθ_i^{(k)} and x − yθ_i^{(l)} have order v/e_i and the same argument applies.
- Corollaries: ord_p(D_θ) ≥ 2·ord_p(θ^{(h)} − θ^{(l)}) for all h ≠ l, so (8) implies the hypothesis of the first corollary; part (i) of the first corollary gives uniqueness and part (ii) gives d_i = e_i = 1 (TdW pp. 232–233; see sourceIssues EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E8 for the reference to part (i)).
- The finite ideal enumeration uses absolute ideal norms, so the fixed norm is |f0^(n−1)c| for either sign of c. Its prime/exponent labels and principal-element reconstruction are distinct obligations; the unramified uniqueness helper proves neither the ramified bounds nor the finite factorization consequence.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.prime_ideal_removing_unramified` (other): Supporting third-corollary uniqueness only: for a primitive integral θ whose minimal polynomial is squarefree mod p and coprime x,y, the nonzero prime ideals above p containing x−yθ form a subsingleton.

**Acceptance.** TdW 5^Ex: for G of the example and p = 5, ord_5(D_θ) = 2 and three degree-one primes above 5; the lemma leaves the five forms 𝔭_{21}^{n_1}𝔭_{31}^{n_2}𝔭_{5j}^{n_3}𝔭_{71}^{n_4}·(bounded) listed on p. 233. If p ∤ D_θ then at most one prime above p divides x − yθ: for G = t³ − 2 and p = 5 (5 ∤ D = −108), x − y∛2 is divisible by at most one prime above 5.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/valuation-certificate`; `mathlib:padicValRat`; `mathlib:Polynomial.integralNormalization`.

**Sources.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §5, Lemma 1 and its corollaries, pp. 230–233. Lemma 1 (i), (ii), the first, second and third corollaries and their proofs, read on the page images (the formulas (5)–(8) are lost in the text layer). `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §6, (9), p. 233. The ideal equation (x − yθ) = 𝔞𝔟𝔭_1^{u_1}⋯𝔭_v^{u_v} with N𝔞 = f_0^{n−1}c.

<a id="ED-2-thue-mahler-s-unit-covering"></a>

### Thue–Mahler S-unit coverings

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-s-unit-covering` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCovering` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, let (g, c, p) be a Thue–Mahler equation (ED.2/thue-mahler-equation), θ = f_0ξ, 𝒪 an order of K containing θ, r := s + t − 1. A Thue–Mahler S-unit covering consists of units ε_1, …, ε_r of 𝒪 and a finite list of cases, each case being (α, π_1, …, π_v, h, s′, t′) with α ∈ 𝒪 ∖ {0}, π_i ∈ 𝒪 generating 𝔭_i^{h_i} for a prime 𝔭_i of degree one above p_i (or π_i := 1, h_i := 0 and s′_i := 0 when there is none, and then the representation is normalized to n_i = 0 in (C)), for active primes integers h_i ≥ 1, 0 ≤ s′_i < h_i and t′_i ≥ 0, such that: (U) every unit of 𝒪 is ζ∏ε_i^{a_i} with ζ a root of unity of K (ζ = ±1 when s ≥ 1); (C) for every (X, Y, z) ∈ thueMahlerSolutions g c p, with x = f_0X, y = Y, there are a case, a ∈ ℤ^r and n ∈ ℕ^v with x − yθ = ±α·ε_1^{a_1}⋯ε_r^{a_r}·π_1^{n_1}⋯π_v^{n_v} (TdW (11)) and z_i = n_ih_i + s′_i + t′_i (TdW (10)); roots of unity other than ±1 are absorbed into the finitely many α. The conditions are input hypotheses of the certificate; for 𝒪 = 𝓞_K they are discharged by the Prime Ideal Removing Lemma (ED.2/prime-ideal-removing-lemma) and the ideal factorisations of f_0^{n−1}c and of the p_i (the supplied exact prime-ideal-factorization identities), principal generators of 𝔞𝔟𝔭_1^{s′_1}⋯𝔭_v^{s′_v} and of 𝔭_i^{h_i}, and the unit certificate the explicit full-unit-generation hypothesis; DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-integral-divisor-representation shows that a finite list of cases always exists. The Lean record fixes r = Units.rank K, excludes zero α and π in every case, and records either h_i=0,π_i=1,s′_i=0 or h_i>0,s′_i<h_i. Inactive exponents are normalized to zero by the representation theorem.

**Hypotheses.** The class number is not needed: any h_i with 𝔭_i^{h_i} principal works (TdW p. 226) (C) is a statement about all normalised solutions; it is not checked by computation inside the certificate Exactly rank(K) unit generators; every case has nonzero α and π_i, with positive active class orders and bounded remainders. A supplied complete unit family, complete finite divisor/principal-ideal representative data and exact factorization/valuation equalities supply the S-unit covering. Prove the covering from these identities and the equation; do not assume the final solution list complete.

**Proof route.**

- From (9): (x − yθ) = 𝔞𝔟𝔭_1^{u_1}⋯𝔭_v^{u_v}; write u_i = h_in_i + s′_i with 0 ≤ s′_i < h_i and t′_i := ord_{p_i}(N𝔟); then (α) := 𝔞𝔟𝔭_1^{s′_1}⋯𝔭_v^{s′_v} is principal and x − yθ = unit·α·∏π_i^{n_i}.
- The unit is ±∏ε_i^{a_i} by (U); finitely many α arise because 𝔞 and 𝔟 range over finitely many ideals.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCovering` (structure): Units, the finite list of cases, and the fields units_generate and covers of the statement. Also rank_eq, α_ne_zero, π_ne_zero and case_wellformed enforce the stated rank and case conventions.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCovering.exists_repr` (characterisation): Every normalised solution has a case and exponents (a, n) with x − yθ = ±α∏ε^a∏π^n and z_i = n_ih_i + s′_i + t′_i.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCovering.ofIdealFactorization` (constructor): From prime-ideal factorisation certificates, principal generators and a unit certificate, the covering of the statement.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCovering.toThue` (compatibility): For v = 0 (no primes) a covering is a factor covering of the Thue equation F(X, Y) = c restricted to coprime solutions.

**Tests.**

- `tmCovering_example_cases` (computation): For G=X³−23X²+5X+24, θ a root in the degree-three field, ordered primes(2,3,5,7) and c=±1, set ω=(2+θ−θ²)/5; π21=22+25θ+6ω, π31=31−41θ+47ω, π51=133+150θ+36ω, π52=89+100θ+24ω, π53=111−90θ−16ω, π71=1−θ. The covering case list is exactly I:(α=1,π5=π51,t3=0), II:(1,π52,0), III:(π53,π52,1), IV:(1,π53,0), V:(π52,π53,1); all h_i=1,s_i=0, and the other π_i are π21,π31,π71 with other t_i=0. Equality of the five records, not merely list length, is asserted. This is a source-derived mathematical existence regression, not a replayed finite producer.
- `tmCovering_no_degree_one` (degenerate): When no degree-one prime is active, π_i=1 and h_i=0: the complete covering representation can be chosen with n_i=0, and z_i=s_i+t_i. The test asserts zero, not merely an unspecified exponent identity.
- `tmCovering_missing_case` (non-example): Dropping Case III (α = π_{53}, π_5 = π_{52}) from TdW's five cases loses the solution (x, y) = (399, 302), F(399, 302) = −3^{13}·5³, listed in Case III with n_3 = 2 (TdW 17Ex): 𝔭_{52}² 𝔭_{53} exactly divides its 5-part, and no other case has this shape (Cases I, II, IV omit 𝔭_{53} or 𝔭_{52}, Case V has 𝔭_{52} to the first power); the remaining list is not a covering.
- `tmCovering_compat_units` (compatibility): For 𝒪 = 𝓞_K and ε = NumberField.Units.fundSystem K condition (U) is Mathlib's NumberField.Units.exist_unique_eq_mul_prod.
- `tmCovering_redundant_units` (non-example): For Units.rank K=1, no covering has r=2; redundant unit generators cannot yield bounded exponent coordinates.
- `tmCovering_nonempty_of_solution` (characterisation): A semantic covering with an actual normalized solution has a nonempty case list. This does not prove the named missing-Case-III arithmetic regression.

**Acceptance.** TdW's five cases of 6^Ex (p. 234) form a covering of their example once (U) and (C) are certified.

### Initial bounds for the Thue–Mahler exponents from Yu's and Matveev's bounds

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-initial-bounds` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.thueMahler_exponents_le_initialBound` · implementation unchecked.

Fix a case of a Thue–Mahler S-unit covering (ED.2/thue-mahler-s-unit-covering) and put N := max_i n_i, A := max_i |a_i|, H := max(N, A). (a) p-adic step (TdW §7–8): for each l with π_l ≠ 1 let θ^{(i_0)} ∈ ℚ_{p_l} be the root corresponding to 𝔭_l and j, k two further indices (roots of two other linear factors of G over ℚ_{p_l}, or the two roots of one factor of degree ≥ 2); with δ_1 := ((θ^{(i_0)} − θ^{(j)})/(θ^{(i_0)} − θ^{(k)}))·α^{(k)}/α^{(j)}, δ_2 := ((θ^{(j)} − θ^{(k)})/(θ^{(k)} − θ^{(i_0)}))·α^{(i_0)}/α^{(j)} and λ := δ_1∏_i(π_i^{(k)}/π_i^{(j)})^{n_i}∏_i(ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)})^{a_i} − 1 = δ_2∏_i(π_i^{(i_0)}/π_i^{(j)})^{n_i}∏_i(ε_i^{(i_0)}/ε_i^{(j)})^{a_i} (TdW (12), from DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/siegel-identity), all factors of the first product are p_l-adic units and ord_{p_l}(λ) = ord_{p_l}(δ_2) + n_lh_l (TdW (13), Lemmas 2–4); λ ≠ 0 because x − yθ^{(i_0)} ≠ 0. A YuConstantCertificate (ED.2/certified-padic-linear-form-constant) for (1 + v + r, n(n − 1)(n − 2), p_l), admissible for (δ_1, π^{(k)}/π^{(j)}, ε^{(k)}/ε^{(j)}) in ℚ(θ^{(i_0)}, θ^{(j)}, θ^{(k)}) with exponent vector b = (1, n, a) ≠ 0 and α^b = 1 + λ ≠ 1, gives, through ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound, n_lh_l + ord(δ_2) < Φ⁺_l·log(n(n−1)(n−2)·max(H, 3)), hence N ≤ c_13(log H + c_14) with explicit rationals c_13, c_14. (b) Archimedean step (TdW §§9–10): with Lemma 6 (A ≤ N[U_{I_0}^{−1}]·|log|ε^{(k)}|| for a suitable k), c_15 := 1/N[U_{I_0}^{−1}] and 0 < c_16 < c_15/(n − 1): if min_i|β^{(i)}| > e^{−c_16A} then A < c_18 + c_17N (Proposition 7), where c_17, c_18 are formed as in TdW from c′_17 := Σ_i max(0, max_j log(p_i^{h_i}/|π_i^{(j)}|)), c′′_17 := Σ_i max(0, log house(π_i)) and c′_18, c′′_18 (c′_17, c′′_17 are the corrected constants of sourceIssues EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E9); otherwise (Case 3, s ≥ 1) the real or complex linear form Λ_0 := log(1 + λ_0) built at an index i_0 ≤ s with |β^{(i_0)}| ≤ e^{−c_16A} satisfies 0 < |Λ_0| < c_27·e^{−c_16A} (c_27 = 1.39c_21 resp. 1.02c_21), and a MatveevConstantCertificate for its nonzero logarithms (terms with zero logarithm deleted, degree bound n(n − 1)(n − 2)) gives through ED.2/certified-linear-form-lower-bound H ≤ c_23 + c_24 log H (resp. the complex analogue with |a_0| ≤ ½(1 + vN + rA)); for s = 0 Proposition 9 bounds A directly. (c) Combining (a), (b) and DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/log-linear-inequality-bound gives a rational K_0 with H ≤ K_0 and N ≤ N_0 for every solution in the case (TdW Theorem 10). All constants are certified rationals computed from the root boxes, the p-adic approximations and ED.2/logarithm-enclosure, and every nonvanishing (λ ≠ 0, Λ_0 ≠ 0) is proved from x − yθ^{(i)} ≠ 0.

**Hypotheses.** One case of the covering; the theorem is applied to every case TdW use Yu (Compositio 1990) and Blass–Glass–Manski–Meronk–Steiner; here the imported bounds are Yu 1994 and Matveev 2000 through the certified constants, and the BGMMS threshold restriction does not arise

**Proof route.**

- (a): the factors π_i^{(k)}/π_i^{(j)} (i ≠ l and i = l by TdW Lemma 3(i)) and ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)} are p_l-adic units (Lemma 2: an algebraic integer whose norm is prime to p has unit conjugates); ord(π_l^{(i_0)}/π_l^{(j)}) = h_l (Lemma 3(ii)) gives (13); Yu's bound for the first expression of λ bounds ord(λ), hence n_l.
- (b): Cases 1 and 2 of TdW §9 bound |ε^{(k)}| through |β^{(k)}| and the conjugates of α and π_i; the product ∏_i(p_i^{h_i}/|π_i^{(k)}|)^{n_i} is at most exp(N·Σ_i max(0, log(p_i^{h_i}/min_j|π_i^{(j)}|))) and ∏_i|π_i^{(k)}|^{n_i} ≤ exp(N·Σ_i max(0, log house(π_i))), which is where the printed c′_17, c′′_17 must be replaced.
- Case 3 follows ED.2/thue-linear-form with π-factors added: Siegel's identity at (i_0, j, k), |e^{Λ_0} − 1| < ½ and the 1.39 resp. 1.02 factors; Λ_0 ≠ 0 because β^{(i_0)} ≠ 0.
- (c): H < c_19 + c_20 log H (Proposition 8) and its Case 3 analogues; DT.4/log-linear-inequality-bound turns each into an explicit bound.

**Acceptance.** For TdW's example (using the Baker–Wüstholz constants of the1993 published correction, p.242) the initial bound is H < c_real < 9.844 × 10^{49} (TdW 11Ex); the reduction of ED.2/thue-mahler-reduced-bounds brings it to n_1 ≤ 19, n_2 ≤ 11, n_3 ≤ 8, n_4 ≤ 6, A ≤ 86 outside six exceptional solutions (TdW 17Ex). The uncorrected1992 Appendix A3 constants do not establish this initial bound: use the1993 Baker–Wüstholz route, or start at1.511×10^50 with the corrected BGMMS factor and its H≤4919 bridge (sourceIssues E29).

### p-adic and real reduction of the Thue–Mahler exponent bounds

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-reduced-bounds` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.thueMahler_exponents_le_reducedBound` · implementation unchecked.

Fix a case of a Thue–Mahler S-unit covering with initial bounds H ≤ K_0, N ≤ N_0 (ED.2/thue-mahler-initial-bounds) and let 𝒮 ⊆ ℤ^{v+r} be the set of exponent vectors (n, a) of the normalised solutions in that case, with weights W ∈ ℕ^{v+r}_{>0}. (a) p-adic step at p_l (TdW §§12–15): let 𝒪_L be ℤ_{p_l} when θ^{(i_0)}, θ^{(j)}, θ^{(k)} ∈ ℚ_{p_l} (first special case; the images of K-elements are given by EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate), or the ring of integers of the extension of ℚ_{p_l} generated by θ^{(j)}, θ^{(k)} (second special case, given by an exact model of 𝒪_L/𝔓^t), with maximal ideal 𝔓 and ramification e_L; for a PadicDiscreteLogCertificate (ED.2/padic-discrete-logarithm-certificate) at level t for γ_0 := δ_1 and the units γ := (π_i^{(k)}/π_i^{(j)})_i, (ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)})_i, every (n, a) ∈ 𝒮 with e_L·(n_lh_l + ord_{p_l}(δ_2)) ≥ t lies in the target coset Γ_0, since then δ_1∏γ^{(n,a)} ≡ 1 (mod 𝔓^t). An ED.1 p-adic reduction certificate (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-reduction) showing that Γ_0 has no point of weighted height ≤ X then gives n_l < (t/e_L − ord_{p_l}(δ_2))/h_l for every (n, a) ∈ 𝒮 with H_W ≤ X (TdW Lemma 14, Proposition 15). (b) Real step (TdW §16): with Λ_0 = ρ_0 + Σn_iλ_{0i} + Σa_iμ_{0i} (+ 2πa_0) from Case 3 and the inequality |Λ_0| < c_27 e^{−c_16A}, an ED.1 real reduction certificate (ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction, lattice from ED.1/linear-form-lattice with the enclosures of ED.2/logarithm-enclosure) gives A ≤ A_1 for every (n, a) ∈ 𝒮 in Case 3 with H_W ≤ X (Proposition 16); Cases 1–2 give A < c_18 + c_17N directly. (c) Iterating (a) for all l and (b) for all real i_0 is an exponent reduction chain (ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain), possibly with enumeration steps (TdW §17, Fincke–Pohst); its soundness gives final bounds n_i ≤ N_i, |a_i| ≤ A_fin for every (n, a) ∈ 𝒮 outside the finite exceptional sets.

**Hypotheses.** The p-adic discrete logarithm exists when the γ^e generate a cyclic subgroup of (𝒪_L/𝔓^t)^× of p-power order; in the first special case this always holds (𝒪_L = ℤ_{p_l}); in the second special case the γ are norm-one elements for the conjugation exchanging θ^{(j)} and θ^{(k)} (TdW (33)) Only the implication 'large n_l ⇒ lattice point' of TdW's Lemma 14 is used

**Proof route.**

- Generate the scalar log enclosures mathematically from ED.2/logarithm-enclosure and ED.2/padic-logarithm-enclosure, then apply ED.0/padic-precision-propagation. For pivot log valuation s, certify precision at least m+s and strict pivot precision>s before forming normalized ratios modulo π^m. Existence of adequate N is proved by the positive-slope tail estimate. A raw congruence checker does not assume completeness of the final solution list.
- (a): ord_{p_l}(λ) = ord(δ_2) + n_lh_l (TdW (13)) and λ = δ_1∏γ^{(n,a)} − 1, so ord_𝔓(δ_1∏γ^{(n,a)} − 1) = e_L·ord_{p_l}(λ) ≥ t; the certificate's soundness gives the coset membership; the ED.1 certificate excludes the coset from the box.
- (b): the lattice argument of TdW Proposition 16 is the ED.1 inhomogeneous reduction; the precision budget is the error of the integers [C·λ_{0i}], [C·μ_{0i}], [C·ρ_0] certified by the logarithm enclosures.
- (c): ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain soundness by induction over the steps.

**Acceptance.** TdW 15Ex–17Ex: alternating p-adic reductions at p = 2, 3, 5, 7 and real reductions bring the bounds to N_i of size at most a few dozen and A ≤ 86 in every case.

<a id="ED-2-auxiliary-prime-sieve"></a>

### Sieving exponent tuples with auxiliary primes

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/auxiliary-prime-sieve` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.thueMahler_sieve_congr` · implementation unchecked.

Fix a case of a Thue–Mahler S-unit covering. Let q be a prime and 𝔮_1, 𝔮_2, 𝔮_3 three distinct primes of K of degree one above q not dividing f_0·c·∏p_i·disc(θ) and not dividing α, π_i, ε_i; let m_i, A_i, P_{ij}, E_{ij} ∈ 𝔽_q be the residues of θ, α, π_j, ε_j modulo 𝔮_i. Eliminating x and y from x − ym_i ≡ ±A_i∏_jP_{ij}^{n_j}∏_jE_{ij}^{a_j} (i = 1, 2, 3) gives the congruence C_1∏_jP_{1j}^{n_j}∏_jE_{1j}^{a_j} + C_2∏_jP_{2j}^{n_j}∏_jE_{2j}^{a_j} ≡ C_3∏_jP_{3j}^{n_j}∏_jE_{3j}^{a_j} (mod q) with C_1 := (m_2 − m_3)A_1, C_2 := (m_3 − m_1)A_2, C_3 := (m_2 − m_1)A_3 (TdW (38)). Every exponent tuple (n, a) of a solution in the case satisfies this congruence for every such q. Hence a tuple violating it for one admissible q is not the tuple of a solution, and the residual box {n_i ≤ N_i, |a_i| ≤ A_fin} can be reduced to the survivors of finitely many such congruences before the exact test; the congruence depends only on (n, a) modulo the orders of the residues, so it is evaluated on residue classes.

**Hypotheses.** The sieve is a necessary condition only; survivors are tested exactly against (11) and F(X, Y) = c∏p_i^{z_i} The three primes are of degree one so that the residues lie in 𝔽_q

**Proof route.**

- Reduce x − yθ = ±α∏ε^a∏π^n modulo 𝔮_i (each element involved is 𝔮_i-integral and the 𝔮_i are distinct of degree one).
- Siegel's identity in 𝔽_q: (m_2 − m_3)(x − ym_1) + (m_3 − m_1)(x − ym_2) + (m_1 − m_2)(x − ym_3) = 0, which is the stated congruence after substitution (the common sign cancels) (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/siegel-identity, in every commutative ring).

**Acceptance.** A tuple failing (38) for one admissible q is eliminated without any exact test; TdW's final box of (N_1 + 1)⋯(N_v + 1)(2A_0 + 1)^r tuples per case is reduced by sieving before testing (TdW 18Ex).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-s-unit-covering`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/siegel-identity`; `mathlib:ZMod.pow_totient`.

**Sources.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §18, (38), pp. 275–276. The sieve with auxiliary primes q having three degree-one prime ideals; only tuples satisfying all congruences (38) are tested further.

### Thue–Mahler solution certificates

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-certificate` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

A ThueMahlerCertificate for a Thue–Mahler equation (g, c, p) (ED.2/thue-mahler-equation) consists of: an S-unit covering (ED.2/thue-mahler-s-unit-covering; its conditions (U), (C) are hypotheses of the soundness theorem); root boxes and p_l-adic root approximations of G (ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate, ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate); for every case: the certified constants and the initial bounds K_0, N_0 of ED.2/thue-mahler-initial-bounds (with their Yu and Matveev constant certificates), an exponent reduction chain with p-adic steps given by discrete-logarithm certificates and ED.1 certificates and real steps given by ED.1 certificates (ED.2/thue-mahler-reduced-bounds), the final bounds N_i, A_fin, the exceptional tuples, and a list of auxiliary primes with their residue data (ED.2/auxiliary-prime-sieve); finally the claimed list L of solutions. ThueMahlerCertificate.Valid is the conjunction of: every constant inequality, discrete-logarithm congruence and ED.1 check; every tuple of the residual box of each case either violates a listed sieve congruence or is tested exactly: the element ±α∏ε^a∏π^n is computed in power-basis coordinates, it is accepted when it equals x − yθ with x, y ∈ ℤ, f_0 ∣ x, gcd(x/f_0, y) = gcd(y, f_0) = 1, and (X, Y, z) := (x/f_0, y, (n_ih_i + s′_i + t′_i)_i) satisfies F(X, Y) = c∏p_i^{z_i}; the exceptional tuples are tested the same way; L is exactly the set of accepted triples. All checks are exact computations with integers, rationals and residue rings. This is the target raw finite format specified in suggestedOmissions. SemanticThueMahlerCertificate is the separately named mathematical summary; its Valid field contains real inequalities and universal solution implications, and has no claimed computational Decidable instance. The raw checker derives those implications from the finite transcript and supplier soundness, including all nonsolution rows.

**Hypotheses.** Finite data; a failed check proves nothing The residual box of each case is finite: (N_1 + 1)⋯(N_v + 1)·(2A_fin + 1)^r tuples

**Proof route.**

- Each check is decidable: rational inequalities, modular exponentiation, exact arithmetic in K, finite enumeration of a box.
- Separate finite check from semantic interpretation: first evaluate the full bounded transcript; then use supplier correctness and the named bound/reduction lemmas to prove the semantic summary. No proof field asserting completeness is accepted as raw data.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCertificate` (structure): The data of the statement with the claimed solutions as a Finset (ℤ × ℤ × (Fin v → ℕ)).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCertificate.Valid` (relation): The conjunction of all exact checks.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCertificate.solutions` (projection): The claimed list L.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCertificate.solutions_subset` (characterisation): Valid implies L ⊆ thueMahlerSolutions g c p.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCertificate.residualBox` (projection): For each case, the finite box of exponent tuples left after the reduction.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticThueMahlerCertificate` (structure): Supporting mathematical summary of the field/root, bounds, reductions and claimed list. It contains proof-bearing supplier/reduction data; not the raw finite certificate.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticThueMahlerCertificate.Valid` (relation): Semantic predicate including the actual real inequalities and solution implications. No finite-evaluation claim is made.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticThueMahlerCertificate.solutions` (projection): The list stored in the supporting semantic record.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticThueMahlerCertificate.solutions_subset` (characterisation): Semantic validity implies that every listed point satisfies the actual equation.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticThueMahlerCertificate.residualBox` (projection): The per-case residual exponent box stored in the supporting semantic record.

**Tests.**

- `tmCert_listed_solution` (characterisation): For g = X³ − 2, c = 1, p = (5), a valid certificate lists (3, 1, 2), since F(3, 1) = 25 passes the exact test.
- `tmCert_wrong_z` (non-example): A certificate listing (3, 1, 1) is invalid: F(3, 1) = 25 ≠ 5.
- `tmCert_unsieved_tuple` (non-example): A certificate whose residual box contains a tuple neither eliminated by a listed congruence nor tested is invalid, even if that tuple is not a solution.
- `tmCert_no_primes` (degenerate): For v = 0 the certificate has no p-adic steps and reduces to a Thue certificate for coprime solutions of F(X, Y) = c.
- `tmCert_compat` (compatibility): solutions_subset with ED.2/thue-mahler-certified-solution-set gives equality of the Finset coerced to Set with thueMahlerSolutions g c p.
- `semantic_tmCert_contains_known_solution` (characterisation): A valid semantic record for x³−2y³=5^z contains (3,1,2).
- `semantic_tmCert_wrong_z` (non-example): Listing (3,1,1) for x³−2y³=5^z contradicts semantic validity.
- `semantic_tmCert_missing_solution` (non-example): A true solution absent from the claimed list contradicts semantic validity; this does not test an omitted nonsolution row.
- `semantic_tmCert_no_primes_listed` (degenerate): Every listed triple has F=c when v=0; this does not construct a raw no-p-adic-step transcript.
- `semantic_tmCert_compat` (compatibility): The semantic list equals the actual normalized solution set under field/root hypotheses.

**Acceptance.** Every check is decidable; a certificate whose residual boxes are not exhausted (an unterminated search) is not valid and proves nothing.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-s-unit-covering`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-initial-bounds`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-reduced-bounds`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/auxiliary-prime-sieve`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/padic-discrete-logarithm-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/padic-logarithm-enclosure`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-precision-propagation`.

**Sources.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §17, p. 271. Candidates passing the cheap tests are tested exactly; the certificate's acceptance test is the exact one.

**Consumers.** Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §§6–18: the complete method as a checkable object. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-certified-solution-set: the soundness theorem. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6: worked Thue–Mahler examples ship such certificates. the ED.6 certificate consumer: certificate schemas for reproducible data.

<a id="ED-2-thue-mahler-certified-solution-set"></a>

### Certified solution sets of Thue–Mahler equations

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-certified-solution-set` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ThueMahlerCertificate.solutions_eq` · implementation unchecked.

Let (g, c, p) be a Thue–Mahler equation and C a ThueMahlerCertificate with C.Valid whose S-unit covering satisfies (U) and (C). Then thueMahlerSolutions g c p = C.solutions. In particular every normalised solution has, in its case of the covering, exponents in the residual box n_i ≤ N_i, |a_i| ≤ A_fin (or among the exceptional tuples), hence z_i ≤ N_ih_i + s′_i + t′_i: there are no solutions outside the enumerated box. Yu's and Matveev's bounds enter only through ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound and ED.2/certified-linear-form-lower-bound with constants computed in the certificate.

**Hypotheses.** Thue–Mahler hypotheses (n ≥ 3, irreducible g, c ≠ 0, gcd(c, ∏p_i) = 1); C.Valid; (U), (C)

**Proof route.**

- For the target raw theorem first derive the mathematical coverage, initial bounds, reduction implications and complete residual evaluation from the checked finite transcript and supplier semantics; then use the following semantic argument.
- ⊇: every listed triple passed the exact test.
- ⊆: a solution has a case and exponents (n, a) by (C); ED.2/thue-mahler-initial-bounds gives H ≤ K_0; ED.2/thue-mahler-reduced-bounds puts (n, a) in the residual box or in an exceptional set; by ED.2/auxiliary-prime-sieve it is not eliminated by any listed congruence, so it was tested exactly and accepted, hence it is in C.solutions.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticThueMahlerCertificate.solutions_eq` (characterisation): The existing semantic validity predicate, with the actual equation and stated field/root hypotheses, implies equality with the solution set. It is a supporting conditional theorem, not raw checker soundness.

**Acceptance.** A theorem row proves that every solution lies in the enumerated box: thueMahlerSolutions g c p equals the listed set and its exponent tuples lie in the residual boxes. Small instance: for g = X³ − 2, c = 1, p = (5) a valid certificate's list contains (1, 0, 0), (−1, −1, 0) and (3, 1, 2); the worked certificates belong to EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6. The p-adic source (Yu, Compositio Math. 91 (1994)) and the archimedean source (Matveev 2000) are registered separately from Tzanakis–de Weger 1992.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-initial-bounds`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-reduced-bounds`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/auxiliary-prime-sieve`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-linear-form-lower-bound`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/thue-mahler-effective-finiteness`.

**Sources.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §17, p. 269. After the candidates found by the Fincke–Pohst step are tested, all solutions except explicitly known ones satisfy the reduced bound for n_i: the enumeration step with exceptional tuples that are tested exactly. `yu-p-adic-logarithms-1994` — §0.1, p. 242. The p-adic source registered separately: its bound Ξ < Φ log(dB) supplies the initial bound only through the certified constant.

<a id="ED-2-s-unit-equation"></a>

### The S-unit equation x + y = 1 over ℚ and its solution set

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-equation` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.sUnitSolutions` · implementation unchecked.

For a finite set S of primes let U_S be the group of rational S-units (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/rational-s-unit-group: x ∈ ℚ^× with padicValRat q x = 0 for every prime q ∉ S). The S-unit equation is x + y = 1 with x, y ∈ U_S, and sUnitSolutions S := {(x, y) ∈ ℚ × ℚ : x ∈ U_S, y ∈ U_S, x + y = 1}. The exponent height of a solution is m(x, y) := max_{p∈S} max(|padicValRat p x|, |padicValRat p y|). Equivalent normalisations: (x, y) ↦ (u, v, w) with u + v = w, pairwise coprime integers composed of primes of S, w > 0 (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-unit-equation-coprime-reduction) — de Weger's equation x + y = z in S-integers with gcd 1 (Chapter 6, (6.1)) is the subset with u, v > 0; the six maps (x, y) ↦ (y, x), (1/x, −y/x), (−x/y, 1/y) and their composites permute sUnitSolutions S and preserve m. Scoped exponential equations are instances: for a, b, c ∈ U_S the solutions of ax′ + by′ = c with x′, y′ ∈ U_S correspond to the solutions (ax′/c, by′/c), and equations such as 2^α + 3^β = 5^γ are the subsets of de Weger's triples with prescribed prime supports.

**Hypotheses.** S finite, consisting of primes x, y range over U_S, signs included

**Proof route.**

- U_S is a subgroup of ℚ^× (DT.4/rational-s-unit-group); the six maps send solutions to solutions because 1 − x = y, 1/x + (−y/x) = 1 and (−x/y) + 1/y = 1.
- The coprime normal form is DT.4/s-unit-equation-coprime-reduction; padicValRat of x = u/w and y = v/w are read off from u, v, w, each prime of S dividing at most one of them.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.sUnitSolutions` (constructor): sUnitSolutions S : Set (ℚ × ℚ) as in the statement.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.mem_sUnitSolutions` (characterisation): (x, y) ∈ sUnitSolutions S ↔ x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ q, q.Prime → q ∉ S → padicValRat q x = 0 ∧ padicValRat q y = 0) ∧ x + y = 1.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.sUnitSolutions_swap` (other): (x, y) ∈ sUnitSolutions S → (y, x) ∈ sUnitSolutions S, and similarly for (1/x, −y/x).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.sUnitExponentHeight` (data): m(x, y) = max over p ∈ S of |padicValRat p x| and |padicValRat p y|.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.sUnitSolutions_finite` (other): sUnitSolutions S is finite (DT.4/s-unit-equation-effective-finiteness).

**Tests.**

- `sUnit_two_three` (computation): For S = {2, 3}: (3, −2), (−2, 3), (1/2, 1/2), (2, −1), (4/3, −1/3) and (−1/3, 4/3) are in sUnitSolutions S (3 − 2 = 1, 1/2 + 1/2 = 1, 2 − 1 = 1, 4/3 − 1/3 = 1).
- `sUnit_empty` (degenerate): sUnitSolutions ∅ = ∅: x, y ∈ {±1} and x + y ∈ {0, ±2}.
- `sUnit_nonunit` (non-example): (5, −4) is not in sUnitSolutions {2, 3} since padicValRat 5 5 = 1 ≠ 0, although 5 − 4 = 1.
- `sUnit_compat_coprime` (compatibility): For S = {2, 3} the solution (9/8, −1/8) corresponds under DT.4/s-unit-equation-coprime-reduction to (u, v, w) = (9, −1, 8).

**Acceptance.** (1/2, 1/2), (2, −1), (−1, 2) ∈ sUnitSolutions {2}, and these are all of its elements.

**Direct prerequisites.** `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/rational-s-unit-group`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-unit-equation-coprime-reduction`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-unit-equation-effective-finiteness`; `mathlib:padicValRat`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — Chapter 6, §6.1, (6.1), p. 115. de Weger's equation x + y = z in S-integers; the set of this node contains his solutions as (x/z, y/z). `de-weger-1989` — Chapter 6, §6.1, p. 115. de Weger's S is the multiplicative set of S-integers; here S denotes the set of primes and U_S the S-unit group.

**Consumers.** de Weger 1989, Chapter 6: the equation x + y = z in S-integers. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-certified-solution-set: the set certified exactly. EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6: the worked S = {2, 3, 5, 7} example.

<a id="ED-2-s-unit-initial-bounds"></a>

### Initial exponent bound for the S-unit equation from certified Yu constants

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-initial-bounds` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.sUnit_padicValRat_le_initialBound` · implementation unchecked.

Let S be a finite set of primes with |S| ≥ 2. For each p ∈ S let Φ⁺_p be the value of a YuConstantCertificate (ED.2/certified-padic-linear-form-constant) for n = |S|, d = 1, admissible for the rationals (−1, (q)_{q∈S∖{p}}) (h_{−1} ≥ log p ≥ π/10 and h_q ≥ max(log q, log p) suffice), and ℓ⁺_p ≥ Real.log p. Put C_p := (11/10)·Φ⁺_p·ℓ⁺_p, C := max_{p∈S} C_p and let X_0 be a rational with X_0 ≥ max(1, (2C/λ⁻)·L⁺) where 0 < λ⁻ ≤ Real.log 2 and L⁺ ≥ Real.log(2C/λ⁻). Then every (x, y) ∈ sUnitSolutions S satisfies |padicValRat p x|, |padicValRat p y| ≤ X_0 for all p. For |S| ≤ 1 every solution has all |padicValRat p x|, |padicValRat p y| ≤ 1.

**Hypotheses.** S consists of primes; |S| ≥ 2 for the Yu step (Yu's statement needs at least two numbers; the sign −1 is one of them) The sign −1 is included in the family, as DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-unit-equation-exponent-bound requires

**Proof route.**

- For p ∈ S, ε ∈ {±1} and b ∈ ℤ^{S∖{p}} with ε∏q^{b_q} ≠ 1: ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound (with exponent vector (b_{−1}, b), b_{−1} ∈ {0, 1}, B ≤ max(max|b_q|, 3)) gives padicValRat p (ε∏q^{b_q} − 1) < Φ⁺_p·log max(B, 3); since log max(B, 3) ≤ (11/10)(1 + log max(1, B)), |ε∏q^{b_q} − 1|_p ≥ (e·max(1, max|b_q|))^{−C_p}.
- This is the hypothesis of DT.4/s-unit-equation-exponent-bound with the constant C, which gives |v_p(x)|, |v_p(y)| ≤ max(1, (2C/log 2)·log(2C/log 2)) ≤ X_0.
- |S| ≤ 1: in the coprime form u + v = w at most one of u, v, w is divisible by the prime of S, the other two are ±1, so the third lies in {0, ±2}; hence S = {2} and every exponent is at most 1 in absolute value.

**Acceptance.** For S = {2, 3, 5, 7}: four certificates (one per p, n = 4, d = 1) give X_0 ≈ 9.8·10^{24} (Yu constants with h_{−1} = log p, h_q = max(log q, log p); the largest C_p is at p = 2, C_2 ≈ 6.4·10^{22}); de Weger's bound for {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13} with older constants is C_8 < 5.60·10^{27} (p. 118).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-equation`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-padic-linear-form-constant`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-unit-equation-exponent-bound`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-unit-equation-coprime-reduction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/logarithm-enclosure`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — Chapter 6, §6.2, p. 116. de Weger's Theorem 6.1 bounds m(xyz) ≤ C_8 using Yu's p-adic bound and Waldschmidt's archimedean bound; the node uses the purely p-adic route of DT.4/s-unit-equation-exponent-bound with Yu's 1994 constant certified here. `yu-p-adic-logarithms-1994` — §0.1, p. 242. The p-adic source, registered separately: the bound Ξ < Φ log(dB) evaluated with d = 1.

<a id="ED-2-s-unit-padic-reduction"></a>

### p-adic reduction for the S-unit equation

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-padic-reduction` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.sUnit_padicValRat_le_of_lattice` · implementation unchecked.

Let S be a finite set of primes, p ∈ S, M ≥ 1, and let ℓ be a PadicDiscreteLogCertificate (ED.2/padic-discrete-logarithm-certificate) at level t = M + 1 (p odd: g = 1 + p, e = p − 1; p = 2: g = 5, e = 2, t = M + 2) for the rationals (q)_{q∈S∖{p}} with γ_0 := 1, and Γ := {b ∈ ℤ^{S∖{p}} : Σ_q b_qℓ_q ≡ 0 (mod p^M)} its lattice. Let (x, y) ∈ sUnitSolutions S with coprime form u + v = w (DT.4/s-unit-equation-coprime-reduction) and suppose p ∤ uv. Then b := (padicValRat q u − padicValRat q v)_{q∈S∖{p}} satisfies: if padicValRat p w ≥ t then b ∈ Γ. Consequently, if an ED.1 certificate (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-reduction) shows that Γ contains no nonzero vector with max_q|b_q| ≤ 2X (or an ED.1 enumeration lists them all, EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete), then every solution with exponent height m(x, y) ≤ X and p ∤ uv has padicValRat p w ≤ t − 1, or b = 0 (then (u, v, w) = (1, 1, 2)), or b is a listed vector. The same holds with per-prime bounds: if |padicValRat q x|, |padicValRat q y| ≤ X_q for all q ∈ S and the ED.1 certificate excludes (or the enumeration lists) the nonzero vectors of Γ with |b_q| ≤ X_q for all q ∈ S ∖ {p} (de Weger's box of radius √(Σ_i f(p_i)²), p. 125), the same conclusion holds for these solutions. By the symmetries of ED.2/s-unit-equation the same bound holds for the unique one of u, v, w divisible by p, so f(p) := t − 1 bounds padicValRat p (uvw) for all solutions of height ≤ X outside the images under the six symmetries of the solutions whose vector b is listed; iterating over p ∈ S is an exponent reduction chain (ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain).

**Hypotheses.** The rationals q ∈ S ∖ {p} are p-adic units, so the discrete logarithms exist |b_q| ≤ X, since b_q = v_q(u) − v_q(v) with 0 ≤ v_q(u), v_q(v) ≤ X and at most one of them nonzero; the box radius 2X of the statement is a safe over-estimate

**Proof route.**

- Generate the scalar log enclosures mathematically from ED.2/logarithm-enclosure and ED.2/padic-logarithm-enclosure, then apply ED.0/padic-precision-propagation. For pivot log valuation s, certify precision at least m+s and strict pivot precision>s before forming normalized ratios modulo π^m. Existence of adequate N is proved by the positive-slope tail estimate. A raw congruence checker does not assume completeness of the final solution list.
- −u/v − 1 = −w/v, so padicValRat p (−u/v − 1) = padicValRat p w ≥ t (p ∤ v), i.e. −u/v ≡ 1 (mod p^t); and −u/v = ±∏_q q^{b_q}. The certificate's soundness (the sign is absorbed since e is even) gives b ∈ Γ.
- If b = 0 then u/v = ±1 with gcd(u, v) = 1, so u, v ∈ {±1}; since w = u + v > 0, (u, v, w) = (1, 1, 2) and padicValRat p w ≤ 1 ≤ t − 1.
- The ED.1 certificate excludes nonzero points of Γ in the box; enumerated points are listed and tested exactly (de Weger §6.5).

**Acceptance.** For S = {2, 3, 5, 7} and p = 7, M = 2 (t = 3, g = 8, e = 6): the solution (u, v, w) = (1, 48, 49) has padicValRat 7 w = 2 < 3 and is not forced into Γ, while every solution with 7³ ∣ w gives b ∈ Γ.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-equation`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/padic-discrete-logarithm-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-unit-equation-coprime-reduction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-reduction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/padic-logarithm-enclosure`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-precision-propagation`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — Chapter 6, §6.3, (6.5)–(6.6), p. 119. de Weger: if ℓ(Γ*_μ) > √(s − 1)·X_1 then (6.2) has no solutions with μ + μ_0 ≤ ord_p(z) ≤ m(xyz) ≤ X_1; the lattice here is the discrete-logarithm lattice, which contains every exponent vector with ord_p(z) ≥ t (t = M + 1 for odd p, t = M + 2 for p = 2) (formulas read on the page image). `de-weger-1989` — Chapter 6, §6.5, p. 124. The iterated sieve with bounds f(p): choose p and μ, enumerate the lattice points, select the solutions, lower f(p).

<a id="ED-2-s-unit-certificate"></a>

### S-unit solution certificates

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-certificate` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SUnitCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

An SUnitCertificate for a finite set S of primes consists of: for each p ∈ S a YuConstantCertificate and the initial bound X_0 of ED.2/s-unit-initial-bounds (or the bound 1 when |S| ≤ 1); per-prime bounds f_0(p) := X_0 and an exponent reduction chain (ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain) whose steps are p-adic reductions of ED.2/s-unit-padic-reduction (a prime p, a level M, a PadicDiscreteLogCertificate and an ED.1 lattice certificate or complete enumeration, lowering f(p) to t − 1 (= M for odd p, M + 1 for p = 2, where t = M + 2) given the current bounds f(q) for all q), ending with bounds f(p) for all p ∈ S and a finite list E of exceptional solutions found by enumeration; and the claimed list L ⊆ ℚ × ℚ. SUnitCertificate.Valid is the conjunction of: every certificate check; L equals the set of pairs (x, 1 − x) with x = ±∏_{p∈S}p^{a_p}, |a_p| ≤ f(p), such that 1 − x ∈ U_S (exact factorisation over S of the numerator and denominator of 1 − x), together with the members of E that pass the same test. The residual box has 2∏_{p∈S}(2f(p) + 1) elements and is enumerated exhaustively. This is the target raw finite format specified in suggestedOmissions. SemanticSUnitCertificate is the separately named mathematical summary; its Valid field contains real inequalities and universal solution implications, and has no claimed computational Decidable instance. The raw checker derives those implications from the finite transcript and supplier soundness, including all nonsolution rows.

**Hypotheses.** Finite data; validity is decidable The bounds f(p) apply to |padicValRat p x| and |padicValRat p y| for every solution outside E

**Proof route.**

- Each check is exact: rational inequalities for the constants, modular exponentiation for the discrete logarithms, the ED.1 checks, and trial division by the primes of S for membership in U_S.
- Separate finite check from semantic interpretation: first evaluate the full bounded transcript; then use supplier correctness and the named bound/reduction lemmas to prove the semantic summary. No proof field asserting completeness is accepted as raw data.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SUnitCertificate` (structure): The data of the statement with the claimed solutions as a Finset (ℚ × ℚ).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SUnitCertificate.Valid` (relation): The conjunction of all exact checks.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SUnitCertificate.solutions` (projection): The claimed list L.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SUnitCertificate.finalBound` (projection): The final per-prime bounds f : S → ℕ.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SUnitCertificate.solutions_subset` (characterisation): Valid implies L ⊆ sUnitSolutions S.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticSUnitCertificate` (structure): Supporting mathematical summary of the field/root, bounds, reductions and claimed list. It contains proof-bearing supplier/reduction data; not the raw finite certificate.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticSUnitCertificate.Valid` (relation): Semantic predicate including the actual real inequalities and solution implications. No finite-evaluation claim is made.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticSUnitCertificate.solutions` (projection): The list stored in the supporting semantic record.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticSUnitCertificate.finalBound` (projection): The per-prime bounds stored in the supporting semantic record.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticSUnitCertificate.solutions_subset` (characterisation): Semantic validity implies that every listed point satisfies the actual equation.

**Tests.**

- `sUnitCert_two` (computation): For S = {2} (|S| = 1, f(2) = 1) the residual box is {±1/2, ±1, ±2} and the valid list is {(2, −1), (−1, 2), (1/2, 1/2)}.
- `sUnitCert_empty` (degenerate): For S = ∅ the box is {±1} and the valid list is empty.
- `sUnitCert_missing` (non-example): For S = {2, 3}, final bounds f(2) = 3, f(3) = 1 are not the end of any valid chain whose exceptional list E omits (9/8, −1/8): (9/8, −1/8) ∈ sUnitSolutions S has padicValRat 3 (9/8) = 2 > 1, so a step lowering f(3) to 1 without listing it contradicts soundness (at p = 3, M = 1 the lattice is 3ℤ and the vector b = ±3 of this solution is enumerated); a notion of validity that did not check the chain steps would accept a list missing (9/8, −1/8).
- `sUnitCert_compat` (compatibility): solutions_subset with ED.2/s-unit-certified-solution-set gives equality with sUnitSolutions S, a finite set in agreement with DT.4/s-unit-equation-effective-finiteness.
- `semantic_sUnitCert_two` (characterisation): Existence of a semantic certificate for S={2} with f(2)=1 and the three listed pairs; no raw evaluation is asserted.
- `semantic_sUnitCert_empty` (degenerate): A valid semantic certificate for S=∅ lists no pairs.
- `semantic_sUnitCert_missing` (non-example): A semantic final f(3)=1 for S={2,3} requires (9/8,−1/8) among exceptions.
- `semantic_sUnitCert_compat` (compatibility): Semantic equality yields finiteness of sUnitSolutions S.

**Acceptance.** For S = {2} the certificate with f(2) = 1 and list {(2, −1), (−1, 2), (1/2, 1/2)} is valid.

The enumeration steps, whose output is the exceptional list E.

<a id="ED-2-s-unit-certified-solution-set"></a>

### Certified solution sets of S-unit equations over ℚ

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-certified-solution-set` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SUnitCertificate.solutions_eq` · implementation unchecked.

Let S be a finite set of primes and C an SUnitCertificate for S with C.Valid. Then sUnitSolutions S = C.solutions. In particular every solution (x, y) satisfies |padicValRat p x|, |padicValRat p y| ≤ f(p) for all p ∈ S or lies in the exceptional list: no solution lies outside the enumerated box. Consequently, for a, b, c ∈ U_S, the solutions (x′, y′) ∈ U_S² of ax′ + by′ = c are exactly the pairs (cx/a, cy/b) with (x, y) ∈ C.solutions, and the solutions of exponential equations ±p_1^{α_1}⋯ ± q_1^{β_1}⋯ = r_1^{γ_1}⋯ in primes of S are read off from C.solutions. Yu's bound enters only through ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound with constants computed in the certificate.

**Hypotheses.** S consists of primes; C.Valid

**Proof route.**

- For the target raw theorem first derive the mathematical coverage, initial bounds, reduction implications and complete residual evaluation from the checked finite transcript and supplier semantics; then use the following semantic argument.
- ⊇: every listed pair passed the exact membership test.
- ⊆: by ED.2/s-unit-initial-bounds every solution has height ≤ X_0; by soundness of the reduction chain (ED.2/s-unit-padic-reduction, ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain) every solution outside E satisfies the final bounds f(p), so x = ±∏p^{a_p} with |a_p| ≤ f(p) lies in the enumerated box and passed the test.
- The scoped exponential equations are the image of sUnitSolutions S under (x, y) ↦ (cx/a, cy/b), a bijection onto the solutions of ax′ + by′ = c.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.SemanticSUnitCertificate.solutions_eq` (characterisation): The existing semantic validity predicate, with the actual equation and stated field/root hypotheses, implies equality with the solution set. It is a supporting conditional theorem, not raw checker soundness.

**Acceptance.** A theorem row proves that every solution lies in the enumerated box: sUnitSolutions S equals the listed set, and every solution has |padicValRat p x| ≤ f(p) for all p ∈ S or lies in the exceptional list E. Small instance: for S = {2, 3} a valid certificate's list consists of the solutions generated by 1 + 1 = 2, 1 + 2 = 3, 1 + 3 = 4, 1 + 8 = 9 under the six symmetries (these four coprime triples a + b = c, a ≤ b, are all of them).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-initial-bounds`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-padic-reduction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-unit-equation-effective-finiteness`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — Chapter 6, Theorem 6.3, p. 123. de Weger's result for S = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13} (x + y = z, (x, y) = 1, x ≤ y): the type of statement this theorem certifies. `de-weger-1989` — Chapter 7, proof of Lemma 7.3, p. 138. For S = {2, 3, 5, 7}: a + b = c, (a, b) = 1, a ≥ b has exactly 63 solutions, deduced from Theorem 6.3; the worked example belongs to ED.6.

## ED.3 — Descent, rank bounds and saturation

**Planets.** Certified 2-Selmer group; 2-descent rank bound; Descent via 2-isogeny; Cremona's height difference bound; Saturation by reduction; Mordell–Weil basis certificate.

<a id="ED-3-local-quotient-cardinality"></a>

### Size of E(ℚ_v)/2E(ℚ_v) at a finite or real place

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/local-quotient-cardinality` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.index_two_nsmul_padic` · implementation unchecked.

Let p be a prime and W an elliptic Weierstrass curve over ℚ_p. Then 2E(ℚ_p) has finite index in E(ℚ_p) and [E(ℚ_p) : 2E(ℚ_p)] = #E(ℚ_p)[2] · |2|_p^{-1}, with |·|_p normalised by |p|_p = p^{-1}; that is, the index equals #E(ℚ_p)[2] for odd p and 2·#E(ℚ_p)[2] for p = 2. For an elliptic Weierstrass curve W over ℝ, 2·[E(ℝ) : 2E(ℝ)] = #E(ℝ)[2]. In the normal form y² = f(x), #E(K)[2] = 1 + #{x ∈ K : f(x) = 0} for K = ℚ_p or ℝ. Because ker μ_K = 2E(K) (Tau Ceti ker_μ_eq over the field K), the same numbers are the orders of the local descent images μ_K(E(K)).

**Hypotheses.** W : WeierstrassCurve K with W.IsElliptic, K = ℚ_p (p prime) or K = ℝ; for the descent-image reading also W.IsCharNeTwoNF. Index means AddSubgroup.index of the range of nsmulAddMonoidHom 2 on W.toAffine.Point; #E(K)[2] means Nat.card of its kernel.

**Proof route.**

- p-adic case. By the reduction filtration (EllipticCurves Layer 4) E₀(ℚ_p) has finite index in E(ℚ_p), E₀(ℚ_p)/E₁(ℚ_p) ≅ Ẽ_ns(𝔽_p) is finite and E₁(ℚ_p) ≅ Ê(pℤ_p) (Tau Ceti WeierstrassCurve.formalPointHomAdicCompletion, an injective additive map Ê(𝔪_v) → E(K_v) for a model over the valuation ring, whose range is O together with the points whose x-coordinate has a pole, by range_formalPointHomAdicCompletion); for r ≥ 2 the formal logarithm (Layer 1 formal groups, via Layer 4) gives Ê(p^rℤ_p) ≅ (p^rℤ_p, +) ≅ ℤ_p. So E(ℚ_p) has a finite-index subgroup U ≅ ℤ_p. The pinned formal-point range theorem describes the pole-valuation locus; its identification with E₁ and the finite reduction/logarithm comparison remain exactly the existing Layer 4 supplier request, not a claimed current implementation.
- For an abelian group B with B[2] and B/2B finite put q(B) = #(B/2B)/#B[2]. The snake lemma for multiplication by 2 on 0 → U → E(ℚ_p) → F → 0 with F finite gives q(E(ℚ_p)) = q(U)·q(F); q(F) = 1 for finite F and q(ℤ_p) = #(ℤ_p/2ℤ_p) = |2|_p^{-1}. This is the Haar-measure count of Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer Lemma 3 in dimension one.
- Real case. Order the real roots of f. If f has one real root e then x ≥ e on E(ℝ), so every μ_ℝ(P) has the sign class of x − e equal to +, the image is trivial and #E(ℝ)[2] = 2. If f has three real roots e₁ < e₂ < e₃ then E(ℝ) lies over [e₁, e₂] ∪ [e₃, ∞); the sign vector of (x − e₁, x − e₂, x − e₃) is (+,−,−) or (+,+,+) (at x = e_i the corrected representative of μX has the same signs, f′(e_i) being (+) for i = 1, 3 and (−) for i = 2 in the relevant slot), so the image has 2 elements and #E(ℝ)[2] = 4. Tau Ceti ker_μ_eq over ℝ turns #image into [E(ℝ):2E(ℝ)]. This agrees with E(ℝ) ≅ S¹ or S¹ × C₂ (Cremona §3.3).
- The 2-torsion count is Tau Ceti card_ker_nsmul_two.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.card_localDescentImage_padic` (compatibility): For p prime and the actual W:WeierstrassCurve.Affine Q_p in elliptic characteristic-≠2 normal form, #range(W.μ)=(if p=2 then 2 else 1)·#ker([2]:W.Point→W.Point), using the pinned W.A, W.M and corrected W.μ.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.two_mul_card_localDescentImage_real` (compatibility): For the actual elliptic W over R in characteristic-≠2 normal form, 2·#range(W.μ)=#ker([2]:W.Point→W.Point).

**Acceptance.** y² = x³ − x over ℚ_3: f has the three roots 0, ±1 in ℚ_3, so [E(ℚ_3) : 2E(ℚ_3)] = 4. y² = x³ − x over ℚ_2: #E(ℚ_2)[2] = 4, so [E(ℚ_2) : 2E(ℚ_2)] = 8. y² = x³ + 1 over ℝ: one real root, [E(ℝ):2E(ℝ)] = 1; y² = x³ − x over ℝ: [E(ℝ):2E(ℝ)] = 2.

**Direct prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-4-elliptic-curves-over-local-fields--reduction-tates-algorithm-the-tate-curve-aec-vii-ataec-ivv`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.ker_μ_eq`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.card_ker_nsmul_two`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point`; `mathlib:Subgroup.index`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.formalPointHomAdicCompletion`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.range_formalPointHomAdicCompletion`.

**Sources.** `flynn-poonen-schaefer-1997` — §7, proof of Lemma 3, p. 16 (arXiv v1). The genus-two (dimension 2) form of the count, giving |2|_p^{-2}; the node is the dimension-one case, proved through the finite-index subgroup ≅ ℤ_p instead of Haar measure. `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.3, p. 69. The sentence continues: or to S¹ × C₂ (when Δ > 0). This gives the real count #E(ℝ)/2E(ℝ) = 1 or 2; the node proves it by the explicit sign description instead.

<a id="ED-3-local-descent-image"></a>

### Certified local image of the 2-descent map

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/local-descent-image` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.CertifiedLocalImage` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, fix W as in the hypotheses and a place v of ℚ, with K_v = ℚ_p (v = p) or ℝ (v = ∞), and write M_v for the square classes (W⁄K_v).M of the local étale algebra A_v = K_v[X]/(f). A certified local image at v (CertifiedLocalImage W v) consists of: (i) a factorisation f = ∏_j f_j into monic irreducibles over K_v — linear factors pinned by Hensel data (ED.0 p-adic embedding certificates), the others certified irreducible by the Newton-polygon criterion (explicit supplied class/unit/factorization data Ore residual irreducibility, with the prime-ideal factorisation of p in the global factor fields), real roots isolated at ∞ (ED.0 archimedean certificates) — so that A_v ≅ ∏_j L_j with L_j = K_v[X]/(f_j); (ii) square-class coordinates: an explicit group isomorphism κ_v : M_v ≅ (ℤ/2)^{n_v} built from the valuation parity and finitely many residual quadratic characters on each L_j^×/L_j^{×2} (for odd p: the valuation mod 2 and the Legendre character of the unit part; for p = 2 the unit part read modulo 8 in each L_j; for ℝ the signs at the real factors); (iii) finitely many x₁,…,x_k ∈ ℚ with f(x_i) a nonzero square in K_v, checked by exact rational arithmetic (for odd p: v_p(f(x_i)) even and the unit part a square mod p; for p = 2: even valuation and unit part ≡ 1 mod 8; for ℝ: f(x_i) > 0), so that each x_i is the x-coordinate of some P_i ∈ E(K_v); (iv) the coordinate vectors c_i = κ_v(class of x_i − T) ∈ (ℤ/2)^{n_v}, computed exactly from x_i. The output is the subgroup H_v = κ_v^{-1}(span_{𝔽₂}{c_1,…,c_k}) of M_v. The certificate is complete when #H_v equals the number of local-quotient-cardinality, that is |2|_v^{-1}·#E(K_v)[2] at a finite place and #E(ℝ)[2]/2 at ∞.

**Hypotheses.** W : WeierstrassCurve ℚ with W.IsElliptic, W.IsCharNeTwoNF and a₂, a₄, a₆ ∈ ℤ; v a prime of ℤ or the real place. μ_v(P_i) is the class of x_i − T because f(x_i) ≠ 0 (Tau Ceti μX_of_eval_f_ne_zero); the y-coordinate of P_i is never needed. The finite local algebra decomposition, irreducible factors, e/f data and coefficient embedding/valuation comparisons are supplied with exact factorization/isomorphism proofs. No Ore-factorization routine or table is a target.

**Proof route.**

- Store the factorisation, the coordinate map κ_v and the rational abscissae; check (iii) exactly on the rational number f(x_i).
- Compute c_i from the valuations and residues of x_i − θ_j in the factors L_j (θ_j a root of f_j): the valuation is read from v_p(f_j(x_i)) and the ramification data, the residual character from an ED.0 valuation certificate of the unit part at fixed precision — one digit beyond the valuation for odd p, three 2-adic digits beyond it for p = 2.
- H_v ≤ μ_v(E(K_v)) because each class is μ_v of an actual point; points with x ∈ ℚ suffice for completeness because μ_v is locally constant on E(K_v) ∖ E[2] and such points are dense, so a complete certificate exists for every v.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.CertifiedLocalImage.span` (data): The subgroup H_v ≤ M_v generated by the classes of x_i − T.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.CertifiedLocalImage.coord` (projection): The certified isomorphism κ_v : M_v ≅ (ℤ/2)^{n_v}.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.CertifiedLocalImage.span_le_range` (characterisation): H_v ≤ μ_v(E(K_v)) for every certificate, complete or not.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.CertifiedLocalImage.span_eq_range_of_card` (characterisation): If #H_v = #(μ_v(E(K_v))) then H_v = μ_v(E(K_v)); promoted to local-image-completeness.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.CertifiedLocalImage.card_span` (simp): #H_v = 2^{rank_{𝔽₂}(c_1,…,c_k)}.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.CertifiedLocalImage.localCondition_eq_comap` (compatibility): For a complete certificate, Tau Ceti's W.localCondition K_v equals the preimage of H_v under W.localRes K_v.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.ellipticLocalImage` (constructor): For the genuine affine curve W over Q_p in characteristic-ne-two normal form, use W.μ and W.M imported from Tau Ceti. Given the local square-class coordinate isomorphism and actual W.Point list, bundle their images.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.ellipticLocalImage_span` (compatibility): The bundled span equals closure of W.μ applied to the actual listed local points; its local condition is comap along Tau Ceti W.localRes.

**Tests.**

- `certifiedLocalImage_real_three_roots` (computation): For y² = x³ − x at ∞ with x₁ = −1/2, x₂ = 2, #H_∞ = 2 and H_∞ = μ_ℝ(E(ℝ)).
- `certifiedLocalImage_empty` (degenerate): With k = 0 points, H_v = ⊥ (the trivial subgroup); it is complete only when |2|_v^{-1}#E(K_v)[2] = 1, e.g. at ∞ for y² = x³ + 1.
- `certifiedLocalImage_odd_good_prime` (compatibility): For y² = x³ − x at p = 5 (good, odd), a complete H_5 equals the unramified classes of norm a square, of order #E(ℚ_5)[2] = 4.
- `certifiedLocalImage_incomplete` (non-example): For y² = x³ − x at p = 2 the single abscissa x = 1/4 (f(1/4) = −15/64, of even 2-adic valuation with −15 ≡ 1 mod 8, so a nonzero square in ℚ_2) gives #H_2 ≤ 2 < 8 = [E(ℚ_2):2E(ℚ_2)], so the certificate is not complete and does not determine the local condition.

**Acceptance.** At ∞ for y² = x³ − x the abscissae x = −1/2 and x = 2 give the coordinate vectors (+,−,−) and (+,+,+); H_∞ has 2 elements, the number required, so the certificate is complete. At p = 3 for y² = x³ − x (f = X(X−1)(X+1), A_3 ≅ ℚ_3³, n_3 = 6) the certificate is complete exactly when its vectors span a subgroup of order 4.

**Sources.** `flynn-poonen-schaefer-1997` — §5, diagram (6) and the sentence after it, p. 12 (arXiv v1). The same local images for the genus-two x − T map; the node is the elliptic instance with certified coordinates. `flynn-poonen-schaefer-1997` — §7, Lemma 4 and proof, p. 17 (arXiv v1). A local point certified by a rational abscissa and a congruence modulo 8, as in (iii).

**Consumers.** Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer §7, Lemma 4: the local images at 2 and 3701 are generated by the images of points with rational abscissae x = 2 and x = −4. <a id="ED-3-local-image-completeness"></a>

### The size check completes a local image

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/local-image-completeness` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.CertifiedLocalImage.span_eq_range_of_card` · implementation unchecked.

Let C be a certified local image for W at a place v (local-descent-image). Then H_v ≤ μ_v(E(K_v)), and if #H_v = |2|_v^{-1}·#E(K_v)[2] for v finite, respectively #H_v = #E(ℝ)[2]/2 for v = ∞, then H_v = μ_v(E(K_v)); consequently Tau Ceti's local condition W.localCondition K_v equals {m ∈ M : localRes_v(m) ∈ H_v}. If #H_v is smaller, H_v ≠ μ_v(E(K_v)): the size check is necessary and sufficient. #E(K_v)[2] = 1 + #{roots of f in K_v} is read off the certified factorisation in C.

**Hypotheses.** C : CertifiedLocalImage W v for W over ℚ as in local-descent-image.

**Proof route.**

- Each generator of H_v is μ_v of an actual point, so H_v ≤ range μ_v.
- ker μ_v = 2E(K_v) (Tau Ceti ker_μ_eq over K_v), hence #range μ_v = [E(K_v):2E(K_v)], which is the stated number by local-quotient-cardinality.
- A subgroup of a finite group of the same order is the whole group (Subgroup.eq_of_le_of_card_ge).
- Tau Ceti mem_localCondition_iff: m ∈ W.localCondition K_v ↔ localRes(m) ∈ range μ_v; substitute H_v.

**Acceptance.** For y² = x³ − x at p = 3, four classes certified from rational abscissae give the full local image. Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer Table 4 and Lemma 4 (genus two): #J(ℚ_2)/ker(x − T) = 2 is generated by one point, the analogue of the check.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/local-descent-image`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/local-quotient-cardinality`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.ker_μ_eq`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.mem_localCondition_iff`; `mathlib:Subgroup.eq_of_le_of_card_ge`.

**Sources.** `flynn-poonen-schaefer-1997` — §7, proof of Lemma 4, p. 17 (arXiv v1). The sentence ends: 2 − T ∉ L₂^{×2}ℚ₂^×. One nontrivial class suffices there because the target order 2 was computed first (Table 4); this is the size check. `flynn-poonen-schaefer-1997` — §7, proof of Lemma 3, p. 16 (arXiv v1). Extraction flattens the exponents |2|_p^2 and |2|_p^{-2}.

<a id="ED-3-good-place-local-image"></a>

### Local images at good odd places are the unramified classes

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/good-place-local-image` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.localCondition_eq_unramified_of_good` · implementation unchecked.

For p prime, p≠2 and an actual W:WeierstrassCurve.Affine ℚ_p with IsElliptic and IsCharNeTwoNF, assume W.badPrimes ℤ_p=∅ (2 and Δ are units and the coefficients are integral). Then W.μ.range = W.selmerGroupA ℤ_p ⊓ W.normM.ker as subgroups of the actual unit square-class group W.M of W.A=ℚ_p[X]/(W.f). Here selmerGroupA is the pinned factorwise even-valuation subgroup over the integral closures of ℤ_p in the factors of W.f; at odd p these are the unramified square classes. For a global normal-form curve over ℚ and a set S containing its bad primes, base-change compatibility implies that the local conditions outside S are automatic on A(S,2)∩ker N.

**Hypotheses.** p prime and p≠2; W:WeierstrassCurve.Affine ℚ_p; W.IsElliptic and W.IsCharNeTwoNF; DecidableEq ℚ_p for the pinned point/descent API. W.badPrimes ℤ_p=∅, using the standard ℤ_p algebra and fraction-field structures. No asserted image size, unramified size or arbitrary candidate subgroup is a hypothesis. For the global consequence only: integral normal-form global model, S containing badPrimes, and the pinned restriction/norm compatibility.

**Proof route.**

- Inclusion ⊆: Tau Ceti range_μ_le_selmerGroupA applied to W over ℚ_p with R = ℤ_p (whose bad primes are empty) and range_μ_le_ker_normM.
- Count: f has distinct roots mod p, so each L_j is unramified over ℚ_p; the unramified classes of L_j^×/L_j^{×2} are the unit classes, two per factor, and the norm map on unit classes is onto ℤ_p^×/ℤ_p^{×2}, so the unramified norm-square classes number 2^{(#factors) − 1} = 1 + #{roots of f in ℚ_p} = #E(ℚ_p)[2].
- local-quotient-cardinality gives #μ_p(E(ℚ_p)) = #E(ℚ_p)[2] for odd p, so the inclusion is an equality.
- Global consequence: Tau Ceti localRes_mem_selmerGroupA sends A(S,2) into the local unramified classes at every good p, and the global norm condition implies the local one.

**Acceptance.** For y² = x³ − x and p = 5: the local condition at 5 is implied by A(S,2) ∩ ker N with S = {2}. Cremona Ch. III p. 80: a quartic H with p odd and p ∤ disc(g) has points mod p that lift, the same statement for the quartic model of a class.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/local-quotient-cardinality`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.range_μ_le_selmerGroupA`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.range_μ_le_ker_normM`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.localRes_mem_selmerGroupA`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.badPrimes`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.selmerGroupA`.

**Sources.** `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.6, Checking local solubility, p. 80. The quartic-model form of the statement; the node states it for the x − T local condition and proves it by counting. `aitken-lemmermeyer-2011` — Appendix B, Theorem 5, p. 17 (arXiv v1). The same automatic local solubility for the 2-isogeny quartics; extraction drops the superscript in b².

<a id="ED-3-two-selmer-certificate"></a>

### Certified 2-Selmer group of an elliptic curve over ℚ

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/two-selmer-certificate` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.TwoSelmerCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, a certified 2-Selmer computation for W (TwoSelmerCertificate W) consists of: (i) a finite set S of primes containing 2 and every prime of W.badPrimes; (ii) for each monic irreducible factor f_j of f over ℚ, with field L_j = ℚ[X]/(f_j) and the primes of L_j above S, a certified finite generating set of the group L_j(S,2) of classes in L_j^×/L_j^{×2} with even valuation outside S (Mathlib's IsDedekindDomain.selmerGroup for the ring of integers of L_j): S-unit generators modulo squares and lifts of generators of the 2-torsion of the S-class group, certified complete by the supplied complete class-and-unit presentation and Tau Ceti's exact sequence S-units → L_j(S,2) → Cl_S[2]; together these give an 𝔽₂-basis of A(S,2), the classes of M unramified outside S (A(S,2) contains Tau Ceti's W.selmerGroupA (𝓞 ℚ), which is the group for the fixed set W.badPrimes (𝓞 ℚ), and equals it exactly when S = W.badPrimes (𝓞 ℚ)); (iii) the norm map N : A(S,2) → ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} on that basis, whose kernel K_S is computed by 𝔽₂-linear algebra; (iv) a complete certified local image C_v (local-descent-image, local-image-completeness) for every v ∈ S ∪ {∞}, with the 𝔽₂-linear maps κ_v ∘ localRes_v on the basis of K_S. Its Selmer group is Sel(C) = {m ∈ K_S : κ_v(localRes_v(m)) ∈ span(C_v) for every v ∈ S ∪ {∞}}, an explicit 𝔽₂-subspace with a computed basis; its order is 2^{s(C)}.

**Hypotheses.** W : WeierstrassCurve ℚ with W.IsElliptic, W.IsCharNeTwoNF and a₂, a₄, a₆ ∈ ℤ. Only the places of S ∪ {∞} carry computed local data; good-place-local-image shows no other place changes the group. A supplied ideal/class/unit presentation has explicit defining relations, integral-basis identities and a proof of full class/unit generation. All local factorization identities used are hypotheses; they do not assert the Selmer or Mordell–Weil answer.

**Proof route.**

- Field factors: take the supplied complete irreducible factorization of f over ℚ, with its polynomial identity, irreducibility and pairwise-coprimality proofs; ED.0 does not produce this factorization; A ≅ ∏ L_j by Tau Ceti AdjoinRoot.equivPiFactors and M ≅ ∏ L_j^×/L_j^{×2} by AdjoinRoot.modPowEquivPiFactors, as in Tau Ceti selmerGroupA.
- Generators of L_j(S,2): Tau Ceti IsDedekindDomain.selmerGroup.ker_toClassGroup and range_toClassGroup give 0 → O_{L_j,S}^×/squares → L_j(S,2) → Cl_S(L_j)[2] → 0; explicit supplied class/unit/factorization data/certified-class-unit-completeness certifies the class group and a unit basis, and explicit supplied class/unit/factorization data/prime-ideal-factor-certificate the primes above S.
- The norm map and all local maps are computed on the explicit basis; Sel(C) is the kernel of an explicit 𝔽₂-matrix.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.TwoSelmerCertificate.selmer` (data): The subgroup Sel(C) ≤ W.M cut out by the computed conditions.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.TwoSelmerCertificate.basis` (projection): An explicit 𝔽₂-basis of Sel(C) as classes of units of A.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.TwoSelmerCertificate.card_selmer` (simp): #Sel(C) = 2^{s(C)} with s(C) the length of the basis.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.TwoSelmerCertificate.mem_selmer_iff` (characterisation): m ∈ Sel(C) ↔ m ∈ A(S,2), N(m) = 1 and localRes_v(m) ∈ H_v for every v ∈ S ∪ {∞}.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.TwoSelmerCertificate.range_μ_le` (relation): im μ ≤ Sel(C); promoted to two-selmer-certificate-sound.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.TwoSelmerCertificate.selmer_eq_selmerGroup₂` (compatibility): Sel(C) = Tau Ceti W.selmerGroup₂ with R = 𝓞 ℚ and the auxiliary family consisting of ℝ alone; promoted to two-selmer-certificate-sound.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.TwoSelmerCertificate.selmer_mono` (other): Under A(S,2)≤A(S′,2) in the actual global square-class carrier and compatibility of all new local conditions, Sel(C)≤Sel(D). With complete sound local data both equal the true Selmer group. The abstract helper records inclusion, not the actual ambient or local factory.

**Tests.**

- `twoSelmer_x3_minus_x` (computation): For y² = x³ − x with S = {2}: #Sel(C) = 4 and Sel(C) is the image of E(ℚ)[2] = {O, (0,0), (1,0), (−1,0)}.
- `twoSelmer_no_places` (degenerate): Without the local conditions the group would be A(S,2) ∩ ker N; for y² = x³ − x (A ≅ ℚ³, each factor contributing ℚ({2},2) = ⟨−1, 2⟩) this group has order 4³/4 = 2⁴, larger than Sel(C).
- `twoSelmer_eq_tauceti` (compatibility): Sel(C) = W.selmerGroup₂ (with R = 𝓞 ℚ and the auxiliary family consisting of ℝ alone) for every certificate with S ⊇ badPrimes.
- `twoSelmer_not_image` (non-example): For the actual Cremona 571a1 model [0,−1,1,−929,−10595], transported to characteristic-≠2 normal form by (x,y)↦(4x,8y+4), certify #range μ=1 and #Sel₂=4 and conclude non-equality. This exact same-name regression is omitted under §13 pending its concrete descent/local-image factory; assumed dimensions do not implement it.
- `twoSelmer_basis_length_two` (computation): For the abstract certificate and a supplied basis of length two, the Selmer summary has cardinality four. This does not construct the x³−x arithmetic factory.
- `twoSelmer_le_unconditioned` (compatibility): For every abstract certificate, its Selmer summary is contained in the supplied unconditioned norm kernel. This proves no numerical order of an actual cubic square-class group.
- `twoSelmer_eq_supplied_localIntersection` (compatibility): Given the explicit outside-place, unramified and membership hypotheses for an arbitrary subgroup sel, the abstract certificate summary equals sel. This does not identify sel with the actual pinned rational-curve Selmer group.
- `twoSelmer_cardinality_gap` (non-example): Given abstract image order one and certificate Selmer order four, the image differs from the certificate summary. The actual 571a1 arithmetic regression is separately omitted.

**Acceptance.** For y² = x³ − x (f = X(X−1)(X+1), S = {2}) the computation gives #Sel(C) = 4 = #E(ℚ)[2], the order of the image of the 2-torsion. Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer Lemmas 1–5 carry out the same steps for a genus-two Jacobian (G, H, H′ there).
