<a id="ED-3-two-selmer-certificate-sound"></a>

### Soundness of the certified 2-Selmer group

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/two-selmer-certificate-sound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.TwoSelmerCertificate.selmer_eq_selmerGroup₂` · implementation unchecked.

For every two-selmer-certificate C of W: (a) Sel(C) = Tau Ceti's W.selmerGroup₂ with R = 𝓞 ℚ and the auxiliary family consisting of ℝ alone, the classical 2-Selmer group of E/ℚ; (b) im μ ≤ Sel(C); (c) Sel(C) is finite of order 2^{s(C)}.

**Hypotheses.** C : TwoSelmerCertificate W with S ⊇ badPrimes and complete local images at S ∪ {∞}.

**Proof route.**

- (b) Tau Ceti range_μ_le_selmerGroupA, range_μ_le_ker_normM and range_μ_le_localCondition give im μ ≤ A(S,2) ∩ ker N ∩ ⋂_v localCondition; local-image-completeness identifies each local condition with the computed H_v.
- (a) ⊆: an element of Sel(C) lies in A(S,2) ∩ ker N and satisfies the conditions at S ∪ {∞}; at every other prime good-place-local-image gives the local condition (Tau Ceti's localRes_mem_selmerGroupA is stated only for m ∈ W.selmerGroupA (𝓞 ℚ), the group for S = badPrimes; when S ⊋ badPrimes the same global-to-local comparison for A(S,2) at primes outside S is proved here by the same argument); so it is in selmerGroup₂ (mem_selmerGroup₂_iff).
- (a) ⊇: an element of selmerGroup₂ satisfies the local condition at every good p, hence (local image ⊆ unramified there) localizes to unramified classes at all good p and lies in A(S,2) by Tau Ceti mem_selmerGroupA_of_forall_localRes; the remaining conditions are those of Sel(C).
- (c) The certificate's basis is a basis by explicit supplied class/unit/factorization data completeness, so #Sel(C) = 2^{s(C)}; in particular selmerGroup₂ is finite.

**Acceptance.** For y² = x³ − x, Sel(C) = selmerGroup₂ has order 4. Finiteness of selmerGroup₂, which Tau Ceti leaves to a separate theorem, follows for every curve with a certificate.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/two-selmer-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/local-image-completeness`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/good-place-local-image`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.selmerGroup₂`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.mem_selmerGroup₂_iff`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.range_μ_le_selmerGroup₂`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.range_μ_le_selmerGroupA`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.range_μ_le_localCondition`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.mem_selmerGroupA_of_forall_localRes`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4`.

**Sources.** `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.6, p. 91. The cohomological identification is EllipticCurves Layer 7's; the node proves the explicit equality with Tau Ceti's selmerGroup₂.

<a id="ED-3-rank-upper-bound"></a>

### Certified 2-descent rank upper bound

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/rank-upper-bound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.rank_le_of_twoSelmerCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

Let W be as in the hypotheses and C a two-selmer-certificate with #Sel(C) = 2^{s}. Put t = log₂ #E(ℚ)[2], where #E(ℚ)[2] = 1 + #{x ∈ ℚ : f(x) = 0}. Then rank E(ℚ) ≤ s − t, i.e. 2^{rank E(ℚ)} · #E(ℚ)[2] ≤ #Sel(C). More generally any finite subgroup Σ ≤ M with im μ ≤ Σ gives 2^{rank E(ℚ)}·#E(ℚ)[2] ≤ #Σ. This bound and two-isogeny-rank-bound are the only rank upper bounds the stage certifies for elliptic curves: a list of independent points proves a lower bound and never replaces them.

**Hypotheses.** W : WeierstrassCurve ℚ, elliptic, char-≠-2 normal form, integral coefficients; C : TwoSelmerCertificate W. rank E(ℚ) means Module.finrank ℤ of W.toAffine.Point.

**Proof route.**

- E(ℚ) is finitely generated: Tau Ceti fg_point_of_numberField.
- im μ ≤ Sel(C) by two-selmer-certificate-sound; Sel(C) is finite.
- Apply Tau Ceti pow_rank_le_card_of_range_μ_le with S = Sel(C); the 2-torsion count is card_ker_nsmul_two.
- Take log₂ (the left side is 2^{rank} · 2^{t}).

**Acceptance.** y² = x³ − x: s = 2, t = 2, so rank E(ℚ) = 0. Curves with rational 2-torsion use two-isogeny-rank-bound instead, which can be sharper.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/two-selmer-certificate-sound`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.pow_rank_le_card_of_range_μ_le`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.card_range_μ`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.card_ker_nsmul_two`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.fg_point_of_numberField`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-6-the-mordellweil-theorem-aec-viii`.

**Sources.** `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.6, p. 79. Stated for the image of E(ℚ)/2E(ℚ); with the Selmer group in place of the image it becomes the upper bound of the node.

<a id="ED-3-quartic-local-solubility"></a>

### Certified local solubility test for y² = g(x)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/quartic-local-solubility` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.quarticLocallySoluble` · implementation unchecked.

For g = ax⁴ + bx³ + cx² + dx + e ∈ ℤ[x] squarefree of degree 4 and a place v, quarticLocallySoluble g v ∈ Bool is defined as follows. v = ∞: true iff a > 0 or g has a real root (certified real root isolation). v = p prime: true iff ZpSoluble(g, 0, 0) or ZpSoluble(g*, 0, 1), with g*(x) = x⁴g(1/x) the reversed quartic (points with x ∈ pℤ_p on g* cover x ∉ ℤ_p and the points at infinity). ZpSoluble(g, x_k, k): let ℓ = v_p(g(x_k)), m = v_p(g′(x_k)); for odd p return true if g(x_k) is a p-adic square or (ℓ ≥ m + k and k > m), false unless (ℓ ≥ 2k and m ≥ k), and otherwise return the disjunction of ZpSoluble(g, x_k + t p^k, k + 1) over t = 0,…,p − 1 (Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Lemma 6); for p = 2 the same with the Lemma 7 rules: true if g(x_k) is a 2-adic square, or k > m and either ℓ ≥ m + k, or ℓ = m + k − 1 with ℓ even, or ℓ = m + k − 2 with ℓ even and the odd part of g(x_k) ≡ 1 mod 4; recurse if m ≥ k and either ℓ ≥ 2k or (ℓ = 2k − 2 and the odd part ≡ 1 mod 4); false otherwise. The recursion stops by depth k = v_p(disc g) + 2 at the latest. The reversal uses all five coefficient positions, even when e=0; Polynomial.reverse agrees on degree-four inputs, but reverses a lower-degree reciprocal by that smaller degree when reused. Zero polynomial values are accepted as squares before taking their totalized valuation. Only ∞ or prime places are in the correctness domain; generalized even degrees require a separate extension.

**Hypotheses.** g ∈ ℤ[x] of degree 4 with nonzero discriminant; p prime. p-adic squares are tested exactly: even valuation and unit part a square mod p (odd p) or ≡ 1 mod 8 (p = 2).

**Proof route.**

- Transcribe Cremona's pseudocode (Qp soluble, Zp soluble, lemma6, lemma7) as a structurally recursive function with the depth bound as fuel.
- Termination: by Cremona's footnote, once k > v_p(disc g) (and k ≥ 2 for p = 2) the undecided branch does not occur, so fuel v_p(disc g) + 2 never runs out.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.quarticLocallySoluble_iff` (characterisation): quarticLocallySoluble g v = true ↔ y² = g(x) has a point over ℚ_v on its smooth projective model (affine or at infinity); promoted to quartic-local-solubility-correct.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.quarticLocallySoluble_reverse` (simp): For degree-four g with nonzero discriminant and g.coeff 0 ≠ 0, and v=∞ or a prime, quarticLocallySoluble g v = quarticLocallySoluble g* v. When g.coeff 0=0, g already has the rational point (0,0); the internal reciprocal chart still uses the fixed five-coefficient reversal.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.quarticLocallySoluble_scale` (other): Replacing g(x) by u²g(x) with u ∈ ℤ ∖ {0} does not change the value. Assume degree four, nonzero discriminant and v=∞ or a prime.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.zpSoluble_fuel` (other): Fuel v_p(disc g) + 2 suffices; larger fuel gives the same value. Assume degree-four g, g.discr ≠ 0 and p prime.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.quarticLocallySoluble_of_good` (relation): For odd p ∤ disc g the value is true.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.zpSoluble` (data): The recursive ℤ_p test ZpSoluble(g, x_k, k) of the statement (Lemma 6 rules for odd p, Lemma 7 rules for p = 2), with an explicit fuel argument bounding the recursion depth.

**Tests.**

- `quartic_lind_reichardt_two` (computation): quarticLocallySoluble (2x⁴ − 34) 2 = true and quarticLocallySoluble (2x⁴ − 34) 17 = true.
- `quartic_negative_definite` (degenerate): For g = −x⁴ − 1, the value at ∞ is false and the value at every odd p ∤ disc g is true.
- `quartic_square_leading` (characterisation): If a is a nonzero square then the value is true at every v (points at infinity).
- `quartic_not_mod_p_only` (non-example): Solubility modulo p alone is not the test: y² ≡ 3x⁴ + 3 (mod 3) has the solutions y = 0, yet quarticLocallySoluble (3x⁴ + 3) 3 = false, since 3x⁴ + 3 has odd 3-adic valuation for every x ∈ ℚ_3 and the leading coefficient 3 is not a square.
- `quartic_reverse_zero_constant` (degenerate): The fixed quartic reversal of X⁴+X is X³+1 and its fixed reversal returns X⁴+X. Polynomial.reverse applied to X³+1 would return X³+1 instead.

**Acceptance.** quarticLocallySoluble (2x⁴ − 34) v = true for v = 2, 17 and ∞ (the Lind–Reichardt quartic). quarticLocallySoluble (−x⁴ − 1) ∞ = false.

<a id="ED-3-quartic-local-solubility-correct"></a>

### Correctness of the quartic local solubility test

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/quartic-local-solubility-correct` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.quarticLocallySoluble_iff` · implementation unchecked.

For g ∈ ℤ[x] squarefree of degree 4 and a place v of ℚ, quarticLocallySoluble g v = true if and only if the smooth projective curve y² = g(x) has a ℚ_v-point. For odd p ∤ disc g the answer is true; for the even quartics g = d₁u⁴ + cu² + d₂ of descent via 2-isogeny, disc g = 16·d₁d₂(c² − 4d₁d₂)², so this covers every odd p ∤ d₁d₂(c² − 4d₁d₂). Hence everywhere local solubility is decided by the finitely many places p | 2·disc g and ∞.

**Hypotheses.** g of degree 4 with disc g ≠ 0; v a prime or ∞.

**Proof route.**

- Soundness and completeness of lemma6/lemma7 are Hensel-lemma statements (Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Lemmas 6 and 7 as transcribed by Cremona); a point with x ∈ ℤ_p or with x ∉ ℤ_p is found by the two calls.
- Good odd p: a smooth genus-one curve over 𝔽_p has an 𝔽_p-point (Aitken–Lemmermeyer Lemma 13 for the 2-isogeny quartics, elementary; in general Hasse's bound for the Jacobian, EllipticCurves Layer 3), and a nonsingular point lifts by Hensel's lemma (Aitken–Lemmermeyer Lemma 14).
- The real test is immediate from the intermediate value theorem.

**Acceptance.** The test returns true for 2x⁴ − 34 at 2, 17 and ∞, in agreement with Aitken–Lemmermeyer Theorem 4. For Fermigier's rank-13 curve the test, run over the primes dividing 2dd′, returns n₂ = 256 and n₂′ = 128, the values Cremona reports.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/quartic-local-solubility`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-3-elliptic-curves-over-finite-fields--the-hasse-bound-aec-v1`; `mathlib:Polynomial.discr`.

**Sources.** `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.6, p. 80. Correctness of the transcribed routine. `aitken-lemmermeyer-2011` — Appendix B, Lemma 14, p. 17 (arXiv v1). The lifting step at good odd primes for even quartics.

<a id="ED-3-two-isogeny-descent-map"></a>

### The descent map for a rational 2-isogeny

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/two-isogeny-descent-map` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.twoIsogenyDescentMap` · implementation unchecked.

Let E : y² = x(x² + cx + d) with c, d ∈ ℤ and d(c² − 4d) ≠ 0, and E′ : y² = x(x² + c′x + d′), c′ = −2c, d′ = c² − 4d. The 2-isogenies are φ : E → E′, (x, y) ↦ (y²/x², y(x² − d)/x²) and φ′ : E′ → E, (x, y) ↦ (y²/(4x²), y(x² − d′)/(8x²)), with φ′ ∘ φ = [2]. The descent map α = α_{c,d} : E(ℚ) → ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} sends O ↦ 1, (0,0) ↦ d, and (x, y) ↦ x for x ≠ 0. For a squarefree divisor d₁ of d (positive or negative) put H(d₁, c, d/d₁) : v² = d₁u⁴ + cu² + d/d₁. α is a group homomorphism with kernel φ′(E′(ℚ)); its image lies in the group generated by −1 and the primes dividing d, and consists of classes d₁ for which H(d₁, c, d/d₁) has a rational point; the φ′-Selmer group S^{(φ′)} is the set of d₁ for which H(d₁, c, d/d₁) is everywhere locally soluble. Write n₁ = #α(E(ℚ)), n₂ = #S^{(φ′)}, and n₁′, n₂′ for the same with (c′, d′).

**Hypotheses.** c, d ∈ ℤ with d ≠ 0 and c² − 4d ≠ 0; E and E′ as Mathlib WeierstrassCurve ℚ (a₂ = c, a₄ = d, other coefficients 0).

**Proof route.**

- The formulas for φ, φ′ and the identity φ′ ∘ φ = [2] are polynomial identities checked on Mathlib's affine addition formulas.
- Homomorphism and kernel: two points have the same x modulo squares iff their difference is in φ′(E′(ℚ)) (Cremona p. 85); x = d₁u², v = uy/x gives a rational point of H(d₁, c, d₂), and conversely (u, v) ↦ (d₁u², d₁uv).
- Image in the S-classes: if a prime ℓ ∤ d divides the numerator or denominator of x to an odd power then it divides x² + cx + d to the complementary odd power, impossible since y² = x(x² + cx + d).

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.twoIsogenyDescentMap` (constructor): α as an additive-to-multiplicative homomorphism E(ℚ) → (ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2}).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.twoIsogenyDescentMap_some` (simp): α(x, y) = class of x for x ≠ 0.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.twoIsogenyDescentMap_zero_zero` (simp): α(0, 0) = class of d.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.ker_twoIsogenyDescentMap` (characterisation): ker α = φ′(E′(ℚ)).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.twoIsogenyDescentMap_mem_selmer` (relation): α(P) ∈ S^{(φ′)} = {d₁ : H(d₁, c, d/d₁) everywhere locally soluble}.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.twoIsogeny_comp` (compatibility): φ′ ∘ φ = nsmulAddMonoidHom 2 on E(ℚ), so 2E(ℚ) ≤ φ′(E′(ℚ)).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.twoIsogenyCurve` (data): The Weierstrass curve y² = x(x² + cx + d) over ℚ (a₂ = c, a₄ = d, other coefficients 0); E′ is the same construction for (−2c, c² − 4d).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.twoIsogeny` (data): φ : E(ℚ) → E′(ℚ), (x, y) ↦ (y²/x², y(x² − d)/x²), as a homomorphism of additive groups.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.twoIsogenyDual` (data): φ′ : E′(ℚ) → E(ℚ), (x, y) ↦ (y²/(4x²), y(x² − d′)/(8x²)), as a homomorphism of additive groups.

**Tests.**

- `twoIsogeny_E24` (computation): For c = −1, d = 1 (E24 : y² = x³ − x² + x): n₂ = 1 and n₂′ = 4 with S^{(φ)} = {±1, ±3}.
- `twoIsogeny_identity` (degenerate): α(O) = 1 and α(P) = 1 for every P ∈ φ′(E′(ℚ)); for d a square, α(0,0) = 1.
- `twoIsogeny_x_nonzero` (characterisation): For P = (x, y) with x ≠ 0, α(P) = 1 iff x is a rational square.
- `twoIsogeny_not_x_coordinate_at_zero` (non-example): α(0,0) is the class of d, not of x(0,0) = 0: the naive rule x ↦ x is undefined there; for y² = x³ − 68x, α(0,0) = −17 ≠ 1.

**Acceptance.** For E : y² = x³ − x² + x (c = −1, d = 1): α(E(ℚ)) = {1}, n₁ = 1. For y² = x³ − 68x: α((0,0)) = −68 ≡ −17.

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.add_some`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/quartic-local-solubility`.

**Sources.** `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.6, Method 1, p. 84. Defines E′, φ, φ′ and H(d₁, c, d₂); extraction loses primes and superscripts. `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.6, p. 85. The map α and its inverse on homogeneous spaces.

**Consumers.** Cremona Ch. III §3.6, Method 1 and the pseudocode 'Algorithm for computing rank: rational 2-torsion case': n₁, n₂, n₁′, n₂′ give rank bounds without class groups of cubic fields. Aitken–Lemmermeyer Appendix B: the Lind–Reichardt quartic is H(2, 0, −34) for c = 0, d = −68, an element of S^{(φ′)} outside α(E(ℚ)). ArithmeticDynamics DY.3 (request to ED.3): rank-zero certificates for E15, E17, E24, E40 and Morton's curve.

<a id="ED-3-two-isogeny-rank-bound"></a>

### Rank bounds from descent via 2-isogeny

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/two-isogeny-rank-bound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.rank_eq_of_twoIsogeny` · implementation unchecked.

With the notation of two-isogeny-descent-map write n_i = 2^{e_i}, n_i′ = 2^{e_i′}. Then rank E(ℚ) = rank E′(ℚ) = e₁ + e₁′ − 2. Consequently, with ñ₁ = 2^{ẽ₁} ≤ n₁ the order of the subgroup generated by classes d₁ for which an explicit rational point on H(d₁, c, d/d₁) is exhibited (and the same with primes), ẽ₁ + ẽ₁′ − 2 ≤ rank E(ℚ) ≤ e₂ + e₂′ − 2, where n₂ and n₂′ are computed by quartic-local-solubility at the places dividing 2dd′ and ∞ (all other places are automatic). The lower bound is used only together with an upper bound certificate; rank = e₂ + e₂′ − 2 is certified when ñ₁ = n₂ and ñ₁′ = n₂′.

**Hypotheses.** E, E′, α, α′ as in two-isogeny-descent-map.

**Proof route.**

- φ′ ∘ φ = [2] gives the exact sequence 0 → E′(ℚ)[φ′]/φ(E(ℚ)[2]) → E′(ℚ)/φ(E(ℚ)) → E(ℚ)/2E(ℚ) → E(ℚ)/φ′(E′(ℚ)) → 0, so #E(ℚ)/2E(ℚ) = n₁n₁′/2 if d′ is not a square and n₁n₁′ if d′ is a square (Cremona p. 86).
- #E(ℚ)/2E(ℚ) = 2^{rank} · #E(ℚ)[2] (Tau Ceti AddSubgroup.index_range_nsmul_of_fg with E(ℚ) finitely generated) and #E(ℚ)[2] = 2 or 4 according as d′ is a non-square or a square; so 2^{rank} = n₁n₁′/4.
- α(E(ℚ)) ⊆ S^{(φ′)} gives n₁ ≤ n₂; exhibited points give subgroups of α(E(ℚ)).
- Local solubility outside 2dd′ ∞ is automatic (quartic-local-solubility-correct; Aitken–Lemmermeyer Theorem 5).

**Acceptance.** Cremona, Fermigier's curve c = 36861504658225, d = 1807580157674409809510400: n₁ = n₂ = 256 and n₁′ = n₂′ = 128, so the rank is 13 (fermigier-rank-thirteen). For the five curves of rank-zero-curves, n₂n₂′ = 4, so the rank is 0.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/two-isogeny-descent-map`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/quartic-local-solubility-correct`; `tauceti:AddSubgroup.index_range_nsmul_of_fg`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.fg_point_of_numberField`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.card_ker_nsmul_two`.

**Sources.** `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.6, p. 84. Extraction renders E′ as 'E 0' and e₁′ as 'e01'. `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.6, p. 85. Restricts the local tests to the places dividing 2dd′.

<a id="ED-3-explicit-height-difference-bound"></a>

### Cremona's rational height difference bound

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/explicit-height-difference-bound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.canonicalHeight_sub_half_naiveHeight_mem` · implementation unchecked.

For a nonsingular integral standard Weierstrass equation W over Q with discriminant Δ, j-invariant j and b₂, let 2*=1 if b₂=0 and 2 otherwise. Put μ_C=((log|Δ| + log⁺j)/6 + log⁺(b₂/12) + log(2*))/2, where log⁺t=log max(1,|t|), exactly as Cremona III Proposition 3.5.1 p.77. For every rational point P, in the PINNED Tau Ceti normalization, −h(j)/24−μ_C−961/1000 ≤ P.canonicalHeight−P.naiveHeight/2 ≤ μ_C+107/100. Cremona uses the doubled height and constants 1.922,2.14; divide the entire inequality and μ by two. Δ≠0 follows from IsElliptic; P=O has both heights zero. The number-field extension has now been independently checked in Silverman Theorem1.1, p.725, with its exact absolute height and archimedean weights recorded in suggestedOmissions; its Lean interface remains omitted.

**Hypotheses.** W a nonsingular integral standard Weierstrass equation over Q, with all a_i integral and Δ≠0; P in W.toAffine.Point, including O. Pinned Tau Ceti ĥ is half Cremona’s displayed height; the normalization is established by the actual limit definitions and Cremona footnote3. General K is a separately omitted weighted-height interface, with primary statement now verified.

**Proof route.**

- Read the integral standard-equation over Q hypotheses of Proposition 3.5.1. Use log⁺t=log max(1,|t|), with (log|Δ|+log⁺j)/6 and log⁺(b₂/12) outside that quotient; distinguish log⁺j from the logarithmic height h(j).
- Apply the proposition to 2·P.canonicalHeight and P.naiveHeight and divide by two. Use the pinned canonicalHeight rather than a fresh limiting function.
- Choose an outward rational enclosure of μ_C+h(j)/24+961/1000 and μ_C+107/100 using ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds; propagate through doubling enclosures. No rational result is generalized to a number field without its own source.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.cremonaMu` (data): μ_C=((log|Δ|+log⁺j)/6+log⁺(b₂/12)+log(2*))/2, with log⁺t=log max(1,|t|), for an integral standard equation over Q.

**Acceptance.** On y²=x³+B for nonzero integral B, the constant reduces to μ_C=log|432B²|/12, and the lower/upper constants are μ_C+961/1000 and μ_C+107/100 because j=b₂=0. Dividing the entire displayed Cremona inequality by two gives the pinned bound; O satisfies it with both heights zero. Refines pinned Point.abs_canonicalHeight_sub_naiveHeight_le, whose bound is existential.

**Direct prerequisites.** `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.canonicalHeight`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.naiveHeight`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.abs_canonicalHeight_sub_naiveHeight_le`; `mathlib:NumberField.absLogHeight₁`; `mathlib:Rat.mulHeight₁_eq_max`; `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.0`.

**Sources.** `cremona-1997` — Chapter III, Proposition 3.5.1, printed p.77 (PDF chapter page16), footnote3. Divide the displayed height difference, μ(E),1.922 and2.14 by two to use pinned Tau Ceti canonicalHeight; the 1.922 constant is the Bremner correction recorded in footnote3. `silverman-1990` — Theorem1.1 and Remark1.2, printed p.725; §3 local/global normalization, pp.729–730. The primary theorem supplies μ_S and constants0.973/1.07 in absolute normalization. This separately omitted interface uses pinned relative heights divided by [K:Q].

<a id="ED-3-canonical-height-enclosure"></a>

### Certified enclosure of the canonical height by doubling

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/canonical-height-enclosure` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.canonicalHeightEnclosure` · implementation unchecked.

For W over ℚ with integral coefficients, a point P ∈ E(ℚ) and n ∈ ℕ, canonicalHeightEnclosure W P n λ⁻ λ⁺ c⁻ c⁺ takes four explicit rational inputs and is a closed interval [ℓ, u] with rational endpoints containing ĥ(P) (Tau Ceti canonicalHeight), computed as follows: form Q = 2ⁿ·P exactly in Mathlib's group law over ℚ; if Q = O then ĥ(P) = 0 and the interval is [0,0]; otherwise H = max(|a|, b) for x(Q) = a/b in lowest terms and [λ⁻, λ⁺] ∋ log H is a certified rational enclosure; with nonnegative rational bounds c⁻ ≥ h(j)/24 + μ_C(W) + 961/1000 and c⁺ ≥ μ_C(W) + 107/100 (explicit-height-difference-bound, logs enclosed the same way), ℓ = (λ⁻/2 − c⁻)/4ⁿ and u = (λ⁺/2 + c⁺)/4ⁿ. The width is at most ((λ⁺ − λ⁻)/2 + c⁺ + c⁻)/4ⁿ, with equality when Q≠O. To obtain any requested width choose the ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds log enclosure to have uniformly bounded width (for example ≤1), choose fixed certified c⁻,c⁺, then increase n. No uniform decay is claimed for arbitrarily widening input log intervals. Pairings ⟨P, R⟩ = (ĥ(P + R) − ĥ(P) − ĥ(R))/2 are enclosed by interval arithmetic on three enclosures.

**Hypotheses.** W over ℚ, integral, elliptic; P∈W.toAffine.Point; n∈ℕ. Explicit rational λ⁻≤λ⁺, c⁻≥0, c⁺≥0. Containment requires λ⁻≤naiveHeight(2ⁿP)≤λ⁺ and c⁻≥h(j)/24+μ_C(W)+961/1000, c⁺≥μ_C(W)+107/100. The Q=O branch returns [0,0] without a logarithm evaluation. ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds supplies certified logarithm/error endpoints at requested precision; this exact-arithmetic constructor does not claim that the supplier has been implemented.

**Proof route.**

- ĥ(2ⁿP) = 4ⁿĥ(P) (Tau Ceti Point.canonicalHeight_nsmul), and explicit-height-difference-bound applied to Q = 2ⁿP gives h(Q)/2 − c⁻ ≤ ĥ(Q) ≤ h(Q)/2 + c⁺; divide by 4ⁿ.
- h(Q) = log H by Mathlib Rat.mulHeight₁_eq_max and Tau Ceti Point.naiveHeight_eq_logHeight₁; interval arithmetic by ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds rational-interval-product.
- Only exact rational arithmetic and the logarithm enclosures enter; no floating-point value is trusted.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.canonicalHeight_mem_canonicalHeightEnclosure` (characterisation): For the explicit λ⁻,λ⁺,c⁻,c⁺ with certified log/error inequalities and integral elliptic W, ĥ(P) lies in canonicalHeightEnclosure W P n λ⁻ λ⁺ c⁻ c⁺.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.canonicalHeightEnclosure_width_le` (other): For explicit λ⁻≤λ⁺ and c⁻,c⁺≥0, width(canonicalHeightEnclosure W P n λ⁻ λ⁺ c⁻ c⁺)≤((λ⁺−λ⁻)/2+c⁺+c⁻)/4ⁿ, including the zero branch. No existential unspecified constant replaces this formula.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.canonicalHeightEnclosure_zero` (simp): canonicalHeightEnclosure W 0 n λ⁻ λ⁺ c⁻ c⁺=[0,0] for arbitrary rational inputs.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.canonicalHeightEnclosure_neg` (simp): With the same rational data on both sides, canonicalHeightEnclosure W (−P) n λ⁻ λ⁺ c⁻ c⁺=canonicalHeightEnclosure W P n λ⁻ λ⁺ c⁻ c⁺.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.neronTatePairing_mem_pairingEnclosure` (compatibility): With integral elliptic W, the three certified naive-height log intervals at 2ⁿ(P+Q),2ⁿP,2ⁿQ and the shared certified c⁻,c⁺, pairingEnclosure contains (ĥ(P+Q)−ĥ(P)−ĥ(Q))/2.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.pairingEnclosure` (data): pairingEnclosure W P Q n bounds c⁻ c⁺ uses bounds:Fin3→Q×Q in order P+Q,P,Q, and forms [(I.lower−J.upper−L.upper)/2,(I.upper−J.lower−L.lower)/2] from their three height intervals with the shared error bounds.

**Tests.**

- `enclosure_torsion` (computation): For y²=x³+1 and P=(−1,0) of order2, canonicalHeightEnclosure returns [0,0] for every n≥1 and every supplied rational endpoint/error input.
- `enclosure_origin` (degenerate): At O the constructor returns [0,0] for every n and all four rational inputs.
- `enclosure_contains_tauceti` (compatibility): On y²=x³+1, for any point and n, explicitly certified rational log/error inputs give containment of the pinned half-height canonicalHeight.
- `enclosure_not_naive` (non-example): For P=(2,3) on y²=x³+1, ĥ(P)=0 while naiveHeight(P)/2=log(2)/2>0. At n=0, certified rational λ⁻≤log2≤λ⁺ and c⁻,c⁺ give an interval containing0; the raw naive value alone fails.
- `enclosure_width_budget` (computation): With log endpoints a,a+1/8 and error bounds2,3 the raw interval width is at most81/(16·4ⁿ), including the Q=O branch. This arithmetic regression distinguishes both the factor1/2 on the log width and the factor4ⁿ.

**Acceptance.** For y²=x³−2 and P=(3,5), certify at n=6 a log interval of width≤1 and nonnegative rational errors with (λ⁺−λ⁻)/2+c⁺+c⁻<40; the exact width is then <10⁻². This is a planned ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds producer regression, not a claimed executed approximation. For a point of order 2^k the computation reaches Q = O for n ≥ k and returns [0,0]; for other torsion points the enclosures contain 0 and shrink to {0}.

<a id="ED-3-regulator-lower-bound"></a>

### Independence and regulator lower bound from certified heights

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/regulator-lower-bound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.linearIndependent_of_det_enclosure_pos` · implementation unchecked.

Let P₁,…,P_r ∈ E(ℚ) and let I_{ij} be rational intervals with ⟨P_i, P_j⟩ ∈ I_{ij} (canonical-height-enclosure; ⟨·,·⟩ Tau Ceti's neronTatePairing, ⟨P,P⟩ = ĥ(P)). If the interval determinant of (I_{ij}) has positive lower endpoint δ > 0, then the images of P₁,…,P_r in E(ℚ)/E(ℚ)_tors are ℤ-linearly independent, rank E(ℚ) ≥ r, and det(⟨P_i, P_j⟩) ≥ δ. If moreover P₁,…,P_r is a basis of E(ℚ)/E(ℚ)_tors then Tau Ceti's regulator satisfies regulator ≥ δ.

**Hypotheses.** W over ℚ elliptic with integral coefficients; enclosures from canonical-height-enclosure.

**Proof route.**

- If Σ n_j P_j is torsion with n ≠ 0, then Σ_j ⟨P_i, P_j⟩ n_j = ⟨P_i, Σ_j n_j P_j⟩ = 0 for all i (bilinearity; Tau Ceti neronTatePairing_eq_zero_of_isOfFinAddOrder_right), so the Gram matrix is singular, contradicting det ≥ δ > 0.
- The interval determinant encloses the true determinant (ED.2 rational logarithm/error bounds interval arithmetic soundness), so det ≥ δ.
- For a basis, regulator_eq_abs_det_neronTateGramMatrix identifies the regulator with |det|.

**Acceptance.** Applied to Cremona's rank-two curve y² = x³ − 673 with P₁ = (29, 154) and the second generator printed in §3.6, a positive lower endpoint certifies rank ≥ 2. A single non-torsion point: r = 1 and δ = lower endpoint of the enclosure of ĥ(P₁).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/canonical-height-enclosure`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.neronTatePairing`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.neronTatePairing_eq_zero_of_isOfFinAddOrder_right`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.regulator_eq_abs_det_neronTateGramMatrix`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.neronTateGramMatrix`; `mathlib:Matrix.det`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure`.

**Sources.** `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.5, p. 76. The certified version replaces 'non-zero' by a positive lower endpoint of an interval enclosure.

<a id="ED-3-height-lower-bound-by-search"></a>

### Lower bound for the canonical height of non-torsion points by a certified search

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/height-lower-bound-by-search` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.le_canonicalHeight_of_search` · implementation unchecked.

Let W over ℚ be integral and elliptic, c⁻ a rational upper bound for h(j)/24 + μ_C(E) + 961/1000 (μ_C is cremonaMu, half of Cremona’s μ) (explicit-height-difference-bound), and B > 0. Let L be the finite set of P ∈ E(ℚ) with naiveHeight(P) ≤ B, enumerated completely (ED.0 bounded-height enumeration of x ∈ ℚ with h(x) ≤ B, followed by an exact rational-solubility test for the Weierstrass quadratic in y at each x, together with O). Put λ = min({B/2 − c⁻} ∪ {ℓ_P : P ∈ L non-torsion}), where this finite set is nonempty because it contains B/2 − c⁻, and ℓ_P is the lower endpoint of a canonical-height-enclosure of P. If L contains no non-torsion point, λ=B/2−c⁻. If λ > 0, then ĥ(Q) ≥ λ for every non-torsion Q ∈ E(ℚ).

**Hypotheses.** W, c⁻ and B as stated; torsion of the points of L decided exactly (Q = O at a multiple bounded by 12, Mazur, or by the torsion certificate).

**Proof route.**

- If naiveHeight(Q) > B then ĥ(Q) ≥ naiveHeight(Q)/2 − c⁻ > B/2 − c⁻ ≥ λ by the lower half of explicit-height-difference-bound.
- Otherwise Q ∈ L, and Q non-torsion gives ĥ(Q) ≥ ℓ_Q ≥ λ.
- Take the minimum over the displayed nonempty finite union. The coordinate-enumeration helpers below are separate supporting interfaces for groups with an already supplied free/torsion decomposition; they are not an implementation of the elliptic point search or a proof that its height form is coercive.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.heightCoordinatePoints` (constructor): For an actual group equivalence e:A≃(Z^r)×T with finite torsion T, enumerate all coordinates in [-D,D]^r and every t∈T, transporting through e⁻¹.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.mem_heightCoordinatePoints` (characterisation): P is enumerated iff every free coordinate of e(P) has |a_i|≤D; the torsion coordinate is unrestricted.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.heightCoordinatePoints_complete` (characterisation): Given λ>0 with λΣa_i²≤height(P), and B<λ(D+1)², every P of height≤B belongs to the enumerated list. The Jacobian supplier must derive this λ from its positive-definite Gram form.

**Tests.**

- `heightLowerSearch_empty_nontorsion` (degenerate): If L contains only torsion, the singleton minimum is B/2−c⁻; no minimum of an empty set is taken. The conclusion is conditional on positivity and remains meaningful at rank zero.
- `heightLowerSearch_negative_endpoint` (non-example): If B/2−c⁻=2 and one non-torsion point has certified lower endpoint−1, λ=−1; the positive lower-bound theorem cannot be applied despite every actual non-torsion height being positive.
- `heightCoordinates_rank_zero` (degenerate): For r=0 every point belongs to the sole finite torsion fibre; no positive-dimensional ball-volume theorem is used.
- `heightCoordinates_torsion_fibres` (computation): For Z×Z/2 with D=0 the list has two elements, one for each torsion value.
- `heightCoordinates_kernel_nonexample` (non-example): The zero form on Z has an infinite bounded set, so semidefiniteness alone cannot supply bounded enumeration.

**Acceptance.** Siksek Example5.1: on y²=x³−73705x−7526231 a source search to naive height5, with h−ĥ_source≤0.8215, excludes non-torsion ĥ_source≤4.1. In ED.3 normalization the corresponding error is0.41075 and lower threshold2.05. Replaying this example requires certified outward bounds and complete points/signs, not treating printed decimals as formal certificates. For a rank-zero curve the bound holds vacuously for every λ.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/explicit-height-difference-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/canonical-height-enclosure`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/bounded-height-enumeration`.

**Sources.** `siksek-1995` — Author preprint, §5 Example5.1, p.19; §1 Theorem1.2, p.2. The finite naive-height search excludes small nonzero canonical heights by the explicit difference bound. The source uses full x-height; ED.3 uses half, so halve the source canonical bound and error. Source decimals illustrate the route and are not replayed certificates.

<a id="ED-3-index-bound"></a>

### Index bound from a height lower bound and Minkowski's theorem

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/index-bound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.saturationIndex_le` · implementation unchecked.

Let P₁,…,P_r ∈ E(ℚ) (r ≥ 1) be independent modulo torsion, L their span in E(ℚ)/E(ℚ)_tors, L̄ = {Q : nQ ∈ L for some n ≥ 1} its saturation and n = [L̄ : L]. Let λ > 0 with ĥ(Q) ≥ λ for every non-torsion Q ∈ E(ℚ) (height-lower-bound-by-search), and let γ_r be any constant such that every positive definite real quadratic form in r variables of determinant D takes a value ≤ γ_r·D^{1/r} at some nonzero integral vector; γ_r = (4/π)·Γ(r/2 + 1)^{2/r} is such a constant (Minkowski), and γ₁ = 1, γ₂ = (4/3)^{1/2} are the exact Hermite values. Then n ≤ R^{1/2}·(γ_r/λ)^{r/2}, where R = det(⟨P_i, P_j⟩) in Tau Ceti's normalisation. If rank E(ℚ) = r then L̄ = E(ℚ)/E(ℚ)_tors and n is the index of the subgroup generated by the P_i and the torsion.

**Hypotheses.** P_i independent modulo torsion (e.g. by regulator-lower-bound); λ as stated; any of the listed γ_r.

**Proof route.**

- L̄ is a lattice of rank r with Gram determinant R(L̄) = R/n² (index–covolume relation for the Gram determinant). This is the same Gram-lattice argument as Siksek equation(27), applied to the saturated rational span; that reduction, and the harmless weakening of >λ to ≥λ, are adaptations rather than extra generality printed in Theorem3.1.
- Minkowski's convex-body theorem (Mathlib exists_ne_zero_mem_lattice_of_measure_mul_two_pow_le_measure) for the ellipsoid {x : ĥ(Σ x_i Q_i) ≤ t} in a basis Q_i of L̄, with InnerProductSpace.volume_ball, gives a nonzero Q ∈ L̄ with ĥ(Q) ≤ γ_r R(L̄)^{1/r}.
- Q is non-torsion, so λ ≤ ĥ(Q) ≤ γ_r (R/n²)^{1/r}; solve for n.

**Acceptance.** Rank2 exact numerical regression: R≤9, λ≥1 and γ₂²=4/3 give n²≤12, hence n≤3. This is an arithmetic bound with supplied certified inputs, independent of unavailable Prickett decimals. r = 1: n ≤ (ĥ(P₁)/λ)^{1/2}.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/height-lower-bound-by-search`; `mathlib:MeasureTheory.exists_ne_zero_mem_lattice_of_measure_mul_two_pow_le_measure`; `mathlib:InnerProductSpace.volume_ball`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.neronTatePairingModTorsion_self_eq_zero_iff`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.PointModTorsion`.

**Sources.** `siksek-1995` — Author preprint, §3 equation(27), pp.14–15; Lemmas3.1–3.2, pp.15–16; Theorem3.1, p.16. The source proves the full-rank index bound. Its same positive-definite lattice proof applies to the saturated rational span of r independent points, even when the ambient Mordell–Weil rank is larger. The printed strict lower bound may be weakened to ≥λ because the proof only uses λ≤height(Q). Under height scaling by1/2, R scales by2⁻ʳ and λ by1/2, leaving the index bound unchanged. Lemma3.1 allows the stated Minkowski constant in every positive dimension.

<a id="ED-3-p-saturated"></a>

### p-saturated subgroups

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/p-saturated` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.IsPSaturated` · implementation unchecked.

Let A be an abelian group, G ≤ A a subgroup and p a prime. G is p-saturated in A (IsPSaturated G p) if every a ∈ A with p·a ∈ G lies in G; G is saturated if it is p-saturated for every prime p. Equivalently: A[p] ≤ G and G ∩ pA = pG. If [A : G] is finite, G is p-saturated iff p ∤ [A : G]; G is saturated iff [A : G] = 1.

**Hypotheses.** A an additive commutative group (A = E(ℚ) or J(ℚ) in the applications); G an AddSubgroup; p prime.

**Proof route.**

- The equivalence: if G is p-saturated then A[p] ≤ G (p·t = 0 ∈ G) and pa ∈ G forces a ∈ G; conversely pa = g ∈ G ∩ pA = pG gives g = pg′, so a − g′ ∈ A[p] ≤ G.
- Finite index: if p | [A:G], Cauchy's theorem in A/G gives a ∉ G with pa ∈ G; if p ∤ [A:G] and pa ∈ G, the class of a has order dividing p and [A:G], hence is trivial.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.IsPSaturated` (constructor): IsPSaturated G p holds iff every a ∈ A with p·a ∈ G lies in G.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.isPSaturated_iff` (characterisation): IsPSaturated G p ↔ A[p] ≤ G ∧ G ⊓ (p • ⊤) = p • G.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.isPSaturated_iff_not_dvd_index` (characterisation): For G of finite index and p prime: IsPSaturated G p ↔ ¬ p ∣ G.index.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.isPSaturated_top` (simp): ⊤ is p-saturated.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.IsPSaturated.inf` (structure): The intersection of p-saturated subgroups is p-saturated.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.index_eq_one_of_forall_isPSaturated` (relation): If G has finite index ≤ N and is p-saturated for every prime p ≤ N, then G = ⊤.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.saturation` (data): The saturation Ḡ = {a : ∃ n ≥ 1, n • a ∈ G}, the smallest saturated subgroup containing G.

**Tests.**

- `isPSaturated_six_int` (computation): In ℤ: (6ℤ) is 5-saturated, not 2-saturated, not 3-saturated.
- `isPSaturated_top_any` (degenerate): ⊤ ≤ A is p-saturated for every p.
- `isPSaturated_index_coprime` (compatibility): For G = (6ℤ) ≤ ℤ with AddSubgroup.index = 6: IsPSaturated G p ↔ ¬ p ∣ 6.
- `isPSaturated_torsion_missing` (non-example): In A = ℤ × ℤ/2, G = ℤ × 0 has G ∩ 2A = 2G but is not 2-saturated, since A[2] ⊄ G: the injectivity of G/pG → A/pA alone is not p-saturation.

**Acceptance.** In A = ℤ, G = 6ℤ is 5-saturated but neither 2- nor 3-saturated. G = 0 in ℤ/pℤ is not p-saturated.

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:Subgroup.index`; `mathlib:exists_prime_addOrderOf_dvd_card`.

**Sources.** `siksek-1995` — Author preprint, §4 opening, p.17, equation(39). The source identifies absence of nontrivial p-division of a full-rank free sublattice with p not dividing its index. The node proves the general additive-group reformulation via p-torsion of A/G, explicitly including A[p]⊆G when A has torsion; that additional generality is established by the packet’s elementary proof.

**Consumers.** Prickett Ch. 3: the saturation algorithm proves V_p = 0, i.e. p-saturation of ⟨P₁,…,P_s⟩. EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.5/subgroup-covers-quotient: p-saturation for every p | N is the coprimality gcd([Γ:H], N) = 1 that the sieve needs. Stoll 2008 §3: the saturation Ḡ of G is what Chabauty's differential kills.

<a id="ED-3-saturation-certificate"></a>

### p-saturation from jointly injective reductions

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/saturation-certificate` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.isPSaturated_of_injective_reductions` · implementation unchecked.

Let A be an abelian group, G ≤ A a subgroup with G/pG finite, p a prime, and ψ_i : A → C_i (i = 1,…,m) homomorphisms into abelian groups with pC_i = 0. If (a) the induced map G/pG → ∏_i C_i is injective and (b) A[p] ≤ G, then G is p-saturated in A. Standard choices: ψ_q : A → B_q → B_q/pB_q with B_q = Ẽ(𝔽_q) (resp. J̃(𝔽_q)) the reduction at a prime q of good reduction (EllipticCurves Layer 4; Jacobians by the RP.1 request), useful when p | #B_q; for p = 2 and A = E(ℚ), the descent map μ : E(ℚ) → M (kernel 2E(ℚ)) or its local components. Condition (b) is certified by the torsion certificate (torsion-by-reduction): it holds when A[p] = 0 or when generators of A[p] are among the generators of G.

**Hypotheses.** A abelian; G ≤ A given by generators g₁,…,g_s, so G/pG is spanned by their classes; p prime; ψ_i homomorphisms with p-torsion targets.

**Proof route.**

- Each ψ_i kills pA, hence G ∩ pA ≤ ker(G → ∏ C_i) = pG by (a); so G ∩ pA = pG.
- With (b), p-saturated by the characterisation in p-saturated.
- Practical form (Siksek §4.1): include free generators and a basis of the torsion modulo p; the p-divisible relation space V_p lies in every kernel of the finite reduction maps. If their joint kernel is zero, V_p=0. General p-primary reduction groups are handled by B_q/pB_q, not by assuming p²∤#B_q.
- For p = 2 and μ: Tau Ceti ker_μ_eq gives ker μ = 2E(ℚ), so injectivity of G/2G → M is decided in the explicit square classes.

**Acceptance.** Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer Lemma 6: G = ⟨D⟩ ≤ J(ℚ), p = 3, ψ the reduction J(ℚ) → J(𝔽₃) ≅ ℤ/9 followed by J(𝔽₃)/3J(𝔽₃); D̃ ∉ 3J(𝔽₃) and J(ℚ)[3] = 0, so ⟨D⟩ is 3-saturated. Poonen 1995 Proposition 2: J(𝔽₃) ≅ ℤ/27 generated by D̃, giving 3-saturation of ⟨[∞⁺ − ∞⁻]⟩.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/p-saturated`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.ker_μ_eq`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-4-elliptic-curves-over-local-fields--reduction-tates-algorithm-the-tate-curve-aec-vii-ataec-ivv`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-3-elliptic-curves-over-finite-fields--the-hasse-bound-aec-v1`; `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.1`.

**Sources.** `siksek-1995` — Author preprint, §4.1, pp.17–18, V_p and equation(40). The source includes a basis of torsion modulo p and tests p-divisibility through finite-field reductions. Independent relations kill V_p. The initial cyclic p-Sylow restriction is removed on p.18 by computing the general p-Sylow group. ED.3 states only the sufficient injectivity criterion; it does not assert that reductions always certify saturation. No §4.2 floating-point lattice-membership heuristic is used. `flynn-poonen-schaefer-1997` — §8, proof of Lemma 6, p. 19 (arXiv v1). The sentence continues (rendered page): by D̃, the reduction of D mod 3, we find that D̃ ∉ 3J(𝔽₃), from which it follows that D ∉ 3J(ℚ). An instance with one reduction map.

<a id="ED-3-reduction-rank-lower-bound"></a>

### Rank lower bound from reductions

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/reduction-rank-lower-bound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.le_finrank_of_reduction_image` · implementation unchecked.

Let A be a finitely generated abelian group, G ≤ A, ℓ a prime and ψ_i : A → C_i homomorphisms with ℓC_i = 0. If the image of G in ∏_i C_i has 𝔽_ℓ-dimension k, then rank G ≥ k − dim_{𝔽_ℓ} A[ℓ]; in particular rank A ≥ k when A[ℓ] = 0. If moreover A_tors = 0 (torsion-by-reduction) and G is generated by m elements satisfying m − k independent explicit relations (so rank G ≤ k), then G ≅ ℤ^k.

**Hypotheses.** A finitely generated abelian (E(ℚ), or J(ℚ) by the RP.1 request); ψ_i from reductions as in saturation-certificate.

**Proof route.**

- dim_{𝔽_ℓ} G/ℓG = rank G + dim_{𝔽_ℓ} G[ℓ] ≤ rank G + dim A[ℓ] (structure of finitely generated abelian groups).
- G/ℓG surjects onto the image of G in ∏ C_i, so dim G/ℓG ≥ k.

**Acceptance.** Stoll 2008 Lemma 4: the degree-0 subgroup of ⊕ℤP_i maps onto (ℤ/3)³ in ∏_{q∈{3,5,7,11,13}} Pic(C/𝔽_q), J(ℚ) is torsion-free, so rank G ≥ 3; six explicit relations give rank G ≤ 3.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/p-saturated`; `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.1`; `mathlib:Module.finrank`.

**Sources.** `stoll-2008` — §3, proof of Lemma 4, p. 8 (arXiv v2). The node abstracts this argument.

<a id="ED-3-torsion-by-reduction"></a>

### Certified torsion subgroups

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/torsion-by-reduction` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.torsion_eq_of_reduction_bounds` · implementation unchecked.

(a) Let A be an abelian group and, for primes q₁,…,q_k, ρ_i : A → B_i homomorphisms into finite groups that are injective on torsion of order prime to q_i. Then for every prime ℓ, v_ℓ(#A_tors) ≤ min{v_ℓ(#B_i) : q_i ≠ ℓ}; if an explicit finite subgroup T₀ ≤ A_tors attains these bounds for all ℓ, then A_tors = T₀. (b) For E/ℚ in the model y² = x³ + ax² + bx + c (a = b₂, b = 8b₄, c = 16b₆, integral), every torsion point has x, y ∈ ℤ and y = 0 or y² | Δ₀ = 27c² + 4a³c + 4b³ − a²b² − 18abc; enumerating these candidates and computing orders gives E(ℚ)_tors exactly (Cremona's algorithm). Reduction at good odd q is injective on E(ℚ)_tors (EllipticCurves Layer 6); for Jacobians of curves over ℚ with good reduction at q, reduction is injective on torsion of order prime to q, and on all torsion for q ≥ 3 (requested from RP.1).

**Hypotheses.** (a) A abelian, B_i finite, and for every prime ℓ there is at least one i with q_i ≠ ℓ; this makes each displayed minimum nonempty and bounds every primary torsion subgroup. (b) W over ℚ elliptic, coefficients integral.

**Proof route.**

- (a) The ℓ-primary part of A_tors embeds into B_i whenever q_i ≠ ℓ (Subgroup.card_dvd_of_injective).
- (b) Lutz–Nagell (Cremona Prop. 3.3.1) and Prop. 3.3.2: if 2P = O then y = 0; otherwise P and 2P are integral and the tangent slope is integral, so y | f′(x) and y² | Δ₀ by the displayed identity; orders by repeated addition until O or a non-integral point (at most 12 steps by Mazur).

**Acceptance.** Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer Prop. 6: #J(𝔽₃) = 9, #J(𝔽₅) = 41, so J(ℚ)_tors = 0. Stoll Lemma 4(1): #J(𝔽₇) = 2·7·11·47, #J(𝔽₁₃) = 3·17·23·43, so J(ℚ)_tors = 0. E11 : y² + y = x³ − x²: the algorithm on y² = x³ − 4x² + 16 finds exactly four nonzero torsion points, all of order 5, so E(ℚ)_tors ≅ ℤ/5.

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:Subgroup.card_dvd_of_injective`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-6-the-mordellweil-theorem-aec-viii`; `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.1`.

**Sources.** `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.3, Propositions 3.3.1–3.3.2, pp. 69–70. Extraction flattens the exponents (y₁², c², a³, b³, a²b²). `flynn-poonen-schaefer-1997` — §7, Proposition 6, p. 15 (arXiv v1). As used there with p = 3, 5 (odd primes; at p = 2 only odd torsion injects). `stoll-2008` — §3, proof of Lemma 4, p. 8 (arXiv v2). Form (a) of the node.

<a id="ED-3-finite-index-subgroup-certificate"></a>

### Certified finite-index subgroup of a Mordell–Weil group

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/finite-index-subgroup-certificate` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.FiniteIndexSubgroupCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

Let A be a finitely generated abelian group (A = J(ℚ) for the Jacobian J of a smooth proper curve over ℚ with a rational point, finite generation from RP.1; or A = E(ℚ)) and Π a finite set of primes. A finite-index subgroup certificate (FiniteIndexSubgroupCertificate A Π) consists of: generators g₁,…,g_s ∈ A of G = ⟨g_i⟩; a natural number r with a certificate of rank A ≤ r (an algebraic descent bound: rank-upper-bound, two-isogeny-rank-bound or genus-two-descent-rank-bound) and a certificate of rank G ≥ r (regulator-lower-bound or reduction-rank-lower-bound); the torsion subgroup A_tors as an explicit finite list (torsion-by-reduction); and for each p ∈ Π a p-saturation certificate for G (saturation-certificate). Consequences: rank G = rank A = r, [A : G] is finite and coprime to every p ∈ Π. A rank upper bound that rests on an unproved hypothesis (for instance the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture) is not a field of the certificate: a theorem using it states the hypothesis rank A ≤ r explicitly.

**Hypotheses.** A an additive commutative group with AddGroup.FG A; Π a finite set of primes.

**Proof route.**

- Finite index: rank G = rank A for a subgroup of a finitely generated abelian group (Module.finrank ℤ) gives A/G finite.
- Coprimality: p-saturated with finite index ⇔ p ∤ [A:G] (p-saturated).

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.FiniteIndexSubgroupCertificate.subgroup` (data): G = AddSubgroup.closure (range g).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.FiniteIndexSubgroupCertificate.finrank_eq` (projection): Module.finrank ℤ A = r.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.FiniteIndexSubgroupCertificate.finiteIndex` (instance): G.FiniteIndex.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.FiniteIndexSubgroupCertificate.coprime_index` (characterisation): For p ∈ Π, Nat.Coprime G.index p.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.FiniteIndexSubgroupCertificate.torsion_eq` (characterisation): The listed torsion is exactly the set of a ∈ A of finite order.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.FiniteIndexSubgroupCertificate.coprime_index_prod` (compatibility): Nat.Coprime G.index N for N a product of primes of Π: the hypothesis of ED.5/subgroup-covers-quotient.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.FiniteIndexSubgroupCertificate.ofMordellWeilBasis` (constructor): A Mordell–Weil basis certificate gives a certificate with G = A for every Π.

**Tests.**

- `finiteIndexCert_fps` (computation): For C₀(5): G = ⟨[∞⁺ − ∞⁻]⟩, r = 1, Π = {3}; coprime_index gives 3 ∤ [J(ℚ):G].
- `finiteIndexCert_rank_zero` (degenerate): If r = 0 and G = A_tors then G = A and the certificate holds for every Π.
- `finiteIndexCert_index_one` (compatibility): If Π contains every prime ≤ N and [A:G] ≤ N then G = A, the Mordell–Weil basis certificate.
- `finiteIndexCert_independent_points_only` (non-example): Independent points P₁,…,P_r without a rank upper bound do not give a certificate: for Stoll's X₀^dyn(6), G ≅ ℤ³ is certified but rank J(ℚ) ≤ 3 is only conditional, so finite index is not certified.

**Acceptance.** Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer: A = J(ℚ) for C₀(5), G = ⟨[∞⁺ − ∞⁻]⟩, r = 1, A_tors = 0, Π = {3}. Rank-zero elliptic curves: G = E(ℚ)_tors, r = 0, Π = all primes (G = A).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/rank-upper-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/two-isogeny-rank-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/genus-two-descent-rank-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/regulator-lower-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/reduction-rank-lower-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/torsion-by-reduction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/saturation-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/p-saturated`; `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.1`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-d-the-relative-picard-functor-and-the-jacobian-scheme`.

The object consumed by Chabauty and the Mordell–Weil sieve when the index is known only to be prime to given primes. `siksek-2010` — §5, pp. 10–11 (arXiv:1010.2603v2). The sentence continues: in J(K) is not divisible by any given small prime p. The coprimality field of the certificate. `stoll-2008` — §1, p. 2 (arXiv v2). The interface the certificate packages.

<a id="ED-3-mordell-weil-basis-certificate"></a>

### Certified Mordell–Weil basis

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/mordell-weil-basis-certificate` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.eq_top_of_mordellWeilBasisCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

Let W over ℚ be elliptic with integral coefficients, T = E(ℚ)_tors certified (torsion-by-reduction), and P₁,…,P_r ∈ E(ℚ). Assume: (i) rank E(ℚ) ≤ r (rank-upper-bound or two-isogeny-rank-bound); (ii) det(⟨P_i, P_j⟩) ≥ δ > 0 (regulator-lower-bound); (iii) λ > 0 with ĥ ≥ λ on non-torsion points (height-lower-bound-by-search) and N = ⌊R⁺^{1/2}(γ_r/λ)^{r/2}⌋ with R⁺ an upper endpoint for det(⟨P_i,P_j⟩) (index-bound); (iv) G = ⟨T, P₁,…,P_r⟩ is p-saturated in E(ℚ) for every prime p ≤ N (saturation-certificate). Then E(ℚ) = G = T ⊕ ℤP₁ ⊕ … ⊕ ℤP_r, rank E(ℚ) = r and regulator(E) = det(⟨P_i, P_j⟩). The four inputs are each required: the conclusion combines an upper and a lower bound only when both certificates exist. For r=0, use the algebraic rank bound and complete torsion directly; the positive-dimensional index formula and γ_r are required only for r≥1.

**Hypotheses.** As listed; T given as an explicit finite set of points.

**Proof route.**

- (i) and (ii) give rank E(ℚ) = r and finite index of G (finite-index-subgroup-certificate).
- [E(ℚ) : G] = [E(ℚ)/T : L] ≤ N by index-bound, since G ⊇ T.
- A prime p dividing [E(ℚ):G] satisfies p ≤ N and contradicts p-saturation (p-saturated: finite index and p-saturated ⇒ p ∤ index); so the index is 1.
- The regulator is |det| on a basis (Tau Ceti regulator_eq_abs_det_neronTateGramMatrix).

**Acceptance.** y² = x³ − x: r = 0, T = E[2], G = T = E(ℚ) (index bound vacuous). Cremona's rank-one strategy (§3.5) is the case r = 1: if λ > R⁺/4, with R⁺ ≥ ĥ(P₁) the upper endpoint used in (iii), then N = 1 and P₁ generates E(ℚ) modulo torsion.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/finite-index-subgroup-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/index-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/saturation-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/regulator-lower-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/rank-upper-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/torsion-by-reduction`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.regulator_eq_abs_det_neronTateGramMatrix`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.regulator`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/two-isogeny-rank-bound`.

**Sources.** `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.5, p. 75. The node certifies the closing of that gap. `siksek-1995` — Author preprint, §4 opening, p.17, finite prime/index criterion. The upper bound makes the prime checks finite. Eliminating every p≤bound proves index1 by elementary finite-index arithmetic. The node does not use §4.2 floating-point membership recognition or its projective enumeration. Rank0 needs complete torsion and rank0, without a positive-dimensional Hermite constant.

<a id="ED-3-genus-two-descent-rank-bound"></a>

### Rank bound for genus-two Jacobians by the x − T descent

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/genus-two-descent-rank-bound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.finrank_jacobian_le_of_xMinusT` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, let C : y² = f(x) with f ∈ ℤ[x] separable of degree 6, C(ℚ) ≠ ∅, J its Jacobian, L = ℚ[T]/(f) and L_K = K[T]/(f) for K = ℚ or ℚ_v. (a) The map x − T sending the class of a good divisor Σ n_P P to Π (x_P − T)^{n_P} is a well-defined homomorphism J(K) → L_K^×/(L_K^{×2}K^×) with image in the kernel of the norm to K^×/K^{×2}; (b) for S ⊇ {2, ∞} ∪ {p | disc f}, the image of J(ℚ) lies in the subgroup H of classes unramified outside S with square norm, and in H′ = {h ∈ H : the image of h in L_p^×/(L_p^{×2}ℚ_p^×) lies in (x − T)(J(ℚ_p)) for all p ∈ S}; (c) [ker(x − T) : 2J(K)] = 1 if f has a root in K or the six roots admit a Gal(K^sep/K)-stable partition into two unordered triples, and 2 otherwise; (d) #J(ℚ_p)/2J(ℚ_p) = |2|_p^{-2}·#J(ℚ_p)[2]. Hence rank J(ℚ) ≤ dim_{𝔽₂} H′ + log₂[ker(x − T) : 2J(ℚ)] − dim_{𝔽₂} J(ℚ)[2].

**Hypotheses.** C, J as stated; J(ℚ) finitely generated (RP.1 request); local images (x − T)(J(ℚ_p)) certified by the method of local-descent-image with the count (d). The finite class/unit presentation used by the descent is supplied with exact basis/ideal relations and a proof of full generation; the theorem deduces the rank bound from these inputs and local images.

**Proof route.**

- (a) Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer Prop. 2 (linear equivalence changes the value by squares times constants; the norm is a square).
- (b) Prop. 3 and diagram (6).
- (c) Prop. 5: ker(x − T)/2J(K) is generated by [2P − ∞⁺ − ∞⁻]; it lies in 2J(K) iff one of its 16 halves is K-rational, which is the stated Galois condition.
- (d) multiplication by 2 is n-to-1 on J(ℚ_p) and multiplies Haar measure by |2|_p^2 (Lemma 3); the Lie-group structure is the RP.1 request.
- #J(ℚ)/2J(ℚ) = 2^{rank}·#J(ℚ)[2] ≤ #H′·[ker : 2J(ℚ)].

**Acceptance.** C₀(5) (fps-genus-two-mordell-weil): H′ = 0 and [ker : 2J(ℚ)] = 2, so rank J(ℚ) ≤ 1.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/local-descent-image`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/two-selmer-certificate`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-d-the-relative-picard-functor-and-the-jacobian-scheme`; `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.1`.

**Sources.** `flynn-poonen-schaefer-1997` — §5, Proposition 2, p. 10 (arXiv v1). The target is the kernel of the norm from L_K^×/L_K^{×2}K^× to K^×/K^{×2}; the extraction garbles the groups. `flynn-poonen-schaefer-1997` — §5, Proposition 5, p. 12 (arXiv v1). Gives the index-one criterion for 2J(K) inside ker(x−T), using either a K-rational root of f or a Galois-stable unordered partition of its six roots into two subsets of size three. `flynn-poonen-schaefer-1997` — §7, proof of Lemma 3, p. 16 (arXiv v1). Part (d); exponents flattened by extraction.

<a id="ED-3-lind-reichardt-torsor"></a>

### The Lind–Reichardt curve: a nontrivial torsor class

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/lind-reichardt-torsor` · application · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.lindReichardt_selmer_not_image` · implementation unchecked.

Under the explicit arithmetic-data hypotheses below, the genus-one curve C : 2z² = x⁴ − 17y⁴ (equivalently U² − 17W² = 2Z², UW = V², or v² = 2u⁴ − 34 with v = 2z/y², u = x/y) has points over ℝ and over every ℚ_p but no rational point. In the 2-isogeny descent for E : y² = x³ − 68x (c = 0, d = −68), C is the homogeneous space H(2, 0, −34); hence the class 2 ∈ ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} lies in the φ′-Selmer group S^{(φ′)} but not in α(E(ℚ)). The quartic's invariants are I = 12·2·(−34) = −816 and J = 0, so its Jacobian is Y² = X³ + 22032X ≅ y² = x³ + 17x (22032 = 6⁴·17), the curve E′ : y² = x³ + 272x up to isomorphism; under the RP.1 identification of S^{(φ′)}/α(E(ℚ)) with Ш(E′/ℚ)[φ′], C is a nonzero element of Ш(E′/ℚ)[2].

**Hypotheses.** Places: ∞, 2 and 17 are the only places where local solubility needs a computation (quartic-local-solubility-correct). Supply the finite local lifting witnesses at2,17,∞ and the exact residue fourth-power table mod17 (or invoke the cited conic theorem instead). Verify them as finite identities. Prove global insolubility by the quartic-residue obstruction, not by assuming a missing rational point list.

**Proof route.**

- Local solubility: quarticLocallySoluble (2u⁴ − 34) v = true for v ∈ {2, 17, ∞} (certified run of quartic-local-solubility); Aitken–Lemmermeyer Theorem 4 with q = 17, d = 2 proves the same by conics.
- No global point: Aitken–Lemmermeyer Lemma 6 — a nontrivial solution forces 2 to be a fourth power modulo 17, but the fourth powers modulo 17 are {1, 4, 13, 16}.
- Descent reading: H(d₁, c, d/d₁) with d₁ = 2, c = 0, d = −68 is v² = 2u⁴ − 34 (two-isogeny-descent-map); everywhere local solubility puts 2 in S^{(φ′)}, the absence of rational points keeps it out of α(E(ℚ)).
- Jacobian: Cremona (3.6.3), E_{I,J} : Y² = X³ − 27IX − 27J with I = 12ae − 3bd + c², J = 72ace + 9bcd − 27ad² − 27eb² − 2c³ for (a,b,c,d,e) = (2,0,0,0,−34).

**Acceptance.** The curve passes the certified local tests at 2, 17 and ∞, and the φ′-Selmer computation for c = 0, d = −68 returns n₂ = 8 (all classes ±1, ±2, ±17, ±34), while α(E(ℚ)) omits 2. The torsor class is labelled as an element of the explicit Selmer group; its Ш reading uses the cohomological identification requested from RP.1, not an assumption.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/two-isogeny-descent-map`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/quartic-local-solubility-correct`; `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.1`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4`.

**Sources.** `aitken-lemmermeyer-2011` — §6, Example 3, p. 12 (arXiv v1). Theorem 4 gives local solubility everywhere and no global solution. `aitken-lemmermeyer-2011` — §7, Lemma 11, p. 14 (arXiv v1). Transfers solubility between the system and the quartic X⁴ − 17Y⁴ = 2Z². `aitken-lemmermeyer-2011` — Appendix B, pp. 16–17 (arXiv v1). With a = 1, b = 0, c = −17, d = 2 the formula gives y² = x³ + 272x; the printed specialisation 'y² = x³ − 2⁴17x' has the wrong sign (sourceIssue EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E10). `cremona-1997` — Ch. III, §3.6, p. 79. The descent interpretation of the torsor.

<a id="ED-3-fps-genus-two-mordell-weil"></a>

### Mordell–Weil group of the Jacobian of C₀(5) (Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/fps-genus-two-mordell-weil` · application · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.fps_C05_certificate` · implementation unchecked.

Under the explicit arithmetic-data hypotheses below, for C₀(5) : y² = x⁶ + 8x⁵ + 22x⁴ + 22x³ + 5x² + 6x + 1 with Jacobian J: J(ℚ) ≅ ℤ, and D = [∞⁺ − ∞⁻] generates a subgroup of index prime to 3. As a finite-index-subgroup-certificate with Π = {3}: generators {D}; r = 1; J(ℚ)_tors = 0; ⟨D⟩ 3-saturated. Certified ingredients: (i) torsion: #J(𝔽₃) = 9, #J(𝔽₅) = 41; (ii) rank ≤ 1: genus-two-descent-rank-bound with S = {2, 3701, ∞}, L of class number 1 with units u₁, u₂, u₃ (explicit supplied class/unit/factorization data certificate), H spanned by u₁ and u₃β₁β₂, local images at 2 and 3701 generated by [(2, √881) − ∞⁻] and [(−4, √185) − ∞⁻], H′ = 0, and [ker(x − T) : 2J(ℚ)] = 2 because the Galois group of f is S₆; (iii) rank ≥ 1: D ≠ 0 and J(ℚ)_tors = 0; (iv) 3-saturation: J(𝔽₃) ≅ ℤ/9 is generated by D̃, so D̃ ∉ 3J(𝔽₃).

**Hypotheses.** J(ℚ) finitely generated (RP.1 request); reduction at 3 and 5 (RP.1 request). Supply the exact finite groups J(F3),J(F5), their full divisor-class tables and reduction identifications, the6-degree field/integral-basis/class/full-unit and prime-factorization data with generation/completeness identities, and the local2-descent image tables with lifting witnesses. Supply the finite Galois identification and D-reduction coordinates. These are inputs to the descent/torsion/saturation theorems; their numerical production is not targeted.

**Proof route.**

- (i) torsion-by-reduction (a) with q = 3, 5.
- (ii) Lemmas 1–5 and Theorem 3 of Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer, each step an instance of genus-two-descent-rank-bound; f(2) = 881 ≡ 1 mod 8 and (185/3701) = 1 certify the local points.

### Mordell–Weil data for the Jacobian of C₁(3₂) (Poonen)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/poonen-genus-two-mordell-weil` · application · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.poonen_C32_partial_certificate` · implementation unchecked.

Under the explicit arithmetic-data hypotheses below, for C : y² = g(x) = x⁶ − 2x⁴ + 2x³ + 5x² + 2x + 1 with Jacobian J: J(ℚ)_tors = 0 (#J(𝔽₃) = 27, #J(𝔽₅) = 43), D = [∞⁺ − ∞⁻] has infinite order (rank J(ℚ) ≥ 1), and D ∉ 3J(ℚ) because J(𝔽₃) ≅ ℤ/27 is generated by D̃. The rank upper bound rank J(ℚ) ≤ 1, which would make ⟨D⟩ a finite-index subgroup of index prime to 3, is not certified: the printed proof uses a 743-adic point (2, √33), but g(2) = 73 and the point on C is (−2, √33); the author's erratum states that the 2-adic information is needed and that the result is unchanged, without printing the corrected computation (gap).

**Hypotheses.** J(ℚ) finitely generated and reduction at 3, 5 (RP.1 request). Supply exact finite J(F3),J(F5) groups, their complete divisor/reduction tables and D-reduction coordinates with geometric compatibility. The corrected2/743-adic descent tables are additional explicit inputs for any rank-upper-bound conclusion, not supplied by the invalid printed point; without them retain only the torsion/lower-bound/saturation conclusions.

**Proof route.**

- Torsion and rank ≥ 1: torsion-by-reduction (a).
- 3-saturation of ⟨D⟩: saturation-certificate with J(ℚ) → J(𝔽₃)/3J(𝔽₃).
- Upper bound: genus-two-descent-rank-bound with S = {2, 743, ∞} and the corrected local data at 743 and 2; this computation is the recorded gap.

**Acceptance.** g(2) = 73 and g(−2) = 33, and (73/743) = −1, so the printed local point is not even a 743-adic point (checked by exact arithmetic). Answers part (b) of the ArithmeticDynamics request except the rank upper bound.

### The subgroup of known points on X₀^dyn(6), with the conditional rank input labelled

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/stoll-genus-four-subgroup` · application · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.stoll_X0dyn6_subgroup` · implementation unchecked.

Under the explicit arithmetic-data hypotheses below, let C = X₀^dyn(6) (genus 4, model G(u,w) = 0 in ℙ¹ × ℙ¹) with Jacobian J and ten known rational points P₀,…,P₉. Certified (algebraic): J(ℚ)_tors = 0 (#J(𝔽₇) = 2·7·11·47, #J(𝔽₁₃) = 3·17·23·43), and the subgroup G generated by the classes of degree-0 divisors supported on P₀,…,P₉ is ≅ ℤ³ (lower bound: reduction-rank-lower-bound with ℓ = 3 and S = {3,5,7,11,13}; upper bound: six explicit linear equivalences). Conditional (analytic, labelled separately): if L(J, s) extends to an entire function with the standard functional equation, the weak Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture holds for J, and L‴(J,1) ≠ 0 is certified, then rank J(ℚ) ≤ 3. Stoll reports L‴(C,1) ≈ 0.83601 numerically and L,L′,L″ vanishing to working precision; these approximations alone are not a proof of the additional nonvanishing hypothesis. Under the hypothesis rank J(ℚ) = 3, G has finite index and J(ℚ) is the saturation Ḡ of G; Stoll's Chabauty step uses Ḡ directly, so no p-saturation certificate is needed or provided by the source.

**Hypotheses.** Hypothesis for the conditional part, stated explicitly and never as a certificate field: rank J(ℚ) ≤ 3. An analytic derivation of rank≤3 additionally requires a certified L‴(J,1)≠0, hence analytic order≤3; numerical vanishing of lower derivatives is not needed for this upper bound and is not certified here. Supply the exact finite Picard/reduction groups and point images at3,5,7,11,13, full order tables, the relation matrices and the actual rational functions proving the six divisor equivalences. An analytic rank bound additionally assumes an identified third-derivative enclosure excluding0, analytic continuation/functional equation and weak BSD. No local-group or L-value table producer is targeted.

**Proof route.**

- Torsion: torsion-by-reduction (a) with q = 7, 13.
- rank G ≥ 3: the degree-0 part of ⊕ℤP_i surjects onto (ℤ/3)³ in ∏_{q ∈ S} Pic(C/𝔽_q); rank G ≤ 3: the six relations (e.g. P₀ + P₆ + P₈ ∼ P₁ + P₇ + P₉), each certified by an explicit rational function.
- Conditional rank: Stoll §4 and Theorem 7; the numerical L-value is not a certified enclosure and the hypotheses are open, so this input never enters a FiniteIndexSubgroupCertificate.

**Acceptance.** Answers the ArithmeticDynamics request on X₀^dyn(6) with the exact split: G ≅ ℤ³ certified; finite index and J(ℚ) = Ḡ only under rank J(ℚ) = 3. Acceptance of the stage: conditional analytic-rank input is labelled separately from algebraic rank certification.

## ED.4 — Classical Chabauty–Coleman

**Planets.** p-adic abelian logarithm; Annihilating differentials; Chabauty's theorem; Coleman's bound; Chabauty–Coleman certificate; Relative symmetric Chabauty.

<a id="ED-4-good-reduction-chabauty-datum"></a>

### Good-reduction Chabauty datum: curve, base point, smooth model and residue discs

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/good-reduction-chabauty-datum` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED4.GoodReductionChabautyDatum` · implementation unchecked.

A good-reduction Chabauty datum (X, O, p, 𝒳) consists of a smooth projective geometrically integral curve X over ℚ of genus g ≥ 1, given by explicit equations; a rational point O ∈ X(ℚ); a prime p; and a smooth projective curve 𝒳 → Spec ℤ_p with geometrically connected fibres together with an isomorphism 𝒳_{ℚ_p} ≅ X_{ℚ_p}. Derived data, fixed by the definition: (i) the special fibre X̃ := 𝒳_{𝔽_p}, a smooth projective geometrically integral curve of genus g over 𝔽_p, and X̃(𝔽_p) its finite set of rational points; (ii) the reduction map red : X(ℚ_p) = 𝒳(ℤ_p) → X̃(𝔽_p) (the equality by the valuative criterion of properness), surjective by Hensel's lemma; (iii) for x̃ ∈ X̃(𝔽_p) the residue disc D(x̃) := red⁻¹(x̃) ⊆ X(ℚ_p), and a local parameter t_x̃, a function regular on a Zariski neighbourhood of x̃ in 𝒳 whose restriction to X̃ is a uniformiser at x̃; t_x̃ maps D(x̃) bijectively onto pℤ_p and, for every finite extension K/ℚ_p, the points of 𝒳(O_K) reducing to x̃ bijectively onto the maximal ideal m_K, the coordinates of the inverse being power series with ℤ_p-coefficients; (iv) the Jacobian J of X with the Abel–Jacobi embedding ι_O : X → J, P ↦ [P − O]; (v) the relative Jacobian 𝒥 := Pic⁰_{𝒳/ℤ_p}, an abelian scheme with 𝒥_{ℚ_p} ≅ J_{ℚ_p} and special fibre J̃ = Jac(X̃), and the reduction map red_J : J(ℚ_p) = 𝒥(ℤ_p) → J̃(𝔽_p) with red_J ∘ ι_O = ι_Õ ∘ red; its kernel is J¹(ℚ_p); (vi) the good-reduction pair (𝒳, Ō) of ColemanIntegration, Ō the closure of O, a section of 𝒳 → Spec ℤ_p and hence finite étale of degree one. The same definition is made over the ring of integers O_v of a completion K_v of a number field K at a finite place v, with 𝔽_p replaced by the residue field k_v and pℤ_p by the maximal ideal of O_v.

**Hypotheses.** X smooth, projective, geometrically integral over ℚ (or over a number field K), genus g ≥ 1; O ∈ X(ℚ). 𝒳 smooth and projective over ℤ_p (resp. O_v) with generic fibre identified with X_{ℚ_p} (resp. X_{K_v}); this is the meaning of 'p is a prime of good reduction' throughout ED.4. Points of X̃ are taken over 𝔽_p unless a finite extension is named; residue discs of non-rational points of X̃ contain no ℚ_p-points.

**Proof route.**

- Reduction: X is proper, so X(ℚ_p) = 𝒳(ℤ_p) and each point reduces to a point of X̃(𝔽_p); smoothness of 𝒳 and Hensel's lemma make red surjective (McCallum–Poonen §5.2(1)).
- Residue discs: a local parameter t_x̃ restricts to a formal coordinate of the completed local ring of 𝒳 at x̃, ℤ_p[[t]] after completion, so points of D(x̃) correspond to t ∈ pℤ_p (Siksek Lemma 3.1(iii)); this is the ℚ_p-point version of ColemanIntegration:L1/residue-disc-parametrisation for the pair (𝒳, Ō).
- Jacobian model: 𝒥 = Pic⁰_{𝒳/ℤ_p} is an abelian scheme of relative dimension g (JacobianChallengePartII:JC1/relative-jacobian) whose fibres are the Jacobians of the fibres (JC1/jacobian-base-change); the section Ō gives the Abel–Jacobi morphism 𝒳 → 𝒥 extending ι_O, which yields red_J ∘ ι_O = ι_Õ ∘ red.
- The section Ō is finite étale of degree one over ℤ_p, so (𝒳, Ō) satisfies the hypotheses of ColemanIntegration:L1/good-reduction-pair.

**API.**

- `GoodReductionChabautyDatum.red` (projection): red : X(ℚ_p) → X̃(𝔽_p), P ↦ reduction of the unique extension Spec ℤ_p → 𝒳 of P.
- `GoodReductionChabautyDatum.red_surjective` (characterisation): red is surjective.
- `GoodReductionChabautyDatum.residueDisc` (constructor): D(x̃) := red⁻¹(x̃); the residue discs over x̃ ∈ X̃(𝔽_p) partition X(ℚ_p).
- `GoodReductionChabautyDatum.localParam_bijOn` (characterisation): For a local parameter t_x̃ the map P ↦ t_x̃(P) is a bijection D(x̃) → pℤ_p, with inverse given by power series in ℤ_p[[t]].
- `GoodReductionChabautyDatum.redJ_comp_abelJacobi` (compatibility): red_J(ι_O(P)) = ι_Õ(red P) for P ∈ X(ℚ_p); in particular ι_O(Q') − ι_O(Q) ∈ J¹(ℚ_p) when red Q = red Q'.
- `GoodReductionChabautyDatum.toGoodReductionPair` (coercion): The good-reduction pair (𝒳, Ō) of ColemanIntegration:L1/good-reduction-pair, whose residue discs over 𝔽_p-points meet X(ℚ_p) in the D(x̃).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED4.ReductionDiscData` (structure): Supporting abstract reduction maps, compatible set map to J, and chosen disc parameters; does not assert smooth curve or geometric Abel–Jacobi properties.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED4.ReductionDiscData.baseResidueDisc` (projection): A residue label and its fibre as a set. This product is not the Coleman good-reduction pair.

**Tests.**

- `datum_C05_three` (computation): For y² = x⁶ + 8x⁵ + 22x⁴ + 22x³ + 5x² + 6x + 1 and p = 3 the two-chart Weierstrass model is smooth over ℤ_3 and X̃(𝔽_3) = {∞⁺, ∞⁻, (0, 1), (0, −1)}: four residue discs.
- `datum_MP_example_one` (computation): For y² = x(x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 5)(x − 6) and p = 7, X̃(𝔽_7) = {(0,0), (1,0), (2,0), (5,0), (6,0), (3,6), (3,−6), ∞}, eight residue discs.
- `datum_elliptic_three` (degenerate): For y²=x³−x over F₃ the genus-one special fibre has four points including infinity. Full disc charts require the geometric factory; infinity is a full formal disc, never an isolated Option.none.
- `datum_not_smooth_at_five` (non-example): The model y² = x(x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 5)(x − 6) over ℤ_5 is not a datum: its reduction y² = x²(x − 1)²(x − 2) is singular at (0, 0) and (1, 0).
- `datum_residueDisc_eq_tube` (compatibility): D(x̃) equals the set of ℚ_p-points of the residue disc ]x̃[ of ColemanIntegration:L1/residue-disc-parametrisation for the pair (𝒳, Ō).
- `datum_param_fibre` (compatibility): For supporting ReductionDiscData, the chosen param at a residue label is a bijection on its set-theoretic fibre. This does not identify a Coleman analytic tube.

**Acceptance.** For C₀(5) at p = 3 the residue discs are the four listed in datum_C05_three, and each of the six rational points lies in exactly one of them. Degenerate case ℙ¹_{ℤ_p}: p + 1 discs, each parametrised by x − a or 1/x.

**Direct prerequisites.** `ColemanIntegration:L1/good-reduction-pair`; `ColemanIntegration:L1/residue-disc-parametrisation`; `JacobianChallengePartII:JC1/relative-jacobian`; `JacobianChallengePartII:JC1/jacobian-base-change`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-d-the-relative-picard-functor-and-the-jacobian-scheme`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-f-abeljacobi-and-the-universal-property`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`.

**Sources.** `mccallum-poonen-2012` — §5 opening, author copy p.5. The datum is exactly this assumption, with the model recorded as data. `mccallum-poonen-2012` — §5.2(1), author copy p.6. Residue-disc parametrisation (iii). `siksek-2010` — §3.4 Lemma 3.1(iii), p.6. Number-field version of (iii); B_υ(Q) is Siksek's υ-unit ball.

**Consumers.** McCallum–Poonen §§5.1–5.5: Coleman's method is set up on residue classes of a smooth proper model over ℤ_p. Siksek, Explicit Chabauty over number fields §§3.2–3.4: the υ-unit balls B_υ(Q) and well-behaved uniformisers at places of good reduction.
