<a id="ED-5-coprime-index-transfer"></a>

### Computing the sieve on a subgroup of index prime to N

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/coprime-index-transfer` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.coprimeIndex_sieve_transfer` · implementation unchecked.

Let Γ be an abelian group, H ≤ Γ and N ≥ 1 with gcd([Γ:H], N) = 1 (native index; ED.3/finite-index-subgroup-certificate and ED.3/saturation-certificate supply H by generators with this coprimality for the primes dividing N). Then (i) H ∩ NΓ = NH; (ii) the inclusion induces a group isomorphism H/NH ≅ Γ/NΓ; (iii) for local data φ_i: Γ → G_i and finite X_i ⊆ G_i (i ∈ S) put ψ_i = (G_i → G_i/NG_i) ∘ φ_i|_H and X̄_i = the image of X_i in G_i/NG_i; for every γ ∈ Γ with φ_i(γ) ∈ X_i for all i ∈ S there is h ∈ H with h − γ ∈ NΓ, and the class of h in H/NH lies in admissibleClasses(S, NH, ψ, X̄); by (ii) this class is determined by γ. Consequently the sieve computed from the generators of H alone, with targets G_i/NG_i, contains the class of every rational point, and its emptiness proves C(ℚ) = ∅. No element of Γ outside H is used.

**Hypotheses.** Γ abelian; H ≤ Γ; N ≥ 1; gcd([Γ:H], N) = 1 with the native index (an infinite index is represented by 0 and is then coprime only to N = 1). S finite; φ_i: Γ → G_i additive; X_i ⊆ G_i finite; H/NH has a finite enumeration.

**Proof route.**

- (i) NH ⊆ H ∩ NΓ. Conversely let h = Nγ ∈ H and d = [Γ:H]; Subgroup.pow_index_mem gives dγ ∈ H, Nat.gcd_eq_gcd_ab gives du + Nv = 1, so γ = u(dγ) + vh ∈ H and h ∈ NH.
- (ii) Surjectivity is subgroup-covers-quotient with L = NΓ; injectivity is (i).
- (iii) ψ_i(NH) = 0 in G_i/NG_i, so the test at i is exact there. If h − γ = Nγ′ then φ_i(h) − φ_i(γ) ∈ NG_i, so ψ_i(h) is the image of φ_i(γ) ∈ X_i; global-soundness for (H, ψ, X̄) gives the claim.
- Testing modulo NG_i instead of φ_i(NΓ) makes the computation independent of the unknown part of Γ: φ_i(Γ) cannot be computed from H when [Γ:H] > 1.

**Acceptance.** Γ = ℤ, H = 3ℤ, N = 2: H ∩ 2ℤ = 6ℤ = 2H and 3ℤ/6ℤ ≅ ℤ/2; with G = ℤ/6 and φ the reduction, the class of 3 is tested modulo 2G = {0, 2, 4} exactly as γ = 1. H = 2ℤ, N = 2: the map H/2H → Γ/2Γ is zero and the odd class is lost; the coprimality hypothesis fails.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/subgroup-covers-quotient`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/global-soundness`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/finite-index-subgroup-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/saturation-certificate`; `mathlib:Subgroup.pow_index_mem`; `mathlib:Nat.gcd_eq_gcd_ab`; `mathlib:powMonoidHom`; `mathlib:QuotientGroup.map`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.4, published p.284. The source's requirement on a known subgroup; the theorem shows why it suffices for the sieve modulo N. `box-2021` — §2.4, arXiv pp.6–7, input (ii). Box replaces the index condition by multiplication by I into G; relative-symmetric-sieve uses that variant, this node the coprime-index one.

<a id="ED-5-sieve-chain"></a>

### The sieve along a descending chain of subgroups

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/sieve-chain` · construction · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.siftChain` · implementation unchecked.

Given places S, local data (φ_i, X_i), subgroups L_0 ≥ L_1 ≥ L_2 ≥ … of Γ with finite quotients, proposed lifts σ_j: Γ/L_j → Γ/L_{j+1} and test sets T_j ⊆ S, define siftChain by A_0 = admissibleClasses(S, L_0, φ, X) and A_{j+1} = refineClasses(T_j, L_{j+1}, L_j, σ_j, A_j). Bruin–Stoll's computation of A(NΓ) is the instance L_0 = Γ with the chain N_0Γ ⊇ N_1Γ ⊇ … ⊇ N_mΓ refined by PrepareLift into steps L_{j−1} ⊇ L_j, σ_j a choice of representatives and T_j = I_j. The value at each level is a finite set; that the chain has reached its intended final level NΓ is recorded in the certificate.

**Hypotheses.** Γ is an abelian group, S a finite set of places, each G_i an abelian group, φ_i: Γ → G_i additive and X_i ⊆ G_i finite; L ≤ Γ has finite quotient Γ/L. Surjectivity of φ_i is not assumed. L_{j+1} ≤ L_j for all j; every Γ/L_j has a finite enumeration; σ_j and T_j are arbitrary data, checked only in sieve-chain-correct.

**Proof route.**

- Recursion on j using coset-lift; each step is a finite loop over A_j and the kernel of Γ/L_{j+1} → Γ/L_j.
- The chain is indexed by ℕ and evaluated at a given level, so no termination question arises.
- PrepareLift's choice of the L_j (prepared-step-target, prepared-step-progress) and FindQSequence's choice of the q_k affect only the cost.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.siftChain` (data): The finite set at level j of the iterated sieve.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.siftChain_zero` (simp): Level 0 is admissibleClasses(S, L_0, φ, X).
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.siftChain_succ` (simp): Level j + 1 is refineClasses(T_j, L_{j+1}, L_j, σ_j, level j).
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.card_siftChain_succ_le` (other): |A_{j+1}| ≤ |A_j|·|ker(Γ/L_{j+1} → Γ/L_j)| (from lift-cardinality).
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.siftChain_eq_admissibleClasses` (characterisation): Under the checks of sieve-chain-correct, level j equals A_S(L_j) (promoted to sieve-chain-correct).
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.range_nsmul_mul_eq_of_padicValNat_le` (other): Let A be an abelian group of finite exponent e (for instance a finite local group G_i), q a prime and M a natural number with v_q(e) ≤ v_q(M). Then (qM)A = MA. Consequently φ(qMΓ) = φ(MΓ) for every homomorphism φ: Γ → A, so by unchanged-local-image the place gives the same test on Γ/qMΓ as on Γ/MΓ and is omitted when lifting from N_{k−1}Γ to N_kΓ = q_kN_{k−1}Γ: only places with v_{q_k}(e_i) ≥ v_{q_k}(N_k) are relevant. Surjectivity of φ is not needed.

**Tests.**

- `siftChain_level_zero` (degenerate): Before any lifting the chain is the direct sieve at L_0.
- `siftChain_no_places` (degenerate): With S = ∅, T_j = ∅ and correct lifts every class survives at every level.
- `siftChain_two_levels` (computation): Γ = ℤ/4, L_0 = Γ, L_1 = 0, φ = id, X = {1}, lift of the class 0 equal to 1 and T_0 = S: level 1 is {1}.
- `siftChain_omitted_changed_test` (non-example): Same data with T_0 = ∅: level 1 has 4 elements, not the direct sieve {1}; the omitted place has φ(L_1) = 0 ≠ φ(L_0).

**Acceptance.** Every level is computed by finitely many finite loops; no expected-size estimate enters. A = ℤ/4, q = 2, M = 4: v₂(4) = 2 ≤ 2 and 8A = 4A = 0. A = ℤ/4, q = 2, M = 2: v₂(4) = 2 > 1 and 4A = 0 ≠ 2A = {0, 2}; the place is relevant. A = ℤ has exponent 0 and is excluded: 2ℤ ≠ ℤ although padicValNat 2 0 = 0.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/coset-lift`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/admissible-classes`; `mathlib:Monoid.exponent`; `mathlib:Monoid.exponent_ne_zero_of_finite`; `mathlib:padicValNat`; `mathlib:powMonoidHom`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — §3.2, published p.277. The chain of moduli N_0 | N_1 | … | N_m = N; the construction iterates the lifting step along any such chain. `bruin-stoll-2010` — §3.3, published p.279. One step of the chain from N_{k−1}Γ to N_kΓ, itself split into the steps L_{j−1} ⊇ L_j. `bruin-stoll-2010` — §3.3, published p.278. The source's relevance test; the lemma is its proof, and shows that the other places have unchanged image subgroups.

<a id="ED-5-sieve-chain-correct"></a>

### Correctness of the iterated sieve

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/sieve-chain-correct` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.siftChain_eq_admissibleClasses` · implementation unchecked.

In sieve-chain assume for every j: σ_j is a section on A_S(L_j) (the projection Γ/L_{j+1} → Γ/L_j sends σ_j(a) to a for every a ∈ A_S(L_j)), T_j ⊆ S, and φ_i(L_{j+1}) = φ_i(L_j) for every i ∈ S∖T_j. Then siftChain at level j equals A_S(L_j) for every j. In particular, if L_t = NΓ the computed set is A(NΓ), and if some level is empty every subsequent level is empty.

**Hypotheses.** Γ is an abelian group, S a finite set of places, each G_i an abelian group, φ_i: Γ → G_i additive and X_i ⊆ G_i finite; L ≤ Γ has finite quotient Γ/L. Surjectivity of φ_i is not assumed. L_{j+1} ≤ L_j; σ_j a section on A_S(L_j); T_j ⊆ S; unchanged image subgroups at the omitted places.

**Proof route.**

- Induction on j. Level 0 is the definition (siftChain_zero).
- If level j is A_S(L_j), relevant-tests with K = L_{j+1}, L = L_j and T = T_j gives refineClasses(T_j, L_{j+1}, L_j, σ_j, A_S(L_j)) = A_S(L_{j+1}).
- quotient-refinement gives the statement about empty levels.

**Acceptance.** PrepareLift and Lift with the corrected prepared subgroups L_j = L_{j−1} ∩ φ_i^{-1}(N_kG_i) (source issue EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E1) and the test sets I_j compute A(N_kΓ). For the ℤ/4 data of siftChain_omitted_changed_test the hypothesis on T_0 fails and so does the conclusion.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/sieve-chain`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/relevant-tests`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/quotient-refinement`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — §3.3, published p.279. The iterated computation; the theorem is its correctness along an arbitrary checked chain.

<a id="ED-5-subgroup-from-membership-test"></a>

### A finite-index subgroup from a membership test (GetSubgroup)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/subgroup-from-membership-test` · construction · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.getSubgroup` · implementation unchecked.

Let Γ be an abelian group generated by b_1, …, b_r and K ≤ Γ a subgroup of finite index with decidable membership. GetSubgroup processes the generators in order, keeping a list A′ of representatives of the image of ⟨b_1, …, b_{k−1}⟩ in Γ/K: for b = b_k it finds the least j ≥ 1 such that jb + a ∈ K for some a ∈ A′, records g_k = jb + a, and replaces A′ by {a + ib : a ∈ A′, 0 ≤ i < j}. The output (g_1, …, g_r) has length r, lies in K and generates K. Bruin–Stoll apply it with Γ = J(ℚ) and K = J(ℚ) ∩ J⁰(ℚ_p), membership being Proposition 5.10's test v_p(δ(κ(P))) = 4v_p(κ(P)). The source states it for a free group; the argument below needs only a generating list.

**Hypotheses.** Γ abelian, generated by the list b; K ≤ Γ of finite index; membership in K decidable.

**Proof route.**

- Termination: [Γ:K]·b ∈ K (pow_index_mem), so the least j is at most [Γ:K].
- Invariant: A′ is a set of distinct representatives of (K + ⟨b_1, …, b_k⟩)/K; minimality of j makes the cosets a + ib distinct.
- Generation: by induction on k, K ∩ ⟨b_1, …, b_k⟩ = ⟨g_1, …, g_k⟩. For x = c·b_k + y ∈ K with y ∈ ⟨b_1, …, b_{k−1}⟩, the integers c with c·b_k ∈ K + ⟨b_1, …, b_{k−1}⟩ form jℤ, so j | c and x − (c/j)·g_k ∈ K ∩ ⟨b_1, …, b_{k−1}⟩.
- With ⟨b_1, …, b_r⟩ = Γ this gives ⟨g_1, …, g_r⟩ = K (Subgroup.closure_le for one inclusion).

**API.**

- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.getSubgroup` (data): The output list g_1, …, g_r.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.closure_getSubgroup` (characterisation): If b generates Γ then the output generates K.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.getSubgroup_mem` (other): Every output element lies in K.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.length_getSubgroup` (other): The output has the same length as the input.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.getSubgroup_top` (simp): For K = Γ the output is the input.

**Tests.**

- `getSubgroup_whole_group` (degenerate): For K = Γ the output equals the input list.
- `getSubgroup_int_four` (computation): Γ = ℤ, b = [1], K = 4ℤ: the output is [4].
- `getSubgroup_parity` (computation): Γ = ℤ², b = [(1,0), (0,1)], K = {(x, y) : x + y even}: the output is [(2,0), (1,1)].
- `getSubgroup_naive_multiples` (non-example): The doubled generators (2,0), (0,2) generate a proper subgroup of the even-sum subgroup K; multiplying each generator into K separately is wrong.

**Acceptance.** The output generates K whenever the input generates Γ, with torsion allowed.

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:Subgroup.closure`; `mathlib:Subgroup.closure_le`; `mathlib:Subgroup.FiniteIndex`; `mathlib:Subgroup.pow_index_mem`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — §5, published p.294. The setting of GetSubgroup; the construction follows the displayed algorithm and adds its correctness proof, which the source does not give. `bruin-stoll-2010` — §5, published p.295. The use of the algorithm for bad information.

**Consumers.** Bruin–Stoll §5, published pp.294–295: computes J(ℚ) ∩ J⁰(ℚ_p) from the generators of J(ℚ) and the test of Proposition 5.10.. ED.5 genus-two-bad-information and padic-quotient-sieve-datum: generators of Γ ∩ U give the presentation of the local quotient Γ/(Γ ∩ U)..

<a id="ED-5-height-coset-separation"></a>

### Each coset of NΓ has at most one point of small height

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/height-coset-separation` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.eq_of_sub_mem_range_nsmul_of_height_le` · implementation unchecked.

Let Γ be an abelian group and ĥ: Γ → ℝ a quadratic map over ℤ (ĥ(nx) = n²ĥ(x), ĥ(x+y) + ĥ(x−y) = 2ĥ(x) + 2ĥ(y)) with ĥ ≥ 0. Let m be such that ĥ(x) ≥ m for every x of infinite order, let N ≥ 1 kill the torsion of Γ (N·x = 0 for every x of finite order; in Bruin–Stoll the exponent of J(ℚ)_tors divides N), and let H′ satisfy N²m > 4H′. If x, y ∈ Γ satisfy x − y ∈ NΓ and ĥ(x), ĥ(y) ≤ H′, then x = y. For Γ = J(ℚ) the Néron–Tate height is such a map and m is the minimal canonical height of a point of infinite order (certified by a short-vector enumeration).

**Hypotheses.** ĥ a quadratic map Γ → ℝ over ℤ with ĥ ≥ 0. m ≤ ĥ(x) for all x of infinite order; N·x = 0 for all x of finite order; 4H′ < N²m.

**Proof route.**

- Write x − y = Nz. The parallelogram law and ĥ(x + y) ≥ 0 give ĥ(x − y) ≤ 2ĥ(x) + 2ĥ(y) ≤ 4H′.
- If z has infinite order then ĥ(x − y) = N²ĥ(z) ≥ N²m > 4H′ (QuadraticMap.map_smul), a contradiction.
- So z has finite order and x − y = Nz = 0.
- For elliptic curves Tau Ceti's canonical height is a quadratic map with ĥ ≥ 0 vanishing exactly on torsion, so the hypotheses are met with any certified m; for Jacobians the Néron–Tate height is requested from RP.0.

**Acceptance.** Γ = ℤ, ĥ(x) = x², m = 1, N = 3, H′ = 2: 9 > 8, and the coset 1 + 3ℤ contains only 1 with x² ≤ 2. Γ = ℤ/2 × ℤ, ĥ(a, x) = x², m = 1, N = 1, H′ = 0.1: (1, 0) and (0, 0) both have height 0 and differ by an element of NΓ; the torsion condition N·(1, 0) = 0 fails.

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:QuadraticMap`; `mathlib:QuadraticMap.map_smul`; `mathlib:IsOfFinOrder`; `mathlib:powMonoidHom`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.2, published p.281. The two conditions on N; the second, N² > 4H′/m, breaks across a symbol in the extracted text and is restated in the node. `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.2, published p.281. Gives separation of bounded-height points within each coset; the node retains the primed height bound H′.

<a id="ED-5-height-bounded-points"></a>

### All points of bounded height from the sieve

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/height-bounded-points` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.mem_candidates_of_height_le` · implementation unchecked.

Let D be jacobian reduction data (P = C(ℚ), Γ = J(ℚ)), ĥ a quadratic map on Γ as in height-coset-separation, h a height on C(ℚ) with ĥ(ι(P)) ≤ d·h(P) + δ for all P (d ≥ 0), H a bound and H′ = dH + δ. Let L ≤ Γ have finite index, S places whose local sets contain the true local images, and for every a ∈ A_S(L) let T_a ⊆ Γ be a finite set containing every x ∈ Γ with q_L(x) = a and ĥ(x) ≤ H′ (certified by a closest-vector enumeration in the lattice (L, ĥ) around a representative, ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete). Then every P ∈ C(ℚ) with h(P) ≤ H has ι(P) ∈ T_a for some a ∈ A_S(L). If moreover L ⊆ NΓ with N as in height-coset-separation, each T_a contains at most one element of height at most H′, so the points of height at most H inject into A_S(L); a candidate x ∈ T_a is accepted by exhibiting a preimage under ι, or rejected by a reduction test (kummer-curve-test in genus two).

**Hypotheses.** D jacobian reduction data with local sets containing the true images; L ≤ Γ of finite index. ĥ quadratic over ℤ; ĥ(ι(P)) ≤ d·h(P) + δ for all P with d ≥ 0; T_a contains every element of the class a of height at most dH + δ.

**Proof route.**

- curve-sieve-soundness puts q_L(ι(P)) in A_S(L).
- ĥ(ι(P)) ≤ d·h(P) + δ ≤ dH + δ = H′ because d ≥ 0, so ι(P) ∈ T_{q_L(ι(P))}.
- height-coset-separation bounds the number of elements of height at most H′ in each class by one when L ⊆ NΓ.
- The constants d and δ come from a height-difference bound (ED.3/explicit-height-difference-bound) and the explicit embedding; their certification for genus-two Jacobians is the recorded height-comparison gap, and the canonical height of J(ℚ) is requested from RP.0.

**Acceptance.** If A_S(L) = ∅ there is no rational point of height at most H. With N divisible by the exponent of J(ℚ)_tors and N² > 4H′/m, each element of A(S, N) corresponds to at most one point of height at most H (Bruin–Stoll §4.2).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/curve-sieve-soundness`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/height-coset-separation`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/explicit-height-difference-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/height-lower-bound-by-search`; `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.0`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.2, published p.281. The conclusion of the finding-points application. `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.2, published p.282. The certified sets T_a are the output of this closest-vector computation in (NJ(ℚ), ĥ).

**Revision notes.** Bounded enumeration requires RP.1 free quotient and positive-definite Gram form plus every finite torsion fibre; ED.3 heightCoordinatePoints is the finite coordinate adapter. Rank0 returns the entire finite torsion set separately. A semidefinite height on an arbitrary group is insufficient.

<a id="ED-5-kummer-curve-test"></a>

### Recognising points of a genus-two curve by reduction

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/kummer-curve-test` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.GenusTwo.mem_range_aj_of_kummer_reductions` · implementation unchecked.

Let C: y² = F(x, z) be a genus-two curve over ℚ with integral binary sextic F, P₀ ∈ C(ℚ) with x(P₀) = (a : b) for coprime integers a, b, and ι(P) = [P − P₀]. For Q ∈ J(ℚ) let (k₁ : k₂ : k₃ : k₄) be its image on the Kummer surface with coprime integer coordinates and h(Q) = log max|k_j|; let γ ≥ h − ĥ on J(ℚ). Let p₁, …, p_m be distinct primes of good reduction with p₁⋯p_m > 3·e^{H′+γ}·max(|a|, |b|)², and, if P₀ ≠ P̄₀, such that the product of those p_j modulo which P₀ and its hyperelliptic conjugate P̄₀ remain distinct exceeds e^{H′+γ} (for instance, every p_j separates them). If Q ∈ J(ℚ) has ĥ(Q) ≤ H′ and the reduction of Q modulo every p_j lies in ι_{p_j}(C̃(𝔽_{p_j})), then Q ∈ ι(C(ℚ)). The factor 3 corrects the printed bound (source issue EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E12). The arithmetic core: if |k_j| ≤ B, every p_j divides k₁a² − k₂ab + k₃b², and ∏ p_j > 3B·max(|a|, |b|)², then k₁a² − k₂ab + k₃b² = 0.

**Hypotheses.** C of genus two with integral sextic model; P₀ rational with x(P₀) = (a : b), gcd(a, b) = 1; ι(P) = [P − P₀]. γ ≥ h − ĥ on J(ℚ); distinct good primes with p₁⋯p_m > 3e^{H′+γ}max(|a|,|b|)²; if P₀ ≠ P̄₀, the p_j separating P₀ and P̄₀ have product > e^{H′+γ}. The prime condition on the separating primes corrects the gap EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E17 in the published proof.

**Proof route.**

- The quadratic k₁X² − k₂XZ + k₃Z² vanishes at the x-coordinates of the degree-two divisor representing Q (Kummer coordinates (1 : x₁+x₂ : x₁x₂ : β₀), gap on the Cassels–Flynn model). If Q mod p_j = ι_{p_j}(R) = [R − (P₀ mod p_j)] = [R + P₀′ − W], with P₀′ the hyperelliptic conjugate and W a canonical divisor, then the degree-two divisor of Q mod p_j contains a point with x-coordinate x(P₀) mod p_j, so p_j divides k₁a² − k₂ab + k₃b² (the printed proof writes k₁b² − k₂ab + k₃a², source issue EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E13).
- |k_j| ≤ e^{h(Q)} ≤ e^{ĥ(Q)+γ} ≤ e^{H′+γ}, so |k₁a² − k₂ab + k₃b²| ≤ (|k₁| + |k₂| + |k₃|)·max(|a|,|b|)² ≤ 3e^{H′+γ}max(|a|,|b|)²; the product of the distinct p_j divides this integer, which therefore vanishes (kummerLineValue_eq_zero).
- Vanishing means the divisor of Q contains a point with x-coordinate x(P₀), so Q = [P − P₀] or Q = [P − P̄₀] with P ∈ C(ℚ). In the second case with P ≠ P̄₀ (so P₀ ≠ P̄₀ and Q ≠ 0): at a prime p_j separating P₀ and P̄₀, Q mod p_j = [P̃ + P̃₀ − W] equals some ι_{p_j}(R) = [R + P̄̃₀ − W] only if P̃ = P̄̃₀, because an effective degree-two divisor outside the canonical class is the only effective divisor in its class; then Q ≡ 0 modulo p_j, so p_j divides k₁, k₂, k₃, which are not all zero, and the product of the separating primes is at most max|k_j| ≤ e^{H′+γ}, a contradiction. (The printed proof distinguishes the cases at a single p_{j₀}, which fails when P ≡ P̄₀ modulo p_{j₀}.)
- γ is the genus-two height-difference bound (height-comparison gap; ED.3/explicit-height-difference-bound covers elliptic curves).

**Acceptance.** Arithmetic core: a = b = 1, |k_j| ≤ 10, primes {2, 3, 5, 7}: an integer divisible by 210 with absolute value at most 30 is zero. The printed estimate fails for (k₁, k₂, k₃) = (1, −1, 1) and a = b = 1: the value is 3 while max|k_j|·max(|a|,|b|)² = 1.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/jacobian-reduction-data`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/explicit-height-difference-bound`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves#layer-10-model-classes--elliptic-hyperelliptic-plane-curves`; `mathlib:Finset.prod`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — Lemma 4.1, published p.281. The conclusion of Lemma 4.1; the hypothesis on the product of primes is corrected by the factor 3 (EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E12). `bruin-stoll-2010` — Lemma 4.1, proof, published p.281. The divisibility step; a and b are interchanged relative to the convention x(P₀) = (a : b) (EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E13), which does not affect the bound.

<a id="ED-5-siksek-lattice-step"></a>

### Refining the subgroup represented by known points (Siksek's step)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/siksek-lattice-step` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.represents_of_siksek_step` · implementation unchecked.

Let j: P → Γ be a map (P = C(ℚ) or the integral points, j = ι), W ⊆ Γ finite and L ≤ Γ such that W represents the image of P in Γ/L: every j(p) lies in W + L. Let φ: Γ → A be a homomorphism with φ(j(p)) ∈ Y for all p (for a good prime q: φ = ρ_q and Y = ι_q(C̃(𝔽_q))), L′ = L ∩ ker φ, and R ⊆ Γ a set meeting every nontrivial coset of L′ in L (every ℓ ∈ L∖L′ is congruent modulo L′ to some r ∈ R). If φ(w + r) ∉ Y for all w ∈ W and r ∈ R, then W represents the image of P in Γ/L′: every j(p) lies in W + L′. Only the values φ(w + r) are needed, not a discrete logarithm of the local image.

**Hypotheses.** j: P → Γ; W ⊆ Γ finite; every j(p) ∈ W + L. φ: Γ → A with φ(j(p)) ∈ Y; R meets every nontrivial coset of L ∩ ker φ in L; φ(w + r) ∉ Y for w ∈ W, r ∈ R.

**Proof route.**

- Write j(p) = w + ℓ with ℓ ∈ L. If ℓ ∉ L′ choose r ∈ R and ℓ′ ∈ L′ with ℓ = r + ℓ′; then φ(j(p)) = φ(w + r) since φ(ℓ′) = 0, so φ(w + r) ∈ Y, contradicting the test.
- Hence ℓ ∈ L′.
- Iterating over primes q gives a decreasing chain of subgroups with the same invariant; (L : L′) is computed from ρ_q on generators.

**Acceptance.** Γ = ℤ, W = {0}, L = 2ℤ, φ: ℤ → ℤ/4, Y = {0}: L′ = 4ℤ, R = {2}, and φ(2) = 2 ∉ Y, so every j(p) ∈ 4ℤ. If φ(w + r) ∈ Y for some pair the step gives no conclusion.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/jacobian-reduction-data`; `mathlib:MonoidHom.ker`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.3, published p.282. Gives the lattice-refinement step and its survivor conclusion with the refined lattice L′. `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.3, published p.283. Attribution of the step.

<a id="ED-5-integral-points-completeness"></a>

### Integral points on hyperelliptic curves from a sieve lower bound

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/integral-points-completeness` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.mem_known_of_height_gap` · implementation unchecked.

Let f ∈ ℤ[x] be separable of degree n ≥ 5, C the smooth projective curve of genus g = ⌊(n−1)/2⌋ with affine model y² = f(x) (AlgebraicCurves Layer 10), 𝓘 = {(x, y) ∈ ℤ² : y² = f(x)} ⊆ C(ℚ), and ι: C(ℚ) → J(ℚ) from jacobian-reduction-data (for n odd, D₁ = ∞, the unique point at infinity). The covering map is the inclusion of the integral points of the affine Weierstrass model into C(ℚ), followed by ι. Let W ⊆ 𝓘 be finite and L ≤ J(ℚ) such that (i) ι(P) ∈ ι(W) + L for all P ∈ 𝓘 (from curve-sieve-soundness with known representatives and siksek-lattice-step); (ii) μ > 0 with ĥ(ℓ) ≥ μ for every nonzero ℓ ∈ L (a short-vector certificate in (L, ĥ)); (iii) ĥ(ι(P)) ≤ d·log max(1, |x(P)|) + δ on 𝓘 with d ≥ 0; (iv) log max(1, |x|) ≤ B for all (x, y) ∈ 𝓘, supplied by DT.4/baker-superelliptic-theorem with n = 2 and b = 1, B = (4N)^{2^{12}N⁴}·e^{50N⁴h(f)} for N = deg f and h(f) = log max(1, |coefficients of f|), or by any certified sharper bound. Put w* = max_{w∈W} ĥ(ι(w)). If √w* < √μ and dB + δ < (√μ − √w*)², then 𝓘 = W.

**Hypotheses.** f separable, deg f ≥ 5; 𝓘 the integral points of y² = f(x); ι injective (genus ≥ 1). (i)–(iv) as stated, each certified: the sieve and Siksek steps for (i), short vectors for (ii), the height comparison for (iii), the DT.4 bound for (iv).

**Proof route.**

- Let P ∈ 𝓘∖W. By (i) ι(P) − ι(w) ∈ L for some w ∈ W; it is nonzero because ι is injective, so ĥ(ι(P) − ι(w)) ≥ μ by (ii).
- √ĥ is a seminorm: ĥ(sx + ty) ≥ 0 for all integers s, t, hence for all reals by homogeneity and continuity, which is the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for the polar form. So √ĥ(ι(P)) ≥ √μ − √ĥ(ι(w)) ≥ √μ − √w* > 0.
- Squaring, ĥ(ι(P)) ≥ (√μ − √w*)² > dB + δ ≥ d·log max(1, |x(P)|) + δ ≥ ĥ(ι(P)), a contradiction.
- The upper bound is stated for the equation itself, so no descent covering is needed; the constants d, δ for the Kummer height of [P − ∞] are the recorded height-comparison gap.

**Acceptance.** Toy instance: Γ = ℤ, ĥ(x) = x², L = 10ℤ, μ = 100, w* = 4, d = 1, δ = 0, B = 30: (10 − 2)² = 64 > 30, so every point is known. The bounds must actually cross: Bruin–Stoll report N near 10^100 from the sieve and subgroups of index up to 10^1800 from the second stage, against Baker-type bounds near 10^600; an uncrossed pair of bounds gives no conclusion.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/siksek-lattice-step`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/curve-sieve-soundness`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/jacobian-reduction-data`; `DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/baker-superelliptic-theorem`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete`; `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.0`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves#layer-10-model-classes--elliptic-hyperelliptic-plane-curves`; `mathlib:QuadraticMap`; `mathlib:Real.sqrt`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.3, published p.282. The sieve gives the lower bound; the theorem combines it with an upper bound. `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.3, published p.282. The combination; the upper bound is imported from DT.4 instead of the unread source [8].

<a id="ED-5-chabauty-sieve-combination"></a>

### Combination of Chabauty–Coleman with the Mordell–Weil sieve

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/chabauty-sieve-combination` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.JacobianReductionData.mem_known_of_chabauty_sieve` · implementation unchecked.

Let D be jacobian reduction data for a curve C/ℚ of genus g ≥ 2 whose Jacobian has rank r < g, and p₀ ∈ S a prime of good reduction with p₀ ≥ 3 and a nonzero ω ∈ Ann_{p₀}(J(ℚ)) (ED.4/annihilating-differentials), scaled to be integral with nonzero reduction ω̄. Let Ū ⊆ C̃(𝔽_{p₀}) be the residue classes R for which ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound gives at most one rational point reducing to R (for instance those with ω̄(R) ≠ 0). Let L ≤ J(ℚ) have finite index with L ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀} (for instance L ⊆ NJ(ℚ) with the exponent of J̃(𝔽_{p₀}) dividing N). Then: (i) if ι(P) − ι(P′) ∈ L then red_{p₀}(P) = red_{p₀}(P′); (ii) P ↦ q_L(ι(P)) is injective on {P ∈ C(ℚ) : red_{p₀}(P) ∈ Ū}; (iii) (residue-class decision) if the sieve with the local set ι_{p₀}(C̃(𝔽_{p₀})∖Ū) at p₀ and the full local images elsewhere is empty, every rational point reduces into Ū; the residue classes outside Ū may instead be settled one at a time by valid ED.4/residue-disc-verdicts, whose lists Z_rat are the rational points of those classes; (iv) if W ⊆ C(ℚ) is a finite set of known points containing every rational point that reduces outside Ū (for instance there is none, by (iii)) and every class of A_S(L) equals q_L(ι(w)) for some w ∈ W, then C(ℚ) = W. While some class of A_S(L) is not represented by W, the computation is open: enlarging S or refining L continues it, and no conclusion about C(ℚ) is drawn.

**Hypotheses.** C/ℚ of genus g ≥ 2, rank r < g; D jacobian reduction data; p₀ ∈ S good, p₀ ≥ 3, with ω ∈ Ann_{p₀}(J(ℚ)) integral with nonzero reduction (ED.4/annihilating-differentials). Ū ⊆ C̃(𝔽_{p₀}) certified by ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound; L of finite index with L ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀}.

**Proof route.**

- (i) ρ_{p₀}(ι(P) − ι(P′)) = 0 since L ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀}; the square gives ι_{p₀}(red P) = ι_{p₀}(red P′), and ι_{p₀} is injective because the Abel–Jacobi map of a curve of genus at least one is a closed immersion (JacobianChallenge Layer F).
- (ii) Two points with the same class share a residue class in Ū, which contains at most one rational point.
- (iii) certified-map-obstruction applied to the points reducing outside Ū, with the smaller local set at p₀.
- (iv) For P reducing into Ū, curve-sieve-soundness puts q_L(ι(P)) in A_S(L), so q_L(ι(P)) = q_L(ι(w)) for some w ∈ W; by (i) w reduces to the same class of Ū, and by (ii) P = w (known-points-completeness on the points reducing into Ū). Points reducing outside Ū lie in W by hypothesis.
- If L ⊆ NJ(ℚ) and the exponent of J̃(𝔽_{p₀}) divides N then ρ_{p₀}(L) ⊆ N·J̃(𝔽_{p₀}) = 0.

**Acceptance.** Bruin–Stoll §4.4 procedure: a prime p ≥ 3 with ω̄_p non-vanishing on C(𝔽_p) gives Ū = C̃(𝔽_p); S and N with the exponent of J(𝔽_p) dividing N; A(S, N) computed; every element the class of a known rational point; conclusion C(ℚ) = W. Without L ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀}, two rational points in different residue classes can share a class modulo a coarse L, injectivity fails and the known points need not be all points.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/jacobian-reduction-data`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/curve-sieve-soundness`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/certified-map-obstruction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/known-points-completeness`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/annihilating-differentials`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/residue-disc-verdict`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-f-abeljacobi-and-the-universal-property`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.4, published p.283. Part (i) in the source's special case L = NJ(ℚ). `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.4, published p.283. Part (ii) and the role of the combination. `mccallum-poonen-2012` — Theorem 5.3(a), author copy p.7. The residue-disc bound with m = ord ω̄ = 0 gives at most one point per class; ED.4 owns it.

<a id="ED-5-relative-symmetric-sieve"></a>

### The relative symmetric Mordell–Weil sieve

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/relative-symmetric-sieve` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.JacobianReductionData.relative_symmetric_sieve` · implementation unchecked.

Let X/ℚ be a smooth projective non-hyperelliptic curve of genus g ≥ 3 with Jacobian J (the setting of ED.4/relative-symmetric-chabauty and Box §2), possibly with a degree-two map π: X → C to a smooth curve C/ℚ, and X^(2) its symmetric square. Input: primes p₁, …, p_r of good reduction for X (and for C, with π extending to the models); divisors D₁, …, D_n generating a subgroup G ≤ J(ℚ) of finite index; an integer I ≥ 1 with I·J(ℚ) ⊆ G; a finite set L ⊆ X^(2)(ℚ) containing a rational degree-two divisor ∞; and for each i a subset L_i^good ⊆ L of known points to which ED.4/relative-symmetric-chabauty applies at p_i (Box Theorem 2.1: the point is the only point of X^(2)(ℚ) in its residue class; or Box Theorem 2.4 for x = π*(P): every point of its residue class comes from C(ℚ)). Put ι(x) = I·([x] − ∞) ∈ G and ι_p(R) = I·([R] − ∞̃) on X̃^(2)(𝔽_p), so that red_p(ι(x)) = ι_p(red_p(x)) (jacobian-reduction-data for degree-two divisors), and M_i^bad = ι_{p_i}^{-1}(red_{p_i}(G)) ∖ red_{p_i}(L_i^good). If no g ∈ G satisfies red_{p_i}(g) ∈ ι_{p_i}(M_i^bad) for every i, then X^(2)(ℚ) = L ∪ π*C(ℚ) (= L when there is no π). The hypothesis is decided finitely: for L₀ = ⋂_i ker(red_{p_i}|_G), of finite index, it holds iff admissibleClasses(S, L₀, red, ι(M^bad)) = ∅ (kernel-level-exactness). This is Caraiani–Newton Theorem 7.4.2 = Box Theorem 2.6.

**Hypotheses.** X smooth projective non-hyperelliptic of genus g ≥ 3 over ℚ; π: X → C of degree two when present; the p_i of good reduction for X and C with π extending. Without π, L_i^good is defined by ED.4/symmetric-chabauty alone. G ≤ J(ℚ) generated by D₁, …, D_n with I·J(ℚ) ⊆ G; ∞ ∈ L ⊆ X^(2)(ℚ) finite; L_i^good certified by ED.4/relative-symmetric-chabauty at p_i.

**Proof route.**

- Caraiani–Newton Proposition 7.4.1 (from ED.4/relative-symmetric-chabauty): if red_{p_i}(x) ∈ red_{p_i}(L_i^good) for some i then x ∈ L ∪ π*C(ℚ).
- Let x ∉ L ∪ π*C(ℚ). For every i, R = red_{p_i}(x) ∉ red_{p_i}(L_i^good) and ι_{p_i}(R) = red_{p_i}(ι(x)) ∈ red_{p_i}(G), so R ∈ M_i^bad and g = ι(x) ∈ G satisfies all conditions, a contradiction (certified-map-obstruction).
- Finite form: kernel-level-exactness for Γ = G, φ_i = red_{p_i}|_G, X_i = ι_{p_i}(M_i^bad); G/L₀ embeds in ∏ J̃(𝔽_{p_i}). Box intersects cosets in ℤⁿ through φ: ℤⁿ → G; the formulations agree because φ is onto G.
- ι need not be injective (multiplication by I kills torsion); only ι(x) ∈ G is used. ED.3/finite-index-subgroup-certificate supplies G and the bound I.

**Acceptance.** Caraiani–Newton Proposition 7.4.5(2): for X = X(s3, ns5) and C = X(ns3, ns5) the sieve with G = ⟨5G₂, Jac_{C₂}(ℚ)[2]⟩ with G₂ = ⟨π₂*D⟩ (printed ⟨5G₁, …⟩), I = 10 and the primes listed in its proof determines the quadratic points not coming from C(ℚ). Box: for X₀(43) the primes 5, 7, 11 suffice. This and the Caraiani–Newton case are source acceptance examples; this packet does not reproduce their full numerical transcripts in ED.6. Shrinking some M_i^bad without an ED.4 justification can lose a point of X^(2)(ℚ) outside L ∪ π*C(ℚ). Caraiani–Newton's printed ⟨5G₁, Jac_{C₂}(ℚ)[2]⟩ in Proposition 7.4.4(3) is the misprint PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23/E9; the instance above uses the corrected ⟨5G₂, Jac_{C₂}(ℚ)[2]⟩.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/jacobian-reduction-data`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/padic-quotient-sieve-datum`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/certified-map-obstruction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/relative-symmetric-chabauty`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/symmetric-chabauty`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/finite-index-subgroup-certificate`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-d-the-relative-picard-functor-and-the-jacobian-scheme`.

**Sources.** `caraiani-newton-2023` — §7.4, arXiv p.99. The key step of the proof of Theorem 7.4.2: a point outside L ∪ π*C(ℚ) reduces into M_i^bad at every p_i. `box-2021` — §2.4, arXiv p.6. Box's form of the conclusion, stated as Theorem 2.6.

<a id="ED-5-genus-two-bad-information"></a>

### Reduction at bad primes for genus-two curves

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/genus-two-bad-information` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.GenusTwo.reduction_exact_of_regular` · implementation unchecked.

Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k with char k ≠ 2 and fraction field L, F ∈ O[X, Z] a squarefree binary sextic, C_F: Y² = F(X, Z) in weighted projective space, J_F ⊆ ℙ¹⁵ the Cassels–Flynn model of its Jacobian, J_F¹(L) = {P : P̄ = O} its kernel of reduction for this model, and J_{F̄}^0 the component of the smooth locus of the special fibre containing the origin. (a) (Theorem 5.11) J_{F̄}^0 is a commutative algebraic group whose law on Mumford pairs (A, B) is Cantor composition and reduction, except when both A vanish at the same singular point x = 0, where φ(X², λXZ²) + φ(X², μXZ²) = φ(X², ((f₂ + λμ)/(λ + μ))XZ²) and the sum is zero if λ + μ = 0. (b) (Proposition 5.10) P ∈ J_F lies in J_F^0 iff δ(κ(P)) ≠ 0. (c) (Corollaries 5.14–5.15) If C_F/O is regular and F̄ is not a square, then 0 → J_F¹(L) → J_F(L) → J_{F̄}^0(k) → 0 is exact, the map reducing the Mumford representation. For an odd prime p at which the given model is regular with one-component special fibre this computes the local datum of padic-quotient-sieve-datum with U = J¹(ℚ_p) as at good primes; at an odd prime where the model is not regular or the special fibre has several components, J(ℚ) ∩ J⁰(ℚ_p) is computed by subgroup-from-membership-test with the test v_p(δ(κ(P))) = 4v_p(κ(P)), and the image of C(ℚ_p) modulo J¹(ℚ_p) by the dual Kummer test of genus-two-deep-information with n = 1. Remark 5.16 (the regular model minus singular points is the Néron model) is stated without proof in the source and is not used.

**Hypotheses.** O complete DVR, char k ≠ 2; F squarefree of degree six over O; for (c) the model C_F/O is regular and F̄ is not a square.

**Proof route.**

- Lift F̄ to a squarefree F̃ over O; for P with P̄ ∈ J^0 and Q in the kernel of reduction the biquadratic forms give κ(P ± Q) = κ(P̄), so P + Q reduces to P̄; hence the kernel is a subgroup acting on the points with smooth origin-component reduction, the quotient is J_{F̄}^0(k), and the group law is inherited; Cantor's algorithm commutes with reduction outside the special case, which follows by a limit argument (Theorem 5.11).
- Proposition 5.5 describes the singular points through (A, B) ∈ D_F, Lemma 5.7 the components, and Proposition 5.10 identifies J^0 by δ(κ(P)) ≠ 0.
- Lemma 5.13 and Corollary 5.14: under regularity, points outside the kernel reduce to smooth points of the origin component; surjectivity of reduction is Hensel's lemma (Corollary 5.15).
- The explicit model facts (the 72 quadrics, the Kummer surface, δ, the biquadratic forms, D_F) are the Cassels–Flynn gap; regular models are StableReduction Layer 5.

**Acceptance.** Remark 5.12: for k = 𝔽_q with q odd, #J_F^0(𝔽_q) depends only on the factorisation pattern of F (Figure 1). F = H² a nonzero square: J_F has three components, the two not containing the origin are principal homogeneous spaces under J_F^0, and the exact sequence (c) is not claimed.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/padic-quotient-sieve-datum`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/subgroup-from-membership-test`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-5-regular-and-minimal-models`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves#layer-10-model-classes--elliptic-hyperelliptic-plane-curves`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — Theorem 5.11, published p.291. Part (a). `bruin-stoll-2010` — Corollary 5.15, published p.294. Part (c).

<a id="ED-5-genus-two-deep-information"></a>

### Deep information for genus-two curves

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/genus-two-deep-information` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.GenusTwo.dualKummer_valuation_of_mem_deep` · implementation unchecked.

Let C be a genus-two curve over ℚ with a Weierstrass model over ℤ_p, p odd, ι: C → J from a rational degree-one class, Jⁿ(ℚ_p) the pⁿℤ_p-points of the formal group (n ≥ 1) and log: J¹(ℚ_p) → (pℤ_p)² the formal logarithm. (a) For Γ = J(ℚ) and K_n = Γ ∩ Jⁿ(ℚ_p), K_n is the kernel of K₁ → (pℤ_p/pⁿℤ_p)² ≅ (ℤ/p^{n−1})², P ↦ log P mod pⁿ; so Γ/K_n is finite and computable from K₁ and logarithms to precision pⁿ. (b) (Lemma 6.2) If P₀ ∈ C(ℚ_p), Q ∈ Jⁿ(ℚ_p) and (η₁ : η₂ : η₃ : η₄) are coordinates of the image of P₀ + Q ∈ Pic¹ on the dual Kummer surface, normalised to minimal valuation zero, then v_p(η₁η₃ − η₂²) ≥ n and v_p(η₄) ≥ 2n. Hence the set Y_n of classes c ∈ Γ/K_n whose chosen representative g, translated to Pic¹ by g↦g+D₁ and to the dual Kummer surface, satisfies v_p(η₄) ≥ 2n and v_p(η₁η₃ − η₂²) ≥ n, contains every class whose coset meets ι(C(ℚ_p)); it is a certified superset for padic-quotient-sieve-datum with U = Jⁿ(ℚ_p). The necessary dual-Kummer congruences supply a superset only; actual membership in the curve embedded in Pic¹ must be checked separately. Translation Pic⁰→Pic¹ is defined on the whole Jacobian, unlike an inverse of the curve embedding.

**Hypotheses.** p odd; Weierstrass model of C over ℤ_p; n ≥ 1; ι from a rational degree-one class.

**Proof route.**

- (a) For p odd the formal logarithm is an isomorphism J¹(ℚ_p) → (pℤ_p)² carrying Jⁿ onto (pⁿℤ_p)² (ED.4/abelian-logarithm); K_n is the preimage of (pⁿℤ_p)² in K₁.
- (b) After a ℤ_p-coordinate change moving P₀ to infinity, P₀ = (1 : 0 : 0 : 0) on the dual Kummer surface and Q has Kummer coordinates (αp^{2n} : βp^{2n} : γp^{2n} : 1); the biquadratic forms A (Lemma 6.1) give η₁η₁′ ≡ 1 and η₄ + η₄′ ≡ 0 modulo p^{2n}, η₄η₄′ ≡ 0 modulo p^{4n} and η₂, η₃ ≡ 0 modulo pⁿ, whence the valuations.
- If a class c meets ι(C(ℚ_p)) then every representative g has translation D↦D+D₁(g) = P₀ + Q with P₀ ∈ C(ℚ_p) and Q ∈ Jⁿ(ℚ_p), so the chosen representative passes the test and c ∈ Y_n; local-overapproximations and curve-sieve-soundness apply.
- The incremental computation over n = 2, 3, … and the linear forms ℓ_m reduce cost only; a verifier re-evaluates the test on the recorded representatives. The Kummer and dual Kummer surfaces and the forms A, B are the Cassels–Flynn gap.

**Acceptance.** Bruin–Stoll §7: information modulo p^m is collected in the order 2, 3, 5, 7, 2², 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 3², …; §8: deep information for all pⁿ < 520 shortens the hardest rank-four computation. The test is one-sided: a class passing it need not meet the curve, and it is used only as a superset.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/padic-quotient-sieve-datum`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/admissible-classes`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/abelian-logarithm`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — Lemma 6.2, published p.297. Part (b); the valuation conclusions follow in the lemma. `bruin-stoll-2010` — §6, published p.296. Part (a).

Test membership in the actual embedded curve in Pic¹ using the dual Kummer equations/regular models; no inverse of Abel–Jacobi on all J exists in genus>1. Formal neighbourhoods and precision must be transported through this translation.

<a id="ED-5-sieve-certificate"></a>

### Mordell–Weil sieve certificate

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/sieve-certificate` · definition · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.SieveCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

A Mordell–Weil sieve certificate for a curve C/ℚ consists of: (1) jacobian reduction data — the curve, a rational degree-one divisor D₁, the places S with their local groups G_p, the values of the local maps on generators, and finite local sets certified to contain the true local images (good data, or bad and deep data from padic-quotient-sieve-datum); (2) the Mordell–Weil input — generators of a subgroup H ≤ J(ℚ) with ED.3 certificates of rank and torsion and of index prime to every prime dividing the modulus N (finite-index-subgroup-certificate, saturation-certificate), or a full Mordell–Weil basis certificate; the rank is labelled conditional when its upper bound rests on an analytic hypothesis; (3) the modulus N, its factorisation and the descending chain L_0 ⊇ … ⊇ L_t with lifts σ_j and test sets T_j; (4) the exhaustive candidate set, siftChain at level t; (5) the known points W and the mode of conclusion: emptiness, Chabauty (a prime p₀ with an annihilating differential and certified residue classes Ū as in chabauty-sieve-combination, L_t ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀}, and every candidate the class of a known point), or height (a bound H, separation data and short-vector certificates). The certificate is checked when every σ_j with j<t is a section on the sieve set at level j, T_j ⊆ S, and every place outside T_j has an unchanged image subgroup. A record whose candidate set is nonempty and not covered by known points certifies nothing about C(ℚ): it is an open computation, not an empty solution set. Checked quantifies only j<length. On invariant-factor presentations, replay each projection and every local table; RawSieveStep.check verifies all new classes, including every lift, by the equivalence next(b) ↔ old(project b) ∧ all-local-tests(b). Chain compatibility and the initial full candidate set are checked separately at the finitely many recorded levels.

**Hypotheses.** The Lean structure records the reduction data, places, chain, lifts, test sets and known points over the global group Γ (J(ℚ), or H transported by coprime-index-transfer); the ED.3 and ED.4 certificates and the height data are inputs of the soundness theorem.

**Proof route.**

- Bundle the data; candidates is siftChain at the final level.
- Checked is the conjunction of the three finite checks of sieve-chain-correct.
- Presentations of the finite groups and maps used to evaluate the checks are the recorded gap on certified finite presentations.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.SieveCertificate.candidates` (data): The exhaustive candidate set: siftChain at the final level.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.SieveCertificate.candidates_eq_siftChain` (characterisation): candidates equals siftChain applied to the recorded data at level length.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.SieveCertificate.Checked` (other): The verifier's checks: sections on the sieve sets, T_j ⊆ S, unchanged image subgroups at omitted places.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.SieveCertificate.candidates_eq_sieveSet` (compatibility): For a checked certificate, candidates = A_S(L_t) of the reduction data.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.SieveCertificate.mk_aj_mem_candidates` (compatibility): For a checked certificate the class of ι(P) lies in candidates for every rational point P.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.SieveCertificate.chain` (projection): The recorded chain of subgroups L_j.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.RawSieveStep` (structure): Proof-free projection table Fin newSize→Fin oldSize, local allowed tables, old and next class sets.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.RawSieveStep.check` (other): Computable exhaustive check of next(b) iff old(project b) and all finite local allowed tests, for every b.
- `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.RawSieveStep.sound` (characterisation): Passing the raw check gives exact equality with the finite lift/filter set. Geometric interpretation requires explicit supplied geometric/Hecke data presentation and table transport, not a claimed arbitrary-group algorithm.

**Tests.**

- `candidates_no_steps` (degenerate): No places, length 0, L_0 = Γ = ℤ/2: candidates is the single class.
- `candidates_mod_four` (computation): One place, identity map on ℤ/4, local image {1}, L_0 = 0, length 0: candidates = {1}.
- `candidates_nonempty_without_points` (non-example): Γ = ℤ/2, two places with local images {0} and {1}, no points, L_0 = Γ, length 0: candidates is nonempty although there is no point; a nonempty candidate set is an open computation, not a point.
- `rawSieve_mod_four` (computation): Lifting class1 mod2 to mod4 with no local tests keeps {1,3}.
- `rawSieve_missing_lift` (non-example): Keeping only {1} fails; the other lift3 is required.
- `rawSieve_empty` (degenerate): A false local test at the unique class gives an empty next set.

**Acceptance.** The certificate carries the index/saturation assumptions, the primes, the local images and the exhaustive candidate set.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/jacobian-reduction-data`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/sieve-chain`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/sieve-chain-correct`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/padic-quotient-sieve-datum`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/coprime-index-transfer`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/finite-index-subgroup-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/saturation-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/mordell-weil-basis-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/rank-upper-bound`.

<a id="ED-5-sieve-certificate-sound"></a>

### Soundness of a Mordell–Weil sieve certificate

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/sieve-certificate-sound` · theorem · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.SieveCertificate.isEmpty_of_candidates_eq_empty` · implementation unchecked.

Let c be a checked sieve certificate for C/ℚ whose global group is J(ℚ), or a subgroup H of index prime to N transported by coprime-index-transfer. (a) If its candidate set is empty, C(ℚ) = ∅. (b) Chabauty mode: if p₀ carries an annihilating differential (ED.4/annihilating-differentials) with every rational point reducing into its certified residue classes Ū (chabauty-sieve-combination), L_t ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀}, and every candidate is the class of a known point, then C(ℚ) = W. (c) Height mode: every P ∈ C(ℚ) with h(P) ≤ H is among the candidates of height-bounded-points, at most one per candidate class when L_t ⊆ NΓ. Each conclusion depends on the recorded assumptions — the ED.3 index and saturation certificates (and the rank, conditional when its upper bound rests on an analytic hypothesis), the primes and local images, and the chain. A certificate whose final candidate set is nonempty and not covered proves nothing about C(ℚ).

**Hypotheses.** c checked; the ED.3 certificates for the global group hold; for (b) the ED.4 data at p₀; for (c) the height data of height-bounded-points.

**Proof route.**

- sieve-chain-correct identifies the candidates with A_S(L_t).
- (a) curve-sieve-soundness, through coprime-index-transfer when the global group is H.
- (b) chabauty-sieve-combination (iv).
- (c) height-bounded-points.
- Conditionality: the rank enters only through the certificate of H; ED.3/rank-upper-bound distinguishes algebraic from analytic upper bounds, and the conclusion carries the label.

**Acceptance.** Bruin–Stoll §3.3: A(N_kΓ) = ∅ for some k proves C(ℚ) = ∅. Bruin–Stoll §4.4: genus-two curves of rank one with a known rational base point, where the procedure terminated in all examples tried. The ℤ/2 non-example of sieve-certificate: a nonempty candidate set with no points gives no conclusion.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/sieve-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/sieve-chain-correct`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/curve-sieve-soundness`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/coprime-index-transfer`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/chabauty-sieve-combination`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/height-bounded-points`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/rank-upper-bound`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — §1, published p.273. Correctness on termination, without a termination claim; the theorem is this statement for a recorded certificate.

<a id="ED-5-small-genus-two-nonexistence"></a>

### Non-existence of points on the undecided small genus-two curves

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/small-genus-two-nonexistence` · application · `TauCeti.MordellWeilSieve.Examples.smallGenusTwo_noRationalPoints` · implementation unchecked.

Among the genus-two curves y² = f(x) with f of degree five or six and coefficients in {−3, …, 3}, the 1492 isomorphism classes left undecided after a search for rational points, a check for local points and a 2-cover descent have no rational point. For Jacobians of rank at most two the proof used good information only, for ranks three and four also bad and deep information; for some curves the rank of J(ℚ) is used under the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, and those cases are conditional. Each of the 1447 curves that needed a sieve computation (§8, p.301) is an instance of sieve-certificate-sound (a) with an emptiness certificate; the other 45 had rank zero or were ruled out directly by information from the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, and the latter are conditional.

**Hypotheses.** The curves, Mordell–Weil generators, ranks and local data of Bruin–Stoll's experiment (gap); the BSD-conditional cases are labelled. The exact1492-case catalogue, its partition into1447 sieve cases and45 other cases, complete MW/reduction presentations, local class tables and per-case BSD conditions are supplied explicitly with geometric compatibility hypotheses. The finite sieve certificates are checked to prove emptiness; emptiness of the rational point sets is not a supplied assertion. No catalogue, point count or MW table producer is targeted.

**Proof route.**

- For each curve: ED.3 certificates for generators and rank (conditional where BSD is used), local data at good, bad and deep places, a chain and an empty candidate set, verified by sieve-certificate-sound.
- The complete per-curve transcripts for the 1492 classes, including the 1447 sieve runs and labels for BSD-conditional cases, are an unreplayed data obligation. ED.6 does not contain these instances.

**Acceptance.** Bruin–Stoll §8: of the 1447 curves that needed a sieve, 521 have rank one (514 decided while collecting local information), 772 rank two, 152 rank three and two rank four. The statement is recorded as conditional on BSD for the curves whose rank was not proved.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/sieve-certificate-sound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/genus-two-bad-information`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/genus-two-deep-information`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/rank-upper-bound`.

**Sources.** `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.1, published p.280. The non-existence result. `bruin-stoll-2010` — §4.1, published p.280. Its conditionality.

<a id="ED-6-certified-solution-set"></a>

### Certified solution sets with completeness labels

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/certified-solution-set` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.CertifiedSolutionSet` · implementation unchecked.

Let α be a type of candidate solutions (integer tuples, S-unit triples, points with rational coordinates), P : α → Prop the Diophantine condition, and H : Prop the conjunction of the unresolved or conditional inputs of the method (H = True for an unconditional certificate). A certified solution set CertifiedSolutionSet H P consists of a finite set S : Finset α together with (sound) every element of S satisfies P, proved unconditionally by exact evaluation, and (complete) H implies that every x with P x lies in S. The certificate is labelled unconditional when H is True and conditional on H otherwise; a conditional certificate keeps H as an explicit parameter, so that discharging or weakening H is a theorem about the certificate and never an edit of it. This is the ED.6 instance of the the ED.6 finite solution-certificate interface schema for explicit examples: the pinned exact inputs are S and the certificate data of the method that proves completeness, and the verification relation is the pair (sound, complete). A list of verified solutions without completeness, a CAS output, or a p-adic candidate list that has not been compared with global points is not a certificate.

**Hypotheses.** α is a type, P : α → Prop and H : Prop. Elements of S are exact objects (integers, rationals, points with rational coordinates); no floating-point value is an element of S. Completeness may depend on H only; soundness never depends on H.

**Proof route.**

- Define the structure with three fields: a finite set of solutions, soundness (every listed element satisfies P) and completeness (under H every x with P x is listed).
- The completeness label is read off from H: H = True is unconditional; any other H is displayed in the theorem that produces the certificate (for example the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis in the descent route of BDMTV 2019 Remark 6.3).
- the ED.6 finite certificate interface supplies the pinned-input record (input data, arithmetic conventions, verification cost); the mathematical content is the structure above, with no new carrier for numbers or points.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.CertifiedSolutionSet.mem_iff` (characterisation): If H holds then x ∈ c.solutions ↔ P x.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.CertifiedSolutionSet.coe_eq_setOf` (characterisation): If H holds then (c.solutions : Set α) = {x | P x}; in particular {x | P x} is finite.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.CertifiedSolutionSet.solutions_eq` (extensionality): Two certificates c₁ (under H₁) and c₂ (under H₂) for the same P have c₁.solutions = c₂.solutions whenever H₁ ∧ H₂ holds.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.CertifiedSolutionSet.unconditional` (constructor): From S, a soundness proof and an unconditional completeness proof, the certificate under H = True.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.CertifiedSolutionSet.mono` (compatibility): A certificate under H is a certificate under any H' with H' → H, with the same solutions.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.CertifiedSolutionSet.discharge` (other): From a certificate under H and a proof of H, the unconditional certificate with the same solutions.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.CertifiedSolutionSet.map` (functoriality): Along an equivalence e : α ≃ β with P = Q ∘ e, the image certificate for Q has solutions S.map e; map along the identity is the identity and maps compose.

**Tests.**

- `certifiedSolutionSet_sq_eq_four` (computation): For α = ℤ, P x := x ^ 2 = 4 and H = True, every certificate has solutions = {−2, 2}.
- `certifiedSolutionSet_false` (degenerate): For the constantly false predicate P and any H, a certificate under H with H true has solutions = ∅.
- `certifiedSolutionSet_sound_only` (non-example): For P x := x ^ 2 = 4 over ℤ there is no unconditional certificate with solutions = {2}: soundness holds but completeness fails at −2.
- `certifiedSolutionSet_toFinset` (compatibility): If H holds then (Set.Finite.toFinset h) = c.solutions for the finiteness proof h of {x | P x} given by coe_eq_setOf (agreement with Mathlib's Set.Finite.toFinset).
- `certifiedSolutionSet_vacuous` (characterisation): For H = False every finite set of verified solutions is a certificate, so a conditional certificate asserts nothing until H is discharged.

**Acceptance.** For x² = 4 over ℤ the unconditional certificate has solutions {−2, 2}. The Thue equation X⁴ − 12X²Y² − 8XY³ + 4Y⁴ = 1 has the unconditional certificate with eight solutions (thue-example-tdw89).

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:Finset`; `mathlib:Set.Finite.toFinset`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2021` — Algorithm 3.12, p.14 (arXiv v4). The algorithm output is a candidate set or FAIL, not yet a solution set; the certificate records the further completeness proof. Stage acceptance: termination conditions and unresolved inputs are advertised through H. `de-weger-1989` — Theorem 6.3, p.123. A typical certified statement: an exact count and list with a completeness proof (OCR text layer checked against the rendered page). `bdmtv-2019` — Remark 6.3, p.927. Example of a conditional input that must be kept as an explicit hypothesis H with its label.

**Consumers.** ED.6 worked examples (thue-example-tdw89, s-unit-example-deweger, thue-mahler-example-tdw92, elliptic-integral-points-tdw89, xs13-rational-points, xs4-13-rational-points, x0plus-genus-three-points): each example theorem produces an unconditional certificate whose set is the published solution list. BDMTV 2019 Proposition 6.2 and Remark 6.3, p.927: the descent route to rk J(Q) = 3 depends on GRH; that hypothesis is carried in H and labelled. the ED.6 finite solution-certificate interface (requested schema): the pinned-data record of an explicit example; database labels and CAS output are data to verify, not theorems. BDMTV 2021 Algorithm 3.12 and §3.4: a non-FAIL output becomes a certificate only after padic-candidate-comparison.

<a id="ED-6-padic-candidate-comparison"></a>

### Comparison of p-adic candidates with global solutions

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/padic-candidate-comparison` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.eq_of_matched_or_excluded` · implementation unchecked.

Let X be a set (the p-adic points X(Q_p) of a curve, or Z_p^k for an equation in k unknowns), R ⊆ X the set of global solutions (X(Q), or the integral solutions), and Z ⊆ X a set with R ⊆ Z (the common zero set of the certified p-adic functions: quadratic Chabauty determinants, annihilating Coleman integrals, or local residue conditions). Let B_1, …, B_m ⊆ X be finitely many sets (balls of radius p^(−n) around candidates computed to absolute precision n through ED.0 p-adic embeddings) with (i) Z ⊆ B_1 ∪ … ∪ B_m and (ii) Z ∩ B_i has at most one element for each i (certified simple-root isolation). Let L ⊆ R be a finite set of verified global solutions. Call B_i matched if it contains an element of L, and excluded if R ∩ B_i = ∅ is certified (by a Mordell–Weil sieve, a second independent function whose zeros avoid B_i, or a local obstruction). If every B_i is matched or excluded then R = L, and L is a certified solution set. Without such a decision for some ball the conclusion is only L ⊆ R ⊆ L ∪ ⋃_{B_i undecided} (Z ∩ B_i), and the computation is open.

**Hypotheses.** R ⊆ Z ⊆ B_1 ∪ … ∪ B_m. Each Z ∩ B_i is a subsingleton. L is finite and L ⊆ R (each element verified exactly). Every B_i is matched (L ∩ B_i ≠ ∅) or excluded (R ∩ B_i = ∅).

**Proof route.**

- Let x ∈ R. Then x ∈ Z, so x ∈ B_i for some i by (i).
- If B_i is excluded, x ∈ R ∩ B_i = ∅ is impossible.
- If B_i is matched by P ∈ L, then P ∈ R ⊆ Z, so x and P both lie in Z ∩ B_i, a subsingleton by (ii); hence x = P ∈ L.
- Together with L ⊆ R this gives R = L; package L with these proofs as an unconditional certified-solution-set.
- Uniqueness (ii) is indispensable: agreement of a p-adic candidate with a known point to precision n does not prove equality, because numerical agreement never proves an algebraic identity (ED.0 acceptance).

**Acceptance.** X_s(13) at p = 17: twenty residue discs; on each, the balls of xs13-first-chart-points, xs13-second-chart-points and xs13-p0-disc are matched by P0, …, P6 and all other balls are excluded by the second Tate class; the conclusion is xs13-rational-points. Necessity of (ii): Z = {0, p^n} ⊆ Z_p, one ball B = p^n Z_p and L = {0}; B is matched, but Z ∩ B has two elements and the theorem does not apply. At depth one, with Z the common zeros of annihilating Coleman integrals, this is the comparison step of ED.4/chabauty-coleman-completeness; with exclusion by the Mordell–Weil sieve it is the combination of ED.5/chabauty-sieve-combination.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/certified-solution-set`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/chabauty-coleman-completeness`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/chabauty-sieve-combination`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — §6, p.926. The comparison step of the X_s(13) proof; stated here in general with the simple-root uniqueness hypothesis made explicit. `bdmtv-2021` — §3.5, p.15 (arXiv v4). Exclusion of unmatched candidates by the sieve (ED.5). `bdmtv-2021` — §3.4, p.12 (arXiv v4). An exclusion certificate for a single candidate ball.

<a id="ED-6-qc-disc-certificate"></a>

### Residue-disc certificate for quadratic Chabauty functions

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/qc-disc-certificate` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.QCDiscCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

Fix a prime p and a residue disc of X(Q_p) with a parameter t identifying it with p Z_p (t = p s, s ∈ Z_p), produced by an ED.0 p-adic embedding certificate. A quadratic Chabauty disc certificate QCDiscCertificate p ι consists of: finitely many functions f_i : Z_p → Q_p, i ∈ ι (the determinants det T of the quadratic Chabauty pairs, written in s as convergent power series whose first coefficients are known modulo p^N and whose tail obeys height-series-valuation-bound); a finite set C ⊆ Z_p of centres; a precision n ∈ ℕ; and proofs of (covers) every common zero s of the f_i satisfies ‖s − c‖ ≤ p^(−n) for some c ∈ C, and (unique) for each c ∈ C the ball ‖s − c‖ ≤ p^(−n) contains at most one common zero. The certificate is produced by root-determination-precision applied to one f_i, the other functions serving to discard centres at which they do not vanish.

**Hypotheses.** p is prime; ι is a finite index type; the f_i are functions on Z_p given by convergent power series in the disc parameter. The centres are elements of Z_p known to precision n (rational or integral representatives).

**Proof route.**

- Define the structure with fields fn, centres, prec, covers, unique; covers and unique are genuine conditions, proved for each disc by root-determination-precision.
- Common zeros are {s | ∀ i, f_i s = 0}; covers and unique imply that this set is finite with at most #C elements.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.SemanticQCDiscCertificate.exists_centre` (projection): Every common zero s of the f_i has a centre c ∈ C with ‖s − c‖ ≤ p^(−n).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.SemanticQCDiscCertificate.eq_of_mem_ball` (characterisation): Two common zeros within p^(−n) of the same centre are equal.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.SemanticQCDiscCertificate.ncard_commonZeros_le` (characterisation): The set of common zeros is finite and has at most #C elements.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.SemanticQCDiscCertificate.commonZeros_eq_empty` (simp): If C = ∅ the f_i have no common zero on the disc.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.SemanticQCDiscCertificate.addFunction` (compatibility): Adding a further function to the family keeps covers and unique, with the same centres; removing a centre c is allowed when some f_i is certified nonzero on the ball around c.

**Tests.**

- `qcDisc_linear` (computation): For p = 17, ι = Unit, f(s) = s − 1, C = {1}, n = 5, the structure exists and the common zero set is {1}.
- `qcDisc_no_zero` (degenerate): For f ≡ 1 the empty set of centres gives a certificate, and there are no common zeros.
- `qcDisc_close_roots` (non-example): For p = 17 and f(s) = s(s − 17^6) no certificate has C = {0} and n = 5, since the ball around 0 contains the two zeros 0 and 17^6.
- `qcDisc_polynomial_roots` (compatibility): If ι = Unit and f is the evaluation of a nonzero polynomial F ∈ Z_p[X], the number of common zeros is at most Multiset.card F.roots ≤ natDegree F (Mathlib Polynomial.card_roots').

**Acceptance.** For p = 17, one function f(s) = s − 1, centres {1} and any precision: a valid certificate whose only common zero is s = 1. A ball containing two zeros 0 and p^6 at precision 5 violates (unique).

**Direct prerequisites.** `mathlib:PadicInt`; `mathlib:Padic`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — §6.4.1, p.933. The per-disc data the X_s(13) proof uses (zero tables in the authors' repository); covers B19 item 89 context. `bdmtv-2021` — Lemma 4.7, p.25 (arXiv v4). The root isolation that produces the centres and precision.

**Consumers.** BDMTV 2019 §6.4.1–§6.6, pp.931–934: one certificate per residue disc of X(F_17) for the two Tate classes Z1, Z2. BDMTV 2021 §4.4, Lemma 4.7 and Proposition 4.6, p.25: the root-finding step (6c)–(6d) of Algorithm 3.12. <a id="ED-6-qc-certificate-sound"></a>

### Soundness of a quadratic Chabauty certificate

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/qc-certificate-sound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.rationalPoints_eq_of_qcCertificate` · implementation unchecked.

Let X/Q be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g ≥ 2 with b ∈ X(Q), Jacobian J of rank r = g with log : J(Q) ⊗ Q_p ≅ H⁰(X_{Q_p}, Ω¹)^*, ρ(J) ≥ 2, and p a prime of good reduction. Let Z_1, …, Z_k be nice classes and (θ_j, Υ_j) the quadratic Chabauty pairs of NC.5 with endomorphism E_j, constant c_j and pairing B_j (BDMTV Lemma 3.7, with Υ_j = {0} under potentially good reduction everywhere, Corollary 3.8). Suppose given: (a) a finite set L ⊆ X(Q) of verified rational points containing b and points P_1, …, P_m such that AJ_b(P_i) ⊗ (E_j(AJ_b(P_i)) + c_j) span E (or E_K = H⁰(Ω¹)^* ⊗_{K_p} H⁰(Ω¹)^* when the heights are K-equivariant); (b) for every x̄ ∈ X(F_p) and every choice (α_1, …, α_k) ∈ Υ_1 × ⋯ × Υ_k, a qc-disc-certificate on ]x̄[ for the family (det T_{j,α_j})_{j ≤ k} of the determinant criterion, whose power-series coefficients are computed by local-height-at-p and Coleman integration to the precision certified by height-series-valuation-bound; (c) for every centre of every disc certificate, a matching with an element of L or an exclusion. Then X(Q) = L, a certified solution set conditional on all the stated geometric, rank, Picard and raw arithmetic-data hypotheses (which are themselves certified inputs). If (b) or (c) fails for some disc, only L ⊆ X(Q) is asserted.

**Hypotheses.** r = g and the p-adic closure of J(Q) has finite index in J(Q_p) (certified rank: xs13-rank-three in the example). ρ(J) ≥ 2 and Z_1, …, Z_k are nice classes (NC.5). p is a prime of good reduction and the residue discs are enumerated from X(F_p) exactly. The local heights away from p are known: Υ_j is computed (or is {0} under potentially good reduction everywhere).

**Proof route.**

- By NC.5 (BDMTV Lemma 3.7, Corollary 3.8, with the correction PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/E8 that only κ(J(Q)) ⊗ Q_p is used) every x ∈ X(Q) satisfies θ_j(x) − B_j(AJ_b(x), E_j(AJ_b(x)) + c_j) ∈ Υ_j.
- By the determinant criterion (BDMTV Lemma 1.5, NC.5) det T_{j,α}(x) = 0 for x ∈ X(Q_p)_α; the matrices T use the points of (a) to eliminate the unknown pairing B_j.
- On each residue disc the entries of T are power series: θ_j from local-height-at-p, AJ_b from Coleman integrals (ColemanIntegration L1 via ED.4/abelian-logarithm); their coefficients are certified by height-series-valuation-bound, and root-determination-precision yields the disc certificates (b).
- X(F_p) is finite, so finitely many balls cover all common zeros; apply padic-candidate-comparison with the matchings and exclusions (c).

**Acceptance.** X_s(13), p = 17, Z_1, Z_2 from T_7 and T_11: X(Q) = {P0, …, P6} (xs13-rational-points). Removing the disc ](1:1:1)[ from (b) leaves the computation open: only {P0, …, P6} ⊆ X(Q) follows.

**Direct prerequisites.** `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.5`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/qc-disc-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/padic-candidate-comparison`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/local-height-at-p`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/height-series-valuation-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/root-determination-precision`; `ColemanIntegration:L1/coleman-integral`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/abelian-logarithm`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — §1.5, p.893. The three explicit steps (local heights away from p, power series for h_p, global heights at known points). `bdmtv-2019` — Lemma 1.5, p.891. The determinant criterion consumed from NC.5 (B19 items 11–13 are NC.5's).

<a id="ED-6-explicit-setup"></a>

### The explicit set-up: affine chart, basis of differentials and Tate class

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-setup` · definition · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.ExplicitSetup` · implementation unchecked.

An explicit quadratic Chabauty set-up over Q consists of: a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X/Q of genus g ≥ 2; an affine open Y ⊂ X over Q; a base point b ∈ Y(Q) integral at p; the boundary D := X ∖ Y with d := #D(Q̄) points, all defined over a number field L; differentials ω_0, …, ω_{2g+d−2} ∈ H⁰(Y, Ω¹) such that ω_0, …, ω_{2g−1} are of the second kind on X and their classes form a symplectic basis of H¹_dR(X/Q) (ω_i ∪ ω_{g+i} = 1 = −ω_{g+i} ∪ ω_i for i < g, all other cup products 0), ω_0, …, ω_{g−1} are holomorphic on X and form a basis of H⁰(X, Ω¹) (the hypothesis BDMTV §4.5 uses, PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/E4), and ω_{2g}, …, ω_{2g+d−2} are of the third kind (only simple poles) and complete a basis of H¹_dR(Y/Q); V_dR(Y) := H¹_dR(Y/Q)^* with dual basis T_0, …, T_{2g+d−2}; and an admissible Tate class Z = Σ Z_ij ω_i ⊗ ω_j, i, j < 2g, given by its coefficient matrix (Z_ij) ∈ M_{2g}(Q), nonzero, with (a) Z ∈ (H¹_dR ⊗ H¹_dR)^{φ = p} over Q_p, (b) Z ∈ Fil¹, which in this basis means Z_ij = 0 for i, j ≥ g, (c) Σ Z_ij (ω_i ∪ ω_j) = 0, which in this basis means Σ_{i<g} Z_{i,g+i} = 0 once (d) holds, and (d) Zᵀ = −Z. Conditions (a)–(d) are NC.5's; the class of a nice correspondence satisfies them, and the converse of BDMTV Lemma 4.7 is not used (E5).

**Hypotheses.** X smooth projective geometrically connected of genus g ≥ 2 over Q; p a prime of good reduction; b ∈ Y(Q) integral at p. ω_0, …, ω_{g−1} holomorphic; ω_0, …, ω_{2g−1} of the second kind with symplectic classes; ω_{2g}, …, ω_{2g+d−2} of the third kind. Z nonzero with (a)–(d). D is nonempty, and L may be enlarged to a finite Galois splitting field so the local-expansion descent is stated over all conjugate boundary points.

**Proof route.**

- Over Q, take a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X of genus g≥2, a nonempty reduced boundary divisor D of degree d=#D(Qbar) and affine open Y=X−D, b∈Y(Q), a good prime p and a smooth Z_p-model with integral b. Put A=Γ(Y,O_Y), K=Q(X)=Frac(A). Choose a finite Galois splitting field L for D and uniformizers t_x identifying completed local rings at x∈D(L) with L[[t_x]] and their fraction fields with L((t_x)); expansions must be the maps induced by K⊗L, not arbitrary Laurent-family maps. Choose ω_0,…,ω_{2g+d−2} in Ω¹(Y/Q) whose classes form a basis of H¹_dR(Y), the first2g of the second kind, the firstg a basis of H⁰(X,Ω¹), with cup matrix C=[[0,I],[-I,0]], and third-kind complement with residue map an isomorphism onto {(r_x):Σr_x=0}. Put V_dR=H¹_dR(X)^* with dual basis T_i. Take nonzero rational tensor Z with antisymmetry, lower-right g×g block0 and zero cup contraction; under crystalline/de Rham comparison require Frobenius weight p, in coordinates FᵀZF=pZ. For height applications additionally supply an actual nice correspondence whose cycle class is Z; do not infer a rational algebraic cycle from these linear/Frobenius conditions. The suggested file keeps only its separately named linear-data helper; the exact geometric signature and API are in suggestedOmissions.
- The residue map from span(ω_{2g}, …, ω_{2g+d−2}) to L^D is injective with image the sum-zero hyperplane, because the kernel of H¹_dR(Y) → L^d is H¹_dR(X) (BDMTV proof of Lemma 4.10); this is the property explicit-connection uses.
- Condition (b) reads Z_ij = 0 for i, j ≥ g only because ω_0, …, ω_{g−1} span Fil¹; condition (c) reads Σ_{i<g} Z_{i,g+i} = 0 only for the symplectic convention.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.ExplicitSetup.residue_injective` (characterisation): A combination Σ_k c_k ω_{2g+k} of the third-kind differentials with Res_x = 0 at every x ∈ D is zero; equivalently the residue matrix (Res_x ω_{2g+k}) has rank d − 1 and columns summing to zero.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.ExplicitSetup.cupMatrix_eq` (data): The cup product matrix of ω_0, …, ω_{2g−1} is fromBlocks 0 1 (−1) 0 in the block decomposition (holomorphic, non-holomorphic).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.AdmissibleTateMatrix.transpose_eq_neg` (projection): Zᵀ = −Z.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.AdmissibleTateMatrix.lowerRight_eq_zero` (projection): Z_ij = 0 for i, j in the non-holomorphic block.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.AdmissibleTateMatrix.trace_cup_eq_zero` (projection): Σ_{i<g} Z_{i,g+i} = 0, equivalently trace(Z · Cᵀ) = 0 for the cup product matrix C.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.AdmissibleTateMatrix.linearConditions` (structure): Matrices satisfying (b)–(d) form a Q-subspace of M_{2g}(Q); admissible classes are its nonzero elements meeting (a).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.ExplicitSetup.functionField` (projection): The actual function field Q(X)=Frac Γ(Y,O_Y), with its induced boundary expansions into L((t_x)); the geometric projection is omitted with ExplicitSetup.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.ExplicitSetup.tateFrobenius` (compatibility): The actual tensor class is identified through crystalline/de Rham comparison and satisfies FᵀZF=pZ at the chosen good prime; linear matrix conditions alone do not imply this.

**Tests.**

- `admissibleTate_xs13_Z1` (computation): The 6×6 integer matrix Z1 of BDMTV p.931 satisfies (b), (c), (d): it is antisymmetric, its lower-right 3×3 block is zero and Z1(0,3) + Z1(1,4) + Z1(2,5) = 10 + 1 − 11 = 0.
- `admissibleTate_zero` (degenerate): The zero matrix satisfies the linear conditions (b)–(d) but is excluded by nonzeroness. This test concerns the matrix carrier, not a construction of the geometric mixed extension.
- `admissibleTate_symmetric` (non-example): The matrix fromBlocks 0 1 1 0 (symmetric, nonzero) fails (d).
- `explicitSetup_cupMatrix_g1` (compatibility): For g = 1 the cup product matrix is the 2×2 matrix with rows (0, 1) and (−1, 0), the standard symplectic form, Matrix.fromBlocks 0 1 (−1) 0.
- `explicitSetup_frobenius_nonexample` (non-example): A nonzero matrix satisfying only(b)–(d), together with F=I and p=17, fails FᵀZF=17Z and cannot supply an ExplicitSetup Tate class. The actual comparison is in the ExplicitSetup omission.

**Acceptance.** X_s(13), Y = {Z ≠ 0}, b = P2 = (0,0), g = 3: ω = (1, x, y, …)dx/Q_y and Z1, Z2 of xs13-tate-classes form a set-up. A symmetric nonzero matrix is never admissible, by (d).

**Direct prerequisites.** `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.5`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.2`; `mathlib:Matrix`; `mathlib:Matrix.fromBlocks`; `mathlib:Matrix.transpose`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — §4.1, pp.909–910. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/39 with the holomorphy of ω_0, …, ω_{g−1} added (E4). `bdmtv-2019` — §4.1, p.909. Printed hypothesis; the corrected set-up adds holomorphy of the first g differentials. `bdmtv-2019` — §4.4, p.913. Condition (d); conditions (a)–(d) are NC.5's admissible Tate classes, the converse Lemma 4.7 is false (E5).

**Consumers.** BDMTV 2019 §§4–5, pp.909–926: all explicit formulas (26)–(49) are written in this basis and trivialisation. BDMTV 2021 Remark 3.1 and §4.1, pp.6, 17: the integral symplectic basis of step (2) of Algorithm 3.12. EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.6/xs13-first-chart-hodge-data: instantiated with X_s(13), Y = {Z ≠ 0}, b = P2.
