<a id="ED-6-explicit-connection"></a>

### The connection of A_Z on the affine chart and the uniqueness of η

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-connection` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.ExplicitSetup.eta_existsUnique` · implementation unchecked.

In an explicit set-up, there is a trivialisation s_0(b, ·) : (Q ⊕ V_dR ⊕ Q(1)) ⊗ O_Y ≅ A_Z(b)|_Y (26) in which ∇ = d + Λ with Λ = −[[0, 0, 0], [ω, 0, 0], [η, ωᵀZ, 0]] (27), in the ordered basis 1, T_0, …, T_{2g−1}, S, where ω = (ω_0, …, ω_{2g−1})ᵀ and η is a differential in the span of ω_{2g}, …, ω_{2g+d−2}. Moreover η is the unique differential in that span for which d + Λ extends to a connection on X without singularities (Lemma 4.10); equivalently, with the gauge data of gauge-transformation, Res_x(Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x − η) = 0 for every x ∈ D (30). In terms of residues: η = Σ_k c_k ω_{2g+k} where (c_k) is the unique solution of Σ_k c_k Res_x(ω_{2g+k}) = Res_x(Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x) for all x ∈ D.

**Hypotheses.** An explicit set-up with admissible Tate class Z. A_Z(b) is the filtered connection obtained by pushing out A_2^dR along Z (NC.5).

**Proof route.**

- Kim's universal property (NC.2, BDMTV Theorem 4.2, corrected as in E6 to pointed objects with v in the fibre at b) gives A_2^dR(Y) = ⊕_{i≤2} V_dR(Y)^{⊗i} ⊗ O_Y with ∇(v ⊗ 1) = −Σ (T_i ⊗ v) ⊗ ω_i (21); Corollary 4.4 identifies A_2^dR(X)|_Y with its maximal quotient extending holomorphically to X.
- Pushing out along Z (which factors through V_dR^{⊗2}/Im ∪^* by (c)) gives a connection of the form (27) with η = Σ_{i ≤ 2g+d−2} α_i ω_i; the change T_i ↦ T_i + α_i S for i < 2g removes the components of η along ω_0, …, ω_{2g−1} (Remarks 4.8–4.9).
- At x ∈ D the gauge transformation C_x satisfies dg_x = Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x − η (29); a formal primitive g_x exists in L((t_x)) if and only if the residue (30) vanishes, which is the condition for the connection to extend over x.
- By explicit-setup's residue injectivity the residue conditions at the d points determine η uniquely in the span of the third-kind differentials.

**Acceptance.** For X_s(13) on Y = {Z ≠ 0}: η_{Z1} = −(44x² + (148/3)xy + 8y²)dx/Q_y and η_{Z2} = (−40x² + 148xy + 36y²)dx/Q_y (xs13-first-chart-hodge-data). The printed step (i) of BDMTV §4.5 uses dΩ_xᵀZΩ_x − η, which determines a different η unless the residues of Ω_xᵀZdΩ_x vanish (PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/E2); the condition here is (30).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-setup`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.2`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.5`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — (26)–(27), Remarks 4.8–4.9, pp.914–915. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/49. `bdmtv-2019` — Lemma 4.10 and (30), pp.915–916. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/51.

<a id="ED-6-gauge-transformation"></a>

### Gauge transformations at the points at infinity

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/gauge-transformation` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.gaugeMatrix` · implementation unchecked.

In an explicit set-up, for x ∈ D with local parameter t_x over L, a trivialisation s_x of A_Z over L[[t_x]] with connection d exists because every unipotent connection on a formal disc is trivial, and the gauge transformation C_x := s_x^(−1) ∘ s_0 ∈ End(Q ⊕ V_dR ⊕ Q(1)) ⊗ L((t_x)) satisfies C_x^(−1) dC_x = Λ (28). Conversely every unipotent C_x with (28) defines such s_x. Explicitly C_x = [[1, 0, 0], [Ω_x, 1, 0], [g_x, Ω_xᵀZ, 1]] where Ω_x ∈ L((t_x))^{2g} and g_x ∈ L((t_x)) satisfy dΩ_x = −ω and dg_x = Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x − η (29); Ω_x and g_x are determined up to additive constants, and the condition of hodge-filtration-explicit does not depend on these constants.

**Hypotheses.** An explicit set-up and the connection matrix Λ of explicit-connection. t_x is a uniformiser at x ∈ D over L, chosen Gal(L/Q)-equivariantly.

**Proof route.**

- Expand C^(−1)dC for C = [[1,0,0],[Ω,1,0],[g,ΩᵀZ,1]]: C^(−1) = [[1,0,0],[−Ω,1,0],[ΩᵀZΩ − g, −ΩᵀZ, 1]] (using ΩᵀZΩ = 0 by antisymmetry) and C^(−1)dC = [[0,0,0],[dΩ,0,0],[dg − ΩᵀZdΩ, dΩᵀZ, 0]].
- Comparing with Λ = −[[0,0,0],[ω,0,0],[η,ωᵀZ,0]] gives dΩ = −ω, dΩᵀZ = −ωᵀZ and dg = ΩᵀZdΩ − η, which is (29).
- Ω_x is a vector of formal primitives of −ω, which exist in L((t_x)) because ω_0, …, ω_{2g−1} are of the second kind; g_x exists exactly when (30) holds (explicit-connection).
- Changing Ω_x by a constant vector c changes g_x by cᵀZΩ_x plus a constant; the principal parts used in hodge-filtration-explicit change by terms involving only Z's columns of holomorphic index and the holomorphic primitives, which are regular.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.gaugeMatrix` (data): gaugeMatrix Ω g Z is the block matrix [[1,0,0],[Ω,1,0],[g,ΩᵀZ,1]] indexed by Unit ⊕ Fin (2g) ⊕ Unit.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.gaugeMatrix_inv` (characterisation): For alternating Z (Zᵀ = −Z with zero diagonal; automatic over Q), the inverse of gaugeMatrix Ω g Z is [[1,0,0],[−Ω,1,0],[−g, −ΩᵀZ, 1]].
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.gaugeMatrix_det` (simp): det (gaugeMatrix Ω g Z) = 1.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.gaugeMatrix_gauge_iff` (characterisation): For a derivation D of a commutative ring R and antisymmetric Z with D-constant entries: gaugeMatrix⁻¹ · D(gaugeMatrix) = Λ(ω, η, Z) if and only if D Ω = −ω and D g = Ωᵀ Z (D Ω) − η.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.gaugeMatrix_shift` (compatibility): gaugeMatrix (Ω + c) (g + cᵀZΩ + e) Z = unipotent(c, cᵀZ, e) · gaugeMatrix Ω g Z for constants c, e (the dependence on primitives).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.connectionMatrix` (data): connectionMatrix ω η Z = −[[0,0,0],[ω,0,0],[η,ωᵀZ,0]].

**Tests.**

- `gaugeMatrix_zero` (degenerate): gaugeMatrix 0 0 Z = 1 for every Z.
- `gaugeMatrix_g1_inverse` (computation): For g = 1 (index Unit ⊕ Fin 2 ⊕ Unit), Z = [[0,1],[−1,0]], Ω = (a, b), g = c: gaugeMatrix Ω c Z * [[1,0,0],[−Ω,1,0],[−c,−ΩᵀZ,1]] = 1.
- `gaugeMatrix_sign_convention` (non-example): With D Ω = +ω (the 2021 convention) and ω ≠ 0, gaugeMatrix⁻¹ · D(gaugeMatrix) ≠ Λ(ω, η, Z).
- `gaugeMatrix_unipotent` (characterisation): gaugeMatrix Ω g Z − 1 is nilpotent of order 3.

**Acceptance.** The 2021 restatement of this step uses dΩ_{x,i} = ω_i and defines g_x through the integral of dΩ_xᵀZdΩ_x − η; both deviate from (29) (EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E15, EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E16).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-setup`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-connection`; `mathlib:LaurentSeries`; `mathlib:Derivation`; `mathlib:Matrix`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — (28)–(29), p.915. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/50; the entrywise check of (28) is the proof step above. `bdmtv-2021` — §4.1, p.18 (arXiv v4). The 2021 restatement; it contains the misprints EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E15 and EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E16, and the 2019 convention (29) is the one used here.

**Consumers.** BDMTV 2019 Lemma 4.10 and Theorem 4.11, pp.915–918: the residues of Ω_xᵀZdΩ_x determine η, and the principal parts of g_x determine γ_Fil and b_Fil. BDMTV 2019 (35), p.917: C_x H B_x^(−1) tests whether the candidate Hodge filtration extends over x. BDMTV 2021 §4.1, p.18: precision loss p^(−2ν) in the computation of η, γ_Fil, b_Fil comes from the principal parts of Ω_x.

<a id="ED-6-hodge-filtration-explicit"></a>

### Explicit Hodge filtration of A_Z (BDMTV Theorem 4.11)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/hodge-filtration-explicit` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.hodgeFiltration_basis` · implementation unchecked.

In an explicit set-up with gauge data (Ω_x, g_x)_{x ∈ D}, let N = (0_g, 1_g)ᵀ ∈ M_{2g×g}(Q), the matrix of Fil⁰V_dR ↪ V_dR. (i) There are unique γ_Fil ∈ O(Y) and b_Fil = (b_g, …, b_{2g−1})ᵀ ∈ Q^g such that γ_Fil(b) = 0 and g_x + γ_Fil − b_Filᵀ Nᵀ Ω_x − Ω_xᵀ Z N Nᵀ Ω_x ∈ L[[t_x]] for every x ∈ D (32). (ii) A basis of Fil⁰A_Z|_Y in the trivialisation (26) is {1 + γ_Fil S, T_g + b_g S, …, T_{2g−1} + b_{2g−1} S} (33); equivalently, with Q ⊕ V_dR ⊕ Q(1) filtered by Fil^(−1) = everything, Fil⁰ = Q ⊕ Fil⁰V_dR, Fil¹ = 0 (31), the filtered isomorphism s^Fil can be chosen with s_0^(−1) ∘ s^Fil = [[1,0,0],[0,1,0],[γ_Fil, β_Filᵀ, 1]], β_Fil = (0, …, 0, b_g, …, b_{2g−1})ᵀ (36).

**Hypotheses.** An explicit set-up (with ω_0, …, ω_{g−1} holomorphic, E4) and the gauge transformations of gauge-transformation. The Hodge filtration of A_Z is the one characterised by Hadian's theorem (NC.2).

**Proof route.**

- Uniqueness in (i): if (γ, b) is the difference of two solutions then γ(b) = 0 and γ − bᵀNᵀΩ_x is regular at each x ∈ D, so dγ + Σ_{i≥g} b_i ω_i is regular on X, hence holomorphic. Its class Σ_{i≥g} b_i[ω_i] lies in Fil¹ = span([ω_0], …, [ω_{g−1}]), so b = 0 by linear independence; then γ is a regular function on X, constant, and γ(b) = 0 gives γ = 0.
- With the actual gauges of the mixed connection, use the principal-parts exact sequence 0→L→Γ(Y_L,O)→⊕_{x∈D(L)} L((t_x))/L[[t_x]]→H¹(X_L,O)→0 and H¹_dR(X_L)/Fil¹≅H¹(X_L,O). The principal parts of the primitives of ω_g,…,ω_{2g−1} map to a basis of the last group. For N=(0,I)ᵀ prove existence and uniqueness of γ∈Γ(Y,O), b_Fil∈Q^g with γ(b)=0 and g_x+γ−b_FilᵀNᵀΩ_x−Ω_xᵀZNNᵀΩ_x regular at every boundary point. Descend from L by uniqueness.
- The conditions in (i) do not depend on the additive constants in Ω_x and g_x: the lower right block of Z vanishes (condition (b)) and the primitives of ω_0, …, ω_{g−1} are regular.
- (ii): with B_x = [[1,0],[NᵀΩ_x,1]], C_x H B_x^(−1) has entries Ω_x − NNᵀΩ_x (regular by holomorphy), Ω_xᵀZN (regular since the lower right block of Z is zero) and g_x + γ_Fil − b_FilᵀNᵀΩ_x − Ω_xᵀZNNᵀΩ_x (regular by (i)) (35); hence the subbundle H spanned by (33) extends over X.
- H satisfies Hadian's three conditions (NC.2, BDMTV Theorem 4.5): Griffiths transversality is vacuous for weights 0 and −1, H maps isomorphically onto Fil⁰ of A_1 (top right block zero, middle block the inclusion), and the identity lies in Fil⁰ since γ_Fil(b) = 0; by uniqueness in Hadian's theorem H = Fil⁰A_Z.

**Acceptance.** X_s(13), Y = {Z ≠ 0}, b = P2: β_Fil,Z1 = (0,0,0,0,1/2,1/2)ᵀ, γ_Fil,Z1 = 5y/6 + 3x/2; β_Fil,Z2 = (0,0,0,0,−1/2,−5/2)ᵀ, γ_Fil,Z2 = −5y/6 − 15x/2. For Z = 0: η = 0, b_Fil = 0, γ_Fil = 0, and Fil⁰A_Z is the split filtration.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-setup`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/gauge-transformation`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-connection`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.2`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.5`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — Theorem 4.11, p.917. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/52. `bdmtv-2019` — §4.5, p.916. The omitted argument is supplied in the proof steps (uniqueness uses E4).

<a id="ED-6-hodge-filtration-algorithm"></a>

### Algorithm for the Hodge filtration data (η, b_Fil, γ_Fil)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/hodge-filtration-algorithm` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.HodgeFiltrationData` · implementation unchecked.

Input: an explicit set-up with exact data over Q and L (the differentials as elements of the function field of Y, the points of D with Galois-equivariant parameters t_x) and an admissible Tate matrix Z. Steps: (i) for each x ∈ D compute the Laurent expansions of ω_0, …, ω_{2g+d−2} at x to certified orders sufficient for every residue and principal part below; these orders must account for products of primitives, not just the largest pole order of an individual differential, and formal primitives Ω_x with dΩ_x = −ω; compute η = Σ_k c_k ω_{2g+k} as the unique solution of Σ_k c_k Res_x(ω_{2g+k}) = Res_x(Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x) for all x ∈ D (condition (30), not the printed step (i), E2); (ii) solve dg_x = Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x − η for the principal part of g_x in L((t_x))/L[[t_x]]; (iii) compute the principal parts of Ω_xᵀZNNᵀΩ_x and solve the finite linear system for b_Fil ∈ Q^g and γ_Fil in a finite-dimensional space of functions on Y with certified pole bounds derived from those principal parts (for X_s(13): H⁰(X, O(2D))) with γ_Fil(b) = 0, as in hodge-filtration-explicit (32); output (η, b_Fil, γ_Fil) and β_Fil = (0, b_Fil). Given these sufficient truncation and pole bounds, all steps are finite exact linear algebra over L and terminate; the output is checked by substituting into (30) and (32), which is the certificate.

**Hypotheses.** Exact input data over Q and L; certified sufficient Laurent truncation orders for the residue and product/principal-part computations are supplied. A finite-dimensional Riemann–Roch space containing γ_Fil is supplied with a certified pole bound for the expressions in (32); a bound from the individual differential poles alone is not claimed sufficient.

**Proof route.**

- Step (i) is a linear system of d equations (one per x ∈ D) in the d − 1 unknowns c_k; it has rank d − 1 by explicit-setup's residue injectivity and is consistent because η exists (explicit-connection), so its solution is unique.
- Step (ii) determines the principal part of g_x because the residue of its derivative vanishes by (i).
- Step (iii) has a unique solution by hodge-filtration-explicit (i) once the chosen finite-dimensional function space contains γ_Fil. A sufficient pole bound must be deduced from g_x, Ω_xᵀZNNᵀΩ_x and b_FilᵀNᵀΩ_x; the maximum pole order of the individual ω_i does not justify this. The general bound and its certified computation are recorded as a gap.
- Verification: the output satisfies (30) and (32) by exact arithmetic over L; no p-adic precision enters, so the Hodge data are exact rational data.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.HodgeFiltrationData` (structure): A structure with fields etaCoeff : Fin (d − 1) → L, bFil : Fin g → L (rational in the application) and gammaFil in the coordinate ring A of Y.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.HodgeFiltrationData.ResidueCondition` (characterisation): The predicate: for every x ∈ D, Σ_k etaCoeff k · Res_x(ω_{2g+k}) = Res_x(Ω_xᵀZdΩ_x), i.e. the residue matrix times etaCoeff equals the target residues.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.HodgeFiltrationData.RegularCondition` (characterisation): The predicate: γ_Fil(b) = 0 and, for every x ∈ D, g_x + γ_Fil − b_FilᵀNᵀΩ_x − Ω_xᵀZNNᵀΩ_x has no terms of negative degree.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.HodgeFiltrationData.ext_of_conditions` (extensionality): Two data satisfying both conditions are equal (hodge-filtration-explicit (i) and explicit-connection).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.HodgeFiltrationData.betaFil` (data): β_Fil := (0, …, 0, b_g, …, b_{2g−1}) ∈ Q^{2g}.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.HodgeFiltrationData.smul` (functoriality): Replacing Z by λZ (λ ∈ Q) replaces (η, b_Fil, γ_Fil) by (λη, λb_Fil, λγ_Fil).

**Tests.**

- `hodgeData_xs13_Z1_beta` (computation): For X_s(13), Z1: betaFil = (0,0,0,0,1/2,1/2) and gammaFil = 5y/6 + 3x/2.
- `hodgeData_zero` (degenerate): For Z = 0 the unique data are η = 0, b_Fil = 0, γ_Fil = 0.
- `hodgeData_printed_step_nonexample` (non-example): Since Z is antisymmetric, the printed residue condition Res_x(dΩ_xᵀZΩ_x − η') = 0 gives η' = −η, which differs from η and violates ResidueCondition whenever some Res_x(Ω_xᵀZdΩ_x) ≠ 0.
- `hodgeData_linear` (compatibility): The map Z ↦ (η, b_Fil, γ_Fil) is Q-linear: the data for Z1 + Z2 are the sums (agreement with the module structure of admissible matrices).

**Acceptance.** X_s(13), Y = {Z ≠ 0}, b = P2, Z = Z1: output η_{Z1} = −(44x² + (148/3)xy + 8y²)dx/Q_y, β_Fil = (0,0,0,0,1/2,1/2), γ_Fil = 5y/6 + 3x/2.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-connection`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/gauge-transformation`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/hodge-filtration-explicit`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — end of §4.5, p.918. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/53, with step (i) corrected to (30) (E2). `bdmtv-2021` — §4.1, p.18 (arXiv v4). In the 2021 algorithm Z is known only modulo p^n; with exact Z (from exact Hecke matrices, xs13-tate-classes) the computation is exact.

<a id="ED-6-transport-matrices"></a>

### Left and right multiplication matrices and parallel transport

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/transport-matrices` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.leftMulMatrix` · implementation unchecked.

Let Z be an antisymmetric 2g × 2g matrix over a commutative ring R. The algebra A_Z(R) = R ⊕ R^{2g} ⊕ R (the quotient of the truncated tensor algebra of V_dR by the kernel of Z on degree two) has multiplication (a, b, c)·(a', b', c') = (aa', ab' + a'b, ac' + a'c + bᵀZb'). In the ordered basis 1, T_0, …, T_{2g−1}, S, left multiplication by u = (a, b, c) has matrix L(u) = [[a, 0, 0], [b, a·1, 0], [c, bᵀZ, a]] and right multiplication has matrix R(u) = [[a, 0, 0], [b, a·1, 0], [c, −bᵀZ, a]] (44). For points b, b_0, x, x_0 in residue discs, with I(x_1, x_2) = 1 + Σ_w ∫_{x_1}^{x_2} w(ω_0, …, ω_{2g+d−2}) the iterated integrals of words of length ≤ 2 (the index range corrected as in EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E24) pushed to A_Z, the transport τ_{b,x} : A_Z^dR(b_0, x_0) → A_Z^dR(b, x) is v ↦ I(x_0, x) · v · I(b, b_0) (41), so its matrix is L(I(x_0, x)) · R(I(b, b_0)), with Coleman (Besser) integrals between different discs and power-series integrals inside a disc. The Frobenius operators satisfy φ_Z(b_0, x_0) = x_0^* Φ_Z and φ_Z(b, x) = τ_{b,x} ∘ φ_Z(b_0, x_0) ∘ τ_{b,x}^(−1) (43).

**Hypotheses.** Z antisymmetric (condition (d)); R commutative. Iterated integrals are Coleman integrals (ColemanIntegration L1), normalised as in (40)–(41) with the orientation of E3.

**Proof route.**

- The multiplication is associative with unit (1, 0, 0): for u = (a, b, c), v = (a', b', c'), w = (a'', b'', c'') both (uv)w and u(vw) have S-coordinate aa'c'' + aa''c' + a'a''c + a''bᵀZb' + a'bᵀZb'' + ab'ᵀZb''.
- Left multiplication: u·(a', b', c') = (aa', ab' + a'b, ac' + a'c + bᵀZb') gives the columns of L(u).
- Right multiplication: (a', b', c')·u = (a'a, a'b + ab', a'c + ac' + b'ᵀZb) and b'ᵀZb = −bᵀZb' by antisymmetry, giving R(u).
- Path composition I(x_1, x_3) = I(x_2, x_3)·I(x_1, x_2) (Lemma 4.3, NC.2) and Besser's Frobenius-equivariant transport (NC.2, BDMTV (41)) give τ_{b,x}; the orientation is I(x_0, x) on the left and I(b, b_0) on the right (E3).

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.leftMulMatrix` (data): leftMulMatrix Z (a, b, c) = [[a,0,0],[b,a·1,0],[c,bᵀZ,a]] indexed by Unit ⊕ Fin n ⊕ Unit.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.rightMulMatrix` (data): rightMulMatrix Z (a, b, c) = [[a,0,0],[b,a·1,0],[c,−bᵀZ,a]].
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.leftMulMatrix_mul` (relation): leftMulMatrix Z (u * v) = leftMulMatrix Z u * leftMulMatrix Z v.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.rightMulMatrix_mul` (relation): For antisymmetric Z, rightMulMatrix Z (u * v) = rightMulMatrix Z v * rightMulMatrix Z u.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.leftMul_rightMul_comm` (relation): leftMulMatrix Z u and rightMulMatrix Z v commute (associativity).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.transportMatrix` (constructor): transportMatrix Z Ixx Ibb := leftMulMatrix Z Ixx * rightMulMatrix Z Ibb, the matrix of v ↦ I(x_0,x)·v·I(b,b_0).
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.mulVec_leftMulMatrix` (simp): leftMulMatrix Z u acting on the coordinate vector of v is the coordinate vector of u * v.

**Tests.**

- `leftMulMatrix_one` (degenerate): leftMulMatrix Z (1, 0, 0) = 1 and rightMulMatrix Z (1, 0, 0) = 1.
- `leftMulMatrix_g1` (computation): For n = 2, Z = [[0,1],[−1,0]], u = (1, (1,0), 0) and v = (1, (0,1), 0): u * v = (1, (1,1), 1) and v * u = (1, (1,1), −1).
- `rightMulMatrix_symmetric_nonexample` (non-example): For the symmetric Z = 1 (n = 1) and u = (1, 1, 0), right multiplication by u on (0, 1, 0) gives (0, 1, 1) while −bᵀZ predicts −1: the formula R(u) needs antisymmetry.
- `transport_orientation` (characterisation): The (2,1) block of transportMatrix Z (1, ∫_{x_0}^x ω, ·) (1, ∫_b^{b_0} ω, ·) applied to (1, ∫_{b_0}^{x_0} ω, ·) is ∫_b^x ω (path composition, E3).

**Acceptance.** For u = (1, 0, 0) both matrices are the identity. L(u)L(v) = L(uv), R(u)R(v) = R(vu), and L(u)R(v) = R(v)L(u) by associativity.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-setup`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.2`; `ColemanIntegration:L1/coleman-integral`; `ColemanIntegration:L1/word-algebra-local-expansion`; `mathlib:Matrix`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — §5.3.1, (44), p.922. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/59 (the operators φ_Z(b, x), diagram (43), and the matrices (44)). `bdmtv-2019` — §5.2.1, (41), p.921. The transport formula; the orientation of its use in §5.3.2 is corrected as in E3.

<a id="ED-6-frobenius-structure-matrix"></a>

### The Frobenius structure of A_Z on a chart (BDMTV (45))

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/frobenius-structure-matrix` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.frobeniusStructure_eq` · implementation unchecked.

In an explicit set-up over Q_p, let φ be an overconvergent Frobenius lift on a strict neighbourhood of ]U[ for an open U ⊆ Y_{F_p}, write φ^*ω = Fω + df with F ∈ M_{2g}(Q_p) and f a column vector of overconvergent functions with f(b_0) = 0 for a Teichmüller point b_0 (explicitly supplied Frobenius/cohomology data, with the RD.7 comparison), and set Λ_φ = −[[0,0,0],[φ^*ω,0,0],[φ^*η, φ^*ωᵀZ, 0]]. Then FᵀZF = pZ, and the inverse G = Φ_Z^(−1) of the Frobenius structure is the unique graded-compatible pointed inverse Frobenius of the actual universal quotient, represented by an invertible (2g+2) × (2g+2) matrix of overconvergent functions with Λ_φ G + dG = GΛ and G(b_0)^(−1) sending 1 to 1, namely G = [[1, 0, 0], [f, F, 0], [h, gᵀ, p]], where g is the column vector with dgᵀ = dfᵀZF (the constant fixed by exactness of the next equation) and h is the function with dh = ωᵀFᵀZf + dfᵀZf − gᵀω + φ^*η − pη and h(b_0) = 0.

**Hypotheses.** An explicit set-up over Q_p; p of good reduction; φ an overconvergent Frobenius lift with b_0 Teichmüller. Z satisfies (a): FᵀZF = pZ where F is the Frobenius matrix on H¹_dR in the basis ω (Z is φ = p-invariant, the cup product has Frobenius weight p).

**Proof route.**

- The Frobenius structure Φ_Z : φ^*A_Z^rig ≅ A_Z^rig is a morphism of connections, so in the trivialisation s_0 its inverse G satisfies Λ_φ G + dG = GΛ.
- NC.2 supplies the unique pointed Frobenius Φ_Z and graded-compatible quotient. G=Φ_Z⁻¹ has diagonal(1,F,p); Φ_Z has diagonal(1,F⁻¹,p⁻¹). Pointed normalization at b0 is f(b0)=h(b0)=0; the remaining g constant is fixed by the cohomological reduction, not by f(b0)=0 alone.
- Write the block equations of Λ_φ G + dG = GΛ: the (2,1) block gives df = φ^*ω − Fω; the (3,2) block gives dgᵀ = dfᵀZF using FᵀZF = pZ; the (3,1) block gives dh = ωᵀFᵀZf + dfᵀZf − gᵀω + φ^*η − pη (checked entrywise: PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/60 note).
- Set g0=−FᵀZf. Actual rigid-cohomology reduction of ξ=(φ*ω)ᵀZf+φ*η−pη−g0ᵀω gives ξ=cᵀω+dh; put g=g0+c and h(b0)=0. BDMTV2021v4(4.5)–(4.7)p19 states this step. Take the overconvergent sections and coefficient/error bounds as explicit hypotheses; verify the displayed differential identities. RD.7 supplies the rigid/de Rham comparison, and NC.2 identifies the resulting matrix with the universal Frobenius. No instance-specific RD.7 data producer is requested.

**Acceptance.** For Z = 0 and g = 1 data with φ^*ω = Fω, f = 0: G = [[1,0,0],[0,F,0],[h, 0, p]] with dh = φ^*η − pη. At p = 17 on ]U_1[ for X_s(13) the matrices F, f, g, h are the data of xs13-first-chart-frobenius.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-connection`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-setup`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.2`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.5`; `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7`; `ColemanIntegration:L1/frobenius-lift`; `ColemanIntegration:L1/word-algebra-frobenius`; `ColemanIntegration:L1/teichmuller-point`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — §5.3.2, (45), pp.922–923. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/60. The rigid/de Rham comparison is imported from RD.7; actual Tuitman coefficient and precision tables are supplied hypotheses (PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/95). `bdmtv-2019` — Lemma 5.2, p.919. Uniqueness of the Frobenius structure (NC.2's, consumed). `bdmtv-2021` — §4.2,(4.5)–(4.7),p19(arXivv4). The g0, ξ, c and H construction fixes the constant term in g by rigid-cohomology reduction.

<a id="ED-6-frobenius-equivariant-splitting"></a>

### The Frobenius-equivariant splitting at Teichmüller and general points

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/frobenius-equivariant-splitting` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.frobeniusSplitting_eq` · implementation unchecked.

With G as in frobenius-structure-matrix and x_0 ∈ ]U[ a Teichmüller point, the Frobenius-equivariant splitting s^φ satisfies s_0(b_0, x_0)^(−1) ∘ s^φ(b_0, x_0) = [[1, 0, 0], [(I − F)^(−1)f, 1, 0], [(1/(1 − p))(gᵀ(I − F)^(−1)f + h), gᵀ(F − p)^(−1), 1]] evaluated at x_0 (the unique unipotent matrix S satisfying G(x_0)S=S diag(1,F,p), equivalently G(x_0)^(−1)S=S diag(1,F^(−1),p^(−1))). For arbitrary b, x in residue discs of ]U[ with Teichmüller representatives b_0, x_0, s_0(b, x)^(−1) ∘ s^φ(b, x) = L(I(x_0, x)) · R(I(b, b_0)) · s_0(b_0, x_0)^(−1) ∘ s^φ(b_0, x_0), with L, R from transport-matrices (the corrected orientation, E3). Writing this matrix as [[1,0,0],[α_φ,1,0],[γ_φ,β_φᵀ,1]], α_φ(b, x) = ∫_b^x ω.

**Hypotheses.** frobenius-structure-matrix; x_0 Teichmüller (φ(x_0) = x_0); p > 1 so 1 − p and F − p, I − F are invertible (the eigenvalues of F are Weil numbers of absolute value p^(1/2)).

**Proof route.**

- At a Teichmüller point Frobenius acts on A_Z^dR(b_0, x_0) by G(x_0)^(−1); s^φ is the unique unipotent isomorphism from Q ⊕ V_dR ⊕ Q(1) with Frobenius diag(1,F^(−1),p^(−1)).
- Solving the unipotent conjugation block by block: α = (I − F)^(−1)f(x_0), β = gᵀ(F − p)^(−1), γ = (1/(1 − p))(gᵀα + h(x_0)); invertibility of I − F, F − p and 1 − p follows from the Weil bounds (ColemanIntegration L1/weil-weight-no-root-of-unity).
- (I − F)^(−1)f(x_0) = ∫_{b_0}^{x_0} ω by Frobenius-equivariance of Coleman integration (ColemanIntegration L1/coleman-integration-characterisation).
- General points: s^φ(b, x) = τ_{b,x} ∘ s^φ(b_0, x_0), and τ_{b,x}(v) = I(x_0, x)·v·I(b, b_0) by (41); hence the product of left multiplication by I(x_0, x), right multiplication by I(b, b_0), and the Teichmüller matrix. The (2,1) block is ∫_{x_0}^x ω + ∫_{b_0}^{x_0} ω + ∫_b^{b_0} ω = ∫_b^x ω.

**Acceptance.** For b = b_0 = x_0 = x the matrix is [[1,0,0],[0,1,0],[(1/(1−p))h(b_0), gᵀ(F−p)^(−1), 1]] with h(b_0) = 0. As printed (p.923) the transport factors have reversed limits, giving α_φ(b, x) = α_φ(b_0, x_0) − ∫_{x_0}^x ω − ∫_b^{b_0} ω, which is not ∫_b^x ω (E3).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/frobenius-structure-matrix`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/transport-matrices`; `ColemanIntegration:L1/coleman-integration-characterisation`; `ColemanIntegration:L1/weil-weight-no-root-of-unity`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.2`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — §5.3.2, p.923. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/61, with the orientation of the transport corrected (E3). `bdmtv-2019` — §5.3.2, p.923. The printed product whose limits E3 corrects.

<a id="ED-6-local-height-at-p"></a>

### The local height at p of A_Z(b, x) (BDMTV Lemma 5.5)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/local-height-at-p` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.localHeight_eq` · implementation unchecked.

Let s be a splitting of the Hodge filtration of V_dR with idempotents s_1, s_2 onto s(V_dR/Fil⁰) and Fil⁰, and χ_p the local component of the fixed idèle class character. For x ∈ X(Q_p) ∩ ]U[, with γ_Fil, β_Fil from hodge-filtration-explicit and α_φ, β_φ, γ_φ from frobenius-equivariant-splitting, the local height of the mixed extension A_Z(b, x) is h_p(A_Z(b, x)) = χ_p(γ_φ(b, x) − γ_Fil(b, x) − β_φ(b, x)ᵀ · s_1(α_φ(b, x)) − β_Fil(b)ᵀ · s_2(α_φ(b, x))). As a function of x on each residue disc it is a convergent power series in the disc parameter whose coefficients are computable from the data above, and θ_Z(x) := h_p(A_Z(b, x)) is the function of the quadratic Chabauty pair.

**Hypotheses.** The splitting s and the character χ are fixed (independence of the zero set from both is NC.5's). x lies in a residue disc of ]U[ where φ is defined and no basis differential has a pole.

**Proof route.**

- By NC.5 (BDMTV Lemma 5.4) D_cris(A_Z(b, x)) ≅ A_Z^dR(b, x) as filtered φ-modules, with A_Z^dR(b, x) = x^*A_Z.
- The height formula (17) (NC.5) expresses h_p of a mixed extension through the matrices of s^φ and s^Fil relative to a vector-space splitting s_0.
- Take s_0 = s_0(b, x) of (26); then s_0^(−1) ∘ s^Fil is given by hodge-filtration-explicit (36) evaluated at x and s_0^(−1) ∘ s^φ by frobenius-equivariant-splitting; substitute into (17).
- On a residue disc, γ_Fil is a rational function, α_φ, β_φ, γ_φ are single and double Coleman integrals in the parameter (power-series integrals inside the disc), so θ_Z is a convergent power series there.

<a id="ED-6-base-point-change"></a>

### Changing the base point (BDMTV Lemma 5.7)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/base-point-change` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.baseChange_splitting_eq` · implementation unchecked.

Let b' ∈ X(Q_p) lie in a residue disc where none of the basis differentials has a pole. Then β_Fil(b') = β_Fil(b) and γ_Fil(b', x) = γ_Fil(b, x) − γ_Fil(b, b') (48), and s_0(b', b')^(−1) ∘ s^φ(b', b') = [[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, β_φ(b, b)ᵀ + 2∫_b^{b'} ωᵀZ, 1]]. Consequently the local heights h_p(A_Z(b', x)) for x in the disc of b', and in particular in a disc where the Frobenius lift is not defined, are computed from the single integrals ∫_b^{b'} ω (Coleman integrals with the original lift) and power-series integrals inside the disc of b'. The formula changes the individual scalar height functions; only the naturally identified Chabauty–Kim locus is base-point independent. For the global rational-point application take rational b′ and transport the NC.5 height-pair data as well.

**Hypotheses.** b' in a residue disc with no poles of ω_0, …, ω_{2g+d−2}; Coleman integrals between discs are taken with respect to the original Frobenius lift (BDMTV §5.5).

**Proof route.**

- The Hodge data: by hodge-filtration-explicit the conditions (32) for b' differ from those for b only in the normalisation γ(b') = 0, giving (48).
- The φ-equivariant unipotent isomorphism A_2^dR(Y)(b, b) → A_2^dR(Y)(b', b'), s_0(b, b)(v) ↦ s_0(b', b')(I(b, b')·v·I(b', b)) (49), passes to the quotient A_Z.
- With L, R of transport-matrices the matrix is L(I(b, b')) · R(I(b, b'))^(−1) · s_0(b,b)^(−1)s^φ(b,b), where I(b', b) = I(b, b')^(−1); multiplying out with Z antisymmetric gives zero (2,1) block and (3,2) block β_φ(b, b)ᵀ + 2∫_b^{b'}ωᵀZ (PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/65 note: the arXiv v1 product order L·M·R^(−1) gives a wrong (3,1) entry).
- Across residue discs the integrals are Coleman integrals; the identification of (41) with the Frobenius-equivariant transport is NC.2's (B19 item 93).

**Acceptance.** For b' = b the formula reduces to s_0(b,b)^(−1)s^φ(b,b) = [[1,0,0],[0,1,0],[0,β_φ(b,b)ᵀ,1]]. X_s(13): b' = P0 = (1:1:1) (xs13-p0-disc).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/hodge-filtration-explicit`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/frobenius-equivariant-splitting`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/transport-matrices`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.2`; `ColemanIntegration:L1/coleman-integral`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — §5.5, Lemma 5.7, p.925. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/65 (with (48)–(49)). `bdmtv-2019` — §5.5, p.925. Purpose of the lemma in the X_s(13) computation.

<a id="ED-6-height-series-valuation-bound"></a>

### Valuation bounds for the coefficients of quadratic Chabauty power series

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/height-series-valuation-bound` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.valuation_coeff_ge` · implementation unchecked.

(i) (BDMTV 2019 §6.4.1.) Let F_1, …, F_m ∈ Z_p[[t]] and let G(t) = Σ_n c_n t^n = Σ_{i,j} a_ij ∫F_i(∫F_j) + Σ_i a_i ∫F_i + Σ_i b_i F_i with a_ij, a_i, b_i ∈ Q_p, where ∫ denotes the formal primitive vanishing at t = 0. Then v_p(c_n) ≥ min_{i,j}{v_p(a_ij), v_p(a_i), v_p(b_i)} − 2⌊log_p n⌋ for n ≥ 1. (ii) For the actual QC function ρ=h−h_p on D⊂X(Q_p)∩]U[, under BDMTV2021§4 standing hypotheses (p-integral F,Z and local expansions of ω,ωᵀZ; fixed End(J)-equivariant Hodge splitting), choose t at x1∈D, t(D)⊂pZ_p and Teichmüller x0. Use ord_p(0)=∞; for matrices/vectors use the minimum of entry valuations, including the diagonal1 of λφ so c1≤0. Certify c1=ord_p(λφ(x1)) by Frobenius evaluation and path-transport precision, v_spl=min valuation of the splitting coefficients, b=ord_p(βFil), a=ord_p(γFil), c2=min{0,v_spl,b,v_spl+b}, and c3=min_j ord_p(d_j) for the genuine global-height expansion h=Σd_jΨ_j. Let d_i(η) be certified lower bounds for the actual degree i−1 coefficient of η (all coefficient/coordinate changes included); the source uses a finite polynomial-coefficient branch and0 after its degree bound, whose sufficiency must be proved for the actual model. With ℓ_i=⌊log_p i⌋ for i≥1 put φ(i)=−ℓ_i+min{d_i(η),−ℓ_i}. The branches are φ(i)=d_i(η)−ℓ_i if d_i(η)<−ℓ_i, otherwise φ(i)=−2ℓ_i; the λφ coefficients have lower bound φ(i)+c1. Explicitly certify i0≥1 such that for every i≥i0, −ℓ_i≤d_i(η), 2(−ℓ_i)≤b and 2(−ℓ_i)≤a−c2 (the floor-half inequalities on publishedp1136). Then ord_p(ρ_i)≥−2ℓ_i+c1+min{c2,c3} for i≥i0 (Proposition4.6). Coefficients0≤i<i0 require their own finite valuation certificates; all-zero βFil,γFil or global-height coefficients use∞ and omit vacuous comparisons instead of assigning integer0. The actual coordinate/differential estimates and algebraic cancellations proving this height bound remain obligations; do not derive it solely from arbitrary matrices or assume the final coefficient inequality. For the elementary single/double-integral estimate of BDMTV2019pp932–933 retain the separate helper iteratedIntegral_valuation_coeff_ge. The source notation φ in preprintv4p24 has an extra+c1 corrected in publishedp1136; use publishedφ and addc1 once to the splitting bound. This is Proposition4.6, not Proposition4.1; the latter evaluates G(P).

**Hypotheses.** F_i have p-integral coefficients (after scaling the disc parameter so that the basis differentials are integral on the disc). The constants c_1, c_2, c_3 and i_0 are computed from certified data (ED.0 valuation certificates). Use Proposition4.6 in arXivv4p25/publishedp1136; Proposition4.1 is a different Frobenius-evaluation statement. Source coefficient estimates are consumed through the precise geometric §13 contract, with zero/finite-index branches explicit.

**Proof route.**

- Integrating t^(n−1) divides by n, which costs v_p(n) ≤ ⌊log_p n⌋; a double integral costs at most twice that, and the coefficients a, b contribute their valuation: this is (i).
- Compute c1 from the actual Frobenius splitting at the disc centre and derive the local transport branch φ(i) from the actual integral expansions; the underlying coordinate coefficient lower bounds must be certified. Combine Nekovář’s formula with βFil,γFil and the fixed equivariant splitting. The required coefficient semantics and all constants are spelled out in suggestedOmissions.
- For i≥i0 use the three explicit threshold inequalities to select φ(i)=−2⌊log_p i⌋. Combine the actual global-height coefficient bound c3 and local-height bound to obtain Proposition4.6. For smaller i use finite certificates; zero coefficients have valuation∞. E30 records the preprint branch corrected in the published paper.
- The valuations of the input constants are certified by ED.0/valuation-certificate.

**Acceptance.** For p = 17 and n < 17, ⌊log_p n⌋ = 0, so the first 16 coefficients lose no precision to integration; at n = 17 the loss is 2. X_s(13): with enough coefficients the slopes beyond the precision are ≥ −1 and give no Q_p-rational zeros (BDMTV p.933). The low-degree branch0≤i<i0 is certified separately; a tail bound alone never certifies the constant coefficient. At equality d_i(η)=−⌊log_p i⌋ both branch formulas agree. With c1≠0, it enters λφ and the final bound once; do not use the preprint’s erroneous φ(i)=−2⌊log_p i⌋+c1.

Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/89 (the elementary estimate; residue-disc zero bounds in general are ED.4's). `bdmtv-2021` — Proposition 4.6, p.25 (arXiv v4). The general bound with the constants c_1, c_2, c_3. `bdmtv-2023-published` — §4.4,pp1135–1136,Proposition4.6 and preceding i0 inequality. <a id="ED-6-root-determination-precision"></a>

### Provable determination of roots in a residue disc

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/root-determination-precision` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.roots_determined_of_truncation` · implementation unchecked.

(BDMTV 2021 Lemma 4.7.) Let F(x) = Σ_{i≥0} F_i x^i ∈ Q_p[[x]] such that F(pT) is restricted (its coefficients tend to zero), and integers k, m, n with n > k, m ≥ 1, min_i{ord_p(F_i) + i} = k, using ord_p(0)=+∞, and ord_p(F_i) + i ≥ n for every i ≥ m (that is, max{i : ord_p(F_i) + i < n} < m; the printed condition max{i : ord_p(F_i) + i = n} < m is too weak, EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E21), and suppose F has at most d roots counted with multiplicity over ℂ_p in the closed disc {ord_p(x) ≥ 1}, where d ≥ 1. Then the roots of F over ℂ_p in {ord_p(x) ≥ 1}, with multiplicity, are determined to precision (n − k)/d by F_0, …, F_{m−1} modulo p^n: After setting G(T)=p^(−k)F(pT), choose an actual polynomial H over Q_p with Gauss norm ||G−H||≤p^(−(n−k)). G and H have the same nonzero reduction and hence the same Weierstrass degree D≤d. Their roots in the closed unit disc over completed C_p, counted with multiplicity, admit a matching within radius p^(−(n−k)/d). Transport these balls by x=pT. A residue class solving a congruence is not itself a polynomial root and carries no multiplicity or lift guarantee. With d = 1 after recentring and rescaling (BDMTV 2021 Remark 4.8), each simple root is isolated in a ball containing no other root, which is the (unique) condition of qc-disc-certificate; the number d itself is bounded by the residue-disc zero bound of ED.4 (Strassmann).

**Hypotheses.** F converges on the closed disc ord_p(x) ≥ 1 (ensured by height-series-valuation-bound). The hypotheses on k, m, n are checked from certified coefficient valuations (ED.0).

**Proof route.**

- G(x) := p^(−k)F(px) lies in Z_p[[x]] ∖ pZ_p[[x]] by the definition of k.
- For α ∈ Z_p the positive slopes of the Newton polygon of G(x + α) are determined by the first m coefficients, since ord_p(F_i) + i ≥ n for i ≥ m makes G a polynomial of degree < m modulo p^(n−k).
- If G is congruent modulo p^(n−k) to a polynomial H with a root α of multiplicity e, the first e coefficients of G(x + α) have valuation ≥ n − k; since G(x + α) has degree ≤ m modulo p^(n−k) and a unit coefficient, its Newton polygon has a segment of slope ≥ (n − k)/d of length at least e.
- The zero count d comes from ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound (Strassmann's theorem, ED.4/strassmann-bound).
- Normalize to G with Gauss norm one, choose the nonzero last unit coefficient and identify its Weierstrass degree D with the closed-disc root count. For a polynomial H congruent to G in Gauss norm, use Weierstrass preparation and Newton polygons to match the two root multisets over completed C_p; certify cluster multiplicities and isolation separately. No implication from a bare solution modulo p^N to an actual root is used.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.root_satisfies_truncation_congruence` (other): Supporting necessary congruence for an existing Q_p root, using the supplied tail valuation. No cluster existence, multiplicity or isolation conclusion.

**Acceptance.** A simple root (d = 1) of F in the closed disc ord_p(x) ≥ 1 is determined to precision n − k from F_0, …, F_{m−1} modulo p^n, and its ball contains no other root. F(x) = x² − p^(2N) (N ≥ 1) has the two roots ±p^N in the disc, so d = 2 and k = 2; the lemma determines them only to precision (n − 2)/2, which illustrates the loss for clustered roots and why simple, separated roots are required for isolation.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/height-series-valuation-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/valuation-certificate`; `mathlib:PowerSeries`; `mathlib:Polynomial.roots`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2021` — Lemma 4.7, p.25 (arXiv v4). The statement used to produce disc certificates. `bdmtv-2021` — Remark 4.8, p.25 (arXiv v4). Simple roots and isolation.

<a id="ED-6-qc-modular-algorithm"></a>

### Quadratic Chabauty for modular curves: algorithm with termination and failure conditions

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/qc-modular-algorithm` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.QCOutput` · implementation unchecked.

Input: a curve X/Q (a modular curve or Atkin–Lehner quotient) with certified rank r = g (from the analytic-rank-one route, GZ.8 and HE.7, or from a descent certificate ED.3), rk NS(J) > 1, and image of J(Q) in H⁰(X_{Q_p}, Ω¹)^* of rank g; a covering of X by affine patches birational to plane curves Q(x, y) = 0 monic in y with p-integral coefficients satisfying Tuitman's Assumption 1 (as corrected in June 2020, RD.7); a prime p of good reduction such that T_p generates End⁰(J); for every prime ℓ not of potentially good reduction, the local height functions X(Q_ℓ) → Ker(NS(J) → NS(X))^*_{Q_p} (NC.5, via a regular semistable model); a starting precision n and a height bound B. All instance-specific arithmetic is supplied explicitly: verified known rational points (a height search is not a producer target), a symplectic differential basis and cup matrix, identified Frobenius/Hecke matrices, an equivariant isotropic splitting, actual cycle classes, Hodge/Frobenius splitting coefficient tables, height-pairing values and finite local root/exclusion data with sufficient certified precision and tails. The finite verification checks basis/cup identities, the Eichler–Shimura relation T_p=F_p+pF_p⁻¹, cycle and splitting identities, height-pairing linear equations, and complete root/subdivision witnesses for every covered disc. The geometric identifications and error bounds are hypotheses; producing these numerical tables is outside this roadmap. Output is FAIL with a recorded reason, or a finite candidate list at precision n′≤n whose associated residue balls cover X(Q_p)_2 on the covered discs. A non-FAIL output becomes a certified solution set only through padic-candidate-comparison: match every candidate ball with a known rational point uniquely or exclude it using ED.5. A FAIL output supplies no emptiness conclusion.

**Hypotheses.** The rank hypothesis r = g and the isomorphism of the p-adic logarithm are certified inputs, not outputs (BDMTV 2021 Remark 3.13–3.14). Tuitman's Assumption 1 for each patch at p (RD.7). Local heights away from p are supplied for every bad prime.

**Proof route.**

- Termination: all verification loops run over the supplied finite patches, discs, cycles, matrices, coefficient tables and complete subdivision trees. Failure to supply enough data yields a failure result; no unbounded search or automatic production of the inputs is asserted.
- Soundness of a non-FAIL output: by qc-certificate-sound, each rational point lies in the common zero set on its disc, and the roots are certified by root-determination-precision with the bounds of height-series-valuation-bound.
- Failure conditions are exactly: no integral symplectic basis (2); unsolvable height pairing (6b); precision loss in root finding (6c); a multiple root at a known point (6d). Increasing n remedies precision loss unless the p-adic logarithm fails to be an isomorphism or roots are multiple for geometric reasons (Remark 3.14).
- Unresolved inputs advertised by the output: the rank certificate, the local heights away from p, and the comparison of A with X(Q)_known.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.QCInput` (structure): The input record: patches/equations, p,n,B, rank/logarithm and local-height hypotheses, and all explicitly supplied basis, cup, Hecke/Frobenius, cycle, splitting, height-pairing, coefficient/error/tail and finite root/subdivision data specified in the statement. No table producer or complete-answer assertion is an input.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.QCFailure` (data): The four failure reasons: noIntegralSymplecticBasis, heightPairingUnsolved, precisionLoss, multipleRootAtKnownPoint.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.QCOutput` (data): Either fail (r : QCFailure) or candidates (A : Finset of points to precision n') with n' ≤ n.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.QCOutput.candidates_sound` (characterisation): If the output is candidates A then every rational point of X in a covered disc reduces modulo p^(n') to an element of A.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.QCOutput.toCertifiedSolutionSet` (constructor): From a candidates output, matchings with X(Q)_known and exclusions, the certified solution set of padic-candidate-comparison.
- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.QCOutput.fail_ne_empty` (other): A fail output yields no certificate: no theorem identifies it with the empty candidate set.

**Tests.**

- `qcOutput_x0plus97` (computation): For X_0^+(97), p = 5, the output is candidates of ten points matching (1:0:0), (−2:1:1), (−1:0:1), (0:0:1), (0:1:0), (0:−1:1), (1:0:1), (1:1:1), (−1:1:0), (5:3:2).
- `qcOutput_no_patch` (degenerate): If the patches cover no residue disc, candidates ∅ asserts nothing about X(Q) (the covered-disc condition is empty).
- `qcOutput_fail_nonexample` (non-example): fail precisionLoss is not candidates ∅: it carries no soundness statement.
- `qcOutput_sieve_compat` (compatibility): If every candidate not in X(Q)_known is excluded by an ED.5 sieve certificate, toCertifiedSolutionSet returns X(Q)_known.

**Acceptance.** X_0^+(97), p = 5: the output consists of the ten known points (x0plus-genus-three-points). X_S4(13), p = 11 on two patches: output the four known points (xs4-13-rational-points).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/qc-certificate-sound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/hodge-filtration-algorithm`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/frobenius-equivariant-splitting`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/padic-candidate-comparison`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/certified-solution-set`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.5/chabauty-sieve-combination`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.5`; `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7`; `ModularCurvesPartII:R14.6`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2021` — Algorithm 3.12, p.14 (arXiv v4). The failure conditions of the algorithm. `bdmtv-2021` — Remark 3.14, p.14 (arXiv v4). Termination versus success: a FAIL is open, not a negative result. `bdmtv-2021` — Assumption 3.10, p.13 (arXiv v4). Tuitman's Assumption 1, imported from RD.7 with the June 2020 correction.

**Consumers.** BDMTV 2021 §5, pp.25–36: all example computations (X_S4(13), X_0^+(N), Program B curves, X_ns^+(17)) are runs of this algorithm. BDMTV 2019 §6, pp.926–934: the X_s(13) computation is the special case with p = 17, two patches and a base-point change for ](1:1:1)[. EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.6 stage acceptance: the algorithm advertises its termination conditions, its failure outputs and its unresolved inputs.

<a id="ED-6-xs13-plane-model"></a>

### Plane quartic model of X_s(13), its seven known points and the residue discs at 17

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-plane-model` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xs13_planeModel` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, let B(X, Y, Z) := (−Y − Z)X³ + (2Y² + YZ)X² + (−Y³ + Y²Z − 2YZ² + Z³)X + (2Y²Z² − 3YZ³) (Baran's quartic) and Q(X, Y, Z) := Y⁴ + 5X⁴ − 6X²Y² + 6X³Z + 26X²YZ + 10XY²Z − 10Y³Z − 32X²Z² − 40XYZ² + 24Y²Z² + 32XZ³ − 16YZ³. (i) X_s(13) ≅ X_0^+(169) over Q, and the canonical model of X_0^+(169) is the smooth plane quartic B = 0, cut out by the quartic relation among the three Galois conjugates of the newform f of xs13-endomorphism-algebra (which satisfy no quadratic relation). (ii) Q(X − Y, X + Y, X + Z) = 16·B(X, Y, Z), so (X : Y : Z) ↦ (X − Y : X + Y : X + Z) is a Q-isomorphism {B = 0} → {Q = 0}; Q is monic in Y. (iii) B = 0 has good reduction at every prime ≠ 13, and Q = 0 at every prime ≠ 2, 13; Q is smooth modulo 17 and #{Q = 0}(F_17) = 20. (iv) The points P0 = (1 : 1 : 1), P1 = (1 : 1 : 2), P2 = (0 : 0 : 1), P3 = (−3 : 3 : 2), P4 = (1 : 1 : 0), P5 = (0 : 2 : 1), P6 = (−1 : 1 : 0) lie on Q = 0 and have seven distinct reductions modulo 17. (v) With U_1 := {Z ≠ 0, ∂Q/∂Y ≠ 0} and U_2 := {X ≠ 0, ∂Q/∂Y ≠ 0} in X_{F_17}, U_1 contains 17 of the 20 points of X(F_17); the other three are (1 : 1 : 0), (1 : −1 : 0) ∈ U_2 and (1 : 1 : 1), which lies in neither (the disc of P0). The boundary D = {Z = 0} consists of the four points (1 : ±1 : 0), (1 : ±√5 : 0), since Q(X, Y, 0) = (Y² − X²)(Y² − 5X²).

**Hypotheses.** X_s(13) is defined as X(13)/C_s^+(13) over Q (R13.4a). Assume the stated plane quartic is isomorphic over Q to the actual split-Cartan modular curve, via the supplied maps with inverse and cusp/CM identifications. The required q-expansion/Sturm comparison identities and exact coefficient data are hypotheses, not computation targets. Supply finite q-expansion coefficient data and their Sturm comparison identities, the exact good-reduction ideal identities, and the complete F17 projective-point/partial-derivative table with its finite ambient coverage. These data are hypotheses; polynomial/model transport, point membership, smoothness and the20/17 counts are deduced by exact verification, without a target to generate a point-count table.

**Proof route.**

- (i) Import X_s(13) ≅ X_0(169)/w_169 from R13.4a; S_2(Γ_0(169))^{w_169 = +1} has dimension 3, spanned by the conjugates of f (supplied geometric/Hecke data with exact identification hypotheses); their q-expansions give the canonical map; no quadratic relation holds (finite linear algebra on q-expansions), so the curve is not hyperelliptic and its canonical image is a plane quartic; B(f_1, f_2, f_3) is a weight-8 cusp form for Γ_0(169) vanishing to order > 8 · 182/12 at ∞, hence zero by the Sturm bound (supplied geometric/Hecke data with exact identification hypotheses).
- (ii) A polynomial identity of ternary quartics over Z, checked by expansion (both sides agree on the grid {0, …, 4}³, which determines a polynomial of degree ≤ 4 in each variable).
- (iii) Good reduction: an exact certificate that the ideal (B, ∂B/∂X, ∂B/∂Y, ∂B/∂Z) ⊆ Z[X, Y, Z] contains 13^k times a power of the irrelevant ideal (resultant or Gröbner certificate); likewise for Q with 2^k 13^l. Smoothness modulo 17 and the count 20 are finite computations over F_17.
- (iv) Exact evaluation of Q at the seven points, and of their reductions.
- (v) Finite computation over F_17: ∂Q/∂Y vanishes at (1 : 1 : 1), and the points at Z = 0 are (1 : 1 : 0), (1 : 16 : 0); Q(X, Y, 0) factors as stated over Q.

<a id="ED-6-xs13-endomorphism-algebra"></a>

### The endomorphism algebra and Picard number of J_s(13)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-endomorphism-algebra` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xs13_endAlgebra` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, let J := Jac(X_s(13)). The weight-two cusp forms for Γ_0^+(169) (that is, S_2(Γ_0(169))^{w_169 = +1}) form one Galois orbit with coefficient field K := Q(α) = Q(ζ_7)^+, α³ + 2α² − α − 1 = 0, f = q + αq² + (−α² − 2α)q³ + (α² − 2)q⁴ + (α² + 2α − 2)q⁵ + (−α − 1)q⁶ + ⋯. J is Q-isogenous to the optimal quotient A_f = J_0(169)/I_f, End(J) ⊗ Q ≅ K, J is absolutely simple of dimension 3, and ρ(J) := rk NS(J_Q̄) = 3. (Context, not used in the proofs: Chen's isogeny Jac(X_s(ℓ)) ∼ Jac(X_0^+(ℓ²)) ∼ J_0(ℓ) × Jac(X_ns(ℓ)), with J_0(13) = 0, explains why Mazur's method does not apply at ℓ = 13.)

**Hypotheses.** f has neither complex multiplication nor inner twists: a CM newform of level N has CM field of discriminant dividing N, and no imaginary quadratic discriminant divides 169; an inner twist of a trivial-character form is by a quadratic character, here χ_13, and f ⊗ χ_13 = f^σ would give σ(a_3) = a_3 (χ_13(3) = 1), hence σ = id since a_3 generates K, and then a_2 = −a_2 (χ_13(2) = −1), contradicting a_2 = α. Assume the supplied newform-orbit identification, Hecke action matrices, characteristic polynomials and de Rham comparison identities hold for the actual Jacobian. General modular/isogeny theory is imported; generating the matrix table is not a target.

**Proof route.**

- The newform orbit and q-expansion are a certified modular-symbols computation (supplied geometric/Hecke data with exact identification hypotheses).
- J ≅ Jac(X_0^+(169)) is isogenous to the w_169-invariant part of J_0(169), which is A_f because S_2(Γ_0(169))^{+} is spanned by the conjugates of f (ModularCurvesPartII R14.5/modular-quotient, R14.5/trivial-character-J0, R14.5/modular-quotient-dimension: dim A_f = [K : Q] = 3).
- End(A_f) ⊗ Q ≅ K and End_Q̄(A_f) ⊗ Q ≅ K for f without CM and inner twists (Shimura Th. 7.14, Ribet Cor. 4.2; requested from R14.5), so J is absolutely simple.
- NS(J_Q̄) ⊗ Q is the Rosati-fixed part of End⁰(J_Q̄) = K, which is all of K since K is totally real; hence ρ = 3.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.finrank_of_xs13_cubic` (other): Supporting algebra only: A generated cubic field is not End(J)⊗Q or an NS-rank computation. This is a supporting implication; the full target is recorded here.

**Tests.**

- `xs13_coeffField_inert_seventeen` (computation): The cubic t³+2t²−t−1 has no root modulo17 and hence is irreducible there. This supplies the residue-field inertness check once the actual coefficient field is identified.

**Acceptance.** ρ = 3 = r = g, so r < g + ρ − 1 = 5 and X_s(13)(Q_p)_2 is finite (NC.5, BDMTV Theorem 2.3); g + ρ − 1 − r = 2 independent nice classes are available.

**Direct prerequisites.** `ModularCurvesPartII:R14.5`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-plane-model`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — §6.1, pp.926–927. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/77. `bdmtv-2019` — §1.1, p.887. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/3 (Chen's decomposition, cited context only).

<a id="ED-6-xs13-analytic-rank-certificate"></a>

### Certified analytic rank one for the conjugates of f

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-analytic-rank-certificate` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xs13_analyticRank_eq_one` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, for each of the three real embeddings σ of K = Q(α), the L-function of f^σ satisfies L(f^σ, 1) = 0 and L'(f^σ, 1) > 0.6; hence ord_{s=1} L(f^σ, s) = 1 for every σ. The vanishing comes from the sign of the functional equation (f is w_169-invariant, so the root number of L(f^σ, s) is −1); the derivative bound is a supplied rational interval enclosure of L'(f^σ, 1) of width < 10^(−100) whose lower endpoint exceeds 0.6.

**Hypotheses.** The functional equation of L(f^σ, s) with conductor 169 and the Atkin–Lehner eigenvalue +1. For every stated conjugate of each newform, assume the displayed rational enclosures of L(f,1), L′(f,1), their error bounds, and the exact functional-equation signs. Any exact vanishing comes from the sign/theory, never from a box containing0; a derivative enclosure excluding0 proves nonvanishing. Proving a general L-value evaluator or generating the enclosure table is not a target.

**Proof route.**

- f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(169))^{w_169 = +1}; for weight two the root number is minus the Atkin–Lehner eigenvalue, so Λ(f^σ, 2 − s) = −Λ(f^σ, s) and L(f^σ, 1) = 0. (BDMTV compute instead the rational number c L(f, 1)/Ω exactly by Agashe–Stein; either route is exact.)
- Use the supplied enclosures of the actual three derivatives, each of width <10^(-100) with lower endpoint >0.6. Their correctness and identification with the L-functions are hypotheses; no series evaluator, coefficient table or derivative enclosure is constructed here.
- The positive lower endpoint proves derivative nonvanishing; combine exact central vanishing from the sign with analytic continuation to deduce a simple zero.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xs13_derivative_ne_zero` (other): For each actual conjugate L-function, a certified lower bound L′(f^σ,1)>0.6 implies L′(f^σ,1)≠0. Together with analytic continuation and exact central vanishing, deduce order exactly1; enclosure production is not asserted.

**Acceptance.** The three enclosures have lower endpoints > 0.6 (BDMTV p.927).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-endomorphism-algebra`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — proof of Proposition 6.2, p.927. Proposition6.2 uses derivative enclosures as arithmetic input; revision4 assumes those data explicitly and proves the analytic-rank implication.

<a id="ED-6-xs13-rank-three"></a>

### The Mordell–Weil rank of J_s(13) (BDMTV Proposition 6.2)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-rank-three` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xs13_rank_eq_three` · implementation unchecked.

Under the explicit modular-identification, analytic-derivative and rank-one supplier hypotheses below, rk J(Q) = 3 for J = Jac(X_s(13)); moreover Sha(J/Q) is finite, and for a prime p inert in K = Q(ζ_7)^+ (so that K_p = K ⊗ Q_p is a field) the p-adic logarithm J(Q) ⊗ Q_p → H⁰(X_{Q_p}, Ω¹)^* is an isomorphism as soon as log(AJ_b(P)) of one rational point P is nonzero; p = 17 is inert (17 ≡ 3 mod 7 and 3 has order 3 in (Z/7Z)^×/{±1}), and xs13-equivariant-height-matrices verifies the nonvanishing with P5. A second route, labelled conditional: three independent points (ED.3/reduction-rank-lower-bound) and a descent upper bound on the genus-three Jacobian (Bruin–Poonen–Stoll; no ED.3 node covers descent beyond genus two) whose class-group input for a degree-28 field of discriminant 2⁴²·13¹² is certified only under the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis (Bruin–Poonen–Stoll).

**Hypotheses.** J ∼ A_f (xs13-endomorphism-algebra); ord_{s=1} L(f^σ, s) = 1 for all σ (xs13-analytic-rank-certificate).

**Proof route.**

- Since J is isogenous to A_f, rk J(Q) = rk A_f(Q).
- Analytic rank one for every conjugate gives rk A_f(Q) = dim A_f = 3 and finiteness of Sha by Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin–Logachev for the modular quotient: the non-torsion trace point over an admissible imaginary quadratic field (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.8/totally-real-trace-point-nontorsion with F = Q, B = M_2(Q)), the Kolyvagin–Logachev descent HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.7/admissible-rm-kolyvagin-logachev (whose non-torsion hypothesis the GZ.8 trace point discharges), and the analytic-rank-one assembly and descent to Q requested from GZ.8 (PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/79, PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/97).
- K = End⁰(J) acts on J(Q) ⊗ Q, which is therefore a K-vector space of dimension 1, and log is K_p-linear onto the free rank-one K_p-module H⁰(Ω¹)^*; when K_p is a field a single point with nonzero logarithm generates, so log is an isomorphism (the hypothesis of BDMTV §1.4).
- Finiteness of Sha supplies the Selmer comparison needed in the corrected Lemma 3.7 (E8).

**API.**

- `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.finrank_restrictScalars_three` (other): Supporting algebra only: Restriction-of-scalars dimension does not establish Q-rank1 over the RM field. This is a supporting implication; the full target is recorded here.

**Acceptance.** The unconditional route uses only the analytic certificate and the GZ.8/HE.7 theorems; the descent route is recorded with the label conditional on GRH.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-analytic-rank-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-endomorphism-algebra`; `GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8`; `GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8/totally-real-trace-point-nontorsion`; `HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.7/admissible-rm-kolyvagin-logachev`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/reduction-rank-lower-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/certified-solution-set`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — Proposition 6.2 and its proof, p.927. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/82; PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/79, /94, /97 are GZ.8's and HE.7's. `bdmtv-2019` — Remark 6.3, p.927. The conditional descent route, kept with its label.

<a id="ED-6-xs13-tate-classes"></a>

### The Tate classes Z1, Z2 from the Hecke operators T_7 and T_11

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-tate-classes` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xs13_tateClasses_admissible` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, in the basis ω of xs13-first-chart-hodge-data, let A_q ∈ M_6(Q) be the matrix of the Hecke operator T_q on H¹_dR(X/Q) (q = 7, 11), obtained from the Eichler–Shimura relation ι(a_q) = Fr_q + q Fr_q^(−1) (50), and C the cup product matrix. Then Z_q := (6A_q − tr(A_q) I_6) C^(−1) are Z1 (q = 7) and Z2 (q = 11), the integer matrices with rows Z1: (0, −976, −1104, 10, −6, 18), (976, 0, −816, −3, 1, 3), (1104, 816, 0, −3, 3, −11), (−10, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0), (6, −1, −3, 0, 0, 0), (−18, −3, 11, 0, 0, 0); Z2: (0, 112, −656, −6, 6, 6), (−112, 0, −2576, 15, 9, 27), (656, 2576, 0, 3, 3, −3), (6, −15, −3, 0, 0, 0), (−6, −9, −3, 0, 0, 0), (−6, −27, 3, 0, 0, 0). They are linearly independent admissible Tate classes: (a) holds because they are cycle classes of the trace-zero correspondences 6T_q − tr(T_q) (NC.5), and (b)–(d) are the exact checks: antisymmetric, zero lower-right 3 × 3 block, and Z(0,3) + Z(1,4) + Z(2,5) = 0.

**Hypotheses.** The basis ω is symplectic with ω_0, ω_1, ω_2 holomorphic (xs13-first-chart-hodge-data). The matrices A_q are exact rational matrices (supplied geometric/Hecke data with exact identification hypotheses). Assume the exact T_7,T_11 matrices and their identification with Hecke correspondences on the actual cohomology, including adjointness and trace relations. Deduce the required Tate classes; do not target production of Hecke tables.

**Proof route.**

- Use the supplied exact rational Hecke matrices and their actual cohomological identifications. The imported special-fibre Eichler–Shimura theorem justifies the Frobenius relation; exact rational reconstruction, Frobenius computation and Hecke-table generation are not targets.
- 6T_q − tr(T_q) is a symmetric trace-zero correspondence (T_q is self-adjoint for the cup product and J is absolutely simple), hence nice (NC.5, BDMTV Lemma 2.4 and §1.5); its cycle class is (6A_q − tr(A_q)I)C^(−1) in tensor coordinates, so (a)–(d) hold.
- The checks (b)–(d) on the printed integer matrices are exact: antisymmetry entrywise, the lower-right block is zero, and 10 + 1 − 11 = 0, −6 + 9 − 3 = 0.
- Independence: the (0,1) and (0,2) entries (−976, −1104) and (112, −656) are not proportional.

**Acceptance.** Z1 and Z2 satisfy (b)–(d) exactly (admissibleTate_xs13_Z1). 6A_q − tr(A_q)I has trace zero.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/explicit-setup`; `AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.5`; `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7`; `ModularCurvesPartII:R14.6`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-endomorphism-algebra`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — §6.4, pp.930–931. Covers the Tate-class part of PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/86 (matrices checked on the rendered page 931); PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/83, /84 are R19.1's and NC.5's.

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-first-chart-frobenius` · construction · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xs13FrobeniusLift` · implementation unchecked.

- P2 = (0, 0): Φ(x)(P2) = 0 and Φ(y)(P2) is the root of Q(0, Y) = Y(Y³ − 10Y² + 24Y − 16) congruent to 0 modulo 17, which is 0 because ∂Q/∂Y(0, 0) = −16 is a unit; so Φ(P2) = P2.

### Equivariant heights and the matrices T_1, T_2 for X_s(13)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-equivariant-height-matrices` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xs13_det_T_eq_zero` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, let a_3 := a_3(f) = −α² − 2α, a generator of K, and ι(a_3) the matrix of T_3 on H¹_dR(X) (Eichler–Shimura); let s be a K-equivariant splitting of the Hodge filtration, so that the global height h is K-equivariant (NC.5, BDMTV Remark 3.9), and K_p := K ⊗ Q_17, E_K := H⁰(X_{Q_17}, Ω¹)^* ⊗_{K_p} H⁰(X_{Q_17}, Ω¹)^* (dimension 3 over Q_17). For z ∈ X(Q_17) and Z ∈ {Z1, Z2} put E_1(z) := AJ_b(z) and E_{2,Z}(z) := E_Z(AJ_b(z)) + c_Z (NC.5, BDMTV Lemma 3.7). Then: E_1(P5) ≠ 0, so it generates H⁰(Ω¹)^* over the field K_p (17 is inert in K) and log : J(Q) ⊗ Q_17 → H⁰(Ω¹)^* is an isomorphism; the vectors E_1(P_k) ⊗_{K_p} E_{2,Z1}(P_k), k = 1, 3, 5, form a Q_17-basis of E_K (certified by a nonzero determinant computed to precision); with ψ_1, ψ_2, ψ_3 the dual basis of ι(a_3)^i(E_1(P5) ⊗ E_{2,Z1}(P5)), i = 0, 1, 2, and Ψ_j(Z, z) := ψ_j(E_1(z) ⊗_{K_p} E_{2,Z}(z)), the 4 × 4 matrices T_i(x) with first row (θ_{Z_i}(x), Ψ_1(Z_i, x), Ψ_2(Z_i, x), Ψ_3(Z_i, x)) and rows (θ_{Z1}(P_k), Ψ_1(Z1, P_k), Ψ_2(Z1, P_k), Ψ_3(Z1, P_k)), k = 1, 3, 5, satisfy det T_i(x) = 0 for every x ∈ X(Q) (indeed on the set cut out by the pair (θ_{Z_i}, {0})). The relations E_1(P_k) ⊗ E_{2,Z1}(P_k) = ι(c_k)(E_1(P5) ⊗ E_1(P5)) with c_1 = 352 + 818α + 294α², c_3 = 162 + 406α + 150α², c_5 = −36 − 62α − 18α² are explicit supplied data whose identities and determinant nonvanishing are verified in the proof; their numerical production is outside this roadmap.

**Hypotheses.** X_s(13) has potentially good reduction everywhere, so the pairs (θ_Z, {0}) are quadratic Chabauty pairs (NC.5, BDMTV Corollary 3.8; R13.5). rk J(Q) = 3 (xs13-rank-three). Assume the exact correspondence/Hecke matrices and identifications with the actual geometric maps; Frobenius, Hodge and local-height data must satisfy the displayed matrix/precision identities. Computing their tables is not a target.

**Proof route.**

- E_1(P_k), E_{2,Z}(P_k) are the extension classes π_1, π_2 of A_Z(b, P_k), read off from the Hodge and Frobenius data at P_k (local-height-at-p data and (13)); they are computed to certified precision.
- A p-adic number known modulo 17^N with valuation < N is nonzero; this certifies E_1(P5) ≠ 0 and the nonvanishing of the 3 × 3 determinant of the three vectors in E_K.
- K-equivariance of h means h is determined by its values on E_K, a 3-dimensional space with basis ψ_j-dual; the global height pairing B = h is the same for Z1 and Z2, so every row (for any Z and any rational point) satisfies the same linear relation θ_Z(z) = Σ_j h_j Ψ_j(Z, z); hence det T_i vanishes at rational points (NC.5, BDMTV Lemma 1.5).
- The rows of T_2 use Z1 at P1, P3, P5 deliberately: the pairing is common to both classes (PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/88 note).

**Acceptance.** det T_1 vanishes at P1, P2, P3, P5 by construction (rows repeated or zero first row at the base point); the vanishing of det T_2 at P1, P3, P5 is a nontrivial consistency check (Remark 6.9). arXiv v1 used P4 in place of P5; the published version uses P5 (P4 is not in the first chart).

### Rational points of X_s(13) on the first chart ]U_1[

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-first-chart-points` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xs13_points_firstChart` · implementation unchecked.

Under the explicit finite-data hypotheses below, on each of the 17 residue discs of ]U_1[ ⊂ X(Q_17), all zeros of det T_1 and of det T_2 are simple, and the only common zeros are P1, P2, P3 and P5. Hence X_s(13)(Q) ∩ ]U_1[ = {P1, P2, P3, P5}.

**Hypotheses.** The matrices T_1, T_2 of xs13-equivariant-height-matrices with power-series entries certified on each disc. Supply the finite Taylor coefficient enclosures for each determinant on every stated disc, strict tail bounds, finite subdivisions, polynomial root/isolation witnesses, simple-root Hensel inequalities and nonvanishing witnesses for the second determinant on rejected balls. Supply exact memberships for the named rational points and the complete local cover. The raw checker verifies these finite assertions; neither the global point set nor completeness of common zeros is an input hypothesis. Mere O(17^5) coefficient notation without tail bounds is insufficient.

**Proof route.**

- For each disc, root-determination-precision applied to det T_1 (with the valuation bounds of height-series-valuation-bound) isolates its zeros in balls containing exactly one zero each, giving a qc-disc-certificate for the pair (det T_1, det T_2).
- Each ball containing one of P1, P2, P3, P5 is matched (det T_1 vanishes there by construction, det T_2 by the check of Remark 6.9).
- Every other ball is excluded: det T_2 is certified nonzero on it (its value or leading coefficient is a 17-adic number of valuation below the working precision), so it contains no common zero, hence no rational point.
- Apply qc-certificate-sound and padic-candidate-comparison on ]U_1[.

**Acceptance.** The zero tables of det T_1, det T_2 on ]U_1[ (authors' repository) are the certificate data; the run regenerates them with certified precision.

<a id="ED-6-xs13-rational-points"></a>

### The rational points of X_s(13) (BDMTV Theorem 1.1)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-rational-points` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xs13_rationalPoints` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic/certificate inputs below, x_s(13)(Q) consists of exactly seven points: in the model Q = 0 of xs13-plane-model they are P0 = (1 : 1 : 1), P1 = (1 : 1 : 2), P2 = (0 : 0 : 1), P3 = (−3 : 3 : 2), P4 = (1 : 1 : 0), P5 = (0 : 2 : 1), P6 = (−1 : 1 : 0), and completeness is deduced from the checked disc certificates. Under the moduli interpretation these are the rational cusp and six CM points, with CM by the imaginary quadratic orders of class number one in which 13 splits (discriminants −3, −4, −12, −16, −27, −43; j-invariants 0, 1728, 54000, 287496, −12288000, −884736000).

**Hypotheses.** rk J(Q) = 3 = g, ρ = 3 (xs13-rank-three, xs13-endomorphism-algebra). Good reduction away from 13 (xs13-plane-model (iii)) and potentially good reduction at 13 (R13.5), so all local heights away from 17 vanish (NC.5). Assume all concrete model/modular-identification, Hecke, analytic-continuation/sign/derivative, Frobenius, integral and local coefficient/error/tail inputs in xs13-plane-model through the three chart-certificate nodes. The finite F17 list and chart cover are supplied with exact correctness/completeness hypotheses. The raw finite disc trees are checked here, so completeness of X(Q) is a conclusion. CM j-values and their modular identifications are supplied separately.

**Proof route.**

- By xs13-plane-model (v), X(F_17) has 20 points: 17 discs in ]U_1[, the discs of (1:1:0) and (1:−1:0) in ]U_2[, and the disc of (1:1:1).
- xs13-first-chart-points, xs13-second-chart-points and xs13-p0-disc give X(Q) ∩ (each disc) ⊆ {P0, …, P6} with each P_i in its own disc; the P_i are rational (xs13-plane-model (iv)).
- padic-candidate-comparison (all balls matched or excluded) gives X(Q) = {P0, …, P6} conditional on the stated finite arithmetic inputs.
- Moduli identification: X_s(13) has a rational cusp (R13.4a); for each of the six discriminants D, a CM curve E/Q with End(E_Q̄) ≅ O_D has ρ_{E,13}(G_Q) in a split Cartan normaliser (CM.4/residual-cartan-normalizer, 13 split and prime to D), giving a rational point above j(O_D) (R13.4a criterion for j ≠ 0, 1728; the fibres above j = 0, 1728 are requested from R13.4a); these seven points have distinct j-values, so they are the seven points of X(Q).

**Acceptance.** #X_s(13)(Q) = 7. Galbraith and Baran found the seven points by a search up to a large height bound; the theorem proves there are no others.

<a id="ED-6-small-prime-split-cartan"></a>

### Existence of non-CM split-Cartan images for ℓ = 2, 3, 5, 7

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/small-prime-split-cartan` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.exists_nonCM_splitCartan_small` · implementation unchecked.

Under the stated geometric supplier hypotheses and the explicit arithmetic inputs of every prerequisite application, for ℓ ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7} there are infinitely many j ∈ Q such that an elliptic curve E/Q with j(E) = j has no CM and ρ_{E,ℓ}(G_Q) is contained in the normaliser C_s^+(ℓ) of a split Cartan subgroup of GL_2(F_ℓ).

**Hypotheses.** X_s(ℓ) ≅ X_0^+(ℓ²) over Q and the rational-point criterion for X_H with −I ∈ H (R13.4a).

**Proof route.**

- Genus zero: X_0(4), X_0(9), X_0(25) have genus 0, so their quotients X_0^+(ℓ²) do; X_0(49) has genus 1 (μ = 56, ν_2 = 0, ν_3 = 2, ν_∞ = 8, g = 1 + 56/12 − 2/3 − 4) and w_49 has h(−196) = 4 fixed points, so Riemann–Hurwitz 0 = 2(2g' − 2) + 4 gives g' = 0 (genus and fixed-point data from R13.4a).
- The cusps 0 and ∞ of X_0(ℓ²) are rational and swapped by w_{ℓ²}, so their common image is a rational point of X_s(ℓ); a genus-zero curve with a rational point is isomorphic to P¹_Q.
- The j-map X_s(ℓ) → X(1) is a nonconstant morphism over Q with a pole at that cusp; for a prime q, rational points t q-adically close to the cusp satisfy v_q(j(t)) < 0, and there are infinitely many such t with pairwise distinct j(t) (the fibres are finite).
- CM j-invariants are algebraic integers (CM.3/integrality), so a non-integral rational j is not CM and is ≠ 0, 1728; the rational-point criterion (R13.4a) gives E/Q with j(E) = j(t) and image in C_s^+(ℓ) (no twist is needed since −I ∈ C_s^+(ℓ)).

**Acceptance.** ℓ = 7 uses the genus-one curve X_0(49) and the four fixed points of w_49. The argument does not use the classification of class-number-one orders.

**Direct prerequisites.** `ModularCurvesPartII:R13.4a`; `ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.3/integrality`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — Theorem 1.2, p.888. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/96: the existence half, by the derived genus-zero argument (not written out in BDMTV). `bdmtv-2019` — §6, p.926. The identification used for the genus computation.

<a id="ED-6-split-cartan-classification"></a>

### The split Cartan case of Serre's uniformity question (BDMTV Theorem 1.2)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/split-cartan-classification` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.splitCartan_primes_eq` · implementation unchecked.

Under the stated geometric supplier hypotheses and the explicit arithmetic inputs of every prerequisite application, the set of primes ℓ for which there is an elliptic curve E/Q without CM with ρ_{E,ℓ}(G_Q) contained in the normaliser of a split Cartan subgroup of GL_2(F_ℓ) is {2, 3, 5, 7}. The case ℓ > 7, ℓ ≠ 13 is the theorem of Bilu–Parent–Rebolledo (X_s(ℓ)(Q) consists of cusps and CM points), an imported input with no owning roadmap (recorded gap); ℓ = 13 is xs13-rational-points; ℓ ≤ 7 is small-prime-split-cartan.

**Hypotheses.** Bilu–Parent–Rebolledo [BPR13] for ℓ > 7, ℓ ≠ 13 (gap).

**Proof route.**

- ℓ ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7}: small-prime-split-cartan.
- ℓ = 13: a non-CM E/Q with image in C_s^+(13) has j(E) ∉ {0, 1728} and gives a non-cuspidal point of X_s(13)(Q) with non-CM j (R13.4a criterion); by xs13-rational-points every point of X_s(13)(Q) is a cusp or a CM point, a contradiction.
- ℓ = 11 and ℓ ≥ 17: Bilu–Parent–Rebolledo, BPR13 (Mazur's method applies since J_0(ℓ) ≠ 0, with Runge's method); recorded as a gap.

**Acceptance.** The answer set {2, 3, 5, 7} is exact: existence below 11, nonexistence above 7.

<a id="ED-6-nonsplit-cartan-13"></a>

### The rational points of X_ns(13) (BDMTV Corollary 1.3)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/nonsplit-cartan-13` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xns13_rationalPoints_card` · implementation unchecked.

Under the stated geometric supplier hypotheses and the explicit arithmetic inputs of every prerequisite application, x_ns(13) ≅ X_s(13) over Q (Baran), so #X_ns(13)(Q) = 7, and all seven points are CM: they are the points above j(O_D) for the class-number-one discriminants D ∈ {−7, −8, −11, −19, −28, −67, −163}, exactly those in which 13 is inert. No modular interpretation of Baran's isomorphism is used.

**Hypotheses.** Baran's isomorphism, certified by explicit plane quartic models of both curves and a matrix M ∈ GL_3(Q) with Q_ns ∘ M = c · Q_s (gap: the X_ns(13) model and M are not in the sources read).

**Proof route.**

- Baran's isomorphism transports xs13-rational-points: #X_ns(13)(Q) = 7.
- For each of the seven discriminants, 13 is inert in O_D and prime to D, so a CM curve E/Q with End(E_Q̄) ≅ O_D has ρ_{E,13}(G_Q) in a non-split Cartan normaliser (CM.4/residual-cartan-normalizer); j(O_D) ∉ {0, 1728}, so the criterion (R13.4a) gives a rational point of X_ns(13) above j(O_D).
- The seven j-values are distinct, so these seven points are all of X_ns(13)(Q).

**Acceptance.** The discriminants with 13 split are −3, −4, −12, −16, −27, −43; with 13 inert −7, −8, −11, −19, −28, −67, −163; 6 + 7 = 13 class-number-one orders.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-rational-points`; `ModularCurvesPartII:R13.4a`; `ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.4/residual-cartan-normalizer`; `ModularCurvesPartII:R13.4b`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — Corollary 1.3, p.888. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/7. `bdmtv-2019` — §1.1, (1), p.888. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/4 (Baran's isomorphism, cited; data gap).
