<a id="ED-6-class-number-one"></a>

### Class number one from X_ns(13) (BDMTV Remark 1.4)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/class-number-one` · theorem · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.classNumberOne` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, the imaginary quadratic fields of class number one are Q(√−d) for d ∈ {1, 2, 3, 7, 11, 19, 43, 67, 163}; equivalently their discriminants are −3, −4, −7, −8, −11, −19, −43, −67, −163.

**Hypotheses.** nonsplit-cartan-13; class numbers of imaginary quadratic fields with |D| ≤ 52 are certified (explicit supplied class/unit/factorization data). The class-number values, complete imaginary-quadratic discriminant list and CM identification data used here are explicit hypotheses, with exact statements for each discriminant. No class-number table computation is a target.

**Proof route.**

- Let K have discriminant D with h(K) = 1 and |D| > 52. Every rational prime ℓ < |D|/4 is inert in K: a split or ramified ℓ would give a principal ideal of norm ℓ, generated by (a + b√D)/2 with (a² + |D|b²)/4 = ℓ, forcing b = 0 and then a² = 4ℓ, impossible. In particular 13 is inert.
- j(O_K) ∈ Q (class number one) and a CM curve E/Q with End(E_Q̄) ≅ O_K has image in a non-split Cartan normaliser at 13 (CM.4/residual-cartan-normalizer), with j ≠ 0, 1728; it gives a rational point of X_ns(13) (R13.4a), so by nonsplit-cartan-13, D ∈ {−7, −8, −11, −19, −28, −67, −163}; with |D| > 52 and D fundamental this leaves −67 and −163.
- For |D| ≤ 52 a finite certified class-number computation gives −3, −4, −7, −8, −11, −19, −43, and the same computation certifies h(−67) = h(−163) = 1 (explicit supplied class/unit/factorization data).

**Acceptance.** The argument recovers d = 67 and d = 163 from Corollary 1.3 and the small cases from a finite computation.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/nonsplit-cartan-13`; `ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.4/residual-cartan-normalizer`; `ModularCurvesPartII:R13.4a`.

**Sources.** `bdmtv-2019` — Remark 1.4, p.888. Covers PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/8; the inert-prime argument is the standard route (Serre).

<a id="ED-6-xs4-13-rational-points"></a>

### The rational points of the exceptional curve X_S4(13) (BDMTV 2021 Theorem 1.1)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs4-13-rational-points` · application · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.xS4_13_rationalPoints` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic/certificate inputs below, let X = X_S4(13), with canonical model 4x³y − 3x²y² + 3xy³ − x³z + 16x²yz − 11xy²z + 5y³z + 3x²z² + 9xyz² + y²z² + xz³ + 2yz³ = 0 (Banwait–Cremona). Then X(Q) = {(1 : 3 : −2), (0 : 0 : 1), (0 : 1 : 0), (1 : 0 : 0)}; the point (0 : 0 : 1) is CM with discriminant −3, and the other three are exceptional (non-CM curves with projective mod-13 image S_4, j-invariants 2⁴·5·13⁴·17³/3¹³, −2¹²·5³·11·13⁴/3¹³ and 2¹⁸·3³·13⁴·127³·139³·157³·283³·929/(5¹³·61¹³)). Certificate: J(X) is isogenous to J_s(13), hence absolutely simple of rank 3 with ρ = 3; X has potentially good reduction at 13, so the local heights away from p vanish; quadratic Chabauty at p = 11 on the two affine patches printed in BDMTV 2021 §5.1, with Z1, Z2 built from T_11 and T_11², the height pairing solved from the four known points with Z1; the common zeros of the two functions are exactly the four points.

**Hypotheses.** The isogeny J(X_S4(13)) ∼ J_s(13) and potential good reduction at 13 (gap: cited from Banwait–Cremona and an MCLF computation, not certified here). T_11 generates the Hecke algebra (checked on X_s(13)). Supply the exact modular-model identification, Hecke matrices and correspondence/cohomology identities, rank-overQ inputs, local-height-vanishing geometry, two affine charts with complete residue coverage, Frobenius/Hodge data and determinant coefficients, strict tails and finite root/Hensel/exclusion witnesses at11. Supply the j/CM dictionary for the displayed points. The checker proves the four-point completeness from these finite inputs; it never takes that completeness as a hypothesis.

**Proof route.**

- Rank and endomorphisms transfer along the isogeny from xs13-rank-three and xs13-endomorphism-algebra.
- Apply the raw QC checker on the two supplied patches at11, verify all local/root/tail witnesses, and deduce that its accepted points are exactly the four listed points. A target to generate the arithmetic tables is not introduced.
- Z2 is not used to solve for the height pairing, so the vanishing of its function at the four points is an independent check.
- padic-candidate-comparison converts the output into the certified solution set.

**Acceptance.** #X_S4(13)(Q) = 4, the four points satisfy the model equation exactly.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/qc-modular-algorithm`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/qc-certificate-sound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/padic-candidate-comparison`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/xs13-rank-three`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/certified-solution-set`; `ModularCurvesPartII:R13.4a`; `ModularCurvesPartII:R13.4b`.

<a id="ED-6-thue-example-tdw89"></a>

### Two quartic Thue equations solved by Tzanakis–de Weger

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/thue-example-tdw89` · application · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.tdw89_thue_solutions` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, (i) X⁴ − 4X³Y − 12X²Y² + 4Y⁴ = 1 has exactly the integer solutions ±(1, 0). (ii) X⁴ − 12X²Y² − 8XY³ + 4Y⁴ = 1 has exactly the integer solutions ±(1, 0), ±(1, −1), ±(1, 3), ±(3, −1). Both are certified solution sets conditional on the stated arithmetic-input hypotheses. Certificate data: K = Q(ϑ) with ϑ⁴ − 12ϑ² − 8ϑ + 4 = 0, which also contains φ = 2/ϑ with φ⁴ − 4φ³ − 12φ² + 4 = 0; the order R = Z + Zϑ + Z(ϑ²/2) + Z(ϑ³/2); fundamental units of R: ε_1 = 1 + ϑ, ε_2 = 3 + ϑ, ε_3 = ϑ²/2 (unimodularly equivalent to the system η_1, η_2, η_3 of TdW Appendix II); a solution gives a unit X − Yξ = ±ε_1^{a_1}ε_2^{a_2}ε_3^{a_3} (ξ = φ for (i), ξ = ϑ for (ii)), and for |Y| > 3 eight inhomogeneous linear forms Λ = δ + a_1μ_1 + a_2μ_2 + a_3μ_3 (TdW (2.5)–(2.6)) with C_5 = 1.211, C_6 = 6.38771·10⁴; an initial bound A := max|a_i| < 3.26·10⁴⁰; reduction with c_0 = 10¹⁴⁰ (lattices Γ_1, Γ_2 with |b_1| > 3.247·10⁴⁶ and 4.846·10⁴⁶, ‖s_3‖ > 0.029 in all eight cases) giving A ≤ 72, then c_0 = 10¹² (|b_1| > 1.293·10⁴ and 1.092·10⁴, ‖s_3‖ > 0.143) giving A ≤ 10; exhaustive enumeration of |a_i| ≤ 10 and of |Y| ≤ 3.

**Hypotheses.** The unit group certificate for R (supplied class/unit/factorization data with exact correctness hypotheses). The initial bound comes from an imported lower bound for linear forms in logarithms through ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant; TdW used Waldschmidt's 1980 theorem (their Appendix II). If the imported DT.3 bound is weaker than 3.26·10⁴⁰, the first reduction step is rerun with a larger c_0 until the ED.1 reduction hypothesis holds, and the later steps start from the bound it returns. The displayed fundamental units, divisor representatives and any integral basis are explicit inputs with proofs of full generation, norm/ideal identities and basis equality. The general ED.2 theorem, not the input, proves that the reported Thue list is exhaustive.

**Proof route.**

- (i) and (ii) are Norm_{K/Q}(X − Yφ) = 1 and Norm_{K/Q}(X − Yϑ) = 1, so X − Yξ ∈ R^× = ±⟨ε_1, ε_2, ε_3⟩ (explicit supplied class/unit/factorization data).
- Siegel's identity among three conjugates turns the unit equation into the linear forms (2.5)–(2.6); |Λ| ≤ C_6 exp(−(4/C_5)A) for |Y| > 3 (TdW Lemma II.2.1), and the imported lower bound gives A < 3.26·10⁴⁰ (ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant, ED.2/thue-certified-solution-set).
- ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction with the approximation lattice of ED.1/linear-form-lattice (C = c_0, W_1 = W_2 = 1), spanned by the columns of the matrix with rows (1,0,0), (0,1,0), ([c_0μ_1], [c_0μ_2], [c_0μ_3]) and the target (0, 0, −[c_0δ]): the certified lower bounds for |b_1| and ‖s_3‖ give A < (1/3.303) log(c_0 · 6.38771·10⁴ / (3 · K)) with K the previous bound, i.e. A ≤ 72 and then A ≤ 10.
- Enumerate all (a_1, a_2, a_3) with |a_i| ≤ 10 and test exactly whether the unit has the shape X − Yξ; check |Y| ≤ 3 directly; ED.2/thue-certified-solution-set packages completeness.

**Acceptance.** Exact evaluation: (1, 3) ↦ 1 − 108 − 216 + 324 = 1 and (3, −1) ↦ 81 − 108 + 24 + 4 = 1 for (ii). The TdW computation took about 35 seconds on an IBM 3083; the certified run checks the same lattices with exact integer LLL (GN.5 via ED.1).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-certified-solution-set`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/certified-solution-set`.

**Sources.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1989` — Theorem B, p.122. Statement read on the rendered page 122 (the text layer drops the equations); part (i) has only ±(1, 0). `tzanakis-de-weger-1989` — proof of Theorem B, p.126. The reduction data c_0 = 10¹⁴⁰, 10¹², bounds 72 and 10 read on the rendered pages 124–126.

<a id="ED-6-elliptic-integral-points-tdw89"></a>

### Integral points on y² = x³ − 4x + 1 (Tzanakis–de Weger Theorem A)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/elliptic-integral-points-tdw89` · application · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.tdw89_integralPoints` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic-input hypotheses listed below, the integral points of the elliptic curve E : y² = x³ − 4x + 1 are exactly the 22 points (x, ±y) with (x, y) ∈ {(−2, 1), (−1, 2), (0, 1), (2, 1), (3, 4), (4, 7), (10, 31), (12, 41), (20, 89), (114, 1217), (1274, 45473)}; an certified solution set conditional on the stated arithmetic-input hypotheses. Consequently the triangular numbers n(n + 1)/2 (n ≥ 1) that are products of three consecutive integers are exactly T_3, T_15, T_20, T_44, T_608, T_22736 (Mohanty's problem). Certificate data: the cubic field L = Q(ψ), ψ³ − 4ψ + 1 = 0, with ring of integers Z[ψ], discriminant 229, class number 1 and fundamental units ψ, 2 − ψ; the factorisation y² = (x − ψ)(x² + xψ + ψ² − 4) into coprime factors, so x − ψ = ±ψ^i(2 − ψ)^j α² with i, j ∈ {0, 1}; for x ≥ 1 the sign + is forced by the real embedding ψ^(1) = 0.254… and i = 0 by ψ^(2) = −2.114…; the cases j = 0 and j = 1 lead to two reducible quartic Thue equations (solved by factoring) and to the irreducible equations m⁴ − 4m³n − 12m²n² + 4n⁴ = 1 and n⁴ − 12n²m² − 8nm³ + 4m⁴ = 1 of thue-example-tdw89.

**Hypotheses.** The class group and unit certificates for L (explicit supplied class/unit/factorization data). x < 0 is a finite check (only x = −2, −1 occur). The displayed integral basis, class/unit presentation and joint index data are explicit hypotheses with exact basis, generation and strict-index statements. These do not assume integral-point completeness; that follows from the reduction/search certificate.

**Proof route.**

- The two factors of x³ − 4x + 1 = (x − ψ)(x² + xψ + ψ² − 4) are coprime in Z[ψ]: a common prime divides 3ψ² − 4, of norm −229, and would force y² = ±229·□ after taking norms, impossible.
- Class number one and the unit group give x − ψ = ±ψ^i(2 − ψ)^j α² (explicit supplied class/unit/factorization data/joint-class-unit-index-certificate, explicit supplied class/unit/factorization data/integral-basis-certificate).
- Comparing coefficients in the basis 1, ψ, ψ² gives the equations (1.4)–(1.7) of TdW; parametrising the resulting conics leads to the Thue equations (1.8), (1.9) and two reducible ones.
- thue-example-tdw89 solves (1.8), (1.9); back-substitution gives the listed points; exact evaluation verifies them on E (WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Equation).

**Acceptance.** (1274, 45473): 1274³ − 4·1274 + 1 = 2067793729 = 45473². Mohanty: m(m + 1)(m + 2) = T_n with x = 2m + 2, y = 2n + 1 transforms to E.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/thue-example-tdw89`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Equation`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/certified-solution-set`.

<a id="ED-6-s-unit-example-deweger"></a>

### The S-unit equation x + y = z for S = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13} (de Weger Theorem 6.3)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/s-unit-example-deweger` · application · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.deWeger_sUnit_solutions` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic/certificate inputs below, let S be the set of positive integers whose prime factors lie in {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13}. The equation x + y = z with x, y, z ∈ S, gcd(x, y) = 1 and x ≤ y has exactly 545 solutions; 514 of them satisfy ord_2(xyz) ≤ 12, ord_3(xyz) ≤ 7, ord_5(xyz) ≤ 5, ord_7(xyz) ≤ 4, ord_11(xyz) ≤ 3, ord_13(xyz) ≤ 3, and the other 31 are listed in de Weger's Table II, the largest being 91 + 1771470 = 1771561 (7·13 + 2·3¹¹·5 = 11⁶). Certificate data: the initial bound m(xyz) := max_p ord_p(xyz) < 5.60·10²⁷ (de Weger §6.2, from Yu's p-adic and Waldschmidt's archimedean bounds); p-adic reduction with the parameters (μ_0, μ) = (2, 605), (1, 385), (1, 275), (1, 220), (1, 165), (1, 165) for p = 2, …, 13 and lattice lower bounds ℓ(Γ*_μ) > √5 · 5.60·10²⁷, giving ord_p(xyz) ≤ 606, 385, 275, 220, 165, 165, so m ≤ 606; a second round (μ = 66, 42, 30, 24, 18, 18) giving m ≤ 67; a third round (μ = 55, 35, 25, 20, 15, 15) giving m ≤ 56; then Fincke–Pohst enumeration of the short vectors of the same lattices down to f(2) = 4, f(p) = 1 for p ≥ 3, and a final exhaustive search.

**Hypotheses.** The initial bound is supplied through ED.2/s-unit-certified-solution-set from the imported p-adic and archimedean lower bounds (DT.3, Yu and Matveev); a weaker imported bound only enlarges the first μ. Supply the exact rational/integer lattice bases, unimodular transforms, rational squared-distance witnesses and reduction parameters for every stated round, and the finite final exponent/candidate tables. Check their identities, thresholds, full branch/row coverage and exact S-unit membership by ED.1/ED.2; do not assume that the finite list is complete or has545 solutions. The own logarithm error formulas justify the residues used by the reduction, so the enumeration theorem stays proved.

**Proof route.**

- Reduce to the coprime S-unit equation and to linear forms in p-adic logarithms (ED.2/s-unit-certified-solution-set, ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice).
- Each p-adic reduction step: if ℓ(Γ*_μ) > √5 · X_1 then ord_p(z) ≤ μ + μ_0 − 1 for solutions with m(xyz) ≤ X_1 (de Weger Lemma 3.14, ED.1/padic-reduction); symmetry in x, y, z bounds ord_p(xyz).
- Below the reduced bounds, ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete (Fincke–Pohst) lists all lattice points of the relevant norm; the corresponding exponent vectors are tested exactly.
- Exact verification of the 545 solutions; completeness from the bounds and the enumeration.

**Acceptance.** 91 + 1771470 = 1771561 = 11⁶. A brute-force search over z ≤ 3·10⁶ finds exactly 545 solutions with largest z = 1771561 (a consistency check of the list, not a completeness proof).

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/s-unit-certified-solution-set`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-reduction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/valuation-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/certified-solution-set`.

**Sources.** `de-weger-1989` — Theorem 6.3, p.123. Statement and parameters read on the rendered pages 123–124 (scanned thesis, OCR checked). `de-weger-1989` — proof of Theorem 6.3, p.124. First reduction step; the second and third give 67 and 56. `de-weger-1989` — Theorem 6.3, p.123, and Table II, p.130. Table II (rendered page 130) lists the 31 large solutions, the last row being 91 + 1771470 = 1771561.

<a id="ED-6-thue-mahler-example-tdw92"></a>

### The Thue–Mahler equation x³ − 23x²y + 5xy² + 24y³ = ±2^a3^b5^c7^d (Tzanakis–de Weger 1992)

**Target.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/thue-mahler-example-tdw92` · application · `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED6.tdw92_thueMahler_solutions` · implementation unchecked.

Conditional on the explicit arithmetic/certificate inputs below, the equation x³ − 23x²y + 5xy² + 24y³ = ±2^{z_1}3^{z_2}5^{z_3}7^{z_4} with x, y ∈ Z, gcd(x, y) = 1 and z_i ≥ 0 has exactly 72 solutions up to the sign ±(x, y), listed in TdW 1992 §18 with x ≥ 0; the largest is (48632, −3729), with value 2¹⁸·5¹³. Certificate data: the cubic field K = Q(ξ) with F(ξ, 1) = 0, which is not Galois; the corrected1993 route starts with c7=1.08672·10⁴⁶ and B<1.511·10⁵⁰; the same first lattices give N1=1153 and H≤4919, placing the search below the old9.844·10⁴⁹ bound so the original subsequent reduction reaches113 and86 (Fincke–Pohst). Alternatively the1993 Baker–Wüstholz route gives the original initial9.844·10⁴⁹ bound directly, followed by a sieve over the remaining exponent tuples (82 tuples, of which 79 give solutions with 10 counted twice, plus 3 exceptional solutions outside the reduced bounds). In a certified run the final test of each tuple is exact integer evaluation, not 15-digit floating point.

**Hypotheses.** The initial bound must be obtained from corrected certified DT.3/DT.4 inputs through ED.2. The original1992 BGMMS constant is insufficient: use the1993 published corrigendum (E29), or another independently certified bound with a validated reduction transcript. Supply an irreducible cubic presentation, full fundamental-unit system with rank/completeness, class/ideal representatives and prime factorization tables with exact correctness/completeness identities. Supply raw integer/rational reduction and residual-row transcripts. ED.0/ED.2 prove the required logarithm/residue errors; the raw checker deduces all bounds, coverage and the count72 rather than assuming that count or the final solution set.

**Proof route.**

- Reduce to the equations N_{K/Q}(x − yθ) = ±2^{z_1}⋯7^{z_4} and to S-unit equations in K (DT.4/thue-mahler-effective-finiteness vian ED.2).
- Apply the1993 corrigendum to the initial archimedean bound: multiply the old c7 by7^15, use B<1.511·10^50, and verify the stated same-lattice first reductions N1=1153,H≤4919. Only then invoke the original later reduction transcript. The alternative Baker–Wüstholz constants restore9.844·10^49; these are two distinct justified routes. Neither has been numerically replayed here.
- Real and p-adic reduction steps (ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction, ED.1/padic-reduction) lower the bound to 113, Fincke–Pohst enumeration (ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete) to 86.
- The sieve over the remaining tuples (TdW §18) leaves 82 tuples; exact evaluation of F at the corresponding (x, y) rejects 3 and confirms 79, among which 10 solutions are counted twice (Cases III and V with n_3 = 1), leaving 69 solutions within the reduced bounds.
- Together with the 3 exceptional solutions found during the reduction this gives 72 solutions; ED.2/thue-mahler-certified-solution-set packages completeness.

**Acceptance.** F(48632, −3729) = 320000000000000 = 2¹⁸·5¹³. F(0, −1) = −24 = −2³·3, the solution with x = 0.

**Direct prerequisites.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-mahler-certified-solution-set`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-reduction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6/certified-solution-set`.

**Sources.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §1Ex, p.225. Read on the rendered page 225 (the text layer drops the equation); the table on pp.278–279 has 72 rows with x ≥ 0. `tzanakis-de-weger-1992` — §18Ex, p.277. The solution table, pp.278–279. `tzanakis-de-weger-1993-correction` — Compositio89(1993),pp241–242. Corrected archimedean constant/initial bound and the same-lattice first reductions; alternatively sharper Baker–Wüstholz input restores the old initial bound.

Let 𝒜 be the Néron model of A over O_K (an abelian scheme when A has good reduction), F̂ its formal group, the completion of 𝒜 along the zero section, a g-dimensional commutative formal Lie group over O_K once formal parameters s = (s₁, …, s_g) are chosen, and A¹(K) := ker(𝒜(O_K) → 𝒜(k)) = F̂(m_K). Let log_F̂ ∈ (K[[s]])^g be the formal logarithm, the unique homomorphism of formal groups F̂ → Ĝ_a^g over K whose linear term is the identity; its coordinates are the formal primitives of a basis of invariant differentials and converge on m_K^g. Put N := #𝒜(k) = [A(K) : A¹(K)] and log_A(x) := N⁻¹ log_F̂(s(N x)), identifying K^g with Lie(A) by ds at 0. The integration pairing is ⟨x, ω⟩ := ω(log_A x) ∈ K for x ∈ A(K), ω ∈ Ω_A. Properties: (a) log_A is a homomorphism, independent of the choices of formal parameters and of N among multiples of the exponent of 𝒜(k); (b) ker log_A = A(K)_tors, which is finite; (c) log_A is continuous, its differential at 0 is the identity, and for n > e/(p − 1) it maps the subgroup F̂(m_K^n) isomorphically onto the lattice (m_K^n)^g; (d) for a homomorphism φ : A → B of abelian varieties over K, log_B ∘ φ = dφ ∘ log_A, i.e. ⟨φ(x), ω⟩ = ⟨x, φ*ω⟩; for a finite extension K'/K, log_{A_{K'}} restricts to log_A on A(K); (e) the pairing A(K) × Ω_A → K is ℤ-bilinear and K-linear in ω, its kernel in Ω_A, {ω : ⟨x, ω⟩ = 0 ∀x}, is 0 and its kernel in A(K) is A(K)_tors; for each ω, x ↦ ⟨x, ω⟩ is the unique locally analytic homomorphism A(K) → K whose differential at 0 is ω. The compatible logarithms over finite K'/K first define log_A on A(ℚ̄_p). Over ℂ_p use the analytic logarithm of the ℂ_p-Lie group, extending this map continuously; the union over finite extensions alone does not define it on all A(ℂ_p) (KRZB Definition 3.8 and Proposition 3.16). Hypotheses: K finite over ℚ_p; A an abelian variety over K. Good reduction is not assumed; when A has good reduction 𝒜 is the abelian scheme extending A and 𝒜(k) is the group of points of its special fibre. Normalisation: Lie(A) = T₀A and the pairing is evaluation of an invariant differential on a tangent vector; no sign or scaling is inserted. **Required signature.** Let C be a genus-two curve over ℚ with a Weierstrass model over ℤ_p, p odd, ι: C → J from a rational degree-one class, Jⁿ(ℚ_p) the pⁿℤ_p-points of the formal group (n ≥ 1) and log: J¹(ℚ_p) → (pℤ_p)² the formal logarithm. (a) For Γ = J(ℚ) and K_n = Γ ∩ Jⁿ(ℚ_p), K_n is the kernel of K₁ → (pℤ_p/pⁿℤ_p)² ≅ (ℤ/p^{n−1})², P ↦ log P mod pⁿ; so Γ/K_n is finite and computable from K₁ and logarithms to precision pⁿ. (b) (Lemma 6.2) If P₀ ∈ C(ℚ_p), Q ∈ Jⁿ(ℚ_p) and (η₁ : η₂ : η₃ : η₄) are coordinates of the image of P₀ + Q ∈ Pic¹ on the dual Kummer surface, normalised to minimal valuation zero, then v_p(η₁η₃ − η₂²) ≥ n and v_p(η₄) ≥ 2n. The necessary dual-Kummer congruences supply a superset only; actual membership in the curve embedded in Pic¹ must be checked separately. ### Light definitions in the companion

These supporting definitions have existing carriers and actual bodies. Their complete API and at least three discriminating tests are recorded here even where they are narrower notation than a heavy target. These are contracts; only the examples actually in the Lean file were elaborated.

#### `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.realIntervalContains`

For l,u∈Q and x∈R, (l:R)≤x≤(u:R); an invalid reversed interval has no members.

**API.** Membership iff the two weak inequalities. Singleton membership iff x is the rational endpoint. Endpoint enlargement preserves membership.

**Tests.**

- [0,1] contains0 and1.
- [1,0] contains no real value.
- [1,1] contains1 and excludes2.

#### `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.complexBoxContains`

For four rational endpoints and z∈C, realIntervalContains lr ur z.re and realIntervalContains li ui z.im.

**API.** Membership iff coordinate memberships. Projection to either coordinate interval. Enlarging both coordinate intervals preserves membership.

**Tests.**

- [0,0]×[1,1] contains i.
- [0,0]×[1,1] excludes -i.
- [0,0]×[0,0] contains0 and excludes1.

#### `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.padicBallContains`

For prime p, c∈Q,N∈Z,x∈Qp, ||x−c||≤p^(−N). It is absolute precision, with the existing norm.

**API.** Membership iff the norm inequality. Increasing precision gives a subset ball. Changing the centre by an error≤p^(−N) leaves the ball unchanged.

**Tests.**

- At p=3, B(0,2) contains9.
- At p=3, B(0,2) excludes3.
- At p=3, B(0,0) contains1 and B(0,-1) contains1/3.

#### `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.realLogPartialSum`

The rational finite sum L_N(x) in ED.2/logarithm-enclosure; the definition is total, while logarithm-error statements require x>0.

**API.** N=0 gives0. x=1 gives0 at every N. For x>0 the explicit E_N error bound holds.

**Tests.**

- L_1(2)=2/3.
- L_N(1)=0.
- L_1(1/2)=-2/3; omitting the sign fails.

#### `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.arctanPartialSum`

The rational finite sum A_N(t) in ED.2/logarithm-enclosure; the error theorem assumes |t|≤1.

**API.** N=0 gives0. Oddness in t. Error≤|t|^(2N+1)/(2N+1) on the closed unit interval.

**Tests.**

- A_1(1)=1 and A_1(-1)=-1.
- A_N(0)=0.
- A_2(1)=2/3; an unsigned geometric sum gives4/3 and fails.

#### `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.padicLogPartialSum`

In the existing Qp carrier, Σ(k<N)(−1)^k(z−1)^(k+1)/(k+1). Finite-extension/branch certificates remain full README targets.

**API.** N=0 gives0. z=1 gives0. The deep-unit tail bound holds for the imported series logarithm.

**Tests.**

- At p=3,z=4,N=4 the sum is−51/4.
- At every prime and N,z=1 gives0.
- At p=2,z=5,N=2 the sum is−4, so a missing alternating sign is rejected.

#### `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED2.supportedOn`

Every prime divisor of n∈N belongs to the finite set S. Positivity is imposed by the triple definition, not by this predicate.

**API.** Prime-divisor membership is necessary. n=1 is supported on every S. Enlarging S preserves the predicate.

**Tests.**

- 12 is supported on{2,3}.
- 5 is not supported on{2,3}.
- 1 is supported on∅, while0 is not supported on any finite S (there are primes outside S).

#### `TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED2.coprimeSUnitTriple`

For x=(a,b,c)∈N³: a>0,b>0,a≤b,a+b=c,gcd(a,b)=1, and each coordinate is supported on S.

**API.** Projection to the equation and coprimality. All three coordinates are positive. Enlarging S preserves membership.

**Tests.**

- (1,2,3) is accepted for{2,3}.
- (2,2,4) is rejected despite the equation/support.
- (1,4,5) is rejected for{2,3};(0,1,1) is rejected for lack of positivity.

### Specialized theorem boundaries

**`TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED3.canonicalHeight_mem_doubling_interval`.** Supporting interval propagation over actual pinned points; the full explicit Cremona/Silverman comparison and enclosures are README targets.

**`TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED2.sUnit_finite_search`.** Final finite-box implication only. The full enumeration pipeline proves the required bound using DT.4, ED.1 and the own ED.2 logarithm errors, not an input equality asserting the answer.

## Supplier requests

These32 mathematical interfaces remain requested from their named owners. Arithmetic tables and concrete evaluations have no requested producer; the exact supplied-data hypotheses at consumers replace that former ownership.

### Request 1: `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.1`

For the Jacobian J of a smooth proper geometrically connected curve C over ℚ with C(ℚ) ≠ ∅ (J(ℚ) = Pic⁰ points as in JacobianChallenge Layer D): (a) J(ℚ) is a finitely generated abelian group; (b) for a prime q at which C has a smooth proper model, a reduction homomorphism J(ℚ) → J̃(𝔽_q) compatible with reduction of points and divisors, injective on torsion of order prime to q and on all torsion when q ≥ 3; (c) for an abelian variety A of dimension g over ℚ_p, A(ℚ_p) has an open subgroup of finite index isomorphic to ℤ_p^g, so #A(ℚ_p)/2A(ℚ_p) = |2|_p^{-g}·#A(ℚ_p)[2].

**Needed by.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/finite-index-subgroup-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/genus-two-descent-rank-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/reduction-rank-lower-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/saturation-certificate`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/torsion-by-reduction`.

### Request 2: `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.1`

For E : y² = x(x² + cx + d) over ℚ with the 2-isogeny φ : E → E′ (E′ : y² = x(x² − 2cx + c² − 4d)) and its dual φ′: the Kummer map E(ℚ)/φ′(E′(ℚ)) → H¹(ℚ, E′[φ′]) ≅ ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} is (x, y) ↦ x (and (0,0) ↦ d); the φ′-Selmer group is the set of d₁ for which v² = d₁u⁴ + cu² + d/d₁ is everywhere locally soluble; and its quotient by the image of E(ℚ) is Ш(E′/ℚ)[φ′] (as defined in EllipticCurves Layer 7).

**Needed by.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/lind-reichardt-torsor`.

### Request 9: `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`

For a smooth projective geometrically integral curve X of genus g over a field k with a rational point O and its Jacobian J (JacobianChallenge layers D–F): (i) the pullback ι_O* : H⁰(J, Ω¹) → H⁰(X, Ω¹) along P ↦ [P − O] is an isomorphism and does not depend on O; (ii) Riemann–Roch consequences: a nonzero regular differential has a divisor of degree 2g − 2, so Σ_{x ∈ X(k)} ord_x ω ≤ 2g − 2; and every degree-zero class D satisfies D + g·O ∼ E with E effective of degree g.

**Needed by.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/abelian-integral`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/coleman-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/good-reduction-chabauty-datum`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/kernel-of-reduction-evaluation`.

### Request 10: `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3`

For a smooth projective curve 𝒳 over a discrete valuation ring R (in particular ℤ_p) with geometrically connected fibres: specialisation of effective divisors from the generic to the special fibre preserves degree and linear equivalence, and h⁰ of line bundles is upper semicontinuous; Hensel lifting of smooth points of the special fibre to R-points. **Needed by.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/bad-reduction-bound`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/good-reduction-chabauty-datum`; `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/kernel-of-reduction-evaluation`.

## Explicit remaining gaps

These27 gaps are preserved as implementation/interface/data boundaries. The primary-source access obstacle is resolved for the nine cited nodes; it does not implement the weighted height signature or any raw checker. Concrete data obligations now mean supplying the stated theorem inputs, never introducing table-generation targets.

### Gap 1: Rank of E11 = X₁(11)

E11 : y² + y = x³ − x² has no rational 2-torsion; rank 0 needs a full 2-descent over the cubic field of x³ − 4x² + 16 (class group and units) or a 5-isogeny descent. No source read here prints that computation (Poonen cites Cremona's tables).

**Needed by.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/rank-zero-curves`.

### Gap 2: Genus-two rank-zero curves (models of X₁(13), X₁(16), X₁(18))

The ArithmeticDynamics request lists y² = x⁶ + 2x⁵ + x⁴ + 2x³ + 6x² + 4x + 1, y² = x⁶ + 2x⁵ + 5x⁴ + 10x³ + 10x² + 4x + 1 and v² = u(u² + 1)(1 + 2u − u²) with their rational points. Poonen 1995 states these are modular curves whose points were computed earlier; no source read here gives the descent and torsion certificates, so J(ℚ) finite and the point lists are not certified.

**Needed by.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/rank-zero-curves`.

### Gap 3: Corrected 2-descent for the Jacobian of C₁(3₂)

The local computation at 743 in Poonen 1995 Proposition 1 uses the non-point (2, √33); the erratum says the 2-adic information completes the descent but does not print it. The local images at 2 and 743 for (x − T) on J(ℚ_2), J(ℚ_743) and the resulting H′ must be supplied with their exact compatibility/completeness hypotheses and checked at the consuming descent theorem.

**Needed by.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/poonen-genus-two-mordell-weil`.

### Gap 4: Explicit points on Fermigier's homogeneous spaces

Cremona reports rational points on 7 + 6 homogeneous spaces giving n₁ = 256, n₁′ = 128 but does not print them; the certified lower bound rank ≥ 13 needs them.

**Needed by.** `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/fermigier-rank-thirteen`.

### Gap 5: Certified finite presentations of Jacobians over finite fields and of sieve quotients

Finite local groups, exact presentations, generator/image tables, full residue-point lists and Smith-form quotient data are explicit theorem inputs with completeness and geometric compatibility hypotheses. ED.5 proves sieve transport, finite checking and global soundness from those hypotheses. No Mumford/Cantor, discrete-log, point-count or table-production target is requested; an application cannot run until its stated inputs are supplied.

## Ownership and restructuring proposals

### 1. rescope: EffectiveDiophantineMethods, ArithmeticDynamics, MordellLawrenceVenkatesh

Strassmann's theorem (a nonzero restricted power series over a complete nonarchimedean field has at most N zeros in the closed unit disc, N its last dominant index) is planned twice: ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/strassmann-theorem (over ℚ_p) and MordellLawrenceVenkatesh:LV.3/strassmann (over finite extensions of ℚ_p, importing DY.6). ED.4 needs it for the exceptional residue discs of Chabauty–Coleman. ED.4 cannot import DY.6: ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3 consumes ED.4 (the Chabauty certificates for C₀(5), C₁(3₂) and X₀^dyn(6)) and DY.6 depends on DY.3, so a DY.6 → ED.4 edge closes the stage cycle ED.4 → DY.3 → DY.6 → ED.4. The verifier of RT-AUDIT-09/7 asked for a single owner, ED.4 or a general owner of p-adic power series.

**Proposal.** Make EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/strassmann-bound (stated for any complete nonarchimedean field, built on Tau Ceti's TauCeti.PowerSeries.exists_max_eq_gaussNorm_of_isRestricted) the single owner. ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6/strassmann-theorem becomes a citation of it (add the stage edge EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4 → ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6, an ownership proposal pending reconciliation of the combined stage projection), and MordellLawrenceVenkatesh:LV.3/strassmann imports it directly (edge EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4 → MordellLawrenceVenkatesh:LV.3).

**Coordination.** Before applying stage edges reconcile the reviewed combined stage cycle ED.4 → ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3 → DY.6 → MordellLawrenceVenkatesh:LV.3 → MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.0 → MP.6 → QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.1 → QM.5 → DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0 → ColemanIntegration:L0 → ED.4. ColemanIntegration proposes moving its unnecessary Dirichlet L0 prerequisite to L3; LV/DY must cite the single ED.4 Strassmann owner. These files are outside this revision. Packet-node acyclicity does not certify the stage projection.

### Resolution of the nine primary-locator findings

- [EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration](#ED-1-short-vector-enumeration): `fincke-pohst-1985`, §2 pp.464–466, (2.6)–(2.8), discussion after(2.12). Positive diagonal square completion gives the recursive closed integer intervals. Boundary equality is retained. Original homogeneous ± pairing and zero stop are distinguished from the stated rational affine-centre extension, whose proof is by the same square completion.
- [EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete](#ED-1-short-vector-enumeration-complete): `fincke-pohst-1985`, Algorithm(2.8), p.465; discussion after(2.12), p.466. Every vector satisfying the weak bound survives all remaining-radius inequalities, and conversely. Retain zero when the target set requires it, and both signs in the homogeneous full vector set. The affine extension must not copy the homogeneous sign shortcut.
- [EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain](#ED-2-exponent-reduction-chain): `fincke-pohst-1985`, §2 pp.464–466, (2.6)–(2.8). The final bounded lattice search is exhaustive by the verified enumeration theorem; intermediate strict distance thresholds are not weakened to equality. This primary paper supplies enumeration, not the entire logarithmic reduction chain.
- [EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/logarithm-enclosure](#ED-2-logarithm-enclosure): `matveev-linear-forms-2000`, §2 (2.1),(2.4), p.1219. A_j≥max(D h_abs(alpha_j),|log alpha_j|,0.16), with nonzero chosen logarithms. ED.2 encloses the actual selected branch. Matveev is motivation for the needed input, not a source of a numerical log evaluator; the finite-series error proof is supplied here.
- [EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant](#ED-2-certified-linear-form-constant): `matveev-linear-forms-2000`, Corollary2.3, bound/constant(2.6) and admissibility(2.4), p.1219. C1=min{κ^(-1)(en/2)^κ 30^(n+3)n^(7/2),2^(6n+20)}. The packet rational majorant dominates the chosen first term for κ=1,2, hence dominates C1. Degree and absolute-height factors and the 1+log D factor are retained.
- [EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/certified-linear-form-lower-bound](#ED-2-certified-linear-form-lower-bound): `matveev-linear-forms-2000`, Corollary2.3, (2.4), and replacement (2.6), p.1219. The nonzero linear form is in chosen nonzero logarithms. B is weighted by A_j/A_n and can be replaced by B*=max|b_j| as stated in(2.6). Nonzero and branch hypotheses cannot be dropped; the rational constant only majorizes the source constant.
- [EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.2/thue-initial-bound](#ED-2-thue-initial-bound): `matveev-linear-forms-2000`, §2 Corollary2.3, (2.1),(2.4),(2.6), p.1219. Apply the homogeneous lower bound only after removing zero logarithms and establishing the nonzero form; the stated degree/height majorants and finite covering inputs are separate ED.2 hypotheses. Matveev does not itself provide Thue units or a covering.
- [EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/explicit-height-difference-bound](#ED-3-explicit-height-difference-bound): `silverman-1990`, Theorem1.1/Remark1.2 p.725; §3 pp.729–730; proof §6 p.738. μS=h_abs(Δ)/12+h∞(j)/12+h∞(b2/12)/2+log(2*)/2, h∞=Σ_arch n_v logmax(1,|.|_v)/d. Bound −h_abs(j)/24−μS−0.973 ≤ hat_h_abs−h_abs(x)/2 ≤ μS+1.07. Pinned number-field relative heights must both be divided by d; Cremona rational constants use the separate halving conversion already retained.
- [EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3/canonical-height-enclosure](#ED-3-canonical-height-enclosure): `silverman-1990`, abstract p.723; §7 pp.739–740; Theorem1.1 p.725. The height comparison is used with exact doubling and rational log intervals; divide by4^n in the pinned half-height convention. Absolute/relative normalization is kept separate. The explicit width claim requires uniformly bounded input log width, not arbitrary widening intervals.

### EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E1 — misprint

**Source.** `bruin-stoll-2010`, Published §3.3, p.279, PrepareLift: the definition of Λ, with φᵢ as defined in §3.2, p.277.

**Observed claim.** Λ = {Lⱼ₋₁ ∩ ker(φᵢ) : i ∈ I′}

**Correction.** At target D=NₖΓ use Lⱼ₋₁∩φᵢ⁻¹(φᵢ(D)); with the source’s surjective maps this is Lⱼ₋₁∩φᵢ⁻¹(NₖGᵢ). Equivalently, first replace Gᵢ by Gᵢ/NₖGᵢ and φᵢ by its composite into that quotient, then take its kernel. The required invariant is D≤Lⱼ≤Lⱼ₋₁.

**Reason and scope.** Let Γ=ℤ, G=ℤ/4, φ reduction, Nₖ₋₁=1, qₖ=2 and Nₖ=2. The selected exponent test holds. The displayed original kernel produces L₁=4ℤ, which fails to contain D=2ℤ. The final assignment Lₜ=2ℤ then makes an ascending step, so the quotient Lₜ₋₁/Lₜ in Lift is not defined. The quotient-target kernel is 2ℤ and preserves the invariant. This is a defect of the literal printed notation, not a claim that the authors’ implementation has this bug. Affects the proof.

**Existing correction evidence.** The authors’ MWSieve-new.m already performs the target quotient before taking Kernel(h): LiftInformation lines 2480–2493. URL https://www.mathe2.uni-bayreuth.de/stoll/magma/MWSieve-new.m; SHA-256 2e4b0cc03da645fdb3bcb554893a7dd736b97cae6b7ec1583942b12b0c31bd7f.

**Correction search.**

- Publisher article page and version-of-record PDF, DOI 10.1112/S1461157009000187, accessed 2026-09-27; no separate corrigendum found on the article page.
- arXiv 0906.1934 version history checked: v1 and v2 dated 10 June and 30 November 2009; no subsequent version listed. The v2 PDF was not read.
- Michael Stoll’s publications page AG31 and Magma directory, accessed 2026-09-27; the author-copy formula agrees with the published kernel notation, while the downloaded implementation already uses the quotient target.

**Independent review.** REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~4: confirmed. PrepareLift must retain the target subgroup: intersecting the original kernels can remove admissible target classes. Rechecked at the locator in the exact version and reading scope recorded by this review; other copies and prior correction searches remain historical provenance.

### EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E2 — misprint

**Source.** `de-weger-1989`, §3.12, definition of y before Lemma 3.15 and proof of Lemma 3.15, printed p. 65 (CWI Tract 65 scan)

**Observed claim.** y = ( 0, ..., 0, β'(μ) )^T … x − y = ( x1, ..., xn−1, xn−β'(μ) )^T … ordp[ Σ xi·θi − (xn−β'(μ)) ] ≥ p^μ

**Correction.** y = (0, …, 0, −β′^(μ))^T, so that x − y = (x_1, …, x_{n−1}, x_n + β′^(μ))^T and Lemma 3.13 gives ord_p(x_n + β′^(μ) − Σ_{i<n} x_iθ′_i) ≥ μ, which is ord_p(Λ′) ≥ μ for Λ′ = β′ − Σ x_iθ′_i + x_n.

**Reason and scope.** With the printed sign, Γ_μ + y is {x : ord_p(x_n − β′^(μ) − Σ x_iθ′_i) ≥ μ}. Example p = 3, μ = 1, n = 2, θ′_1 = 3 (so θ′_1^(1) = 0), β′ = 1: Γ_1 = ℤ × 3ℤ and Γ_1 + (0, 1) = {x_2 ≡ 1 (mod 3)}, while {x : ord_3(1 − 3x_1 + x_2) ≥ 1} = {x_2 ≡ 2 (mod 3)}. The proof also writes θ_i for θ′_i and '≥ p^μ' for '≥ μ'. Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §15, Lemma 14 uses the corrected sign y = (0, …, 0, −W_{v+r}β_0^(m)). Affects a stated result.

**Existing correction evidence.** new

**Correction search.**

- de Weger's publication page https://math.deweger.net/ (the CWI Tract is listed without an erratum)
- CWI repository record https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/13190 (no erratum attached)
- Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §15 (a 1992 paper by the same author with the correct sign; it does not mention the thesis slip)

**Independent review.** REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~4: confirmed. The sign of the affine translate is forced by subtracting the target vector; the corrected congruence matches Λ′. Rechecked at the locator in the exact version and reading scope recorded by this review; other copies and prior correction searches remain historical provenance.

### EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E5 — misprint

**Source.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1989`, §II.2, Lemma 2.1, p. 107 (definition of U_I) with (2.1), p. 108

**Observed claim.** The source defines U_I=(log|ε_i^{(h_l)}|)_{1≤i≤r,1≤l≤r}, putting units indexed by i in the rows and embeddings indexed by l in the columns. It writes U_I^(−1)=(u_il) and takes max_{1≤i≤r} Σ_{l=1}^r|u_il| as the norm.

**Correction.** l indicates a row and i a column: (U_I)_{l,i} = log|ε_i^{(h_l)}|, so that (2.1) (log|β^{(h_l)}/μ^{(h_l)}|)_l = U_I·(a_1, …, a_r)^T holds and a = U_I^{−1}(…) gives max|a_i| ≤ N[U_I^{−1}]·max_l|log|β^{(h_l)}/μ^{(h_l)}||.

**Reason and scope.** With the printed orientation the l-th entry of U_I·a is Σ_i log|ε_l^{(h_i)}|·a_i, not log|β^{(h_l)}/μ^{(h_l)}| = Σ_i a_i log|ε_i^{(h_l)}|, so (2.1) would be false; the row-sum norm of the inverse of the transposed matrix differs in general (for U = ((2, 1), (0, 1)) the row-sum norms of U^{−1} and (U^T)^{−1} are 1 and 3/2). Tzanakis–de Weger's 1992 paper (Lemma 6, p. 239) displays U_I with rows indexed by the embeddings, as corrected here. Affects nothing.

**Existing correction evidence.** new

**Correction search.**

- Tzanakis–de Weger, Compositio Math. 84 (1992), Lemma 6, p. 239 (uses the corrected orientation without comment)
- the University of Twente repository record of the 1989 article (no erratum attached)

**Independent review.** REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~4: confirmed. The embedding-vector identity fixes rows as embeddings and columns as units; transposition changes the inverse row-sum norm. Rechecked at the locator in the exact version and reading scope recorded by this review; other copies and prior correction searches remain historical provenance.

### EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E6 — error

**Source.** `de-weger-1989`, §3.13, Lemma 3.17(i), p. 67

**Observed claim.** The source gives Γ#_μ⊆Γ*_μ⊆Γ_μ. At p=2 it claims equality throughout; at p=3 it claims Γ*_μ=Γ_μ. For p≥3 it assigns (p−1)/2 to #(Γ_μ/Γ*_μ), p−1 to #(Γ_μ/Γ#_μ), and 2 to #(Γ*_μ/Γ#_μ).

**Correction.** For p = 2 only Γ*_μ = Γ_μ holds in general; for p ≥ 3 the indices divide (p−1)/2, p−1 and 2 respectively, with equality when the residues of the α_i generate (ℤ/p)^× (as in Chapter 6, where p_0 is chosen to be a primitive root).

**Reason and scope.** p = 2, α = (3, 5), μ = 0: ord_2(log_2 3) = ord_2(log_2 5) = 2 = μ_0, so Γ_0 = ℤ², but Γ#_0 = {x : 3^{x_1}5^{x_2} ≡ 1 (mod 4)} = {x_1 even}. p = 5, α = (6, 11), μ = 0: μ_0 = 1, Γ_0 = ℤ² and ξ ≡ 1 (mod 5) always, so Γ#_0 = Γ_0 and #(Γ_0/Γ#_0) = 1 ≠ 4. Affects a stated result.

**Existing correction evidence.** new

**Correction search.**

- the CWI repository record ir.cwi.nl/pub/13190 (no errata attached)
- de Weger's Chapter 6 (pp. 118–119), which avoids the issue by choosing p_0 a primitive root

**Independent review.** REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~4: confirmed. At p=2 the logarithm-kernel comparison does not give the odd-prime index assertions; generation assumptions are also necessary for equality. ### EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E7 — gap

**Source.** `tzanakis-de-weger-1989`, §II.3, (3.8) and the summary procedure, pp. 117–118

**Observed claim.** The source computes a continued fraction for ξ̃, keeping b₀,…,b_{k+1} as partial quotients and p_i/q_i as convergents, where 1≤i≤k and q_k≤C<q_{k+1}. Its tests on the convergents combine (3.8) with F(p_i,q_i)=m.

**Correction.** Condition (3.8), a_{k+1} > |q_k|^{n−2}/C_1 − 2, is proved for the partial quotient a_{k+1} of ξ^{(i_0)}; applied to the computed partial quotients b_{k+1} of ξ̃ it is not justified. Either test every convergent p_i/q_i of ξ̃ with q_i ≤ C directly (F(Zp_i, Zq_i) = m with Z^n ∣ m), or compute ξ^{(i_0)} precisely enough to determine a_{k+1}.

**Reason and scope.** The proof shows that p_k/q_k is a convergent of both ξ^{(i_0)} and ξ̃, but the next partial quotients can differ: if |ξ̃ − ξ^{(i_0)}| is close to its allowed maximum 1/(6C²) and q_k is close to C, then |ξ̃ − p_k/q_k| ≈ 1/(6q_k²), which forces b_{k+1} ≤ 5, while a solution with Y = q_k makes a_{k+1} > q_k^{n−2}/C_1 − 2 large; a test of (3.8) with b_{k+1} would then discard that solution. Affects the proof.

**Existing correction evidence.** new

**Correction search.**

- the University of Twente repository record of the article (no erratum attached)
- de Weger 1989, Chapter 3 (the thesis restates the reduction, not this test)

**Independent review.** REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~4: confirmed. A partial quotient of the true root is not automatically the partial quotient of a rational approximation; scanning all bounded convergents repairs the search. Rechecked at the locator in the exact version and reading scope recorded by this review; other copies and prior correction searches remain historical provenance.

### EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E12 — error

**Source.** `bruin-stoll-2010`, Lemma 4.1 and its proof, published p.281 (same in arXiv v2 and the author copy)

**Observed claim.** The source assumes p₁⋯p_m>e^{H′+γ}max{|a|,|b|}² and bounds the absolute value of its integer by e^{H′+γ}max{|a|,|b|}². It concludes that the integer must be zero because every p_j divides it.

**Correction.** |k1 b^2 − k2 ab + k3 a^2| ≤ (|k1| + |k2| + |k3|)·max{|a|,|b|}^2 ≤ 3e^{H′+γ}max{|a|,|b|}^2; the hypothesis should read p1 p2 · · · pm > 3e^{H′+γ} max{|a|, |b|}^2, under which the divisibility step gives k1 a^2 − k2 ab + k3 b^2 = 0 (the last step of the proof needs the further correction recorded as a separate gap).

**Reason and scope.** With coprime Kummer coordinates (k1, k2, k3) = (1, −1, 1) and a = b = 1 the integer is 3, while max|kj|·max{|a|,|b|}^2 = 1; the claimed estimate only bounds each of the three terms separately. Affects the proof.

**Existing correction evidence.** new

**Correction search.**

- Bruin–Stoll arXiv:0906.1934v2 and the author copy of 20 May 2009: the same text.
- The publisher article page (doi:10.1112/S1461157009000187) and Stoll's publication page were searched for a corrigendum on 2026-09-27; none is listed. No other correction was found in the references read here.

**Independent review.** REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~4: confirmed. Triangle inequality requires all three quadratic terms, giving the factor3 in the product threshold. Rechecked at the locator in the exact version and reading scope recorded by this review; other copies and prior correction searches remain historical provenance.

### EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E13 — misprint

**Source.** `bruin-stoll-2010`, Proof of Lemma 4.1, published p.281 (same in arXiv v2 and the author copy)

### EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E15 — misprint

**Source.** `bdmtv-2021`, Version of record, Compositio159 (2023), p.1129, item(3) after(4.2); same in arXiv:2101.01862v4 p.18.

### EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E17 — gap

**Source.** `bruin-stoll-2010`, Lemma 4.1, last sentence of the proof, published p.281 (same in arXiv v2 and the author copy)

**Observed claim.** The proof treats P₀≠P̄₀ as sufficient to distinguish both curve-image possibilities using just p_{j₀} as a reduction prime.

**Correction.** Require that the primes p_j separating P0 from P̄0 have product greater than e^{H′+γ} (for instance that every p_j separates them). At each separating prime the test then forces Q ≡ 0, so these primes divide k1, k2, k3, which are not all zero since Q ≠ 0: a contradiction.

**Reason and scope.** For P ∈ C(ℚ) with P ≠ P̄0 and P ≡ P̄0 modulo p_{j0}, the class Q = [P − P̄0] = [P + P0 − W] reduces to 0 = ι(P̃0) modulo p_{j0}, so it passes the test there, and it passes at every p_j where P0 ≡ P̄0; yet Q ∉ ι(C(ℚ)), since P + P0 is the unique effective divisor in its class and Q = −ι(P̄). One separating prime does not distinguish the two cases. Affects the proof.

**Existing correction evidence.** new

**Correction search.**

- Bruin–Stoll arXiv:0906.1934v2 and the author copy of 20 May 2009: the same text.
- The publisher article page (doi:10.1112/S1461157009000187) and Stoll's publication page: no corrigendum listed.

**Independent review.** REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~4: confirmed. The final coefficient-divisibility argument needs a sufficiently large product of primes separating the two conjugate points. Rechecked at the locator in the exact version and reading scope recorded by this review; other copies and prior correction searches remain historical provenance.

### EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E21 — error

**Source.** `bdmtv-2021`, Version of record, Compositio159 (2023), Lemma4.7, p.1136; same in arXiv:2101.01862v4 p.25.

**Observed claim.** max{i ≥ 0 : ordp(Fi) + i = n} < m

**Correction.** Require ord_p(F_i)+i≥n for every i≥m, equivalently max{i≥0:ord_p(F_i)+i<n}<m. This is the coefficient condition needed for the degree bound on G(x+α) modulo p^(n−k) used in the proof.

**Reason and scope.** With G(x) = p^(−k)F(px), the coefficient G_i has valuation ord_p(F_i) + i − k, so G is a polynomial of degree < m modulo p^(n−k) exactly when ord_p(F_i) + i ≥ n for i ≥ m. The printed condition only restricts the indices with ord_p(F_i) + i = n. For F = p² − p·x and n = 5 the printed set is empty, so m = 1 is allowed, k = 2, and the lemma would determine the roots from F_0 = p² modulo p⁵; but F has the root x = p in the disc, which F_0 does not see. Affects a stated result.

**Existing correction evidence.** new

**Correction search.**

- arXiv:2101.01862v4 (the version read)
- The published version (Compositio Math. 2023) was not opened

**Independent review.** REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~4: confirmed. The truncation must bound ord(F_i)+i for every tail index; the printed alternative cannot justify the claimed degree reduction. ### EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E36 — error

**Source.** `siksek-1995`, Exact author preprint infart2.pdf, printed/PDF p18, §4.2 projective representative conditions(1)–(2) before equation(41). Author-linked preprint dated February5,1995, 25 PDF/printed pages, SHA256 36b3079bb5277f819fbc0083d5020d774c8cb1cf6559fc82eebd5028510c31b3. Only this exact copy was visually verified; no assertion about the unread published version of record.

**Observed claim.** The source takes S_p inside Z^(r+s) with zero excluded, yet labels vector entries up to b_p throughout. Under Condition(2), all vectors in V_p, zero included, are quantified over, and β may be any scalar in F_p.

**Correction.** Write each vector as (b₁,…,b_(r+s)). For the computable surviving subspace V′_p, choose exactly one bounded integral lift of each one-dimensional subspace of V′_p; equivalently, every nonzero a∈V′_p has a unique representative b∈S_p with a=β(b mod p) for some β∈F_p^×. Then the required coverage also holds for V_p minus zero, since V_p⊆V′_p. Zero requires no projective representative; if V′_p={0}, take S_p empty. This states a sufficient corrected representative construction, not a claim that the full numerical point-recognition procedure is certified.

**Reason and scope.** At a=0, every b∈S_p satisfies the printed congruence with β=0, so uniqueness fails whenever S_p has at least two elements; with S_p empty existence fails. Even when S_p has one element the zero clause does not express a projective class. For example a two-dimensional F₂ surviving space has three projective classes, all representing zero when multiplied by0. The missing nonzero scope is essential to the literal condition. The b_p notation is independently dimensionally inconsistent with Z^(r+s) and the r+s-term sum(41). Affects a stated result.

Stable node IDs, synchronized omission records, full API/test coverage and the removed-owner boundary were checked; the [review handoff](../handoff/REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~4.md) records what formalization still requires. A follow-up implements the stated mathematical targets, supplies each conditional example’s exact arithmetic inputs, resolves the explicit supplier/geometric/normalization gaps and proves the declared statements. It must keep numerical replay claims scoped to the transcripts actually checked. This revision completes one planning job and does not claim a second issue.
